items.author: ZAFAR BHUTTA
items.content:
The Petroleum Division has placed Jura Energy's petroleum rights matter before the Economic Coordination Committee (ECC) after the Law Division cited rules providing for revocation of all petroleum rights due to their transfer without prior consent of the government.
Sources familiar with the matter said the Petroleum Division had prepared a summary titled "Disposition of Controlling Shares of Jura Energy Corporation from Phoenix Exploration Limited to IDL Investments Limited without Prior Consent of the Government" and submitted two options for consideration of the ECC.
The case pertains to the transfer of all 73.3% controlling shares of Jura Energy by Phoenix Exploration, a Bermuda-based company, to IDL Investments, a British Virgin Islands-based investment entity, without obtaining prior consent of Pakistan's government.
Sources said Spud Energy and Frontier Holdings were the holders of working interest in several petroleum exploration rights under the Petroleum Concession Agreements with the government and the Petroleum Division treated the transaction at the ultimate parent-company level, resulting in change of effective control of the petroleum rights holders. Despite the legal position, the Petroleum Division has not proceeded directly with revocation of the petroleum rights and has instead approached the ECC with two alternatives.
Under the first option, the government may revoke all petroleum rights held by Spud Energy and Frontier Holdings on account of transfer of shares from Phoenix Exploration to IDL Investments without prior government consent. Under the second option, the Petroleum Division has proposed that it be authorised to issue a warning to the companies and retrospectively regularise the share transfer.
Sources said the Petroleum Division cited the fact that the disputed transaction took place at the ultimate parent-company level and also highlighted the importance of existing petroleum rights to the business of relevant companies.
The regulatory issue stems from provisions governing changes in ownership and effective control of companies holding petroleum rights.
Sources said the Directorate General of Petroleum Concessions had earlier initiated proceedings against the companies over the alleged change in control and the matter subsequently went through legal and regulatory scrutiny. The Petroleum Division sought the opinion of the Law and Justice Division and subsequently held a meeting with the minister for petroleum and the minister for law to seek further clarity on the legal position.
Sources said the Law Division, in its advice, maintained that both Rule 68 of the 1986 Rules and Rule 69 of the 2001 Rules provided that the government "may revoke" petroleum rights where the prescribed grounds existed and the required procedure had been followed. The Law Division explained that the use of word "may" was enabling in nature and conferred discretionary power on the federal government. According to sources, the Law Division specifically advised that the question of whether the power of revocation should or should not be exercised was essentially an administrative and commercial determination to be made by the Petroleum Division, as the concerned authority, after taking into account all relevant facts, efficacy, financial obligations, contractual obligations and the overall circumstances of the case.
Sources said the legal advice did not make revocation mandatory merely because prescribed grounds may exist, but recognised the government's discretion to exercise the revocation power after considering the administrative, commercial and contractual circumstances.
Jura has taken the position that the transfer of Phoenix Exploration shareholding in Jura Energy to IDL Investments did not result in the change in effective control of Frontier Holdings or Spud Energy, which continued to remain under Jura as their parent company. According to the company's position, there was therefore no disposition of the share capital of petroleum rights holders themselves and consequently there was no requirement for prior government approval under the applicable rules. The Petroleum Division, however, has taken a different position and considers that the transaction at the ultimate parent-company level resulted in the change in effective control pertaining to the petroleum rights held by Frontier Holdings and Spud Energy.
The matter has assumed additional significance because of the Petroleum Division's earlier handling of the legal issue concerning the imposition of an off-grid levy on third-party gas suppliers.
Sources said the government had relied on Law Division's advice while extending the captive power levy framework to the third-party companies supplying gas to captive power plants. The legal advice in that case was used to support the government's position that the levy could be extended to such suppliers through the relevant statutory mechanism.

The City Traffic Police have asked the Regional Transport Authority (RTA) to temporarily suspend Green Electric Bus services on two routes due to ongoing construction of underpasses on Peshawar Road.
In a letter to the RTA secretary, Chief Traffic Officer (CTO) Farhan Aslam identified Route No. 1, which operates from Saddar Stop to Bhatta Chowk, and Route No. 4, which runs from Marrir Metro Bus Station to Chowk 26 No. via Peshawar Road.
The ongoing construction has forced authorities to divert traffic through narrower roads, including routes from Abid Majeed Turn toward Convoy Road and from the Rafay Mall area toward Chairing Cross and Maryam Hospital.
The CTO said these roads have limited capacity and that the wider Green Electric Buses could cause congestion and increase the risk of accidents. He requested suspension of the routes until construction ends to facilitate commuters and prevent accidents.
The request comes after a nine-year-old girl died when a Green Bus hit the motorcycle carrying her and her father on Adiala Road on Wednesday. Angry protesters later set the rear of the bus on fire.
The district administration has also closed schools along Peshawar Road for two months and directed them to conduct online classes. Parents have criticized the decision, saying authorities could have completed major construction work during the summer vacation.

items.author: Hope Abah
items.content:
Former Governor Samuel Ortom on Saturday accused the administration of Governor Hyacinth Alia of attacking him and the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) governorship candidate, Chief Michael Aondoakaa, as a means of diverting attention from issues confronting the state.
Ortom, who spoke through his former Special Adviser on Media and Publicity, Terver Akase, said the recent attacks by the governor and his media aides had failed to address questions arising from the reported obstruction of the presidential candidate of the National Democratic Party (NDC) in the 2027 election, Peter Obi, during his recent visit to Benue State.
He said rather than explain the circumstances surrounding Obi’s movement in Makurdi while on a humanitarian visit to internally displaced persons (IDPs), the administration had focused on attacking its political opponents.
He noted that the government should account for the resources accruing to the state since the removal of the fuel subsidy and explain how the funds had been deployed to projects and services across the 23 local government areas.
Gunmen kill 3 herders, 50 cattle in fresh Plateau attack
I Inherited N11,000, 5 Pieces Of Cloth From My Father — Emir Of Zazzau
Ortom also questioned the administration’s response to insecurity, agriculture, infrastructure, employment, education, healthcare and the welfare of displaced persons, saying these issues would be more important to voters ahead of the 2027 governorship election.
He further criticised what he described as the government’s response to the security situation in Ayilamo, Logo Local Government Area, where residents and security personnel were reportedly killed in an attack by armed men.
The former governor said the reported attack should attract greater attention from the government, given its responsibility for the protection of lives and property in the state.
Ortom, while reacting to the allegation that he was secretly supporting Obi while publicly backing President Bola Tinubu, described the claim as contradictory.
He said he supported Obi during the 2023 presidential election openly, while his subsequent support for Tinubu was also publicly declared.
He also rejected attempts to link him to the controversy surrounding Obi’s visit to Benue, describing such claims as politically motivated.
The former governor instead alleged that the growing attacks on Aondoakaa showed that the PDP candidate had emerged as a major challenger to the governor ahead of the 2027 election.
He maintained that the attention being given to Aondoakaa by the Alia camp indicated that the PDP candidate was being regarded as a serious political challenger.
Ortom posited that Aondoakaa had presented himself as an alternative focused on security, accountability, local government autonomy and the return of displaced persons to their ancestral communities.
He stressed that the PDP candidate had also pledged to enforce the Open Grazing Prohibition and Ranches Establishment Law, 2017, in order to secure farming communities and create conditions for farmers to return to their farms.
He therefore urged the Alia administration to focus on its record in office rather than attacks on political opponents, saying the 2027 election would ultimately be determined by the performance of the government.
“The 2027 contest in Benue State will not be about propaganda or insults. It will be a referendum on failure versus competence, excuses versus solutions and misplaced priorities versus purposeful leadership,” the former governor posited.

Now, let’s take a look at some of the other major developments involving listed new-age tech companies this week.
RentoMojo To List Next: Furniture and appliance rental startup RentoMojo’s IPO closed with a subscription of 72.88X, receiving bids for 158.68 Cr shares against 2.18 Cr shares on offer. Its shares are tentatively scheduled to list on the bourses on Thursday (September 17).
Shiprocket Cuts Loss: The logistics company’s consolidated net loss narrowed 24% YoY and 16% QoQ to ₹13.7 Cr in Q1 FY27. Its operating revenue jumped 34% YoY and 7% QoQ to ₹592.1 Cr. Shiprocket shares gained 1.99% during the week to close at ₹134.05.
Cofounder Pledges EaseMyTrip Shares: Cofounder and chairman Nishant Pitti pledged 34.51 Cr EaseMyTrip shares, worth around ₹211.9 Cr, to Motilal Oswal Financial Services for “personal use”. The latest pledge represents 8.66% of the online travel aggregator’s total share capital. Pitti’s total encumbered holding now stands at 44.87 Cr shares, equivalent to 11.26% of the company’s share capital.
Swiggy-Udaan Deal: Swiggy will sell retail distribution platform LYNK to Udaan through a share-swap transaction valued at around ₹500 Cr. In return, Swiggy will receive a roughly 2.8% stake in Udaan and invest another ₹75 Cr for an additional 0.4%, taking its total holding in the B2B ecommerce unicorn to about 3.2%.
Veefin Eyes Mainboard Migration: BSE SME-listed fintech SaaS company Veefin Solutions submitted an information memorandum to the BSE to migrate to its mainboard. It also plans to apply for direct listing on the NSE after receiving the requisite approval from the BSE.
Meesho Scraps CPO Role: Ecommerce major Meesho discontinued the position of chief product officer as part of a restructuring of its product leadership team. Consequently, incumbent CPO Prasanna Arunachalam ceased to be part of the company’s senior management personnel.
Go Digit Director Resigns: Go Digit independent director Giridhar Aramane resigned following an increase in his responsibilities after being appointed chairman and managing director of Unitech Ltd.
BlackBuck Sets Up Subsidiary: BlackBuck’s board approved the incorporation of wholly owned subsidiary BlackBuck Transport Services Pvt Ltd to provide trucking and logistics services. The subsidiary may own or lease commercial vehicles, develop platforms for transport-asset transactions, and provide fleet management, warehousing, and related services.
Against this backdrop, here is a look at the broader market performance during the week.
Markets Fall For Fifth Week
India’s benchmark indices ended lower for the fifth consecutive week amid elevated crude oil prices, rising global bond yields, and concerns over US inflation.
The Sensex declined 2.27% during the week to close at 74,781.76, while the Nifty 50 fell 2.09% to 23,398.10. The midcap and smallcap indices also declined 1.40% and 0.88%, respectively.
Crude oil added to market pressure, with Brent briefly crossing $110 per barrel yesterday before ending the week at $104.61, up 8.7%, amid the escalating US-Iran conflict and disruptions along key Middle Eastern shipping routes. Persistently high oil prices could add to India’s imported inflation, widen the current account deficit, increase costs for companies, and put further pressure on the rupee.
Meanwhile, the US 10-year Treasury yield moved closer to 5%. A sustained increase in US bond yields could strengthen the dollar and accelerate foreign portfolio investor outflows from emerging markets such as India.
Foreign portfolio investors pulled out around ₹7,443 Cr from Indian equities in the first week of September after turning net buyers in July and August.
The ongoing correction follows a mixed performance in August. While the Nifty 50 declined 1.24% during the month, the Nifty Midcap 150 and Nifty Smallcap 250 gained 1.72% and 2.52%, respectively. The Nifty Microcap 250 rose 5.41%.
Despite the near-term volatility, brokerages remain constructive on India’s longer-term prospects. Morgan Stanley expects the Sensex to reach 89,000 by June 2027, provided crude oil prices moderate. Jefferies sees opportunities emerging from India’s next industrial cycle across manufacturing, semiconductors, electronics, space, and data-centre infrastructure.
Investors will now track the US Federal Reserve’s policy decision, domestic inflation data, crude oil prices, and developments in the US-Iran conflict for further cues.
Now, let’s take a look at the performance of the week’s biggest gainer and the fintech group.
ESDS Extends Blockbuster Run
ESDS Software emerged as the standout performer among recently listed new-age tech companies, with its stock nearly doubling during its first full week of trading despite weakness in the broader market. The enterprise cloud and AI infrastructure company made its market debut on September 4. Its shares closed their debut session at ₹895.50 on the BSE, more than double the IPO price of ₹429.
The rally continued throughout the week, with the stock touching its upper circuit in every session.
Its circuit limit was subsequently narrowed from 20% to 10%.
ESDS shares ended at ₹1,716.35 on the BSE yesterday, up 91.65% from their debut-day closing price. The stock is now 300.1% above its IPO price.
The company’s market capitalisation stood at around ₹20,118 Cr (about $2.11 Bn) at the end of the week, compared with an IPO valuation of about ₹5,028 Cr.
The rally highlighted strong investor appetite for listed AI infrastructure plays. ESDS’ ₹720 Cr IPO was subscribed 135.88X, with the portion reserved for qualified institutional buyers (QIBs) booked 261.51X.
Optimism from the Street provided another trigger. Choice Institutional Equities initiated coverage on ESDS with a ‘Buy’ rating and a price target of ₹1,550, citing its AI infrastructure opportunity and $1.25 Bn contract with Sharon AI.
ESDS crossed Choice’s target price within five trading sessions.
Fintech Stocks Ride MDR Hopes
Shares of listed fintech companies rallied during the week of the Global Fintech Fest (GFF) 2026, with the possibility of MDR being introduced on certain UPI transactions providing investors with a potential earnings trigger.
Pine Labs was among the biggest beneficiaries, gaining 14.17% during the week to close at ₹202.35.
The stock surged 16.9% during yesterday’s session alone, while Paytm, MobiKwik, and AvenuesAI also posted sharp gains.
The rally followed a report that an MDR of around 40 basis points could be introduced on UPI transactions involving larger merchants or higher transaction values.
UPI currently operates under a zero-MDR regime, limiting the direct revenue that banks and payment companies earn from such transactions and leaving them dependent on adjacent services and government incentives.
Introducing MDR, even on a limited set of transactions, could therefore create a direct revenue stream for banks, acquiring entities, and third-party application providers.
Brokerage Bernstein named Paytm its top fintech pick, citing the possible introduction of MDR, growth in merchant lending, and improving operating leverage as potential earnings drivers.
The developments coincided with GFF 2026, where UPI and the next phase of India’s digital payments ecosystem took centre stage. Prime Minister Narendra Modi called for expanding UPI’s international footprint and linking it with more global payment systems, while NPCI unveiled initiatives spanning ticketing, contactless payments, and international RuPay credit card payments through UPI.

items.author: Daily Trust
items.content:
Former National Chairman of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), Alhaji Bamanga Mohammed Tukur, is dead.
He passed away at the age of 90.
Tukur, a former governor of the old Gongola State, Minister of Industries, businessman and presidential aspirant, died on Saturday, September 12, 2026, according to a statement issued by his family.
His son, Hon. Awwal D. Tukur, who announced the death on behalf of the family, said arrangements were underway to take his remains to Yola, Adamawa State, for burial.
&#8216;Committed party man&#8217;, PDP mourns Bamanga Tukur
Bamanga Tukur for burial Sunday – Family
The family, in the statement, said Tukur died after a life dedicated to service to his family, community, Adamawa State and Nigeria.
“It is with profound sadness and total submission to the will of Almighty Allah that the family announces the passing of our beloved father and patriarch, Alhaji Bamanga Mohammed Tukur, who returned to his Creator today 12th September 2026,” the statement said.
It described him as a man whose “wisdom, generosity and commitment to the development of our nation touched countless lives,” adding that his legacy would endure for generations.
The family thanked those who had offered prayers, condolences and support following his death and said details of the Janazah, or funeral prayer, and other burial arrangements would be announced.
The family also prayed that Almighty Allah would forgive his shortcomings, accept his good deeds and grant him Aljannatul Firdaus.
“Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji’un,” it added.
Born on September 15, 1935, Tukur would have turned 91 three days after his death.
He had a career spanning public administration, politics, business and economic advocacy, rising to national prominence through the Nigerian Ports Authority (NPA), where he served as General Manager and Chief Executive from the mid-1970s into the early 1980s.
He later ventured into partisan politics and became governor of the old Gongola State, which was subsequently divided into present-day Adamawa and Taraba states.
Tukur assumed office in October 1983 on the platform of the then National Party of Nigeria (NPN). His tenure, however, lasted about three months before the military coup of December 31, 1983, which brought the Second Republic to an end.
During the transition programme under military President Ibrahim Babangida, Tukur returned to frontline politics and contested for the presidency on the platform of the defunct National Republican Convention (NRC) in the botched Third Republic.
He later served as Minister of Industries during the military administration of General Sani Abacha in the 1990s.
Outside government, Tukur established business interests associated with the DADDO Group and became involved in efforts to promote private-sector participation in Africa’s economic development.
He served as Executive President of the African Business Roundtable and chaired the NEPAD Business Group, where he worked with business leaders and policymakers on investment and economic development issues.
His international engagements also included positions in maritime and business organisations. He served as Vice Chairman of the International Ports and Harbours Association and Chairman of the International Cargo Handling Association, among other roles.
Tukur later emerged as a prominent figure in the PDP and was elected National Chairman of the party in March 2012 during the administration of former President Goodluck Jonathan.
His tenure came amid internal tensions within the then-ruling party, including the 2013 rebellion that led to the emergence of the “New PDP” faction involving several governors and senior political figures.
He resigned as PDP National Chairman in January 2014 and was later appointed Ambassador-at-Large by the Jonathan administration.
Tukur also held the traditional titles of Tafidan Adamawa and Wakilin Ganye and was a recipient of the Commander of the Order of the Niger (CON).
In a tribute to mark his 88th birthday in 2023, President Bola Tinubu described Tukur’s career as one that spanned Nigeria’s private and public sectors, highlighting his service as governor, NPA chief, Minister of Industries, PDP chairman and African business leader.
His death marks the end of a long public career that spanned Nigeria’s post-independence public service, the Second and Third Republic political eras and the Fourth Republic.

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
A proposed overhaul of Sindh’s local government law ran into fierce opposition on Saturday, with MQM-P, PTI and Jamaat-e-Islami rejecting key government proposals and accusing the provincial administration of seeking to curb elected mayors’ powers and pave the way for unelected administrators.
A parliamentary committee constituted to examine amendments to the Sindh Local Government Act met at the Sindh Assembly, with government and opposition lawmakers taking part. The meeting reviewed the proposed new local government legislation, while representatives of participating parties also submitted their own amendments.
Speaking to the media after the meeting, Sindh Home Minister Ziaul Hassan Lanjar said the government had proposed a mechanism for the period following the completion of local representatives’ terms.
Read: Sindh moves to keep mayors, chairmen in power after term
Under the proposal, he said, the Election Commission of Pakistan would be formally approached 120 days before local government elections, allowing sufficient time for delimitation and other electoral preparations.
Lanjar said delimitation was essential before elections and pointed out that different schedules had been issued during previous polls. Once an election schedule was announced, he added, the Election Commission would make the necessary arrangements, while an administrator would handle day-to-day affairs in the interim.
He said the government wanted to strengthen the Election Commission, adding that political parties represented in the committee had also put forward their proposed amendments.
The government’s position, however, drew a sharp response from opposition members.
MQM-P lawmaker Taha Ahmed rejected the committee proceedings outright, alleging that the government was treating the Sindh Assembly as a “personal domain” and deliberately resisting the transfer of powers to elected local representatives.
He demanded that mayors be given full powers under Article 140-A of the Constitution and called for implementation of the PPP’s own 2008 manifesto commitment on devolution of local government powers.
Ahmed questioned the proposed removal of the mayor’s authority over the master plan, solid waste management and the Water Board, alleging that legislation was being tailored to strengthen a “fake mayor”.
He warned that MQM-P would launch protests across the country if what he described as controversial legislation was not stopped.
Also Read: Karachi mayor’s office affected as fire breaks out at KMC building
MQM-P’s Iftikhar Alam also rejected the proposed law, saying the party had serious reservations about making mayors administrators. Such an arrangement, he argued, could compromise the transparency of elections, particularly if polls were delayed because the proposed amendments did not clearly define the administrator’s tenure.
Alam said the committee had also failed to address the transfer of powers to local governments in line with Supreme Court directives, describing the proceedings as a “joke”.
PTI’s Shabbir Qureshi said his party had rejected the government’s proposals, particularly the suggestion to place unelected representatives in union councils. PTI, he said, had instead demanded the appointment of internal administrators.
Qureshi also criticised the existing arrangements for solid waste management and alleged that powers had been taken away from the Water Board and the Sindh Building Control Authority. He called for the implementation of the Sindh Local Government Act 2013 in accordance with Article 140-A and Supreme Court judgments.
Jamaat-e-Islami’s Muhammad Farooq said Sindh already had a local government law, but the system remained powerless because authority had not been genuinely devolved.
He said JI had proposed holding local government elections within 120 days and opposed appointing administrators, but its amendments were not accepted. The party also rejected a proposed oversight mechanism in place of transferring powers down to the union council level.
Farooq said none of the proposals submitted by JI three months ago had been accepted and warned that the party would approach the courts if the proposed amendments were enacted.

items.author: Afaq Wajdan Malik
items.content:
Apple’s iPhone Duo is finally official, bringing the company into the foldable phone market after years of watching Samsung, Oppo, Google, and others refine the category.
It is also Apple’s first major new iPhone form factor since the original iPhone arrived 19 years ago. That makes the Duo significant regardless of whether foldable phones eventually become mainstream.
But as GSMArena points out in its analysis of the device, Apple has not somehow eliminated the compromises that have followed book-style foldables for years. In several areas, the iPhone Duo still asks buyers to accept worse hardware in exchange for a folding display.
$2,000 Is Still a Lot for a Phone
The first problem is obvious: price.
The iPhone Duo starts at around $2,000, putting it close to double the price of a conventional flagship phone.
That is hardly unusual for a premium foldable, but seven years after the original Galaxy Fold, the category has still struggled to justify why folding hardware should command such a large premium.
Apple has historically been better than most companies at convincing customers to pay more for new categories, but recent products such as the Vision Pro and iPhone Air have shown that even Apple cannot assume high-priced hardware will automatically become a success.
The Duo may be less expensive than some earlier rumors suggested, but $2,000 remains a substantial commitment.
It Still Is Not Really a Phone and Tablet in One
Foldables are often sold as a smartphone and tablet combined into a single device.
In practice, the experience is more complicated.
As GSMArena notes, a proper tablet still gives users considerably more screen space, longer battery life, and a layout that is better suited to productivity, drawing, and media consumption.
Foldable displays are larger than ordinary phone screens, but not always by enough to replace a tablet. Video is a good example: because the outer and inner displays can have similar usable width in landscape mode, opening the phone does not necessarily produce a dramatically larger viewing experience.
The phone side comes with compromises as well. Foldables are generally thicker, heavier, and harder to protect, while cameras, cooling, and batteries frequently suffer because of the space required by the hinge and folding display.
The iPhone Duo does not completely escape those trade-offs.
Cameras Take a Step Back
One of the clearest compromises is the camera system.
The iPhone Duo has a main camera and an ultra-wide camera, but there is no dedicated telephoto lens.
GSMArena notes that while the ultra-wide is comparable to the unit used on the iPhone 18 Pro, the main camera itself is not at the same level.
That makes for an unusual proposition: buyers are paying far more than they would for an iPhone 18 Pro while receiving a less complete camera system.
The reason is largely physical. A foldable is effectively two extremely thin phone halves joined together, leaving less depth for large camera modules.
Battery Life and Cooling Also Suffer
The same space limitations affect the battery.
Foldables generally need to split their batteries across both halves of the device, which is less space-efficient than placing one large battery inside a conventional phone.
According to Apple’s own figures cited by GSMArena, the iPhone Duo delivers shorter battery life than the iPhone 18 Pro Max, even when using its smaller outer display. The difference grows when the larger folding screen is used for activities such as video streaming.
Charging is also slower.
Thermal performance presents another challenge. The Duo uses the same chipset as the iPhone 18 Pro, but each side of the device is thinner, leaving less material and space available to dissipate heat.
Under sustained workloads, that could cause the Duo to reduce performance sooner and more aggressively than a conventional Pro iPhone.
Foldables Are Still More Fragile
Durability remains one of the hardest problems for the entire category.
Every foldable adds a large mechanical hinge and a softer folding display, introducing potential failure points that simply do not exist on a standard smartphone.
Apple has at least given the iPhone Duo an IP68 rating, which is stronger protection than many earlier foldables offered.
Even so, the flexible inner screen is inherently more vulnerable than the glass covering a normal iPhone display, and foldable cases are generally less effective because they cannot fully protect the hinge and moving parts.
Touch ID Returns, With the Usual Side-Sensor Problems
The iPhone Duo also brings back Touch ID, with the fingerprint reader positioned on the side of the phone.
That is necessary because providing Face ID hardware for both the outer and inner displays would create additional design complications.
It is still a downgrade in convenience for people accustomed to Face ID.
Side-mounted fingerprint sensors have a smaller scanning area and are also less comfortable for some users, particularly left-handed users.
Apple has additionally moved the volume buttons to the top edge of the Duo, another design choice that may require some adjustment.
The Crease Is Better, But It Is Still There
Perhaps the most visible reminder that the Duo is a foldable is the crease running across its inner screen.
Apple has made significant progress here.
The inner display uses a matte nano coating, which reduces reflections that normally make a foldable crease more obvious. Early hands-on footage also suggests the panel itself is comparatively flat.
GSMArena notes that the result is one of the least noticeable creases seen on a foldable.
But it has not disappeared entirely.
For anyone who finds even a subtle crease distracting, the iPhone Duo does not provide the completely flat flexible display the industry has been chasing.
Where Apple Has Done Better
The story is not entirely about compromises.
One of the iPhone Duo’s biggest strengths could be software optimization.
Android foldables have existed for years, yet many apps still simply stretch their normal phone interfaces across the larger inner screen.
Apple has already demonstrated apps designed specifically for the Duo’s two displays, and its tighter control over iOS and the App Store could encourage developers to optimize their software more quickly.
Display transitions also appear significantly more polished.
In hands-on demonstrations highlighted by GSMArena, games can move between the outer and inner screens without restarting, while orientation changes happen smoothly.
Apple is also making more deliberate use of the half-folded position.
Apps can divide controls and content between the two halves, video playback controls can move to the lower screen, and games can place virtual controls on one section while displaying gameplay on the other.
The phone can even sit on its edges in a nightstand-style mode with dedicated widgets.
Even the Speakers Have Been Rethought
Apple has also addressed an issue that rarely receives much attention on foldables: stereo speakers.
The Duo places its two speakers diagonally across the device.
Software then determines how the phone is being held and adjusts the left and right channels accordingly, accounting for both speaker position and distance.
It is a small detail, but one that shows Apple has put considerable thought into how a folding device behaves in different orientations.
A Better Foldable, Not a Compromise-Free One
The iPhone Duo appears to improve the foldable experience in several meaningful ways, particularly through software, display transitions, half-folded modes and app support.
But Apple has not rewritten the basic physics of foldable phones.
The Duo is still expensive, less durable than a conventional iPhone and compromised in cameras, battery life and sustained performance. Its crease is smaller rather than nonexistent, and the larger screen still does not fully replace a dedicated tablet.
As GSMArena’s analysis concludes, that does not necessarily make the iPhone Duo a bad product. It simply means buyers need to understand that foldables remain devices built around compromise.
Apple may have produced one of the most polished versions yet, but spending more than $2,000 still requires accepting that a folding iPhone does some things better and several important things worse than a standard flagship.
The post Even iPhone Duo Does Not Fix The Biggest Problems With Foldables appeared first on ProPakistani.

items.content:
The MQM-P has renewed its push for new provinces, declaring that the case for a separate administrative unit in urban Sindh is stronger than anywhere else in the country and warning that a transparent census and corrected voter lists could force the PPP to confront the demand itself.
Speaking at a seminar titled “National Dialogue” organised by the MQM-P Graduate Forum Pakistan at a local hotel on Saturday, party chairman and Federal Education Minister Dr Khalid Maqbool Siddiqui said the demand for new provinces dated back to the APMSO era, well before the formation of the MQM.
“Pakistan is our motherland, while provinces are merely administrative units,” Siddiqui said, arguing that provinces should be divided on the basis of population to improve governance and facilitate development.
Read: Parliament to decide on creating new provinces: Sanaullah
He maintained that although the existing provinces had been formed largely along linguistic lines, the MQM-P was seeking new provinces on administrative grounds. Of all demands for new provinces across the country, he said, the case of urban Sindh was “the strongest and most justified” because the region carried a major share of Pakistan’s economic burden while continuing to face deprivation.
Siddiqui further claimed that if an honest and transparent census were conducted in Sindh and voter lists were properly corrected, the PPP itself would be compelled to demand the creation of a new province.
Senior MQM-P leader Dr Farooq Sattar said the country’s four provinces were effectively controlled by a handful of families, while the status quo had survived despite the devolution of powers to provinces under the 18th Amendment.
He said provincial powers had failed to trickle down to the grassroots and announced that the MQM-P had already submitted a constitutional amendment bill in the National Assembly seeking to empower local governments under Article 140-A.
Sattar also called for a public referendum on the creation of new provinces under Article 48(6), urging people from different walks of life to unite for what he described as a historic rally on Sharae Faisal in support of their survival and development.
Karachi Chamber of Commerce and Industry President Rehan Hanif, trader leader Atiq Mir and former bureaucrat Barrister Shahab Imam also spoke in favour of new administrative units and an empowered local government system, saying Karachi’s economic infrastructure had deteriorated and that restrictions on hiring local residents in public institutions, coupled with the appointment of non-local personnel, had aggravated a sense of injustice.

items.author: Afaq Wajdan Malik
items.content:
Humanoid robots have spent years looking impressive on exhibition floors while remaining far too large, expensive or specialized for an ordinary living room. PrimeBOT’s latest machines suggest that gap may finally be starting to close.
At IFA 2026 in Berlin, GizmoChina’s Will Chu spent time with the PrimeBOT Q1 and T1, two robots designed around companionship and everyday use rather than factory work. His hands-on impressions point to a different direction for consumer robotics: smaller machines that can talk, follow people, carry things, help children and fit into a home without dominating it.
PrimeBOT itself describes the idea simply as “Your First Personal Robot.” Rather than positioning these machines as replacements for workers, the company wants them to live alongside their owners and gradually become part of everyday routines.
Q1 Is Small Enough to Live With
The PrimeBOT Q1 is the more conventional humanoid of the two, but its size immediately separates it from the large robots usually associated with the category.
At roughly 88cm tall, the Q1 is small enough to carry and potentially transport in a large bag. GizmoChina’s hands-on report describes it as light enough to carry under one arm, with a design closer to a polished consumer gadget than laboratory equipment.
That size matters inside a home. A full-size humanoid walking through a bedroom or sitting next to a child can easily feel excessive. Q1’s smaller proportions make it less imposing while still allowing it to walk, move its arms and interact physically.
During the demonstration, the robot could walk while holding a person’s hand and adjust its pace. It also supports spoken interaction in around nine languages and can answer basic questions through its onboard speaker.
GizmoChina demonstrated this by asking Q1 what a child should do after being hit by another student at school. The robot advised against fighting back and suggested documenting what happened and telling a teacher. It is a small example, but one that shows where PrimeBOT sees the product fitting: somewhere between an AI assistant, educational tool and companion.
It Is Also Built for Developers
Q1 is not only intended to answer questions.
PrimeBOT is positioning it as an open platform for developers, educators and robotics enthusiasts. Users can modify its behaviour and use it as a physical platform for experimenting with embodied AI, giving developers something more tangible than running another model on a laptop.
That could make the robot useful in schools and universities as well as homes.
Instead of requiring a dedicated robotics lab, students could potentially work with a machine that is compact enough to sit alongside normal classroom equipment.
This combination of portability and programmability may prove more important to consumer robotics than simply making a humanoid stronger or faster.
T1 Takes a Different Approach
The PrimeBOT T1 tackles another problem: one robot body is rarely ideal for every situation.
T1 can change between a humanoid-style configuration and a four-legged form. PrimeBOT says the design is intended to let it operate across different indoor and outdoor environments rather than being confined to one type of movement.
In practical terms, that means the robot could stand near a desk when interacting with someone, lower itself to move through another part of the house, and change its posture again depending on the task.
PrimeBOT is also targeting creators with the T1.
The robot can follow a person and hold a camera, opening the possibility of using it for automatically filmed videos or vlogs. The company has also demonstrated carrying functions that could allow it to transport smaller items during activities such as shopping.
That makes it closer to a mobile companion than a traditional smart speaker with legs.
Why Personal Robots Are Starting to Make More Sense
The most interesting thing about Q1 and T1 is not any single feature.
Voice assistants can already answer questions. Cameras can already track people. Robot vacuums already navigate houses. Smartphones already contain powerful AI models.
What personal robots potentially add is the ability to combine those functions into something that can physically move through the same environment as its owner.
Q1 shows how shrinking a humanoid can make it less intimidating and easier to integrate into normal spaces. T1 shows why future robots may need bodies that can adapt rather than remain locked into a single human-like shape.
For families, that could eventually mean a robot that moves between rooms, talks to children, provides information, follows people during activities and assists with simple physical tasks.
For developers, the same hardware becomes a programmable AI platform.
They Are Not Quite Appliances Yet
There is still an important distinction between an impressive demonstration and a product as established as a smartphone or television.
Public information about pricing, battery endurance, long-term reliability and broad international availability remains limited. Some independent tracking also notes that several key specifications and retail details have not yet been fully established.
That means it would be premature to declare that everyone will have one next year.
The demonstrations nevertheless show how the category is changing.
For years, humanoid robotics has largely focused on proving that machines can walk, run, lift boxes or perform industrial jobs. PrimeBOT is instead asking a more relevant consumer question: what would make someone actually want a robot inside their home?
Based on GizmoChina’s hands-on experience with the Q1 and T1, the answer may be smaller size, approachable design, useful AI, adaptability and the ability to become part of everyday life rather than simply completing one repetitive task.
Personal robots still have plenty to prove, but for the first time, machines like these are starting to look less like research projects and more like something that could realistically share a living room.

items.author: Arooj Fatima
items.content:
The Pakistan Football Federation (PFF) has launched the FIFA Football for Schools program in Pakistan, targeting three million students across 3,000 public schools as part of a major grassroots development initiative.
Backed by FIFA in collaboration with the Prime Minister’s Youth Programme and UNESCO, the program will distribute 162,000 footballs among participating schools.
More than 50 master trainers have already completed specialized training under FIFA instructors led by Antonio Buenano Sanchez, FIFA’s Senior Football for Schools Manager.
PFF President Syed Mohsen Gilani said grassroots development would remain central to the federation’s strategy, adding that the program would also help identify talented young players from across the country.
With football infrastructure remaining a major challenge in Pakistan, the initiative will initially focus on public schools. FIFA has set criteria for selecting schools and teachers, while PFF’s partners are assisting with the selection process.
District and Regional Football Associations will later connect participating schools with the wider football structure.
Under the program’s cascading training model, the existing master trainers will return to their districts to train more teachers, potentially creating a network of around 450 trainers. Educators will also have access to the Football for Schools app in Urdu.
PFF Technical Director Adeel Rizki said more schools and districts would be added gradually as the program expands.
He also announced that the FIFA Talent Development Scheme is scheduled to launch in January 2027, providing a structured pathway for identifying and developing age-group talent.
The initiative will also focus on inclusion, with Prime Minister’s Youth Programme focal person Syeda Amna Batool calling for meaningful opportunities for girls.
The program aims to strengthen Pakistan’s grassroots football structure while creating a pathway for identifying and developing young talent.

items.author: Akshit Pushkarna
items.content:
For years, we at Inc42 have tracked the Indian tech startup ecosystem and seen it grow from a kid to an adult. Among the clearest signs of evolution and maturity of this ecosystem is the growing number of startups eyeing a public listing now.
For Indian companies, achieving a public listing has for long symbolised operational progression, transparency, and long-term viability. For startups, it’s a relatively new but increasingly critical rite of passage, one that not only signals coming of age but also creates pathways for investor exits and wealth creation.
Currently, a handful of startups, including the likes of Razorpay, OYO, PhonePe, among others, are in various stages of their IPO journey. Meanwhile, over 70 Indian new-age tech companies have already crossed the milestone and are now listed on the bourses.
The list now also includes Indian companies like MakeMyTrip and Freshworks, which are listed on Nasdaq in the US.
India’s startup IPO wave reached its peak in 2025, surpassing the previous year’s momentum.
While 13 startups went public in 2024, the number has already been overtaken this year, with 18 companies making their market debut in the previous year. The list of new-age tech companies that went public in 2025 included Meesho, Ather Energy, Urban Company, Lenskart, Groww, Pine Labs and PhysicsWallah.
The list is only expected to grow further this year.
12 new-age companies — ESDS, Purple Style Labs, Turtlemint, Klassroom, Shiprocket, LEAP India, Kissht, Aye Finance, Fractal Analytics, Amagi, Shadowfax and SEDEMAC — have already made their public market debut in 2026.
As of now, the total market capitalisation of the listed companies stands at over $192 Bn.
To consolidate all the information about listed startups, Inc42 has launched the Indian Listed New-Age Tech Company Tracker. Inside The Dalal Street Startup Ride
Indian startups had gained a reputation for being “loss making” by prioritising growth at all costs and market share over immediate profitability. The trend of putting scale ahead of the bottom line was at its peak amid the funding boom of 2020-22.
While prioritising growth is not wrong for startups, especially at early stages, the start of funding winter in 2022 gave a reality check to the Indian startup ecosystem. Subsequently, startups started pushing for profitability. Giving further wings to the aggressive profitability push was the ambition to list on the exchanges.
While new-age tech companies look to turn profitable before filing their draft IPO papers, those that cross the line manage to stay in the green, data shows. About 64% of the listed new-age tech companies, 41 to be precise, are currently profitable.
In terms of profits, Groww now leads the pack of new-age tech companies, posting a net profit of ₹2,083 Cr in FY26. Prominent internet companies Paytm and Eternal trail Groww in terms of profitability, raking in profits of ₹553 Cr and ₹366 Cr in FY26, respectively.
It is pertinent to mention that these companies have been listed on the bourses for years now, with Info Edge making its public market debut in 2006. While these companies trace their origin back to the 90s, a large majority of the new-age tech stocks under Inc42’s purview are about a decade old.
From a broad perspective, Inc42 data reflects that the median time taken for a startup to get listed on the bourses is 11 years. While listing for 18-year-old ixigo and 19-year-old Fino Payments Bank came relatively much later, ArisInfra’s IPO materialised within four years of its operations.
Meanwhile, the new-age tech companies that have made their public market debuts this year generally turned profitable right before their public market debuts. For instance, eyewear major Lenskart reported a net profit of around ₹297 Cr , a significant turnaround from a ₹10 Cr loss in FY24. The company maintained profitability in FY26, raking in a PAT of ₹494 Cr in the fiscal.
Urban Company also reported its first consolidated net profit of approximately ₹240 Cr for FY25, it returned to the red in FY26. For the full year FY26, the company reported a net loss of ₹234.8 Cr against a net profit of ₹239.8 Cr in previous year despite seeing a revenue growth of 36% YoY to ₹1,555.5 Cr
Sectors Driving India’s Startup IPO Boom
The startup sectors producing the most number of listed companies is proportional to the private funding trends witnessed in the Indian startup ecosystem.
The three most funded sectors, fintech, ecommerce and enterprise tech, also house the highest number listed startups.
While fintech leads the race with 13 listings, enterprise tech and ecommerce sectors dominates new-age tech IPOs with 12 listings and 11 listings, respectively, so far
The dominance of the fintech and ecommerce sectors on the bourses is expected to continue as the likes of PhonePe, Zepto and OYO would soon be making their public market debuts.
Delhi NCR Home To Highest Number Of Listed Startups
While Bengaluru continues to be the startup capital of India, Delhi and its neighbouring cities Gurugram and Noida account for the most number of listed new-age tech companies. Overall, the Delhi NCR region is home to 256listed new-age tech companies, ahead of Bengaluru’s fifteen and Mumbai’s eleven.
While sixteen companies, including Eternal, Delhivery, and Lenskart, call Gurugram their home, Awfis, EaseMyTrip, MapmyIndia and E2E Networks are from Delhi. Noida on the other hand is home to six listed new-age tech companies, including Paytm and IndiQube.
Delhi NCR contributes $121.3 Bn in the cumulative $192 Bn market cap of new-age tech companies.
Last updated: Sep 12
The Indian Listed New-Age Tech Company Tracker will be updated periodically with fresh data.

Asif Mahmood, a retired Navy commando, expert diver and paragliding pilot associated with Khanpur Dam, was killed in a paragliding accident in Upper Chitral after going missing during bad weather.
The 55-year-old, a resident of Wah Cantt, had taken off from Zaini Pass in Upper Chitral on Thursday afternoon as part of a six-member paragliding group.
According to Zahiruddin Baber, president of Upper Chitral’s paragliders’ association, the weather deteriorated about an hour into the flight. Five members of the group managed to land safely, while Mahmood continued flying toward Chitral city.
The group remained in radio contact with Mahmood for around one and a half hours after takeoff before his signal was lost. Rescue teams subsequently launched a search operation amid concerns that he may have crashed or been forced to make an emergency landing in the difficult mountainous terrain.
Rescue 1122 teams searched the high-altitude Barum hills for Mahmood. The operation was suspended overnight due to darkness and poor visibility before resuming early Friday.
Mahmood’s body was discovered on Friday afternoon in the highland pasture of Oveer Valley after a shepherd spotted him.
According to Baber, Mahmood had suffered head and spinal injuries after crashing into a hillock.
The incident is reported to be the first of its kind in Chitral in more than 25 years.

items.author: Arooj Fatima
items.content:
Former Pakistan captain Wasim Akram has called for the revival of club cricket and greater consistency in team selection following Pakistan’s defeats against England in the ongoing Test series.
Speaking to the media in Lahore, Akram said the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) should give its newly introduced domestic system at least three to four years to produce results.
He also raised concerns over Pakistan’s talent development, particularly in batting.
“PSL has completed 10 years, but not a single batter has emerged from it,” Akram said, while acknowledging that the league had produced several bowlers.
The former pacer said Pakistan’s recent defeats against Bangladesh, both at home and away, had already highlighted deeper problems in the national setup.
“The alarm bells were already ringing, but no action was taken,” he said.
Akram added that changing coaches would not solve the problem unless the overall talent pool improved.
“Whatever the coach, even if you bring the best coach, I or [Gary] Kirsten, the talent you have is the same,” he said.
He also questioned Pakistan’s approach to team selection, saying the side needed stability rather than repeatedly bringing back the same players.
“The team should have consistency, but the same boys keep coming and going,” he said.
Akram stressed that Pakistan must rebuild its grassroots cricket structure, arguing that genuine talent should emerge through club cricket.
“Talent has to come from club cricket,” he said.
He urged the PCB to invest Rs. 100 million each in Karachi and Lahore to strengthen cricket at the grassroots level.
According to Akram, Pakistan’s white-ball team is currently in a better position, while red-ball cricket remains a major concern.
“White-ball is fine, but red-ball is not. We face difficulties in that,” he said.
Commenting on Pakistan’s fast bowlers, Akram said they should be given enough time to develop before conclusions are drawn about their abilities.
“Bowling one delivery at 150 kilometers per hour is not a major achievement, while maintaining 140kph throughout the day is exceptional,” he said.
The former captain also questioned Shaheen Afridi’s reduced pace, describing him as an experienced bowler whose presence remains important in English conditions.
“If I were there, I would say I need Aaqib Javed. He has bowled well in England recently,” Akram said.
He further stressed the importance of having variety in the pace attack, noting that Pakistan had previously succeeded in similar conditions by using different types of fast bowlers instead of relying on bowlers operating at similar speeds.

items.author: Ahtesham Khan
items.content:
The federal government has declared 26 districts across six regions of Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa as hard areas and approved a security risk allowance for administrative and police officers posted in these terrorism-hit areas.
The Establishment Division, Islamabad, has formally conveyed the decision to the K-P chief secretary through an official letter. Under the decision, eligible officers will receive a security risk allowance equivalent to 250 per cent of their basic pay, which will be borne by the federal government. The allowance, however, will be subject to income tax.
According to the official communication, the allowance will take effect from July 1. Its payment will immediately cease when an officer is transferred out of a designated hard area.
Also Read: K-P police seek federal security package
Officers will also not be entitled to the allowance during suspension, while posted as Officers on Special Duty (OSD), during joining time or throughout training periods. The allowance will not be counted for the purpose of calculating pension or gratuity.
The districts declared hard areas include Peshawar, Khyber, Mardan, Charsadda, Mohmand, Nowshera, Kohat, Hangu, Karak, Kurram, Orakzai, Bannu, Lakki Marwat, North Waziristan, Dera Ismail Khan, Tank, Upper and Lower South Waziristan, Swat, Buner, Shangla, Bajaur, Upper and Lower Dir, and Upper and Lower Chitral.
However, officers posted in Swabi district and the Hazara Division will not be eligible for the security risk allowance.
The federal government has taken the decision in view of the growing threat of terrorism, security challenges and risks faced by government officers while performing their duties in these districts.

items.content:
Dalam memperkenalkan Galaxy S26 FE, Samsung mencoba menghadirkan sebuah paket komplit pengalaman smartphone flagship ke dalam banderol harga sedikit lebih terjangkau. Tidak hanya pada aspek performa hingga kecerdasan Galaxy AI yang dibawa, namun juga pengalaman kamera flagship. Termasuk fitur stabilisasi andalan lengkap bersama Horizontal Lock, yang siap hasilkan video super stabil tanpa alat bantu seperti gimbal.
Ya, dalam menghasilkan sebuah visual yang lebih jelas hingga sinematik, sebelumnya kita memerlukan sebuah perangkat atau aksesori penunjang tambahan, seperti tripod atau gimbal agar tangkapan video minim efek goyang, terutama ketika harus bergerak mengikuti obyek dan berpindah posisi. Fitur Super Steady sendiri mencoba menjawab tantangan tersebut, dan opsi Horizontal Lock bisa menggantikan peran aksesori tambahan demi kepraktisan dalam proses pembuatan konten.
Samsung Galaxy S26 FE sendiri membawa setup kamera komplit pada sisi depan maupun sisi belakang perangkat. Lewat sebuah perangkat ringkas, Gizmo friends bisa menangkap semua subyek secara luas lewat sensor ultra-wide, detail terbaik lewat sensor utama, maupun obyek yang jauh memanfaatkan sensor telefotonya. Termasuk hasilkan video berkualitas lengkap dengan stabilisasi kelas flagship teranyar.
Baca juga: Galaxy S26 FE: Kenali My FanCam Sebelum Rekam Idola Favorit Saat Konser atau Fan Meeting
Cara Pakai Fitur Horizontal Lock di Samsung Galaxy S26 FE
Saat merekam video, Samsung Galaxy S26 FE menawarkan opsi stabilisasi tingkat lanjut melalui fitur Super Steady, dan di dalamnya terdapat opsi Horizontal Lock yang baru diperkenalkan oleh Samsung pada Galaxy S26 Series. Sesuai namanya, ketika opsi ini diaktifkan, smartphone akan secara otomatis menjaga horizon pada video agar tetap lurus—walaupun posisi atau bodi smartphone ikut bergerak hingga berputar saat perekaman video berlangsung. Memanfaatkan semua sensor seperti akselerometer, giroskop, dan tentunya pemrosesan berbasis software.
Hasilnya? Video yang direkam menggunakan fitur Horizontal Lock pada Samsung Galaxy S26 FE akan benar-benar stabil dengan horizon yang lurus, seolah direkam menggunakan aksesori gimbal profesional. Fitur ini benar-benar siap memudahkan Gizmo friends dalam merekam momen penting maupun menarik sepanjang hari, termasuk agar dapat dibagikan ke media sosial sebagai konten yang lebih engaging ketika dilihat atau ditonton.
Cara pakai fitur Super Steady with Horizontal Lock di Samsung Galaxy S26 FE sendiri sangat mudah. Cukup akses aplikasi kamera bawaan, masuk ke mode perekaman video, tekan ikon stabilisasi di sisi atas layar, lalu pilih ikon Super Steady with Horizontal Lock yang berupa visual orang di dalam sebuah kotak. Setelah dipilih, kamu bisa lebih fokus untuk menangkap momen menarik, dan smartphone secara otomatis berikan stabilisasi terbaik.
Bantu Penangkapan Momen Spesial Lebih Berkualitas
Seperti yang sudah disinggung sebelumnya, fitur Super Steady with Horizontal Lock pada Samsung Galaxy S26 FE siap membuat penggunanya lebih mudah merekam momen tanpa alat bantu. Alih-alih membawa gimbal yang umumnya berukuran besar dan harus diisi daya lebih dulu, kamu hanya perlu menggenggam sebuah smartphone ringkas, agar bisa lebih fleksibel untuk berpindah posisi demi mendapatkan angle terbaik. Tidak memerlukan setup yang lebih rumit.
Fitur ini tentu tidak hanya cocok bagi para kreator profesional—Gizmo friends yang sedang ingin eksplorasi kemampuan merekam momen, juga akan terbantu agar bisa eksplorasi angle lebih leluasa, tanpa harus memikirkan risiko umum seperti video yang blur atau goyang. Hasil akhir bakal tetap rapi dan on point, tanpa harus terus menerus mengoreksi orientasi perangkat.
Fitur Super Steady with Horizontal Lock sendiri juga pas digunakan untuk mengabadikan banyak momen. Mulai dari aktivitas seperti dance performance atau dance cover, olahraga sepatu roda alias rollerblade, konten bepergian alias travelling, hingga aktivitas lainnya dengan lebih banyak gerakan seperti hiking, konten lari, dan lainnya bersama teman atau keluarga.
Tertarik untuk menangkap momen lebih berkualitas dengan Galaxy S26 FE? Gizmo fiends bisa mendapatkannya dengan harga lebih terjangkau selama periode penjualan perdananya. Tersedia dalam tiga opsi warna yakni Pistachio, Blueberry, dan Graphite, smartphone ini dibanderol mulai Rp11,999 juta. Namun Gizmo friends bisa mendapatkannya dengan harga promo mulai Rp9,249 juta saja dengan syarat dan ketentuan yang berlaku.
Sejumlah benefit tambahan ditawarkan untuk para konsumen, mulai dari bank cashback hingga Rp750 ribu, trade-in cashback sampai Rp500 ribu, serta diskon tambahan dari Samsung Reservation+ senilai hingga Rp500 ribu. Plus, gratis berlangganan Google AI Pro dan cloud storage 5TB senilai Rp1,8 juta.

items.author: Fiaz Mahmood
items.content:
The Islamabad High Court (IHC), hearing a case against the PTI’s September 27 protest, on Saturday sought affidavits from the Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa chief secretary and inspector general of police after the former assured the court that government machinery or resources would not be used for any political gathering.
The court directed both officials to submit affidavits confirming that government machinery and resources would not be used for political gatherings.
The larger bench also sought arguments from the Islamabad advocate general and prosecutor general at the next hearing.
Read: Tariq Fazal warns PTI of ‘other options’ if Sept 27 march goes ahead
A two-page written order was issued by the bench comprising Chief Justice Sarfraz Dogar, Justice Azam Khan and Justice Muhammad Asif.
According to the order, the advocates general of K-P, Punjab, Sindh and Balochistan had completed their arguments. The court noted that the KP secretary had given an undertaking that government machinery or resources would not be used for any political gathering.
The court subsequently directed the K-P chief secretary and inspector general of police to submit affidavits to this effect at the next hearing.
The case will be heard on Monday at 10am. 
The court clarified that the chief secretaries and inspectors general of police of the provinces were not required to appear in person.

items.author: Reuters
items.content:
BRICS leaders on Saturday called for greater efforts to prevent and peacefully resolve conflicts amid the wars in Iran and Ukraine, while opposing any forced displacement of Palestinians from the Gaza Strip.
The calls were included in the New Delhi Declaration, unanimously adopted on the first day of the bloc's two-day summit in the Indian capital.
Expressing "deep concern" over continued violence in Gaza despite the October 2025 ceasefire agreement, BRICS leaders called for an end to "any policies aimed at forced displacement of Palestinians from the Gaza Strip".
The declaration also expressed "concern regarding arrangements that may prejudice the inalienable rights of the Palestinian people and legitimise or prolong occupation".
"We reaffirm that a just and lasting solution to the Israeli-Palestinian conflict can only be achieved by peaceful means and depends on the fulfilment of the legitimate rights of the Palestinian people, including the rights to self-determination and return," it said.
The bloc also rejected "any unilateral measures that seek to alter the legal and historical status of occupied Jerusalem".
"We urge full respect for the sanctity of all religious sites and holy places in the city and for the rights of all to access and to observe their religious rites without hindrance," the New Delhi Declaration said on Saturday.
The bloc also condemned attacks on the UN Interim Force in Lebanon (UNIFIL) installations and personnel, emphasising that "such attacks are a violation of international law".
Noting the "current global context of polarisation and distrust", BRICS members called on the international community to respond to challenges and related security threats through "politico-diplomatic measures to lower conflict potential".
The bloc also stressed the "need to engage in conflict prevention efforts, including through addressing their root causes".
"We encourage the active role of regional organizations in conflict prevention and resolution and support all efforts conducive to the peaceful settlement of crises," the declaration said.
BRICS leaders also expressed concern over the growing risks of nuclear conflict and called for disarmament, arms control and nonproliferation.
The declaration voiced "serious concern" over "deliberate attacks" on civilian infrastructure and peaceful nuclear facilities.
"Nuclear safeguards, safety, and security must always be upheld, including in armed conflicts, to protect people and the environment from harm," it said.
Condemn unilateral trade measures
The BRICS leaders noted that the multilateral trading system "has long been at a crossroads".
"The proliferation of trade-restrictive actions that are inconsistent with World Trade Organisation (WTO) rules, whether in the form of indiscriminate rising of tariffs and non-tariff measures," the statement said.
"We voice serious concerns about the rise of unilateral tariff and non-tariff measures which distort trade and are inconsistent with WTO rules," it added.
The BRICS bloc condemned the imposition of unilateral coercive measures that "are contrary to international law, and reiterate that such measures, inter alia in the form of unilateral economic sanctions and secondary sanctions, have far-reaching negative implications for human rights, including the rights to development, health and food security, of the general population of targeted states, disproportionately affecting the poor and people in vulnerable situations, deepening the digital divide and exacerbating environmental challenges".
Xi urges BRICS peace role in Middle East
Chinese President Xi Jinping urged the BRICS bloc to be a peacemaker in the Middle East conflict, in ​an address to a summit of member countries in New Delhi.
China will work with other BRICS members in that role, as the war "does not serve the common interests of the international community", state-run CCTV quoted Xi as saying.
BRICS, originally comprising ​Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa and expanded to include Egypt, Ethiopia, ​Indonesia, Iran and the United Arab Emirates, was set up in 2009 ⁠to challenge a world order dominated by the United States and its ​Western allies.
Its members account for more than 40% of the world's population and ​almost a quarter of the global economy.
The Chinese leader called the bloc a "leading group" in the Global South and a model of self-reliance among emerging and developing countries that should ​promote innovation-driven development.
He said China would assume the BRICS chairmanship next year and ​host the 19th BRICS summit, according to CCTV.
In a meeting with Indian Prime Minister Narendra ‌Modi ⁠on the sidelines of the summit, Xi said China views ties with India from a "strategic, long-term perspective", state-run Xinhua News Agency reported.
China and India can learn from each other's strengths and achieve shared development, Xinhua quoted Xi as saying.
Xi's ​visit to New Delhi, ​his first to ⁠India in seven years, should further the diplomatic thaw between the giant neighbours, but there are few signs as ​yet that their business ties will improve, analysts said.
China and India ​fought a ⁠brief war in 1962, setting the backdrop for a wary relationship since then, which soured after a 2020 border skirmish killed 20 Indian and four Chinese soldiers. ⁠Still, ​ties have improved in recent years, especially since ​Modi visited China last year and as both nations grapple with volatile relationships with the US.

items.author: Onsa Mustafa
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
WhatsApp is rolling out a new feature that allows users to watch video status updates at 2x speed. The feature is currently being tested with some WhatsApp beta users on iOS and could make it easier to quickly go through multiple status updates.
WhatsApp Rolling Out 2x Video Playback for Status Updates
According to WABetaInfo, the feature is available with WhatsApp beta for iOS 26.36.10.70 through TestFlight. WhatsApp is gradually expanding access to more beta testers, so it may not be available to everyone yet.
How to Watch WhatsApp Status at 2x Speed
The new feature does not require users to open any settings or enable a playback option manually. Instead, WhatsApp uses a simple gesture.
Users need to open a video status and press and hold the right side of the screen. WhatsApp will immediately increase the playback speed to 2x while the finger remains on the screen.
As soon as the user releases the screen, the video returns to its normal playback speed. This also allows users to switch between normal and 2x playback whenever they want while watching a status.
Useful for Longer Status Videos
The new playback option could be particularly useful as WhatsApp recently increased the maximum length of music clips in status updates.
Previously, users could add music clips of up to 15 seconds to a status. A recent update increased the limit to 30 seconds, giving users more flexibility when creating status updates.
However, longer status videos can also take more time to watch, especially for people who regularly view a large number of updates. The 2x playback feature gives users a quick way to get through these videos without skipping them completely.
The feature is not limited to status videos with music. It can be used with any video shared through WhatsApp Status.
Familiar Gesture for Users
The press-and-hold gesture may feel familiar to users of other popular video platforms. Services such as Instagram, TikTok and YouTube already offer similar ways to temporarily increase video playback speed.
WhatsApp is bringing a similar experience to its Status section. Since the feature only works while users hold their finger on the screen, they do not need to learn or manage any additional controls.
Currently Limited to iOS Beta Testers
WhatsApp is currently making the 2x status playback feature available to some users running iOS beta version 26.36.10.70.
The feature is still in the testing phase, and WhatsApp has not confirmed when it will reach all users. The company is expected to expand availability.
The post WhatsApp Rolling Out 2x Video Playback for Status Updates appeared first on PhoneWorld.

OPPO has started teasing its upcoming Find X10 series in China. The company has confirmed several key details about the OPPO Find X10 and Find X10 Pro Max ahead of their official launch later this month.
The Find X10 Pro Max will stand out with a powerful camera setup featuring three 200-megapixel cameras. OPPO says all three cameras will support 8K video recording, making the phone a strong option for users who want advanced photography and video features.
OPPO Find X10 Pro Max Confirmed to Feature Three 200MP Cameras
The Find X10 Pro Max will feature three 200MP sensors, covering different photography needs. The main camera will offer up to 17 stops of dynamic range and will include OPPO’s DeepPix technology.
All three cameras will also be capable of recording videos in 8K resolution. This could give users more flexibility when switching between cameras while recording high-resolution videos.
OpenGate Capture Support
OPPO has also confirmed OpenGate capture for the Find X10 Pro Max. This feature allows the phone to use the full area of its image sensor when taking photos or recording videos.
Users can then crop the footage during post-production without being limited to a standard frame. OPPO is also adding integration with the Blackmagic Camera app, allowing users to access features such as O-Log2 and OpenGate directly through the app.
8,000mAh Battery and ColorOS 17
Both the Find X10 and Find X10 Pro Max will come with an 8,000mAh silicon-carbon battery. The phones will run Android 17-based ColorOS 17 out of the box.
OPPO has also confirmed a new Tianma OLED display for the series. The panel can reduce its brightness to as low as 1 nit, which should make the screen more comfortable to use in dark environments.
OPPO Find X10 Specifications
The standard Find X10 will also receive a high-end camera setup. It will feature two 200-megapixel cameras along with a second-generation Danxia color sensor.
The additional color sensor should help improve color accuracy. OPPO says the Find X10 can achieve up to 15 stops of dynamic range.
The phone will also feature extremely slim bezels measuring just 0.99mm, giving it a more immersive display design.
Find X10 Series Launch
OPPO will launch the Find X10 series in China this September. The company is gradually revealing more specifications ahead of the official launch, with the Find X10 Pro Max expected to be the most advanced model in the lineup.

items.content:
Apple akhirnya resmi masuk ke pasar smartphone layar lipat atau foldable lewat iPhone Duo. Dibandingkan Samsung, Google, Huawei, dan produsen Android lainnya, kehadiran iPhone lipat pertama Apple ini memang terbilang terlambat.
Namun dari sudut pandang perusahaan berbasis di Cupertino tersebut, persoalannya lebih dari sekadar menjadi paling pertama. 
Baca Juga: Sony Lepas Physint Hideo Kojima, Apa yang Terjadi?
Dalam wawancara bersama Tom’s Guide, CEO Apple John Ternus dan Senior Vice President of Worldwide Marketing Greg Joswiak mengungkap beberapa hal penting sebelum perusahaan adopsi foldable ke iPhone.
Baik dari rasa permukaan layar saat disentuh, kontinuitas antarmuka ketika perangkat dibuka dan ditutup, hingga kesiapan aplikasi pihak ketiga untuk mengoptimalkan layar iPhone yang lebih besar.
“Apple menunggu sampai memiliki ide produk yang memenuhi standar perusahaan dalam kualitas, durabilitas, dan desain,” kata John Ternus, sebagaimana dikutip dari Tom;s Guide, Sabtu (12/9/2026).
Nano-texture Jadi Titik Penting iPhone Duo
Salah satu momen bagi Ternus muncul ketika ia melihat teknologi nano-texture diterapkan pada prototipe iPhone Duo. “Rasanya sepert, ‘ya, itu dia’,” ujar bos baru Apple tersebut ketika menjelaskan reaksinya saat melihat teknologi itu terpasang di prototipe foldable Apple.
Setelah arahnya tepat, tantangan berikutnya adalah bagaimana membuat teknologi itu benar-benar diproduksi. Sebetulnya, nano-texture bukan teknologi benar-benar baru bagi Apple.
Permbuat iPhone itu sudah menggunakan teknologi tersebut pada beberapa perangkat lainnya, tetapi iPhone Duo butuh pendekatan berbeda karena layar fleksibelnya menggunakan permukaan polimer.
Menurut Apple, lapisan nano-texture membantu mengurangi pantulan sekaligus meminimalkan visibilitas bekas lipatan pada layar bagian dalam. Layar dalam iPhone Duo berukuran 7,6 inci, sementara bagian luar menggunakan layar 5,4 inci. Keduanya memiliki rasio aspek yang sama agar konten bisa berpindah secara proporsional ketika perangkat dibuka atau ditutup.
Apple Tak Mau iPhone Lipat Setengah Matang
Namun layar bukan satu-satunya pertimbangan Apple. Greg Joswiak cukup terbuka ketika membahas apa yang sudah dilakukan produsen lain di kategori foldable.
“Apa yang kami lihat dilakukan orang lain tidak terlalu menginspirasi,” ujar Joswiak. Ia menambahkan, Apple tidak ingin terburu-buru masuk ke sebuah kategori dengan sesuatu yang belum matang benar.
Pernyataan tersebut tentu merupakan pandangan Apple terhadap produk kompetitor, bukan berarti seluruh persoalan foldable Android belum terselesaikan. Bahkan dalam beberapa tahun terakhir, produsen Android telah membuat kemajuan besar dalam desain yang semakin tipis, ringan, serta matang dari sisi hardware.
Namun komentar Joswiak memberi gambaran mengenai area yang ingin dijadikan pembeda Apple pada iPhone Duo: integrasi antara hardware, sistem operasi, dan aplikasi.
iOS 27 secara khusus disesuaikan untuk form factor tersebut. Apple memindahkan sejumlah elemen navigasi dan kontrol ke sisi layar agar mudah dijangkau baik ketika perangkat tertutup maupun terbuka.
Ternus mencontohkan bagaimana posisi kontrol tetap berada di bawah ibu jari kanan, dan ketika pengguna berpindah dari layar luar ke layar dalam. Intinya, Apple ingin penggunaan dua layar terasa sebagai satu pengalaman yang berkelanjutan, bukan dua antarmuka berbeda yang harus dipelajari ulang.
iOS 27 juga menghadirkan Split View untuk membuka dua aplikasi secara berdampingan, kemampuan menjalankan dua jendela dari aplikasi yang sama seperti Safari, sampai menyimpan pasangan aplikasi untuk digunakan kembali.
iPhone Duo Akan Hadir di Indonesia
Apple membanderol iPhone Duo mulai USD 1.999 di Amerika Serikat untuk varian penyimpanan 256GB. Perangkat ini tersedia dalam warna star white dan night sky, dengan kapasitas hingga 2TB. Pre-order global dimulai 16 Oktober 2026 dan penjualan di sejumlah pasar berlangsung mulai 23 Oktober.
Sementara itu, Apple Indonesia sudah memastikan iPhone Duo akan segera tersedia di Tanah Air. Namun hingga saat ini perusahaan belum mengumumkan harga maupun tanggal penjualan resminya untuk pasar Indonesia.
Pada akhirnya, klaim Apple perusahaan menunggu hingga pengalaman foldable cukup matang masih perlu dibuktikan setelah iPhone Duo digunakan lebih luas.
Nano-texture menawarkan pendekatan berbeda terhadap salah satu kompromi layar fleksibel, sementara iOS 27 dirancang agar perpindahan antara dua layar terasa konsisten. Tetapi pembeda yang lebih sulit direplikasi mungkin justru berada pada ekosistem aplikasinya.
Jika dukungan developer bisa mengikuti ambisi Apple, datang terlambat ke kategori foldable mungkin tidak menjadi masalah besar. Jika tidak, iPhone Duo tetap harus menghadapi pertanyaan yang sama seperti foldable lain: seberapa banyak layar besar tersebut benar-benar mengubah cara pengguna memakai smartphone sehari-hari?
