items.author: Christopher Louis
items.content:
Apple resmi memperkenalkan AirPods 5 sebagai generasi terbaru earphone open-ear miliknya. Salah satu perubahan yang paling disorot adalah hadirnya Active Noise Cancellation (ANC) pada model yang menjadi opsi lebih terjangkau dalam lini AirPods. Apple mengklaim kemampuan peredaman suara eksternalnya meningkat hingga 50 persen dibandingkan AirPods 4 dengan ANC, berkat arsitektur akustik multiport baru dan algoritma computational audio yang diperbarui.
Selain peningkatan ANC, AirPods 5 membawa Adaptive EQ generasi baru yang diklaim mampu menghasilkan suara lebih detail pada bentuk telinga yang berbeda. Apple juga mempertahankan Transparency Mode, Adaptive Audio, serta Conversation Awareness. Di sisi ketahanan, perangkat ini mendapatkan peningkatan perlindungan terhadap debu, keringat, dan air. Apple menawarkan AirPods 5 mulai dari US$129, sementara varian dengan Wireless Charging Case dibanderol US$149.
Namun, daya tarik AirPods 5 tidak hanya terletak pada perangkat keras. Apple juga mengaitkannya dengan perkembangan Apple Intelligence dan Siri AI di iOS 27. Pengguna dengan iPhone yang mendukung Apple Intelligence dapat memanfaatkan sejumlah kemampuan AI melalui AirPods secara hands-free. Meski demikian, fitur-fitur tersebut tetap bergantung pada perangkat yang kompatibel, bahasa, wilayah, serta ketersediaan Siri AI yang saat ini masih berstatus beta.
Baca Juga: Apple Kabarnya akan Berikan Mode Pro dalam Aplikasi Camera
ANC Lebih Kuat pada Desain Open-Ear
Apple membawa ANC ke AirPods 5 dengan pendekatan open-ear. Perusahaan mengklaim perangkat mampu mengurangi suara eksternal hingga 50 persen lebih banyak dibandingkan AirPods 4 dengan ANC. Peningkatan ini berasal dari kombinasi arsitektur akustik multiport dan computational audio yang lebih baru.
Di sisi lain, desain open-ear tetap memiliki kompromi dibandingkan earphone dengan eartip yang menutup kanal telinga. Kemampuan isolasi suara secara fisik tentu tidak sama, sehingga performa ANC dapat bergantung pada lingkungan dan bentuk telinga pengguna. Apple juga menyebut Transparency Mode dibuat lebih natural agar pengguna tetap dapat mendengar suara di sekitar.
Siri AI hingga Live Translation
AirPods 5 turut mendapatkan integrasi dengan Siri AI yang hadir sebagai beta di iOS 27. Pengguna dapat meminta Siri mencari informasi dari pesan, email, atau melakukan tindakan tertentu melalui aplikasi yang kompatibel. AirPods juga mendukung respons terhadap Siri menggunakan gerakan kepala, seperti mengangguk untuk menyetujui atau menggeleng untuk menolak.
Fitur lain yang ikut diperluas adalah Live Translation. Dengan Apple Intelligence dan aplikasi Translate, pengguna dapat mendengar percakapan dalam bahasa yang dipilih secara langsung melalui AirPods. Namun, fitur ini membutuhkan perangkat dan sistem operasi yang kompatibel serta belum tersedia untuk seluruh bahasa dan wilayah. AirPods 5 sendiri mulai tersedia pada 18 September dengan harga US$129, sedangkan versi Wireless Charging Case dibanderol US$149.

items.title: iPhone 18 Pro Series Punya Dynamic Island Baru dan Kamera dengan Variable Aperture
items.summary:
Sesuai rumor yang sudah terus menguat dalam beberapa pekan terakhir, akhirnya Apple meresmikan kehadiran flagship terbarunya di akhir tahun 2026, dan siap meramaikan satu tahun berikutnya. iPhone 18 Pro Series hadir dalam desain yang familiar, namun sejatinya membawa sejumlah perubahan menarik. Mulai dari aspek layar, performa, kamera, hingga daya tahan baterai.
Ya, mengingat generasi sebelumnya baru saja dibuat sepenuhnya berubah, maka wajar bila tampilan desain iPhone 18 Pro Series masih dibuat mirip—setidaknya konsumen kini diberikan sejumlah opsi warna baru, termasuk warna Burgundy yang menjadi opsi warna utama alias hero color.
Tahun ini Apple hanya memperkenalkan dua varian iPhone 18 Pro Series saja, yakni dalam pilihan Pro dan Pro Max. Sementara pilihan lain hanyalah foldable perdananya, dan untuk varian standar dikabarkan baru akan dirilis awal tahun depan. Lantas apa saja yang baru di iPhone 18 Pro Series?
Baca juga: John Ternus Jadi CEO Apple, Ujian Besar Menanti 9 September
items.author: Prasetyo Herfianto
items.content:
Sesuai rumor yang sudah terus menguat dalam beberapa pekan terakhir, akhirnya Apple meresmikan kehadiran flagship terbarunya di akhir tahun 2026, dan siap meramaikan satu tahun berikutnya. iPhone 18 Pro Series hadir dalam desain yang familiar, namun sejatinya membawa sejumlah perubahan menarik. Mulai dari aspek layar, performa, kamera, hingga daya tahan baterai.
Ya, mengingat generasi sebelumnya baru saja dibuat sepenuhnya berubah, maka wajar bila tampilan desain iPhone 18 Pro Series masih dibuat mirip—setidaknya konsumen kini diberikan sejumlah opsi warna baru, termasuk warna Burgundy yang menjadi opsi warna utama alias hero color.
Tahun ini Apple hanya memperkenalkan dua varian iPhone 18 Pro Series saja, yakni dalam pilihan Pro dan Pro Max. Sementara pilihan lain hanyalah foldable perdananya, dan untuk varian standar dikabarkan baru akan dirilis awal tahun depan. Lantas apa saja yang baru di iPhone 18 Pro Series?
Baca juga: John Ternus Jadi CEO Apple, Ujian Besar Menanti 9 September
Yang Baru di iPhone 18 Pro & 18 Pro Max
Langsung terlihat dari sisi depannya, layar iPhone 18 Pro Series memiliki setup sensor-sensor yang dibuat jauh lebih ringkas. Ya, tepatnya pada area Dynamic Island, di mana Apple berhasil memindahkan sejumlah sensor agar ukurannya mengecil, sehingga tampilannya bisa terlihat lebih utuh. Sekaligus bisa menampilkan hingga tiga aktivitas aplikasi secara simultan.
Kalau area sekitar kamera depan dibuat mengecil, bagaimana dengan kamera belakangnya? Kamera iPhone 18 Pro tetap dibekali dengan tiga sensor berbeda dalam resolusi 48MP, masing-masing berjenis wide, ultra-wide, dan telefoto 4x optical zoom. Yang baru adalah sensor wide utamanya, di mana kini mendukung variable aperture f/1.48 – f/4.0. Secara teknis mampu memberikan penangkapan cahaya lebih maksimal, dan kendali lebih untuk efek kedalaman atau depth of field.
Akhirnya Apple juga sematkan mode profesional pada aplikasi kamera iPhone 18 Pro Series, agar pengguna bisa mengubah sejumlah parameter manual mulai dari shutter speed hingga diafragma sensor kamera utama. Fitur baru seperti focus tracking saat merekam video, perekaman video sinematik dalam 60fps, time-lapse 4K HDR, hingga Audio Mix yang bisa difokuskan pada musik di sekitar juga ikut ditambahkan.
Performa iPhone 18 Pro Series juga ikut ditingkatkan lewat penggunaan cip Apple A20 Pro yang kini menggunakan fabrikasi 2nm. Apple janjikan peningkatan performa hingga 20% pada inti tercepatnya, GPU 7-inti yang lebih kencang hingga 40%, serta neural accelerator baru untuk kemampuan pemrosesan AI lebih baik. Plus, neural engine yang kini punya 32 inti, naik dari 16 inti. Semua secara total meningkatkan bandwidth memori sampai 50%.
Desain chipset-nya juga diubah, dan kini lebih dekat dengan vapor chamber untuk pendinginan lebih maksimal. Ukurannya juga dibuat tiga kali lebih luas, dengan lapisan grafit yang lebih banyak, dan material lainnya untuk performa kencang lebih lama—dua kali lebih stabil dibandingkan iPhone 16 Pro.
Harga Naik Untuk Kedua Varian
Peningkatan daya tahan baterai juga diutamakan. Di mana baterai iPhone 18 Pro disebut setara dengan iPhone 17 Pro Max, bisa memutar video hingga 36 jam. Bagaimana dengan baterai iPhone 18 Pro Max? Membawa peningkatan tertinggi di sejarah iPhone, bisa memutar video sampai 45 jam nonstop, atau 30 jam penggunaan intensif. Pengisian dayanya juga jauh lebih cepat, hanya memerlukan waktu 15 menit untuk mencapai 50%.
Kemampuan chipset yang lebih baik, juga berpengaruh positif pada kemampuan kecerdasan atau AI pada iPhone 18 Pro Series. Disebutkan bila nantinya lebih banyak pemrosesan AI bisa berjalan secara lokal alias on-device, dan pengguna bisa memanfaatkan sejumlah kemampuan ekstra seperti suara Siri yang lebih ekspresif, maupun kemampuan dikte pesan teks yang lebih responsif saat mengetik.
Semua dikemas ke dalam desain bodi yang familiar, namun tersedia dalam pilihan warna baru. Selain warna silver dan hitam pekat, warna iPhone 18 Pro Series juga tersedia dalam opsi baru, Glacier yang terlihat seperti biru muda, dan tentunya Burgundy sebagai warna utamanya. 
Dan seperti yang sudah disampaikan oleh pihak resmi Apple sebelumnya, harga iPhone 18 Pro Series menjadi semakin mahal. Yakni mulai USD1199 untuk varian Pro (atau sekitar Rp21 jutaan), sementara harga iPhone 18 Pro Max mulai USD1299 (Rp22,7 jutaan). Keduanya tersedia dalam opsi storage mulai 256GB, dan kini kedua varian diberikan opsi sampai 2TB. Apakah Gizmo friends sudah berencana untuk upgrade ke iPhone 18 Pro Series, atau memilih iPhone lipat pertama?

items.author: Press Release
items.content:
aik by BankIslami, has launched aikTijarat, the country’s first Shariah-compliant merchant and business app. The dedicated app segregates merchants and businesses from the consumer ecosystem, giving them a platform built entirely around the way they earn, pay and grow.
With aikTijarat, a shopkeeper, small trader or service provider can open a completely Shariah-compliant business account without visiting a branch. Onboarding is fully digital, powered by CNIC and biometric verification, and existing BankIslami and aik consumer app customers can move across through a shortened journey instead of registering from scratch. Once onboarded, merchants can collect payments instantly through static and dynamic QR over Raast, pay suppliers and utility bills directly from their business balance, and track every transaction with shareable digital receipts — all from their smartphone.
Commenting on the launch, Ashfaque Ahmed, Chief Officer of aik Digital, said: “Pakistan’s merchants are the backbone of our economy, yet they have largely been left out of the digital banking conversation. With aikTijarat, we are giving them a dedicated, Shariah-compliant platform built around their business, not just their transactions.” He added, “This is a direct contribution to the Prime Minister’s vision of a cashless Pakistan and the State Bank’s Go-Cashless agenda. A truly cashless economy can only be built by digitising the merchant counter itself.”
Ghuffran Abbasi, Chief Business Officer at aik, said: “We didn’t build aikTijarat to be another payments app we built it to solve the everyday challenges merchants face and become the digital backbone of their businesses. Our success will not be measured by onboarding numbers, but by how many merchants grow because aikTijarat gives them seamless access to payments, suppliers, financing and growth tools all within one Shariah-compliant ecosystem. That is the long-term value we are building.”
The significance of this launch extends well beyond any single merchant. Pakistan’s informal retail economy includes several million shopkeepers, traders and service providers who have largely operated outside formal banking, a segment digital payment providers have long struggled to bring onto documented rails. By offering these merchants a genuinely Shariah-compliant business account, aikTijarat removes the one barrier that has kept many of them out of the formal system altogether. As more merchants move their sales, savings and supplier payments onto a single digital platform, the impact compounds: greater transparency across supply chains, a broader base of businesses eligible for future credit and financial services, and a fuller, more accurate picture of Pakistan’s real economic activity.
Beyond payments, aikTijarat is designed as the starting point of a larger ambition — to build one of Pakistan’s largest and most connected merchant networks. From the neighbourhood shopkeeper to growing retailers and service providers, aik by BankIslami aims to move merchants from simply digitising transactions to being fully digitised businesses, with future phases expected to bring merchant financing and additional business growth solutions onto the platform.
Through this launch, aik by BankIslami reinforces its commitment to financial inclusion and providing Riba-free and shariah-compliant digital financial solutions, advancing BankIslami’s mission of Saving Humanity from Riba through ethical, accessible and technology-driven Shariah-compliant financial solutions.
The post aik by BankIslami Launches aikTijarat, Pakistan’s First Shariah-Compliant Merchant App appeared first on ProPakistani.

items.author: Team Inc42
items.content:
Ecommerce giant Flipkart has launched a standalone app for its quick commerce service, Minutes.
The app, which is still in beta mode, is live on Google Play Store. However, it is only available for a select number of users. Inc42 could verify the availability of the service in limited pockets of Delhi NCR.
On the app, Minutes claims to offer “zero platform fees”, discounts and free deliveries on orders above ₹99. The product catalogue currently includes kitchen staples, fruits, gourmet products and other daily essentials.
The limited launch suggests that Flipkart is testing the app’s performance and customer experience before making it available more widely.
The dedicated app marks a shift from Flipkart Minutes’ earlier positioning as a service housed within the main Flipkart application. By giving Minutes its own interface, Flipkart is likely looking to create a more focused experience for customers looking to buy products quickly, while also building a separate identity for the business.
The app launch comes amid intensifying competition in the Indian quick commerce arena as rivals Blinkit, Zepto and Swiggy Instamart continue to invest heavily in dark stores, delivery networks and customer discounts.
Meanwhile, Flipkart too has been aggressively scaling its dark store and banking on its ecommerce network effects to narrow the gap with established players.
As of June, Minutes boasted 1,000 micro-fulfilment centres across 130 cities. At the time, Flipkart Minutes head Kunal Gupta reportedly said the company planned to expand the network to 1,500 centres across 180 cities.
Last week, brokerage firm UBS said that Minutes could add another 1,000 dark stores by mid-2027, ahead of next year’s Big Billion Days sale. If the expansion materialises, it would nearly double Minutes’ network to around 2,000 stores.
Giving an insight into Flipkart’s quick commerce operation, the UBS report noted that Minutes dark stores clock an average of 800-1,000 orders per day, while mature stores (operational for five to six months) process around 1,200-1,500 orders daily.
The report also noted Minutes’ net order value, excluding mobile phones, stands at ₹500-₹530, while metro cities contribute around 60%-65% of demand on the platform. UBS also added that Minutes’ gross margins are improving but remain well below Blinkit’s.
Meanwhile, Flipkart is also exploring additional categories and services around its quick commerce infrastructure.
Flipkart’s Food Delivery Tryst
Minutes’ standalone app went live barely hours after Flipkart began piloting its food delivery service, called Eat In, among its employees in Bengaluru.
As per Moneycontrol, the Walmart-owned ecommerce giant plans to roll out the offering to all Flipkart employees by September 15. It will then subsequently debut the food delivery platform for end consumers in Bengaluru.
As reported by Inc42 earlier this month, Minutes will initially manage orders and fulfilment. With roughly 500 Mn registered users and around 40 Mn SuperCoins users, Flipkart has a large base to which it can cross-sell food orders without starting from zero.
To minimise cash burn during rollout, Flipkart initially plans to leverage Ekart’s logistics network and ONDC integration for restaurant onboarding. It is also centring its pitch on merchant economics and is considering a base commission of 12%-13% to address the restaurant industry’s main grievances against Zomato and Swiggy.
While Flipkart will be looking to tap into its deep pockets to challenge the duopoly of Eternal’s Zomato and Swiggy, scale alone has not helped earlier challengers. Amazon Food, Ola, Paytm, Tata Neu and others previously tried and failed to alter consumer behaviour.
At the heart of all this is India’s growing foodtech ecosystem, which is reportedly projected to become a $46 Bn opportunity by 2034.

items.author: Anne Florentyna
items.content:
Xiaomi has landed in fresh trouble in India. The serious fraud investigation office (SFIO) has reportedly recommended a probe into alleged irregularities in the smartphone maker’s business model and compliance with the foreign exchange management act (FEMA).
According to Reuters, SFIO has recommended a detailed investigation to examine the movement of funds by Xiaomi. The agency has also reportedly called for probing whether the company sought mandatory investment approvals after India tightened scrutiny of Chinese investments following border clashes between the two nations in 2020.
Sources reportedly said that the Centre is examining the memorandum that was drafted in May this year. Based on the report, the proposed investigation would examine:
Xiaomi’s foreign investors and beneficial ownership
Movement of funds between Xiaomi and related entities
Whether required government approvals were obtained for investments post 2020
Possible violations of India’s foreign direct investment (FDI) rules
Whether financial statements and auditor reports contain material mis-statements
The company’s relationships with sellers and ecommerce platforms
As per the report, the SFIO proposal said that it was recommending action against Xiaomi based on complaints and ​inputs received from the commerce ministry. It also called for “coordination” between other government agencies to flag overlapping violations.
While the proposal did not specify the information that SFIO had reviewed, the agency, however, reportedly dished out a 21-point investigation framework with methodology and plan of action, including possible summoning of company executives if needed.
“The inquiry should specifically cover whether preferential ​and exclusive launches of Xiaomi products on selected e-commerce platforms …. defeated the intent of the FDI policy applicable to ecommerce (companies),” SFIO reportedly said in its recommendations.
Inc42 has reached out to Xiaomi for comments on the development. The story will be updated based on their response.
However, a Xiaomi spokesperson told Reuters that the company has not received any notice or communication from the SFIO. “We ​accord paramount importance to the laws of the land and comply with them fully at all times,” the company reportedly added.
The development comes as Xiaomi continues to be under regulatory scrutiny in India, with authorities examining alleged FEMA violations and customs-duty evasion.
In January 2022, the government issued three show-cause notices to the original equipment manufacturer (OEM) and sought ₹653 Cr in customs duty for the period between April 2017 and June 2020.
In addition, the Enforcement Directorate (ED) in 2022 seized ₹5,551 Cr from Xiaomi India’s bank accounts under FEMA norms, alleging that the company had illegally remitted money overseas as “royalty”.
The development also comes as Chinese President ​Xi Jinping is expected to visit India over the weekend to attend a BRICS summit.
The post SFIO Seeks Detailed Probe Into Xiaomi India’s Business Model appeared first on Inc42 Media.

items.author: Anne Florentyna
items.content:
Reliance Jio has introduced a new pricing structure for rich communication services (RCS) business messaging, allowing brands to send marketing, transactional and one-time password (OTP) messages to iPhone users on its network.
The new rates came into effect on September 1, as per an ET report citing emails sent by the company to businesses. Marketing messages will cost ₹0.27-0.30 per message, while transactional messages will be charged at ₹0.25 and OTPs at ₹0.11-0.16 per message.
The new pricing replaces Jio’s earlier flat RCS tariff of ₹0.08-0.10 per message, as per the report.
The development follows Apple’s expansion of business RCS support on iPhones in partnership with telecom operators. Unlike Apple’s consumer RCS implementation, which enables messaging between individuals across iOS and Android, business RCS allows companies to send application-to-person (A2P) messages to customers.
Apple has supported RCS on iPhones since iOS 18, although availability depends on mobile operators. Jio was among the first operators in India to bring RCS to iPhone users through its partnership with Apple in 2025.
Jio already offers RCS-based business messaging through its Jio Business Messaging platform. The service enables businesses to send branded and interactive messages, including rich media, carousels and action buttons, directly to customers’ native messaging inboxes. Jio describes the platform as being powered by RCS, through partnerships with Google and Apple.
Therefore, the latest development marks an expansion of Jio’s existing RCS ecosystem into commercial business messaging for iPhone users, rather than the introduction of a new Jio-Apple RCS partnership.
Apple is gradually rolling out business RCS in other markets, including the US, UK, Germany, France and Spain, through partnerships with local telecom operators. However, the commercial pricing is set by individual telecom operators rather than Apple or Google, as per reports.
Jio’s move could give businesses another channel for customer communication as they increasingly rely on rich messaging services for marketing, transaction updates and authentication. RCS offers features such as verified business profiles, images, videos, carousels and interactive buttons, while being delivered through the native messaging application. Jio’s business RCS offering also supports both Android and iOS users on its network.
The move comes as RCS adoption grows in India. According to data cited by Infobip, RCS interactions in the country increased 108% between H1 2025 and H1 2026, with financial services and fintech companies accounting for more than three-fourths of RCS traffic.
Inc42 has reached out to Jio for comment. The story will be updated if the company responds.
The development comes at a time when Jio Platforms is gearing up for a major public market debut. The company has received SEBI’s approval for an IPO which could probably be one of the largest IPOs to hit the Indian markets till now.
The company filed its DRHP with the SEBI for a fresh issue only IPO in June, proposing raising fresh capital by issuing 27 Cr equity shares with a face value of ₹10 each.
The company plans to use the net proceeds to prepay or repay, in full or in part, certain borrowings of its material subsidiary, Reliance Jio Infocomm Limited (RJIL), as well as for general corporate purposes.
Of the total amount that would be raised via the IPO, ₹27,500 Cr would be used towards the prepayment of certain outstanding borrowings of its material subsidiary Reliance Jio Infocomm Ltd.
The post Jio Introduces New RCS Business Messaging Rates For iPhone Users In India appeared first on Inc42 Media.

items.author: Daily Trust
items.content:
Kaduna State Government said that emphasis will still be on Human Capital Development in the 2027 budget, with agriculture, health and education given priority in the Appropriation bill.
The Commissioner of Planning and Budget, Hon Muktar Ahmed Monrovia, made this known in his opening remarks at the 2027 Expenditure And Revenue Budget Defence on Wednesday.
Speaking on the proposed budget, the Commissioner maintained that next year’s budget will be a ‘’consolidation of what has happened in the last three and half years.’’
Hon Monrovia pointed out that although ‘’attention will still be on Human Capital Development, there is the latest entrant into the budget cycle, which is Early Child Development.’’
According to the Commissioner of Planning and Budget, the new budget line will strengthen Human Capital Development and will cater for children from 0 to 5 years.
He further said that Social Protection, security and infrastructural development will still be given priority in next year’s budget, in line with Governor Uba Sani’s government’s determining to secure Kaduna State and cater for the underserved.
The Commissioner noted that ‘’in the last three and half years, His Excellency has done much in the area of security and the policies and programmes will continue next year.’’
Hon Moronvia pointed out that this next year’s budget will be the fourth in the Governor Uba Sani administration and the last budget cycle of his first term.
Justifying why Agriculture will be given priority in the next budget, he said that a survey has shown that Kaduna State has more than one million out of the 42 million farming households in the country.
‘’That is why His Excellency has focused attention on Agriculture and in the last three years, he has distributed free fertilizers and improved seeds to smallholder farmers.
‘’The rural transformation agenda of the Governor is also aimed at connecting farms to markets. This will boost the local economy and reduce the rural-urban migration,’’ he argued.

items.title: Govt Wants to Give Rs. 2 Trillion Loan to Small Businesses
items.summary:
The federal government wants to increase financing for small and medium-sized businesses to Rs. 2 trillion by June 2028, as SME lending has already crossed Rs. 1 trillion and reached nearly 324,000 borrowers.

items.author: Business Desk
items.content:
The federal government wants to increase financing for small and medium-sized businesses to Rs. 2 trillion by June 2028, as SME lending has already crossed Rs. 1 trillion and reached nearly 324,000 borrowers.
The target was discussed during the fourth meeting of the Access to Finance Steering Committee, chaired by Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb at the Finance Division in Islamabad on Wednesday.
The committee was informed that SME financing stood at Rs. 1.067 trillion by the end of August 2026, covering 323,987 borrowers. SME loans currently account for 9.9 percent of domestic private advances.
Under the government’s medium-term plan, SME financing is expected to rise to Rs. 2 trillion by June 2028, while the number of borrowers is targeted to increase to 775,000. This would raise the share of SME financing in domestic private advances to 13 percent.
Aurangzeb directed authorities to maintain the pace of SME lending and develop clear bank-wise plans to increase credit to small and medium-sized businesses.
The meeting also reviewed progress on a wholesale SME financing framework, which is expected to help banks extend financing to a larger number of businesses.
The Finance Minister said improving access to formal financing would require more than simply increasing loan limits. He stressed the need to improve SMEs’ financial management, documentation and cash-flow visibility so that more businesses can qualify for bank financing.
The committee also reviewed financing for agriculture, which reached Rs. 1.268 trillion by the end of August 2026. The financing covered 3,392,092 borrowers and represented 10.9 percent of domestic private advances.
The government aims to increase agriculture financing to Rs. 2 trillion and expand the number of borrowers to 5.5 million by June 2028.
Under the Zarkhez-e-Asaan Zarai Qarza program, which provides uncollateralised financing to small farmers including tenant farmers, 58,919 farmers had registered by the end of August.
The program had received 35,838 applications. Banks had approved 16,964 loans worth Rs. 7.349 billion, while 5,174 loans worth Rs. 1.956 billion had been disbursed.
Aurangzeb called for faster conversion of approved agricultural loans into actual disbursements so that farmers can receive financing without unnecessary delays.
The committee also reviewed the Wazir-e-Azam Apna Ghar Program: Ghar Ho To Apna. The scheme provides housing finance for periods of up to 20 years, with a fixed interest rate of 5 percent for the first 10 years.
By September 4, approved housing financing under the program had reached Rs. 351.3 billion, up Rs. 38.3 billion from the end of August.
Banks had received 156,813 applications, of which 60,349 loans worth Rs. 351.3 billion had been approved. So far, 9,717 loans worth Rs. 51.13 billion had been disbursed.
The Finance Minister directed officials to speed up disbursements against approved housing loans and work on measures to make mortgage financing easier for applicants.
Progress under the Pakistan Accelerated Vehicle Electrification (PAVE) Program was also reviewed.
The program has 17 participating banks. So far, 17,118 applications involving Rs. 2.581 billion have been approved, while 4,228 loans worth Rs. 804 million have been disbursed.
A total of 1,860 electric bikes have been delivered to beneficiaries.
The committee said the focus should now be on speeding up deliveries for applicants whose financing has already been approved and disbursed.
The Small and Medium Enterprises Development Authority (SMEDA) briefed the committee on its financial literacy program, SME financing help desks and other tools designed to help businesses access formal financing.
SMEDA plans to conduct 560 financial literacy training programs across Pakistan. Around 100 have already been completed.
Five SME Financing Help Desk sessions were also conducted during the last month in collaboration with partner banks.
The initiatives are aimed at helping businesses understand financing requirements, improve their financial preparedness and navigate the formal banking system.
Aurangzeb said wider access to finance was important for the government’s goal of achieving private-sector-led economic growth.
He directed the relevant sub-committees to continue working on their respective initiatives and bring key recommendations and implementation issues to the main Steering Committee for timely decisions.

items.author: Afaq Wajdan Malik
items.content:
Xiaomi has expanded its self-developed semiconductor efforts with three new Xring chips, including the Xring O100, a dedicated AI accelerator designed to handle more demanding artificial intelligence workloads directly on devices.
Founder, chairman and CEO Lei Jun announced the new chips during Xiaomi’s Autumn flagship product launch event.
Built for Faster On-Device AI
The Xring O100 delivers up to 1.22TB/s of memory bandwidth and is described by Xiaomi as the world’s first 6nm 3D wafer-level stacked advanced packaging solution.
It uses an advanced hybrid bonding process with an extremely small bonding pitch.
According to Xiaomi, the design provides 16 times the memory bandwidth of traditional mobile phones and enables on-device AI inference speeds of up to 330 tokens per second.
3D Stacking Reduces the Memory Bottleneck
The chip vertically stacks logic and high-speed DRAM dies using wafer-on-wafer technology and hybrid bonding.
This reduces the physical distance between processing components and memory, allowing data to move more quickly.
Xiaomi says the approach is designed to address a major limitation for running large language models on edge devices. Even when mobile processors have enough computing power, AI performance can still be restricted by slow data transfer between memory and processing units.
The O100’s high bandwidth and dense connections are intended to improve token-generation speeds for local AI models.
Multi-Core NPU and Dynamic Data Routing
The Xring O100 uses a multi-core NPU architecture optimized for different stages of AI inference.
It also supports dynamic data routing, allowing workloads to be handled more efficiently depending on the task.
Xiaomi has already demonstrated prototype devices using the chip, including tablet-style systems and its Xiaomi AI Cube mini-PC.
These prototypes combine the O100 with other Xring processors to support sustained local AI workloads.
Commercial Devices Expected in 2027
Xiaomi expects commercial applications for the Xring O100 to begin in 2027.
Potential uses include smartphones, tablets, robotics and other devices that require powerful local AI processing.
The O100 forms part of Xiaomi’s wider Xring chip strategy, which also includes flagship mobile processors and chips designed for vehicles.
Rather than focusing only on smaller manufacturing processes, Xiaomi is also investing in improved memory bandwidth and advanced packaging technologies.
The company says the goal is to make generative AI faster, more private and usable even without an internet connection.

items.author: Shahbaz Rana
items.content:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif has approved a draft of a new five-year auto policy, continuing protection to existing assemblers of conventional vehicles for four more years but offering substantial tax incentives on new energy vehicles (NEVs) to substantially reduce their prices.
It was also decided that hybrid electric vehicles and Internal Combustion Engine (ICE) conventional vehicles will be treated equally in terms of duties and taxes.
During Wednesday's proceedings, the premier made certain changes in the proposed policy, particularly instructing to separate Range Extended Electric Vehicles (REEVs) and Plug-In Electric Vehicles (PHEVs) from Battery Electric Vehicles (BEVs). He also asked to abolish the proposed federal excise duty on below 1000 cc conventional cars and cut the customs duty rate from 30% to 15% on all cars for the fifth year of the policy – fiscal year 2030-31.
The prime minister approved the draft policy for 2026-31 and to bring it largely in line with the National Tariff Policy(NTP), the rates will be implemented from the current year to offset the impact of the delay.
After the prime minister's clearance, the policy will now be legally vetted by the Ministry of Law, and the Ministry of Finance has been instructed to take up the draft with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) for its vetting.
Massive relief for NEVs
The committee constituted to achieve consensus on the new policy had proposed equal treatment of BEVs, REEVs and PHEVs as per the New Energy Vehicles Policy. But the prime minister did not agree. BEVs will have the most preferential tax treatment, followed by REEVs and then PHEVs.
There will be only 1% sales tax on NEVs, their completely knocked down (CKD) kits, parts, inputs and raw materials. There will also be exemption of federal excise duty (FED), Capital Value Tax (CVT) and Withholding Tax (WHT) on NEVs, according to the decision. But the government has decided that there will be additional FED on conventional vehicles to compensate for the price drop due to tariff reductions.
According to another incentive, the loan limit for buying NEVs has been approved to be enhanced from Rs3 million to Rs10 million, and the tenor of the loan will be up from three years to five years. The government decided that there will also be 1% customs duty on the import of charging stations, and swap stations will be supported through Viability Gap Funding.
Tariff wall largely stays
According to the approved draft, there will be up to 80% reduction in automobile tariff with no regulatory duty, and additional customs duty on the import of cars will also end after two years. But due to other changes, the overall protection available to existing assemblers largely remains in place for the first two years and then will go down in the next two years.
Government officials involved in policy-making said the proposed tariffs for completely built units would remain within upper tariff limits of the NTP except in the last year. The tariff will be reviewed after two years on the basis of energy cost, tax, interest rates, exchange rate flexibility and export performance, they added.
The Industry Ministry had presented the first draft of the auto policy to the prime minister in June, who referred the matter to Minister for Climate Change Dr Musadaq Malik. Then another committee was constituted under Minister for Power Sardar Awais Laghari. The deputy prime minister also took up the recommendations.
Laghari's committee held 14 sessions and proposed the draft when the committee called it an "attempt to strike a balance between the need for protection and opening the automobile industry to competition".
The stated objectives of the policy are to grow exports by linking auto parts into global value chains, set upfront performance targets with clear penalty and reward mechanisms, promote EVs across all categories, improve quality and lower prices of all vehicles except the luxury segment, and open competition for innovation, technology and better vehicle features.
It has been decided that statutory regulatory orders will be phased out by fiscal year 2029-30. The tariffs for the first two years will remain unchanged.
According to the approved policy, for over 1801 cc SUVs and cars, the customs duty rate will be 40%, FED 60% and sales tax 25% for FY26-27 and FY27-28. For FY28-29, customs duty will reduce to 40% and the rest of the taxes will stay the same. For FY29-30, it will go down to 30%. But for FY30-31, customs duty will be 15%, FED 60% and sales tax 25%.
Foreign consultant Stefan Dercon had recommended 40% customs duty, 30% FED and 20% GST for over 1800 cc cars. For cars of 1001-1800 cc, customs duty will be 50%, FED 15% and GST 25% for FY26-27 and FY27-28. For FY28-29, customs duty will be 40%, FED 15% and GST 15%. For FY29-30, customs duty will be 30%, FED 15% and GST 25%. For FY30-31, customs duty will be 15%, FED 15% and GST 25%. For up to 1000 cc cars, customs duty will be 50% and GST 25% for FY26-27 and FY27-28. For FY28-29, customs duty will reduce to 40%, and for FY29-30 to 30%. For FY30-31, customs duty will be 15% and GST 25%.
Based on these rates, there will not be any substantial reduction in prices of up to 850 cc ICE vehicles. Prices in the first year of implementation will reduce only 5.5% due to the government's decision to impose 4.5% additional customs duty. This will be almost equal to comparable NEV prices, according to the policy document.
For up to 1000 cc ICE cars, prices will also not reduce in the first years, but during the fifth year of implementation, these can go down by 9% – a benefit that may be offset due to annual price increases. The government will impose 5% FED on 1500 cc cars to deny some benefits of price reduction, but in the fifth year, prices will be cut by 11% or Rs650,000. However, this benefit may also reduce due to annual price increases.
The price of the Toyota Fortuner is projected to reduce from Rs20.5 million in the first year to Rs18.6 million in the last year – a reduction of Rs2 million or 9%.
Under the new policy, the government will offer fiscally neutral duty and local tax drawback schemes to encourage exports, and there will be legally binding and enforceable mandatory export regimes. There will also be a target to attract at least five anchor parts manufacturing firms and establish SME clusters around them. The manufacturing license will be linked to agreement with principals for a share in the global export market, and there will be separate CKD import for left-hand drive vehicles. There will be no duty on the import of parts used for exports, and an Auto Parts Export Council will be set up for coordination and developing synergy. There will be a minimum domestic value addition requirement to measure and enforce value addition, and contract manufacturing will reduce production costs by allowing the use of existing idle capacity.

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
Australian High Commissioner Timothy Kane has said negotiations on a modernised Pakistan-Australia Bilateral Investment Treaty are expected to conclude by December, a move that could encourage greater Australian investment in Pakistan, according to a statement issued on Wednesday.
Australia and Pakistan have a treaty dating back to 1998, but it needs to be modernised according to the changing requirements of both economies, Kane said while speaking at the Lahore Chamber of Commerce and Industry (LCCI).
Bilateral trade in goods declined from $973 million in 2024-25 to $672 million in 2025-26, according to State Bank of Pakistan figures. Pakistan's exports to Australia fell from $285 million to $275 million, while imports dropped from $688 million to $397 million.
LCCI President Faheemur Rehman Saigol urged joint efforts to reverse this trend and set a target of taking bilateral trade to at least $3 billion. Pakistan's exports to Australia mainly comprise home textiles, apparel, rice, surgical instruments and sports goods. Industrial workwear, safety gloves, auto parts, engineering goods, leather products, spices, pink salt, marble and furniture were identified as promising areas for export expansion.
Saigol called for the early convening of the Pakistan-Australia Joint Trade Committee, which has not met since March 2023, and negotiations on a preferential trade arrangement, pointing out that several competing countries enjoy duty-free access to Australia while Pakistani exporters do not.
The mining and mineral sector offers significant opportunities for joint ventures, as Pakistan possesses substantial mineral resources while Australia has world-class expertise in exploration and mineral processing. Education and skills development, particularly vocational education, technical training and digital skills, were identified as another key area for bilateral cooperation.
Kane said agriculture remained a major area of cooperation, with Australian agricultural trade with Pakistan worth almost one billion Australian dollars last year. He said more than 100,000 Australian cattle had been exported to Pakistan, with most going to Punjab, and Australian cattle genetics could significantly improve milk production.
Australia is looking forward to exporting GMO canola to Pakistan following the country's approval of genetically modified canola. A Pakistani delegation will visit Australia next month to examine opportunities in pulses.

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
Investors remained jittery at the Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) on Wednesday as the spreading Middle East war sparked caution, which pulled the KSE-100 index down by 698.56 points, or 0.40%, at close.
The market moved within a broad range, hitting the high of 173,174.19 and slipping to the low of 171,801.67. Stock selling intensified in the final hours, dragging the index further into negative territory.
Market mood was influenced by the continuing US-Iran conflict, with escalating attacks on military, shipping and energy assets, fuelling concerns of wider regional instability and a fresh rise in crude oil prices. Investors remained wary of the potential economic fallout from disruptions to energy supplies.
According to Ahmed Sheraz, equity trader at KTrade Securities, the KSE-100 index closed at 171,943.60, down 698.56 points, or 0.40% with trading in approximately 159 million shares.
The trading session remained mixed, where selling pressure was primarily witnessed across commercial bank, cement and fertiliser sectors. Among individual stocks, Fauji Fertiliser, MCB Bank, Lucky Cement, Meezan Bank and other index-heavy names shed value, while selective buying lent some support to the broader market.
Looking ahead, investors are likely to remain cautious amid heightened geopolitical uncertainty, as Brent crude crossed the $100-per-barrel mark following an overnight escalation between the US and Iran, while shipping traffic through the Strait of Hormuz remained disrupted.
"The sharp rise in oil prices, coupled with ongoing geopolitical tensions, could continue to weigh on Pakistan's external account and inflation outlook, keeping the PSX sensitive to further developments in the coming sessions," Sheraz noted.
JS Global analyst Mubashir Anis Naviwala observed that the KSE-100 index traded cautiously and touched the intra-day low of 171,801.67. Selling pressure became more visible towards the closing hours. Commercial banks, cement and fertiliser firms were the key drags on the index. Some support came from miscellaneous, chemical and automobile sectors. Overall, the sentiment remained cautious amid renewed geopolitical uncertainty, he added.
"Market sentiment stayed subdued amid geopolitical uncertainty following fresh attacks across the Middle East. International oil prices continued to strengthen, with WTI at $94.97 (+1.9%) and Brent at $100.40 (+2.46%) in the evening," commented Ali Najib, Deputy Head of Trading at Arif Habib Limited (AHL).
On the macro front, Pakistan's remittances increased 17% year-on-year to $3.7 billion in August, while 2MFY27 inflows rose 15% to $7.3 billion. Pakistan Services, UBL, Oil & Gas Development Company, Lucky Core and Sazgar Engineering collectively added 269 points to the benchmark index, while FFC, MCB Bank, Lucky Cement, Meezan Bank and Mari Energies erased 411 points amid selective profit-taking.

HMD has revived the Asha name from Nokia’s past with a new entry-level smartphone aimed at users who want basic smartphone features without paying for a more capable Android device.

Design and Display
The HMD Asha 305 is available in black and lime green.
It measures 10.2mm thick and weighs just 145 grams, giving it a compact and lightweight design.
The front features a 5-inch LCD with a resolution of 854 × 480 pixels.
There is also a 2MP front-facing camera positioned above the display.
Internals and Software
The phone is powered by a Unisoc T137 processor, paired with 2GB of RAM and 16GB of internal storage.
Storage can be expanded by up to 128GB using a microSD card.
It supports dual 4G SIMs, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth 4.2, GPS, and USB Type-C connectivity.
The device runs Pulse OS, which is based on Android but does not include Google Play services or Google’s usual applications.
Instead, HMD provides its own app store containing lighter applications. HMD specifically mentions TikTok Lite, while unofficial reports suggest apps such as Facebook Lite, Instagram Lite, WhatsApp, and YouTube may also be supported.
The software is designed to keep the experience focused on basic communication and entertainment.
Cameras
The HMD Asha 305 comes with a 2MP rear camera accompanied by an LED flash.
A matching 2MP selfie camera is located on the front.
The camera hardware is considerably simpler than what is normally found on modern budget Android smartphones.
Battery and Pricing
The phone includes a removable 2,500mAh battery with support for 5W charging.
HMD claims the battery can provide up to 32 hours of use.
Official global pricing has not yet been announced, although the device has appeared in markets including the Philippines for around $65.
HMD is positioning the Asha as a lightweight smartphone sitting between its basic feature phones and more powerful budget Android devices.
Its small display, simple cameras, and lightweight software could also make it suitable as a secondary phone. However, unlike HMD’s more digital-detox-focused feature phones, the Asha still provides access to social media and other apps.
The removable battery, compact size, and revived Asha branding may particularly appeal to users familiar with the original Nokia Asha 305.

items.author: Gaurav Bagur
items.content:
Noida-based sustainable critical mineral producer LOHUM claims to have become “first Indian company to start lithium operations globally”, announcing the dispatch of its first tranche of lithium ore from Zimbabwe’s Matabeleland South Province.
In a social media post, the startup said it now holds mining rights across ten spodumene-bearing blocks in Zimbabwe covering approximately 1,100 hectares, with an option to extend to 90 additional blocks.
LOHUM is targeting an annual production capacity of roughly 30,000 tonnes of lithium carbonate within two to three years.
“We remain committed to building integrated capabilities from mine to cathode to circularity, with concentration capacity developed in Zimbabwe so that value addition is shared,” LOHUM said.
Founded in 2018 by Rajat Verma, LOHUM produces sustainable energy transition materials through integrated battery recycling & raw material refining and battery repurposing.Its offers critical mineral products like lithium, cobalt, nickel, platinum, among other rare earth metals.
It used multi-stage hydrometallurgical energy transition material recycling tech to produce pure metallic lithium in September 2023, becoming the first non-Chinese company to do so through recycling.
The startup last raised $54 Mn in its Series B round back in 2024 to expand into new energy transition materials markets in North America, the EU, the Middle East, Africa, and Asia. Backed by the likes of Singularity, Vyoman India Private Limited, VenturEast, among others, it has raised over $120 Mn till date.
India Pushes For Critical Mineral Import Independence
India currently relies on imports for nearly 100% of its lithium-ion (Li-ion) battery requirements. By starting international operations, LOHUM says that it is advancing the goal of the Central Government’s ₹34,300 Cr National Critical Mineral Mission, which aims to acquire up to 50 overseas mining assets to reduce import vulnerability.
Notably, union minister for coal and mines G Kishan Reddy has in the past said that India could potentially meet the demand for critical minerals, such as lithium, locally within three to four years.
The ministry of mines had also earlier sought assistance from several foreign countries including Australia and the US with technical help on lithium processing, per reports from 2024.
India’s EV industry is seeing steady growth and adoption from consumers and enterprises. At the same time, several startups have also entered the battery technology space, with some aiming to support EV makers by recycling batteries and recovering critical minerals.
For example, Delhi NCR-based battery recycling startup BatX Energies recently raised ₹105 Cr in a Series A funding round led by IvyCap Ventures. Karo Sambhav, another startup that focuses on e-waste recycling to recover critical, precious and high-value materials, also raised ₹56 Cr in pre-Series A funding from Rainmatter.

items.content:
Apple’s long-awaited foldable iPhone may arrive with a different name and a lower-than-expected starting price. Previous reports suggested the device could cost more than $2,000, with estimates reaching around $2,199, but a last-minute rumor now places the starting price at $1,999.
According to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, the foldable will reportedly be called the iPhone Duo, rather than iPhone Ultra. The device was initially rumored as the iPhone Fold before more recent reports began referring to it as the iPhone Ultra.
iPhone Duo Specs and Price
The iPhone Duo is expected to start with 256GB of storage and come in white and dark blue.
It will reportedly use Apple’s A20 Pro chip alongside the company’s new C2 modem.
The phone is said to feature two 48MP rear cameras and a 12MP front camera designed specifically for video conferencing.
Other expected features include a magnetic hinge and support for the Apple Pencil.
The device could go on sale as early as October, starting at around $1,999, which is roughly $200 lower than Gurman’s previous estimate. Higher-storage versions could still approach $3,000.
iPhone 18 Pro Models
Apple is also expected to unveil the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max at today’s event.
Both phones are said to look almost identical to their predecessors, although the orange color option will reportedly be replaced by a new burgundy red finish.
At least the Pro Max is expected to feature a variable-aperture main camera, while both models will use the A20 Pro chip.
They are also rumored to offer longer battery life and redesigned vapor chambers for improved heat management.
The Dynamic Island is expected to become smaller and support three live tasks simultaneously, compared with two on current models.
Both phones are reportedly set to cost $100 more than their predecessors.
Apple Watch and AirPods Updates
Gurman also claims the Apple Watch Series 12 will bring back a ceramic option alongside new colors, while the Apple Watch Ultra 4 will offer improved battery life.
The watches will work with a redesigned Health app and a new Readiness app, featuring some functions similar to Oura and Whoop devices.
Apple is also reportedly adding a privacy-focused feature that analyzes a user’s day and summarizes events, including conversations, without recording or storing audio or providing transcripts.
Meanwhile, Apple’s rumored AirPods with cameras have reportedly been delayed until next year.
The AirPods 5, however, are still expected to debut today with what is described as dramatically improved noise cancellation.

items.author: Reuters
items.content:
Apple on Wednesday unveiled a $1,999 foldable phone called Duo, introducing the biggest change in years in the company's flagship product.
The Duo ​is sized and shaped like a passport, with rounded edges. It opens into a horizontal, 7.6-inch-wide (19 cm) screen that can also be viewed vertically. There is a smaller single screen on the ‌front when the phone is folded. When open, it is Apple's thinnest phone, the company said.
The folding phone event, the first with new CEO John Ternus at the helm, is the most noticeable overhaul of Apple's flagship product since it removed the physical home button from the iPhone X in 2017. The iPhone brought in $209.6 billion, or just over half of Apple's sales, in its most recent fiscal year.
Apple positioned the iPhone Duo as a business productivity device, showing how it would manage Zoom calls with multiple participants and a broader view ​of the Slack messaging app. The Duo's larger screen will support multiple app windows at once, a move aimed at productivity that Apple has made with some of its iPads.
Apple unveils the iPhone Duo, the company's first foldable smartphone. Prices start at $1,999 and the phone will be available for preorder starting Oct. 16 in more than 70 countries and regions. Bloomberg's @edludlow reports from Cupertino https://t.co/bkgXItbgVf pic.twitter.com/fvVxLv5u79
— Bloomberg TV (@BloombergTV) September 9, 2026
Ternus criticised existing foldables as awkward ​and poorly suited for common tasks such as scrolling and video viewing, saying the Duo was designed to deliver an iPad-like experience in a pocket-sized device through a custom ⁠hinge, dual displays with a consistent aspect ratio, and a new titanium body.
"It's entirely new and at the same time remarkably familiar. A similar size to your passport, it feels familiar to hold and comfortable to use with one ​hand," Ternus said.
Apple said the iPhone Duo will feature the A20 chip to drive its displays and also a new C2 modem chip designed by Apple, part of its move away from Qualcomm's wireless data chips.
Apple's first foldable iPhone will start at $1,999.
The new iPhone “Duo” phone will fit comfortably in a pocket and allows people to use more than one app at a time. 🔗: https://t.co/aNSfuddMn8 pic.twitter.com/gpaPcnGINX
— The Wall Street Journal (@WSJ) September 9, 2026
“Apple has created a new ​premium growth opportunity, opened up another revenue stream and injected fresh momentum into the iPhone business," PP Foresight analyst Paolo Pescatore said. Shares were down 1.8% at the end of the presentation.
Ternus emphasises privacy focus
Former CEO Tim Cook handed over the leadership baton to Ternus at the start of the presentation with a video about how to start the event. The video ended with a close-up of Cook, who said, "Not me. That's your guy," pointing back toward Ternus.
Ternus touted the iPhone platform as a personal AI hub that focused on ​privacy, saying that others wanted to collect and store personal data. "Honestly, trust only goes so far when your data is no longer yours to control," he said. "That's why Apple Intelligence runs on device whenever it can."
Apple's Lilian Rincon, who ​oversees AI products for the iPhone maker and was recruited from Google earlier this year, described an updated Siri assistant that will work with 300,000 apps at release.
Executives also showed off the iPhone 18 Pro and the 18 Pro Max handsets that are ‌the latest ⁠versions of Apple's well-known line, which do not fold. Pricing for the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max starts at $1,199 and $1,299, up $100 from the starting prices of the 17 Pro and Pro Max.
AirPods and Apple Watch updates
Apple also unveiled a feature aimed at addressing growing concerns over AI-generated and manipulated images. It introduced a new standard it calls "Apple Reference Image" to prove the authenticity of the images taken with the new iPhone 18 Pro cameras and said it will also support the emerging SynthID standard for identifying images that have been created or edited with AI. The Apple Reference Image feature will not be available in the EU or China.
The iPhone 18 Pro will also include the new A20 Pro chip, ​which brings improvements to help advanced AI models run directly on iPhones.
The company also said a new ⁠version of AirPods would start at $129 with noise cancellation, a first for its budget line of earbuds, and that a $149 version would be available with extra features such as wireless charging and on-stem volume control that would allow users to adjust the volume by swiping up or down on the stem.
Apple also introduced the Apple Watch Series 12 and ​Apple Watch Ultra 4, positioning them as major health-focused upgrades. That includes a redesigned sensor system that collects heart rate more frequently than before and powers new features ​that gauge recovery and fitness. ⁠The company said the watches use new Apple silicon and improved sensors to deliver what it called the most accurate heart-rate tracking in a wearable.
Premium pricing challenge
Ternus previously served as Apple's hardware chief but has kept a low public profile aside from a handful of product introductions and sustainability initiatives. It will fall to Ternus to persuade Apple's customers that they need a foldable device costing about $2,000, a new high for a global brand that has defined mass luxury.
While Samsung Electronics and Huawei Technologies have ⁠sold folding phones ​since 2019, the devices have remained a niche among tech enthusiasts. But even with a steep price tag, analyst firms such as International Data ​Corporation expect Apple to sell every foldable iPhone it can produce and secure a 40% share of the lucrative niche by the end of next year.

items.author: Gaurav Bagur
items.content:
At the Global Fintech Fest (GFF) 2026 in Mumbai, UPI operator NPCI announced a series of digital infrastructure initiatives to expand credit access across India.
It also unveiled two AI initiatives aimed at streamlining enterprise fintech operations.
Sanjay Lohiya, secretary of the Department of Financial Services (DFS), launched open-source android ATMs. These are designed to function as digital banking units (DBUs) in transit hubs and rural areas, as well as corporate parks and educational campuses, handling account openings, loan applications, and cheque deposits.
They are also capable of instantly issuing RuPay cards and merchant UPI QR codes, reducing onboarding turnaround times from weeks to minutes.
“The solution aims to expand the role of ATMs from just cash withdrawal and deposit machines to intelligent customer service and banking access points. Customers can receive their cards directly from the machine without waiting for courier delivery or making a branch visit, while merchants can obtain QR codes instantly for UPI-based payment collections,” the NPCI said in a statement.
 
Nine major lenders, including State Bank of India, Bank of Baroda, and Slice Small Finance Bank, are trialling the ATMs alongside manufacturers Hitachi Payment Services, Perto India, and Vortex Engineering.
NPCI’s AI Push
The NPCI rolled out AiNxt, an open-source, enterprise-grade agentic AI platform designed to build, test, and deploy custom intelligent agents.
The suite incorporates four core components: AiNxt OS, AiNxt Code (a plugin for integrated development environments or IDEs), AiNxt CLI, and AiNxt Enterprise. These will enable development teams to build, test, and deploy across IDEs and command-line environments.
The platform can be used to build custom AI harnesses directly within existing development environments. Under a Bring Your Own Models (BYOM) framework, it enables AI agents to be deployed through low-code, no-code tools.
Additionally, the NPCI also unveiled agentic orchestration & messaging (AtOM), an AI-driven agentic orchestration platform engineered to handle complex integration, change management, and partner onboarding across UPI. The platform produces digitally signed, machine-readable interactions to establish verifiable audit trails for compliance.
Besides these, the NPCI is also expected to launch an ‘Unified Agent Protocol’ at the GFF. This would be a framework which would see AI agents execute small-ticket digital payments without requiring explicit user authorisation for every transaction.
Finance Ministry Expands Scope Of Credit Line On UPI
In addition to the above launches, the Ministry of Finance also expanded the ‘Credit Line on UPI’ facility to cover government-backed priority sector credit schemes, the Kisan Credit Card (KCC) and PM MUDRA Yojana (PMMY). The integration allows beneficiaries to link pre-sanctioned credit lines directly to UPI for digital merchant transactions.
The overall credit base under these schemes spans over 7.7 Cr active KCC accounts with sanctioned limits exceeding ₹10 Lakh Cr and more than 57 Cr PMMY loans totaling over ₹40 Lakh Cr.
Currently, ten banks have enabled Credit Line on UPI for KCC account holders, while eight banks have enabled it for PMMY beneficiaries, with more expected to join the ranks in coming months.
The DFS also introduced the Aadhaar Enabled Payment System (AePS) Three-Party Cash Deposit service, an interoperable assisted-banking service allowing depositors to deposit cash directly into third-party beneficiary accounts via local AePS Touchpoint Operators.
The system relies on Aadhaar biometric eKYC authentication to verify the depositor and provides pre-transaction SMS name verification to prevent misdirected transfers. It aims to bring formal cash deposit facilities to rural, semi-urban and underserved customers.
It also has added benefits like reducing travel time, validating the beneficiary and transaction, and assisting those who may not be digitally savvy.
Fourteen institutions, including State Bank of India, Bank of Baroda, and YES Bank, have enabled the service.

Perlindungan IP68 ini juga sangat relevan untuk pengguna harian, di mana sering kali ponsel kena cipratan atau ketumpahan air minus saat diletakkan di atas meja atau berada dekat dengan wastafel.

items.author: Yus Lianson
items.content:
Samsung Galaxy A57 5G baru saja diluncurkan di pasar Indonesia, dan menjadi salah satu smartphone baru perusahaan asal Korea Selatan tersebut yang dilengkapi perlindungan IP68 terhadap air dan debu.
Karenanya, HP baru Samsung itu tahan terhadap cipratan air atau hujan saat dalam perjalanan. Kemampuan ini juga menjadi salah satu syarat utama untuk menjawab kebutuhan pengguna yang menginginkan ponsel andal sepanjang hari dan dalam kondisi apa pun.
Baca Juga: Mengenal Muse, Personal AI Agent yang Diciptakan oleh Meta
Perlindungan IP68 ini juga sangat relevan untuk pengguna harian, di mana sering kali ponsel kena cipratan atau ketumpahan air minus saat diletakkan di atas meja atau berada dekat dengan wastafel.
“Kami memahami bahwa smartphone tidak hanya digunakan dalam kondisi ideal, tetapi selalu dibawa ke berbagai aktivitas dan situasi sehari-hari,” ujar Annisa Maulina, MX Product Marketing Senior Manager Samsung Electronics Indonesia, dalam keterangannya, Rabu (9/9/2026).
Walau memberikan perlindungan ekstra terhadap air, label IP68 masin memiliki batas yang perlu dipahami banyak pengguna.
Arti IP68 pada Galaxy A57 5G
IP atau Ingress Protection menunjukkan tingkat perlindungan perangkat terhadap benda padat dan air. Dengan label IP68, angka 6 merujuk pada perlindungan terhadap debu, sementara angka 8 menunjukkan ketahanan terhadap perendaman di air dalam kondisi tertentu.
Galaxy A57 5G kena tumpahan air.
Di Galaxy A57 5G, raksasa teknologi asal Korea Selatan ini menggunakan pengujian laboratorium berupa perendaman air tawar. Samsung mengklaim, HP barunya ini mampu bertahan hingga kedalaman 1,5 meter selama maksimal 30 menit.
Kondisi uji tersebut perlu menjadi acuan saat membaca klaim tahan air. Paparan cairan dalam aktivitas harian belum tentu sama dengan lingkungan pengujian laboratorium.
Samsung juga menyatakan perangkat tidak disarankan untuk digunakan di pantai atau kolam renang. Ketahanan terhadap air dan debu dapat berkurang seiring waktu akibat pemakaian normal.
Dari informasi tersebut, IP68 di HP Android baru Samsung tersebut lebih tepat dianggap sebagai perlindungan tambahan bila insiden yang tidak diinginkan terjadi. Perlu diingat, rating ini tidak menjamin ponsel bebas risiko dalam setiap situasi melibatkan air.
Perlindungan Kaca di Galaxy A57 5G
Selain IP68, Galaxy A57 5G juga sudah dilengkapi dengan Gorilla Glass Victus+ untuk membantu melindungi permukaan depan dan belakang ponsel agar lebih tahan terhadap goresan serta benturan.
Kehadiran kaca pelindung juga tidak berarti perangkat kebal terhadap kerusakan. Pengguna tetap perlu berhati-hati saat membawa atau meletakkan ponsel, termasuk ketika beraktivitas di luar ruangan.
Menurut Annisa, kombinasi ketahanan terhadap air, debu, dan perlindungan kaca ditujukan untuk mendukung penggunaan ponsel dalam berbagai situasi sehari-hari.
Update One UI dan Android hingga Enam Generasi
Samsung turut melengkapi Galaxy A57 5G dengan dukungan hingga enam generasi pembaruan Android OS dan One UI, serta hingga enam tahun pembaruan keamanan.
Periode dukungan tersebut dihitung sejak peluncuran global pertama perangkat, bukan sejak tanggal pembelian. Ketersediaan dan jadwal pembaruan dapat berbeda sesuai model serta pasar.
Galaxy A57 5G tersedia dalam pilihan RAM dan penyimpanan 8GB/128GB, 8GB/256GB, serta 12GB/256GB. Pilihan warna mencakup Awesome Gray, Awesome Navy, Awesome Icy Blue, dan Awesome Lilac.
Bagi pengguna yang mempertimbangkan ponsel untuk pemakaian jangka panjang, ketahanan fisik dan dukungan pembaruan dapat menjadi pertimbangan bersama performa, kamera, serta kapasitas baterai.

items.summary:

items.author: Gaurav Bagur
items.content:
India has spent years celebrating founders who built companies from scratch. But what rarely gets discussed is what happens to the company, its shares and the family when a founder is suddenly gone.
The recent tragic passings of prominent names in the Indian startup ecosystem, including Icertis’ Samir Bodas, Table Space’s Amit Banerji, Epigamia’s Rohan Mirchandani, Xpedize’s Regan Mithani and Whatfix’s Khadim Batti, have brought sharper focus on this question.
An untimely founder death can leave behind more than grief — it can create a complicated trail of questions around ownership, unvested shares, succession and the future of the business.
This is where estate and succession planning becomes critical. Putting the right provisions in place beforehand can help protect a founder’s family financially while giving the company a clearer path in their absence.
“From a family standpoint, a founder may have created significant wealth. But when institutional investors come in, the founder’s shares are often subject to vesting clauses. If those agreements are not clearly worded, the family may not be able to recover the founder’s full stake,” said the founder of digital estate planning startup Yellow, Nikhil Varghese.
While planning for one’s demise could be uncomfortable for many, it is crucial to understand that estate and succession planning is important in several other situations. For instance, divorce, separation or disputes between cofounders can create questions around ownership and the division of assets.
Therefore, this is less of a contingency plan and more of a governance issue that founders and investors need to address from the outset.
So, What Happens When A Founder Passes?
Preparation can only take one so far. Even with careful planning, what follows is hardly a speedy and straightforward process.
“In the interim period, we have to give the family some time to adjust. Even if these principles are included in the documents, you can’t pick up the phone and say I’m going to enforce this right now. That’s not humane,” said Ashwini Thulsaram, a principal at 3one4 Capital, who leads the governance function for the VC firm.
According to her, investors often assess whether a secondary transaction can be undertaken, while taking the preferences of the family or legal heirs into consideration. They also look at whether the legal heirs have the business acumen and the willingness to lead the company.
“However, a secondary transaction is always a preference. This is because founders generally want to protect and create liquidity for their family,” she said, adding that a secondary could involve selling their stake to other investors at market value, at a certain discount, or at whatever price investors are willing to pay.
These conversations could take 2-3 months. Generally, the immediate focus is to ensure that shares get bought at a certain price to ease the financial burden on the family, as per Thulsaram. More often than not, the company’s senior leadership team is prepared to step in and take over.
How Can Founders Protect Their Legacy?
While investors assist, it is the founders who should ensure the terms of the shareholding agreement match their needs.
“Founders are often most focused on raising funds during their first round of investment. But if these issues are not addressed in the first agreement, those terms become the foundation for future rounds. It can then be much harder to negotiate better terms later,” Varghese cautioned.
Understanding the vesting schedule and negotiating favourable terms requires the founder to have the right advisors.
“Making a will is the basic thing that everyone should do but, for most startup founders, they should consider trusts to ringfence their liabilities,” Varghese added.
A trust is a legal entity that holds assets on behalf of a beneficiary. It is a critical aspect of estate planning, especially when it comes to businesses, said Sandeep Nerlekar, founder of Terentia Consultants, an advisory firm that helps individuals, families, and businesses with their estate and succession planning.
“Founders can hold wealth in different forms, including preference shares, CCPS, OCDs, NCDs and DVR shares. These assets can be transferred to a trust, creating a separate pool of assets and helping diversify the risk,” Nerlekar said.
“This basically separates ownership from benefits. Then if liabilities come your way, they sit on your personal balance sheet and do not percolate into the assets held by the trust,” Varghese explained.
Jurisdiction also becomes a major factor as Indian startups continue to attract capital from around the world. While India does not have any tax on inheritance or estate tax that applies to properties transferred on death, this is not true for the rest of the world.
How Can Investors Prepare For The Worst
Drawing from his experience, Bluegreen Ventures’ founding partner Anup Jain said investors are often left to manage their own crisis when a founder dies unexpectedly.
This can involve supporting the founder’s family, helping the remaining founding team reach an agreement, and finding a suitable replacement with the right equity arrangement.
“Life is uncertain. We plan to include succession planning provisions in all our deals going forward, because these concerns are not age-related. There are examples showing that tragedies can happen at any time,” Jain said.
VCs also play an active role from the early stages of funding, ensuring that founders plan for potential risks and the future, said Thulsaram.
When investors come on board, founders are generally subject to a vesting schedule wherein their equity unlocks at different stages after specified periods of time, similar to how ESOPs work. This helps keep founders aligned with investors while ensuring the company has greater stability if a founder exits.
Exigency clauses are generally included by institutional investors when they participate in a deal. In case of a founder’s untimely passing, the term sheet might include provisions enabling the family to immediately unlock unvested equity, or allowing direct transmission of shares to nominees while bypassing the approval of other investors.
“The terms for each situation vary by investor in terms of whether the family or a legal heir gets all the shares vested or only a proportion, or how many months get accelerated,” Thulsaram added.
For India’s startup ecosystem, recent tragedies have shown why estate and succession planning can no longer be an afterthought. As startups grow larger and founder wealth becomes increasingly tied to company equity, planning for what happens next has to become an essential part of protecting both the founder and the business.
[Edited by Akshit Pushkarna]
The post The Legacy Question: What Happens When A Startup Founder Passes Away? appeared first on Inc42 Media.

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
Eight months after the Gul Plaza tragedy, the affected shop owners say the building’s debris remains uncleared, and reconstruction has yet to begin, prompting them to give the Sindh government a seven-day deadline to address their grievances.
Gul Plaza Owners Association General Secretary Arif Qadri said on Wednesday that around 850 shop owners, including more than 100 women, had lost their businesses in the deadly blaze, leaving some 1,200 families facing an uncertain economic future.
Addressing a protest camp set up by the association at the site of the demolished plaza, Qadri said nearly 800 affected shop owners had received neither relief nor compensation. “The government has compensated tenants, but the actual shop owners have received nothing,” he said.
Read More: Challan holds Gul Plaza administration responsible for fire, exonerates govt bodies
Qadri demanded the immediate removal of the debris and the announcement of a reconstruction plan, along with financial assistance for the affected traders. He warned that if the government failed to respond within seven days, the traders would stage a sit-in on MA Jinnah Road. “Stop forgetting us. Do not force us to cross the line,” he said.
Business leader Abdul Rauf Ibrahim also warned of a prolonged protest and possible closure of MA Jinnah Road. He urged Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah to personally hear the grievances of the affected traders. Ibrahim also called for an audit of the compensation distributed among the victims.
Former FPCCI vice president Asif Sakhi claimed that the Sindh government had distributed Rs4.5 billion in compensation following the tragedy, but said the shop owners had received no share of the funds. He alleged that the compensation was distributed through the “main accused” in the tragedy and said the matter would have to be taken up at the federal level.
The affected traders reiterated their demand for immediate reconstruction of Gul Plaza and compensation for shop owners, warning that failure to meet their demands would trigger a prolonged sit-in on MA Jinnah Road.
Defence puts govt institutions in the dock
A judicial magistrate hearing the Gul Plaza fire case rejected a defence plea seeking the formation of a Joint Investigation Team (JIT), observing that such teams were generally constituted in terrorism cases.
The court will decide at the next hearing whether to approve the charge sheet and whether government institutions should also be nominated as accused in the case.
Tanveer Pasta, president of the Gul Plaza Traders Association, and others appeared before the judicial magistrate (South) as the prosecution and defence exchanged arguments over alleged negligence in the deadly fire that claimed more than 70 lives.
Prosecutor Hassan Bhatti told the court that Pasta was guilty of the “highest degree of negligence”, alleging that he failed to call the fire brigade after the blaze broke out.
Defence counsel Javed Mir, however, disputed the allegations and accused the new investigation officer (IO) of attempting to protect government institutions.
Read More: Gul Plaza owners cry foul
He said the court had previously ordered that government departments be included in the investigation, but the latest charge sheet had given a clean chit to the Karachi Metropolitan Corporation (KMC), Sindh Building Control Authority (SBCA), Fire Brigade and other institutions.
“Tanveer Pasta is neither the builder nor the owner, while the SBCA took no action against the builder,” the lawyer argued.
Mir said the fire had started on the ground floor, where no deaths were reported, and claimed that more than 5,000 people had been present and were evacuated. “These people did not die because of the fire but due to suffocation caused by the negligence and incompetence of government institutions,” he added.
The lawyer further argued that the fire brigade had no water available and that people had continued screaming for help for around one-and-a-half hours.
He questioned why the IO had failed to record the statement of the deputy commissioner (South), who, according to him, had reached the site within five minutes of the incident.
Mir also questioned the nomination of a child and his father as accused, saying the child’s elder brother had also been present at the site but was not included in the case.
IO DSP Aamir Warik informed the court that there were 16 doors on the ground floor, which was why no one had died there. He said iron windows had been installed at the premises.
The defence counsel rejected the IO’s explanation, saying people had been “burnt to ashes” and that the investigation failed to properly establish responsibility for the deaths.
The court also asked whether the Civil Defence Department had been included in the investigation. The IO replied that statements of two Civil Defence officials had been recorded.
He further said government institutions had broken windows and doors during rescue operations. The defence, however, maintained that the doors had been broken only on the second day.
Also Read: Gul Plaza fire probe leaves blame unresolved
Mir alleged that the IO had ignored the seven points identified by the court when it ordered a fresh investigation.
Pasta also addressed the court and said people had remained alive for two to two-and-a-half hours after the fire broke out. “Five of my colleagues were martyred, but there is no mention of them in the charge sheet,” he said.
He claimed that a snorkel had malfunctioned and that several lives could have been saved had it continued working. “I was saved by people; otherwise, I too would have died. Our people died, and we have been made accused,” Pasta said while breaking down in tears.
He also claimed that more than Rs7 billion had been distributed among the victims on his recommendation.
The court rejected the defence plea for formation of a JIT and adjourned the hearing until September 18, when it will decide on approval of the charge sheet and the question of whether government institutions should be made accused in the case.
