items.author: Tom Jackson
items.content:
Nigerian startup Shuttlers, the technology-enabled shared mobility platform, has launched a new service that offers commuters a scheduled and shared ride from doorstep to destination, with the option to book privately.
Founded in 2016, Shuttlers transforms how professionals move through African cities, with operations in Lagos, Abuja, and Port Harcourt spanning shared commute routes, corporate employee transport, vehicle rental, and fleet operator partnerships.
With over 10 million journeys completed, more than 11,000 daily riders, and over 430 buses operating daily, Shuttlers is building the infrastructure for the future of urban mobility in Africa.
The startup has now announced the launch of Shuttlers Pod, a scheduled, door-to-door car service for commuting to work, events, and other destinations across Lagos. Shuttlers Pod is designed for commuters who need a comfortable ride at an affordable fare for a planned journey.
The service matches commuters travelling the same route with a single scheduled trip, picking up three to four riders and dropping each at their exact destination. Riders can also book the vehicle privately. Every trip comes with a named driver, known as a Pilot, a fixed fare and a guaranteed pickup, with no surge pricing or roadside negotiation.
The service applies Shuttlers’ scheduled bus model to private vehicles, replacing the traditional bus stop with door-to-door pickups and drop-offs. It offers an alternative to conventional car hire and on-demand journeys, with each Pod trip costing roughly 50 per cent less than typical ride-hailing fares, enabled by its advance-booking and fixed-pricing model.
“Nigeria’s cost of living is rising faster than incomes. With that reality, the smartest way to move people is through shared mobility. We’ve spent the last decade making scheduled, shared transport reliable and affordable; and Shuttlers Pod brings that same thinking to scheduled private and shared trips that are safe, premium and affordable, from your doorstep to exactly where you need to be,” said Shuttlers CEO and co-founder Damilola Olokesusi.

Alasannya? Konon karena konsumen di sini lebih familiar dengan penamaan “Pro”. Jadi spesifikasi yang dihadirkan di Indonesia, sama seperti TECNO CAMON 50 Ultra yang ada di luar sana ya.
Selain pengalaman fotografi yang impresif, smartphone ini juga menawarkan fitur AI komplit, visual layar yang baik, hingga baterai yang tahan seharian penuh. Apakah mutlak jadi opsi terbaik? Berikut review TECNO CAMON 50 Pro 5G selengkapnya.
Desain
Dibandingan CAMON 40 Series terdahulu, desain TECNO CAMON 50 Pro 5G terlihat lebih sleek sekaligus premium. Kini lebih banyak sudut yang dibuat lebih tumpul, sementara bodinya terlihat lebih ramping berkat lengkungan di kedua sisi kiri dan kanan (baik depan dan belakangnya). Meski begitu, aspek durabilitas justru tetap jadi yang utama.
Ya, TECNO CAMON 50 Pro 5G membawa sertifikasi hingga IP69K, yang artinya tidak hanya sekadar tahan dari debu dan air, namun juga semburan air kencang hingga suhu air lebih ekstrem. Plus, mengantongi sertifikasi MIL-STD-810H, yang bisa memberi rasa aman ekstra bila selama penggunaan terjadi skenario seperti jatuh secara tidak disengaja.
Dan rasanya skenario tersebut besar kemungkinan terjadi. Pasalnya, meski terlihat stylish, bodi TECNO CAMON 50 Pro 5G tidak bisa memberikan grip yang benar-benar solid dalam genggaman, alias sedikit licin. Padahal permukaan bodi belakangnya yang berupa kaca, sudah membawa finishing matte, sehingga tidak membekas sidik jari. Jadi harus lebih hati-hati terutama bagi Gizmo friends yang telapak tangannya mudah basah.
Selebihnya, meski relatif ringan hanya 178 gram, bodi smartphone masih cukup terasa solid. Selain warna Nebula Titanium, opsi Cyprus Green juga tidak kalah menarik, dengan corak warna hijau yang cukup mewah. Saya juga suka dengan desain bodi belakang yang tidak melulu meniru iPhone. Plus, casing bawaan paket penjualan yang juga premium dengan corak khusus dan material keras.
Layar
Selain desain yang terlihat premium, layar TECNO CAMON 50 Pro 5G membawa panel yang berkualitas, berjenis AMOLED 1.5K dengan refresh rate maksimum 144Hz, sudah mendukung standar HDR10+, hingga 2160Hz PWM dimming yang bisa mereduksi efek flickering pada tingkat pencahayaan lebih rendah sehingga mata tidak mudah lelah. Keempat sisi bezel juga dibuat tipis dan terlihat simetris.
Berukuran 6,78 inci, dimensinya terasa luas namun tetap kompak dalam genggaman—tidak lain berkat tepi bezel tipis dan sedikit lengkung pada sisinya. Kabar baiknya, saya tidak pernah mengalami risiko misstouch yang kerap menjadi kekurangan pada layar lengkung smartphone terdahulu. Reproduksi warnanya vibrant, dan TECNO bahkan memberikan opsi profil warna yang lebih pekat bila Gizmo friends lebih menyukai visual gonjreng alias lebih kaya.
Sudah terproteksi Gorilla Glass 7i, layar TECNO CAMON 50 Pro 5G tidak terpasang pelindung layar bawaan pabrik. Namun sebagai gantinya, diberikan tempered glass terpisah yang sudah termasuk ke dalam paket penjualan. Sejujurnya, saya tidak merasakan perbedaan signifikan dibandingkan layar 120Hz smartphone lain. Namun tetap saja nice to have.
Yang menjadi sedikit kekurangan pada layar TECNO CAMON 50 Pro 5G, lagi-lagi ada pada mode always-on display-nya. Seperti beberapa smartphone rilisan Transsion Group sebelumnya, walau nama fiturnya “always-on display”, tidak ada opsi untuk membuatnya terus menyala, alias hanya bisa bertahan sekian detik saja. Mungkin untuk membuat layar lebih awet, atau demi efisiensi daya baterai? Setidaknya bisa diberikan opsi agar pengguna dapat memilih.
Kamera
Beralih ke bagian yang menurut saya bisa menjadi nilai jual utama smartphone TECNO Rp5 jutaan satu ini. Ya, setup kamera TECNO CAMON 50 Pro 5G tergolong superior untuk segmen harganya, membawa tiga sensor kamera dengan peran berbeda, dan kamera selfie 50MP yang nggak cuma tinggi secara resolusi, namun juga menawarkan sudut pandang lebar, kemampuan autofokus, plus perekaman video 4K30.
Bagaimana dengan setup kamera belakangnya? Sensor utama TECNO CAMON 50 Pro 5G gunakan Sony LYT-700C 50MP f/1.8 dengan OIS, dan spesialnya lagi dipasangkan dengan sensor telefoto periskop 50MP (Omnivision OV50M) f/2.2 yang memberikan 3x optical zoom. Terakhir, dan yang paling inferior, adalah sensor ultra-wide 8MP (GalaxyCore) f/2.2, sayangnya tanpa autofokus.
Secara hardware, sensor ultra-wide terbilang inferior termasuk bila dibandingkan dengan penawaran Samsung. Namun setidaknya ketiga sensor lainnya termasuk sangat oke di segmennya, bahkan dengan sensor telefoto 3x zoom yang lebih superior dibandingkan flagship Samsung rilisan tahun ini. Dan dengan algoritma fotografi TECNO yang sudah semakin matang sejak generasi sebelumnya, berpengaruh positif terhadap hasil foto.
Dalam kondisi luar ruangan atau pencahayaan berlimpah, bisa dibilang pengalaman kamera TECNO CAMON 50 Pro 5G sudah terasa flagship-grade, baik dari segi detail hingga reproduksi warnanya. White balance tergolong akurat, dan saya suka dengan opsi focal length yang variatif termasuk opsi 35mm dan 85mm, baik pada mode foto biasa sampai portrait. Lagi-lagi, tidak semua flagship menawarkan “pintasan” simpel namun bermanfaat satu ini.
Kualitas foto dari sensor telefoto TECNO CAMON 50 Pro 5G tergolong baik, meski saat low-light memang tidak bisa se-detail realme 16 Pro+ 5G (yang notabene punya banderol harga lebih mahal), namun sudah lebih baik dari Motorola Edge 60 Pro (yang pakai sensor setara Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra). Masih sangat usable, terutama dengan bantuan night mode.
Dari pengalaman saya jepret foto menggunakan kamera TECNO CAMON 50 Pro 5G, saya suka dengan preset default yang cenderung natural dan tidak over-processed (meski diberikan opsi lain yang lebih vibrant), sehingga lebih enak saat di-edit dengan aplikasi pihak ketiga seperti Snapseed, misalnya. Kamera selfienya sudah tergolong oke, hanya ultra-widenya saja yang bakal hasilkan gambar sangat halus terutama dalam kondisi low-light.
Saya juga suka dengan dua fitur ekstra pada aplikasi kameranya. Yang pertama, FlashSnap memungkinkan kamera TECNO CAMON 50 Pro 5G menangkap momen gerak cepat otomatis, mampu mengenali jenis olahraga yang sudah umum, menggunakan sensor 3x zoom sekalipun. Yang kedua, Aqua Mode untuk mempermudah penangkapan momen di bawah air (selama airnya merupakan air bersih, ya).
Hasil foto lengkap dari kamera TECNO CAMON 50 Pro 5G, bisa Gizmo friends akses lewat album berikut ini ya.
Baik kamera utama, telefoto, dan kamera selfie TECNO CAMON 50 Pro 5G sama-sama bisa merekam video hingga 4K30 atau 1080p60 dengan stabilisasi aktif, sementara ultra-wide mentok di 2K30. Tetapi bila Gizmo friends menggunakan resolusi 1080p30, maka bisa berpindah antar sensor kamera belakang selama perekaman berlangsung.
Kualitas visual yang dihasilkan tergolong cukup baik, tidak jauh berbeda dengan warna pada hasil foto. Sedikit catatan, saat gunakan sensor telefoto, kontras terlihat lebih tinggi—jadi lebih dramatis, memang, namun bakal terlihat berbeda bila Gizmo friends “memasangkannya” dengan footage dari sensor utama. Kamera selfie-nya juga pas untuk vlogging dengan sudut pandang lebar, meski memang penangkapan audio dari mikrofon bawaan bukan yang paling jernih.
Fitur
TECNO CAMON 50 Pro 5G hadir dengan HiOS 16 berbasis Android 16, serta janji setidaknya tiga kali peningkatan versi OS dan lima tahun pembaruan keamanan rutin. Bukan yang paling impresif, namun sudah jauh lebih baik dibandingkan generasi smartphone TECNO terdahulu.
Saya sangat menyukai tampilan antarmuka HiOS terbaru yang hadir pada smartphone TECNO setidaknya sejak tahun lalu—dan tahun ini terlihat semakin cantik, meski tidak dapat dipungkiri, semakin mendekati smartphone Apple. Mulai dari efek transparan yang ditampilkan sampai beberapa gaya kustomisasinya, meski memang TECNO menawarkan kustomisasi yang lebih variatif.
Poin plus lainnya, meski terlihat clean, ada banyak fitur yang bisa Gizmo friends eksplor lebih jauh. Asisten virtual Ella, misalnya, tidak hanya bisa menjawab pertanyaan simpel, namun bisa melakukan banyak hal lain. Mulai dari menjawab soal matematika berupa gambar, sampai generate sebuah foto menjadi video. Belum lagi fitur AI lainnya yang bisa membantu produktivitas, sampai One-Tap FlashMemo yang mampu catat atau ekstrak konten di layar ke dalam ruang digital yang mudah diakses dalam sekali sentuh.
Ya, TECNO CAMON 50 Pro 5G punya tombol khusus di sisi kiri smartphone dengan fungsi akses One-Tap FlashMemo kalau ditekan satu kali secara singkat. Sementara saat ditahan, fungsinya bisa seperti Action Button pada iPhone, untuk akses pintasan yang bisa dikustomisasi sesuai keinginan.
Mau kustomisasi lampu LED di belakang? Bisa. Kendalikan perangkat rumah seperti TV dan AC? Ada sensor inframerah di sisi atas untuk fungsi tersebut. Ya, fitur ekstra pada TECNO CAMON 50 Pro 5G benar-benar melimpah sekaligus bermanfaat untuk keseharian. Terakhir, setup speaker stereonya sudah cukup oke dengan output relatif lantang. Ada efek Dolby Atmos yang bisa dimanfaatkan untuk kesan lebih imersif.
Performa
Dari semua aspek yang dibawa oleh smartphone TECNO stylish satu ini, bagian performa terasa paling standar. Ya, urusan dapur pacu, performa TECNO CAMON 50 Pro 5G diperkuat oleh cip Dimensity 7400 Ultimate dari MediaTek, dengan fabrikasi 4nm, RAM LPDDR5x hingga 12GB, dan storage berjenis UFS 2.2. Varian yang saya uji merupakan yang paling standar dengan RAM 8GB dan storage 256GB.
Sejak awal, smartphone ini dapat melibas berbagai macam aplikasi yang saya jalankan. Namun perihal kecepatan membuka aplikasi, multitasking, hingga pemrosesan gambar memang bukan yang paling gegas di kelasnya. Buat main game masih oke kok, di mana sejumlah game bisa berjalan pada fps yang lebih tinggi seperti MLBB maupun PUBG Mobile.
Ya, cip milik TECNO CAMON 50 Pro 5G sejatinya sama seperti POVA 8 Pro 5G yang baru saja diluncurkan, hanya saja TECNO sematkan cip grafis khusus pada seri POVA terbaru demi fps yang lebih tinggi lagi. Overall, bukan yang paling kencang secara benchmark, tetapi masih lebih dari cukup untuk akses berbagai jenis aplikasi terkini. Suhu perangkat juga relatif terjaga, tidak pernah sampai terlalu panas.
Saya juga merasa bila setelah melalui beberapa kali pembaruan software, transisi antar menu dan tampilan antarmuka secara keseluruhan terasa sedikit meningkat. Bila Gizmo friends inginkan performa multitasking lebih andal, mungkin bisa melirik varian dengan RAM yang lebih lega ya.
Baterai
Dalam profilnya yang relatif tipis dan ringan, TECNO mampu berikan peningkatan kapasitas daya yang signifikan, di mana kini baterai TECNO CAMON 50 Pro 5G mencapai 6500 mAh. Ya, secara angka memang tergolong sangat positif. Namun apakah sesuai ekspektasi? Sejujurnya, iya dan tidak.
Dengan siklus penggunaan yang lebih intensif (mengingat smartphone ini sangat menyenangkan untuk digunakan sebagai pengganti kamera saku), baterai TECNO CAMON 50 Pro 5G tahan sampai satu hari penuh, bahkan hingga keesokan harinya. Namun saya pribadi merasa, dengan kapasitas yang dibawanya, seharusnya masih bisa sedikit lebih lama. Bila TECNO terus merilis pembaruan software secara berkala, semoga juga bisa lebih ditingkatkan efisiensi dayanya ya.
Saya tekankan lagi, jauh dari kata “boros” ya. Dan yang menurut saya terbilang sangat baik, adalah kecepatan pengisian dayanya. Iya, secara angka kan bukan yang paling tinggi, yakni 45W ketika beberapa smartphone lain di segmen harganya bahkan bisa berikan watt dua kali lebih instan. Tapi pengalaman mengisi daya smartphone ini sudah terasa instan.
Memang di 15 menit pertama tidak terasa begitu instan, hanya mencapai sekitar 23% saja. Begitu pula 30 menit, masih sedikit di bawah 50%. Tapi kalau Gizmo friends terbiasa isi daya smartphone hingga penuh, hanya membutuhkan waktu sekitar 70 menit kok. Untuk kapasitas baterai TECNO CAMON 50 Pro 5G yang cukup besar, dengan charging “hanya 45W”, sudah oke banget.
Selebihnya, TECNO CAMON 50 Pro 5G juga membawa fitur ekstra terkait proteksi baterai. Mulai dari fitur pengisian daya pintar berbasis AI, limitasi pada persentase tertentu bila diperlukan, hingga bypass charging yang lebih pas untuk skenario gaming.
Kesimpulan
Di tengah masa kenaikan harga komponen, TECNO masih bisa hadirkan smartphone kelas menengah dengan fitur yang benar-benar komplit, termasuk setup kamera superior melalui kehadiran TECNO CAMON 50 Pro 5G. Tampil dalam kemasan yang stylish sekaligus durable, juga menawarkan segudang kemampuan AI komplit lewat Ella dan lainnya.
Performanya memang bukan yang paling kencang, dan lini CAMON memang tidak berfokus pada aspek tersebut. Setidaknya urusan fotografi, rasanya opsi dari TECNO satu ini masih jadi yang paling andal di segmen harganya, setidaknya sampai ulasan ini dibuat. Juga cocok bagi Gizmo friends yang membutuhkan sebuah smartphone all-rounder dengan daya tahan baterai seharian penuh dalam bodi ringkas nan ringan.

Fans are getting closer to the launch of Grand Theft Auto (GTA) 6, but those waiting for the next version of GTA Online may have to be much more patient.
Rockstar Games is scheduled to launch GTA 6 on November 19, 2026. The game has already faced delays, but recent updates suggest that development is moving forward as planned. However, Rockstar has not provided a release date for the online multiplayer experience.
Delayed Again? GTA 6 Online Could Take Years to Arrive After the Game’s Launch
When GTA 6 arrives, players will initially get its single-player experience. Rockstar has also confirmed that there will not be additional purchases at launch beyond the premium editions of the game.
This means players should not expect a new GTA Online experience alongside the main game on day one. Rockstar has remained quiet about when the online component could arrive.
The lack of information has led to plenty of speculation among fans.
items.author: Onsa Mustafa
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Fans are getting closer to the launch of Grand Theft Auto (GTA) 6, but those waiting for the next version of GTA Online may have to be much more patient.
Rockstar Games is scheduled to launch GTA 6 on November 19, 2026. The game has already faced delays, but recent updates suggest that development is moving forward as planned. However, Rockstar has not provided a release date for the online multiplayer experience.
Delayed Again? GTA 6 Online Could Take Years to Arrive After the Game’s Launch
When GTA 6 arrives, players will initially get its single-player experience. Rockstar has also confirmed that there will not be additional purchases at launch beyond the premium editions of the game.
This means players should not expect a new GTA Online experience alongside the main game on day one. Rockstar has remained quiet about when the online component could arrive.
The lack of information has led to plenty of speculation among fans. According to reports, Rockstar currently has little reason to rush the launch of a new GTA Online platform.
GTA Online is Still Making Money
The current GTA Online remains extremely successful years after its original release. Rockstar continues to earn significant revenue from the game through its virtual currency and Shark Card purchases.
Because of this success, Rockstar may not want to immediately replace the existing online experience with a new version. Launching a completely new online world would also require significant development and testing.
Rockstar could instead take its time to build the next generation of GTA Online while continuing to support the current version.
PC Pelease Could Also Play A Role
Another factor is the number of platforms available at launch. GTA 6 is initially coming to PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. A PC version is expected eventually, but it is not part of the initial release.
Rockstar may prefer to wait until the game reaches more platforms before launching its new online world. This could help the company bring more players into the new multiplayer experience from the beginning.
See Also: Rockstar Confirms No Microtransactions or Generative AI in GTA 6
GTA 6 Online May Be Years Away
Rockstar has not officially confirmed that GTA 6 Online will take years to launch. However, the company’s silence and the continued success of the existing GTA Online suggest that there may be no need to rush.
The studio could spend additional time testing its new online features, fixing bugs, and preparing a larger multiplayer world. Rockstar and publisher Take-Two Interactive have already seen how successful GTA Online can become, so expectations for its successor will be extremely high.
For now, players should focus on the November 19 launch of GTA 6. The single-player game is arriving first, while the next generation of GTA Online could remain a long-term project. If Rockstar chooses to take its time, fans may have to wait considerably longer before entering its new online world.

items.author: Onsa Mustafa
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Xiaomi has officially introduced the Xiaomi 18 Fold, its first wide-format foldable smartphone. The new device combines a large folding display with Xiaomi’s own Xring O3 chipset, a 6,000mAh battery, and a powerful 200MP main camera. It is one of the company’s most awaited smartphones. One question is in everyone mind is whether the Xiaomi 18 Fold will be available in Pakistan or not. Before answering the question, let’s first check the key specs of the phone.
Xiaomi 18 Fold with Xring O3 Chip is Now Official – Will it be Available in Pakistan?
The Xiaomi 18 Fold uses a wide design that gives it a different look from traditional book-style foldable phones. It is available in several colors, including a striking cherry red option. Xiaomi has also introduced a ceramic special edition for buyers looking for a more premium finish.
Large 120Hz displays
The phone features a 7.58-inch internal display with a resolution of 2364 x 1672 pixels. On the outside, there is a 5.38-inch cover screen with a resolution of 1168 x 1712 pixels.
Both displays support a 120Hz refresh rate and can reach up to 4,000 nits of peak brightness. The cover screen is protected by Xiaomi’s Shield Glass 3.0, adding extra durability to the outer display.
Powered by Xiaomi’s Xring O3
One of the biggest highlights of the Xiaomi 18 Fold is its Xring O3 system-on-chip. The chipset is Xiaomi’s own development and is paired with up to 16GB of RAM and 1TB of storage.
The base configuration comes with 12GB of RAM and 256GB of storage, while other versions offer 12GB or 16GB of RAM with up to 1TB of storage. The 16GB models use faster LPDDR6 memory, while the 12GB versions use LPDDR5X RAM.
200MP Main Camera
Xiaomi has equipped the 18 Fold with a 200MP primary camera. It uses Samsung’s ISOCELL HP5 sensor with a 1/1.56-inch sensor size.
The main camera is joined by a 50MP periscope telephoto camera. It offers 3.5x optical zoom and can provide up to 7x in-sensor lossless zoom. There is also a 50MP ultrawide camera on the back.
For selfies and video calls, the phone has a 16MP camera on both the inner and outer displays.
Large Battery with Fast Charging
The Xiaomi 18 Fold packs a 6,000mAh battery with 20% silicon content. It supports up to 67W wired charging and 50W wireless charging.
The device runs HyperOS 4 based on Android 17. Other features include a side-mounted fingerprint scanner built into the power button and stereo speakers with Dolby Atmos support.
Slim Design and Pricing
Despite its large battery and foldable construction, the Xiaomi 18 Fold weighs 219 grams. When folded, it measures 117.8 x 83.6 x 10.68mm. Once unfolded, it is 117.8 x 163.8 x 5.02mm.
The phone comes in black, cherry red, Warm Gold, and a ceramic special edition.
Pricing starts at CNY 10,999, or around $1,638, for the 12GB/256GB model. The 12GB/512GB version costs CNY 11,999, while the 16GB/512GB model is priced at CNY 12,999. The top 16GB/1TB model costs CNY 14,999. The ceramic special edition with 16GB RAM and 1TB storage costs CNY 15,999.
For now, Xiaomi has confirmed that the 18 Fold will remain exclusive to China. The company does not plan to launch the foldable in international markets. Unfortunately, it will not be available in Pakistan.

items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
The Ministry of Information Technology and Telecommunication (MoITT) is seeking a senior telecom policy and strategy consultant to oversee key digital connectivity and fibreisation reforms under the World Bank-assisted Digital Economy Enhancement Project (DEEP).
The consultant will play a central role in supervising the development of a Single Window Right of Way (RoW) Portal and the National Fiberization Policy and Operational Plan, besides advising the government on telecom taxation, affordability, infrastructure resilience and Pakistan’s positioning as a regional digital connectivity hub.
According to the terms of reference, DEEP is aimed at enhancing the government’s capacity to deliver digitally enabled public services to citizens and businesses. The project also supports digital public infrastructure, including responsible data exchange, digital authentication, verifiable credentials and digitisation of public services.
MoITT is the sponsoring agency, with execution support from the Board of Investment, National Database and Registration Authority, National IT Board and Ignite – National Technology Fund. The ministry is also implementing the National Fiberization Policy and Plan to expand fixed broadband access, increase tower fibreisation and strengthen nationwide digital connectivity.
The proposed consultant will provide technical oversight to a firm separately engaged by MoITT under DEEP for the RoW portal and National Fiberization Policy and Plan.
A key responsibility will be to facilitate the development and commissioning of an online Single Window RoW Portal, aimed at streamlining the process for obtaining no-objection certificates (NOCs) for telecom infrastructure. The system will integrate RoW agencies, re-engineer business processes, enable online NOC issuance and, where applicable, facilitate secure online payment of fees.
The portal will also include complaint and case management mechanisms, interactive dashboards and real-time information on applications, approvals, payments and complaints.
The consultant will supervise a gap assessment, including GIS mapping, and ensure that major RoW owners are brought onto the platform.
Another major assignment will involve overseeing the preparation of a comprehensive National Fiberization Policy and Operational Plan, including an actionable roadmap, milestones, resource allocation and feasibility workstreams.
The policy is expected to examine regulatory, technical and financial aspects of fibre-optic infrastructure development, benchmark Pakistan against peer countries and identify investment opportunities and challenges.
The consultant will also advise the government on measures to improve telecom affordability and generate demand, from both operator and consumer perspectives. In addition, the assignment includes an analytical review of the telecom taxation regime and proposals for policy, regulatory and fiscal reforms aimed at reducing service costs, improving ease of doing business and promoting sector growth.
The consultant will further support international cooperation with governments, development partners, international financial institutions and industry stakeholders, including knowledge exchange, technical cooperation and benchmarking against international best practices.
The assignment also carries a strategic objective of strengthening Pakistan’s telecommunications infrastructure resilience and helping position the country as a regional digital connectivity hub, while supporting data sovereignty, Data Embassies and cross-border digital connectivity initiatives.
The consultant will be required to have at least 16 years of education in electrical, computer, electronics, telecom, IT or a relevant field and 18 years of professional experience, preferably in telecom, ICT or the digital sector.
The position is based in Islamabad and the consultant will report to the Programme Director, Project Management Unit, through MoITT’s Telecom Wing.
The consultant will be appointed on a contract basis until July 31, 2028, with procurement to be conducted under the World Bank’s applicable regulations for selection of individual consultants.

items.author: Palak Sharma
items.content:
B2B pharma distribution startup Fundly.ai has raised $4 Mn (about ₹38 Cr) in a pre-Series A funding round co-led by existing investor Accel and Multiply.
Former RBL Bank executive director Rajeev Ahuja and a group of undisclosed angel investors also participated in the round.
Separately, the startup secured $900K in venture debt from Alteria Capital. With the latest infusion, Fundly.ai’s total funding has crossed $7 Mn.
The Mumbai-based startup plans to deepen its presence in its existing markets before entering new cities. It will also expand its transaction and SaaS infrastructure beyond its ongoing Pune pilot and bring more distributors onto the platform.
Fundly.ai is building payment and settlement infrastructure that integrates with distributors’ ERP systems and manages payment cycles. Its Pune pilot covers about 3,000 retailers and multiple distributors.
The startup also plans to introduce programmes for pharmaceutical companies, enabling manufacturers to derive distribution-level insights from the commerce and transaction data generated through its network.
Further, Fundly.ai intends to build an intelligence layer over this data to improve demand forecasting and credit underwriting.
“India’s medicine distribution runs on WhatsApp, phone calls and paper ledgers. It works, but nothing connects. We’re building the coordination layer that sits underneath it, where ordering, payments and credit finally talk to each other,” Fundly.ai founder and CEO Amit Chawla said.
Founded in 2021 by Chawla and Shreeram Ramanathan, Fundly.ai began as a lender to businesses operating in the pharmaceutical supply chain. It has since expanded into a broader B2B distribution platform spanning commerce, transaction infrastructure, and embedded lending.
Its B2B ecommerce platform, FundlyMart, allows retailers and distributors to discover and order medicines, with credit embedded directly into the checkout process.
Fundly.ai said its lending decisions are based on commerce and payment data generated through the platform instead of relying only on borrowers’ conventional financial statements.
The startup claims to have served more than 4,100 retailers across over 24 cities and more than 600 pin codes. It plans to increase retailer and distributor density in its existing markets to improve the economics of its network before expanding geographically.
Prior to this round, Fundly.ai raised $3 Mn in seed funding led by Accel India in 2023.
India’s pharmaceutical distribution and logistics market is valued at $19.35 Bn in 2026 and is projected to reach $25.35 Bn by 2031, growing at a CAGR of 5.55%. Despite its scale, much of the trade still runs through old systems, with retailers and distributors relying on phone calls, WhatsApp and traditional ledgers for ordering, payments and credit.
The fragmented nature of the supply chain has created opportunities for startups attempting to digitise different parts of pharmaceutical distribution. SwishX, for instance, is using AI to automate back-office sales and distribution workflows for pharma companies, including contracts, tenders and sales operations.
At the retail end, Zeelab is building an affordable pharmacy network by reducing costs across the supply chain. It has expanded its offline store network while building its online business and is targeting ₹200 Cr in revenue in FY27.
Meanwhile, healthcare supply chain startup DocPharma recently raised $2 Mn to expand its distribution network and dark-store infrastructure.

items.title: The Ground Reality For The Gig Workers Powering India’s Instant Help Boom
items.summary:
It’s festive season again and in Bengaluru’s upscale neighbourhoods, the sight of women in colourful uniforms — black, purple, pink or green — is becoming too commonplace to ignore. Most of these women, gig workers for the likes of Urban Company, Snabbit or Pronto, are stationed just outside the gates of the large community that they visit routinely.
Many of them spend hours waiting for the next order or a ride back home. In inclement weather, there’s no shelter or cover. Some sit on the back of a parked motorbike or perch themselves at a bus stop if there’s one nearby. Many often mill at roadside tea stalls, if they find a safe space.
That last part is key. A few have taken to the steps of a nearby temple, phone in hand, scrolling, waiting for the next booking to land so that they are finally able to earn their dues of the day.

items.author: Bismah Malik
items.content:
It’s festive season again and in Bengaluru’s upscale neighbourhoods, the sight of women in colourful uniforms — black, purple, pink or green — is becoming too commonplace to ignore. Most of these women, gig workers for the likes of Urban Company, Snabbit or Pronto, are stationed just outside the gates of the large community that they visit routinely.
Many of them spend hours waiting for the next order or a ride back home. In inclement weather, there’s no shelter or cover. Some sit on the back of a parked motorbike or perch themselves at a bus stop if there’s one nearby. Many often mill at roadside tea stalls, if they find a safe space.
That last part is key. A few have taken to the steps of a nearby temple, phone in hand, scrolling, waiting for the next booking to land so that they are finally able to earn their dues of the day.
“Typically, the waiting can stretch for hours and even though we are out of our homes for a living, we don’t earn anything unless an order is placed. When someone books the service it is assigned to the nearest professional or the one who can reach you within 10 minutes,” said Jhanki Devi (name changed on request) who works with Urban Company’s InstaHelp vertical.
On a good day, she completes 4-5 hours of household work within a single gated community but on most days, this is not enough to meet her app commitments. She then has to continue being logged in to go to the home where the next order comes from. Gig workers along the way keep the chain going, because if she can’t find the right bus, she has to book an auto or a bike taxi using Namma Yatri, Uber or Rapido.
While the scene of gig workers outside prominent gated communities has become ubiquitous in dense residential neighbourhoods in Bengaluru, Mumbai and Delhi NCR, not much focus has landed on the plight of the gig workers fuelling this boom. With another festive season upon us, it’s pertinent to see where things are headed.
Because just under a year ago, Inc42 wrote about the festive season rush that created the instant help category. Now the rush in 2026 is taking Snabbit, Urban Company and Pronto to expand, grow more profitable and extract more from its gig worker base.
In Diwali 2025, when the category was still finding its feet, the focus was on bringing in more workers. Now this Diwali, the category doesn’t need a festive season to prove itself; the focus is on maximisation.
Order volumes touched record highs in August, weeks before the festive season began.
A nearly 6x rise in consolidated order volumes has been seen since October 2025, i.e. from 8 Lakh monthly bookings to more than 50 Lakh bookings in July 2026.
The upcoming festive season will further lead to a spike in bookings and the need for the overall industry to meet the demand, but it’s not just about adding more workers, there’s also some focus on maximising revenue. And in this churn, gig workers are getting squeezed even further..
A New Growth Era For Instant Help
Speaking to Inc42, Bengaluru-based Pronto’s spokesperson said the company’s professionals served more than 1.5 Mn bookings in August alone across 10 cities — up from 1.25 Mn, 950,000 and roughly 837,000 in the three months before that.
One year ago, Pronto had operations in two cities and about 20 micromarkets, serving a few thousand bookings a day. But this 5x growth in terms of city presence was expensive.
Pronto closed its Series B funding round at $45 Mn (₹425.3 Cr) in May 2026, led by Physical Intelligence founder Lachy Groom. The startup raised the round at a valuation of $200 Mn (₹1,890 Cr), double compared to $100 Mn at which it reportedly raised funds just a few months prior in March 2026.
Similarly, Snabbit raised $56 Mn (about ₹527 Cr) in its Series D round co-led by Susquehanna Venture Capital, Mirae Asset Venture Investments and Bertelsmann India Investments. These big deals have fuelled the latest round of growth, but will this growth last or will these startups turn profitable?
Even Urban Company, which has well over a decade of operational experience in home services, has not managed to turn profitable when it comes to instant services.
All three platforms are still in the red, competing on discounts to hold onto share, and all three depend on the same scarce resource to keep it going:women willing to do this work, at the pay and on the terms currently on offer.
Founders and investors believe the boom isn’t because of discounts alone or funding-fuelled customer acquisition, but in fact is possible due to a consistent supply of gig workers. This in turn allows companies to expand into new cities without spending too heavily.
So, a year on since the advent of instant help services, it’s pertinent to see how satisfied the workers are when it comes to earnings, social security benefits and working conditions.
Inc42 has sent a detailed questionnaire to Snabbit and Urban Company on the payment structures, leave policies and other welfare initiatives for its partners. We will update the story as and when these companies respond, but based on our interviews with workers and some insiders in the companies, here’s where things stand.
Urban Company’s Tier-Based Payouts
When Insta Help launched in March 2025, the pitch to workers was straightforward: a promised, largely assured monthly income for showing up.
Urban Company assured a minimum of ₹20,000 per month, contingent on a worker logging 132 hours in that month.
That’s not how it works today.
Partners are now grouped into tiers described to us as diamond, gold and silver, based on customer ratings and the number of hours logged on the app.
“I working as a diamond tier professional, hence some of the benefits like access to more orders, salary cuts if we take more leaves than sanction within 15 days or a month period and earnings are better than those who are in the other tiers,” one professional, working in a North Bengaluru locality, said.
She said that the volume of orders for any worker is tied to ratings within that tier and this can translate into better pay if the worker consistently gets high ratings .
Meanwhile, Urban Company’s claims of assured salary were disputed by a majority of the workers who told us that the company follows the broader industry wage structure now. This means tying payments to logged-in hours and customer ratings.
Notably, InstaHelp currently advertises an assured income of ₹20,000–25,000 a month at an hourly rate of ₹150–180, with the company’s own claim that its top 5% of workers earn more than ₹50,000 a month.
Inc42 could not independently verify whether any workers in Bengaluru earn that high an amount every month.
Meanwhile, an independent survey of workers from March 2026 put InstaHelp’s average monthly pay at roughly ₹21,000 for an eight-hour day.
This is in the same range the company cites — and separately the survey found that a worker who logs out mid-shift for an emergency can be docked a full day’s pay, not just for the hours missed.
The payout, according to the UC InstaHelp workers we spoke to, comes every 15 days or every 30 days, depending on the tier. Plus. earnings are strictly tied to being logged in 6 to 8 hours each day of the month. The company permits workers only two days of paid leaves a month, and these days are not accounted for when payouts are calculated.
Inside A 12-Hour Snabbit Day
Snabbit is not publicly listed and as such the company is not obligated to disclose how many workers it currently engages for instant help services.
The company’s public numbers have stayed in a fairly narrow band over the past year, even as its order volumes multiplied more than tenfold.
After its Series B round in May 2025, Snabbit said workers on a 12-hour shift earned “upward of ₹40,000” a month, with four hours a day translating to just over ₹10,000. By its Series C round that October, the figure being quoted had shifted to a ₹25,000–30,000 every month.
However, this pay was still hour-linked, and most certainly not fixed.
Snabbit’s annual revenue rate is said to have been around $11 Mn at its peak in 2025 (FY26) and as per media reports, it’s currently on track to achieve close to $40 Mn in revenue by the end of the ongoing FY27 fiscal year.
But Snabbit has not disclosed its audited financials for the past fiscal year (FY26) and without this, it’s hard to verify these numbers.
Earlier this year, Snabbit’s CEO Aayush Agarwal claimed that time spent on the app has increased by 50%, and the company is said to have displaced Urban Company in terms of monthly order volume with 1.5 Mn orders in the month of June 2026
Snabbit has onboarded more than 15,000 workers just this year, according to numbers reviewed by Inc42.
But the pay structure, according to four Snabbit workers we spoke to, has remained unchanged since last year.
Social media posts have alleged that Snabbit workers lose an average of ₹1000 for every day of missed work. This repeatedly came up during our conversations with workers, but Agarwal had denied that any such policy exists in previous statements.
Is Pronto Any Different Than The Others?
The youngest company of the trio told Inc42 that its professionals earn a fixed component every month, which is linked to the hours they work and a variable component tied to completed bookings, with a 12-hour day resulting in an average ₹1,000 payout for workers.
“There is no promised fixed minimum monthly salary. Earnings depend on the availability and how much work a professional takes on,” the company said in an emailed statement to Inc42.
The worker-side app breaks down each day’s earnings and any deductions in real time.
Separately, Pronto’s own in-app pricing has been reported to be as low as ₹1 an hour for first-time bookings and around ₹50 an hour for utensil-cleaning bookings. This pricing floor raises its own questions about how this claimed fixed-plus-variable structure would hold up, when the customer-side pricing is so aggressive.
Pronto is one of the most aggressive when it comes to discounts in the space. Its discounts are primarily funded from the company’s balance sheet, not impacting the worker wage structures, the company claimed.
But again, this is not a company that has disclosed its financials in the past fiscal year i.e FY26. These claims will only be tested and the company’s confidence in its business model can only be justified when the numbers are out in the open.
The Unpaid Hours In Between
Beyond work hours, what becomes even more challenging for a worker on the field is the waiting time between jobs. This part of the job is not paid.
Pronto founder and CEO Anjali Sardana had earlier stated that the waiting period roughly constitutes 13-20% of the working day on average.
But our conversations with instant help workers revealed going to and fro bookings is largely left to the worker themselves. Most rely on public transport, or simply walk, because the cost of an auto ride might be too high.
Pronto, responding to our questions, said the vast majority of its workers get to their next job on foot, with a smaller share covered on Yulu bikes that the company provides in certain localities. Workers are urged to wait close to the neighbourhoods where they get bookings from, which the company says, helps reduce travel time.
Yulu CEO Amit Gupta told Inc42 earlier that the company has partnered with instant help apps in some areas and he expects the demand to increase because workers can afford the daily rental cost of ₹200 for bikes.
Another issue plaguing gig workers currently is unavailability of waiting spots or restrooms in high demand areas, where usually access to facilities is not available.
“We use public washrooms, wherever possible. It is a hindrance because we cannot directly ask just any customer to allow us access to their washrooms,” 28-year-old Anisa (name changed), who works with Pronto in Bengaluru, told us
Waiting outside large gated societies is not always safe and some workers have complained about safety and security risks too.
Pronto had reportedly started setting up local waiting centres or hubs in some areas of Bengaluru, however it is not clear whether these facilities are adequately distributed or have the amenities that gig workers might need.
On the safety side, each of the platforms claim to have introduced some sort of feature within the app for workers to reach out when in distress.
However, when we asked how many such SOS complaints or queries have been fielded by these companies in the past year, we did not get a specific answer from either Pronto, Urban Company or Snabbit.
Shaik Salauddin, the national general secretary of the Indian Federation Of App Based Transport Workers (IFAT) which also looks at the welfare of other gig workers, told us that the union has received complaints from women workers related to harassment, including alleged sexual harassment by customers. The pressure of poor ratings, complaints or account suspension can force women workers to tolerate unacceptable behaviour, he added.
“The algorithmic allocation of orders, that could also lead to pressure on women workers to accept jobs even when a location or customers feel unsafe has also been reported to us,” Salauddin added.
New Festive Season, Same Old Math
Now with another peak demand season here, instant help apps are expecting major growth numbers this year. They are working on top of a bigger base as compared to 2025, catering to millions of customers who had never heard of the app one year ago.
But for the all-women workforce of these instant help apps, working conditions are yet to change for the better and for others, the situation is getting worse.
The real question is whether the companies will invest in infrastructure and higher incentives for workers when they see the outcome after this boom.
While platforms have invested heavily in the consumer side of the business by waging a discounts war, the companies cannot retain the workers under existing conditions and that is probably why even the instant help segment has worker supply and retention problems.
Jhanki Devi, who was quoted earlier in the story, said candidly that the instant help industry which is entirely driven by women workers is yet to realise the challenges that women face while going about their daily work and responsibilities. She brought it back to one simple thing: menstruation leave. “In physically demanding jobs like this, we aren’t even entitled to one day of period leave. And that should tell you why many of us cannot see ourselves doing this kind of gig work for long.”
For instant help platforms like Snabbit, Urban Company and Pronto who often pat themselves on the back for providing a platform for unemployed women, fixing these arcane practices should be the biggest priority this festive season.
[Edited By Nikhil Subramiam]

items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
The Ministry of Information Technology and Telecommunication has prepared a new draft of the Pakistan Telecommunication (Reorganization) Amendment Bill after the government withdrew the previous version amid controversy over private property and right-of-way provisions.
According to sources, the revised bill has been drafted in light of recommendations made by a committee constituted by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif to review the disputed clauses.
The new version is expected to be presented during the next session of the National Assembly, while the government is also likely to consult coalition partners before formally introducing the legislation.
The development follows the withdrawal of the earlier Pakistan Telecommunication (Reorganization) Amendment Bill, 2026, from the Senate on August 28, 2026. The government had announced at the time that it would bring a revised bill after addressing concerns raised over the original draft.
Revised Bill Addresses Right-of-Way and Property Concerns
The previous legislation had drawn criticism over provisions related to private property and telecom right-of-way arrangements.
The National Assembly had passed the bill on June 11, 2026, after which it was introduced in the Senate. On June 15, the upper house referred the legislation to its standing committee for further review.
The standing committee subsequently raised concerns over clauses dealing with private property, while criticism of the proposed amendments also emerged on social media.
Following the controversy, the prime minister constituted a committee headed by Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar to review the disputed provisions and suggest improvements.
According to sources, the committee recommended changes aimed at strengthening protections for private property and revising the framework governing right of way for telecom infrastructure. The latest draft has now been prepared on the basis of those recommendations.
The government withdrew the earlier bill before the completion of its 90-day constitutional period in the Senate.
Under the legislative process, once the specified period expires, the matter can proceed to a joint sitting of Parliament. As no joint session was scheduled at the time, the government opted to withdraw the controversial version and prepare a fresh draft instead.
The revised bill is now expected to return to the National Assembly after consultations with coalition partners are completed.

items.author: Shrishti Bisht
items.content:
Watertech startup DigitalPaani has raised ₹22 Cr (about $2.3 Mn) in a funding round led by Navam Capital. Enzia Ventures, Chakra Growth Capital, 3one4 Capital, Momentum Capital, Achieving Women Entrepreneurs Early Growth Fund, and Echo River Capital also participated in the round.
The startup did not disclose the funding round’s stage or its valuation.
DigitalPaani plans to use the fresh capital to expand across industrial and municipal markets, scale its operations to serve more institutional customers, and enter international markets. It will also deploy part of the proceeds to strengthen its core operations.
Founded in 2020 by father-daughter duo Mansi Jain and Rajesh Jain, the Delhi NCR-based startup operates an AI- and IoT-powered software platform that helps businesses, utilities, and municipalities manage water and wastewater infrastructure.
The platform collects real-time data from water assets and compares their performance with their designed operating parameters. It then identifies the causes of operational inefficiencies and helps automate processes such as equipment management, maintenance, inventory tracking, and coordination among service teams.
DigitalPaani’s technology is used by sewage treatment plants and other water facilities to increase wastewater recycling, reduce operational losses, and prevent avoidable breakdowns. Its platform also offers real-time water tracking, predictive maintenance, and workflow management.
The startup claimed that 75% of critical water assets in India, including sewage treatment plants, operate at severely reduced capacity because of operational challenges rather than equipment failures.
DigitalPaani currently serves more than 95 facilities across India, which collectively treat over 150 Mn litres of water every day. Its customers include Britannia, Leela Hotels, Tata Group, and Delhi Jal Board.
It claimed its deployments have helped make non-compliant plants fully operational while reducing costs by 25%. DigitalPaani added that its revenue has grown nearly sixfold over the past two years, without disclosing the figures.
The startup was also recently recognised by UpLink, the World Economic Forum’s innovation platform, for its water management technology.
The fundraise comes as water shortages, tighter environmental regulations, and a growing emphasis on reuse increase demand for wastewater treatment and recycling infrastructure from Indian cities and industries.
India’s wastewater treatment market was valued at $10.4 Bn in 2025 and is projected to reach $19.4 Bn by 2034, growing at a compound annual rate of 7% between 2026 and 2034, according to IMARC Group.

items.title: How Can D2C Founders Scale Business Without Losing Control?
items.summary:

items.author: Inc42 BrandLabs
items.content:
When a D2C brand is small, it is relatively easy to know what is working for it. A founder can see which products are selling, which customers are returning and where the money is being spent. But as the business grows, that visibility can start to fade.
This leaves D2C founders with a deceptively simple question: as the business gets bigger, how do you know what is actually working?
The question becomes harder to answer as brands expand across marketplaces, quick commerce, offline retail and their own channels. Each route to market brings a different set of customers, costs and operating challenges, making it increasingly important for founders to understand what is driving growth, and what is quietly eating into it.
Against this backdrop, Inc42, in collaboration with PhonePe Payment Gateway, hosted a closed-door roundtable during the D2C & Retail Summit 2026 on D2C Brands’ Roadmap To Scaling Without Losing Control.
The discussion brought together founders and senior leaders from across India’s consumer ecosystem to examine the changes that occur as D2C businesses scale.
Moderated by Puneet Gupta, partner, deals – transaction services, PwC India, the discussion explored how brands can identify what is driving growth, where margins are being lost through inventory, dead stock and returns, and how founders can maintain visibility as business operations become more complex.
Here is the lineup of speakers who participated in the discussion:
Akash Agarwal, VP & head of international business, Noise
Alok Paul, COO, Littlebox
Anuj Nevatia, cofounder, Bacca Bucci
Harshit Vij, founder & CEO, FREECULTR
Prateek Bhagchandka, founder & CEO, M.O.M Meal of the Moment
Prateek Kedia, founder, Wise Life
Shreyansh Jain, founder, Nutrabay
Syed Shamoail Haque, founder, Barosi
When Growth Starts Hiding Inventory And Margin Leakages
As D2C brands grow, a growing top line can make it harder to see where the business is actually losing money. A product may sell well overall, but certain sizes could remain unsold, and returns quietly erode margins.
Looking only at sales as a metric can therefore give founders an incomplete picture of how healthy the business really is.
According to Anuj Nevatia of Bacca Bucci, a product can look healthy overall even when some SKUs become dead stock. With more than 3,500 SKUs, Bacca Bucci tracks contribution margins and inventory at the SKU level and monitors ageing, with stock held beyond 90 days requiring attention.
Littlebox’s Alok Paul looks at inventory differently. The brand maintains finished goods inventory of 17-20 days and forecasts 15 days ahead. When inventory rises and products stop moving, the brand has to use discounts to clear the stock.
Akash Agarwal of Noise highlights another challenge: returns. With relatively lower gross margins in electronics, returns can have a disproportionate impact on profitability. Therefore, Noise tracks where customers drop off across the purchase journey and looks closely at returns and other leakages.
Taken together, these examples point to the same problem: sales alone cannot tell a founder whether growth is working. The answer often lies deeper in the business, at the SKU, inventory, return, and contribution-margin levels.
But product-level economics is only one part of the equation. As brands expand across channels, they also need to understand whether each channel can deliver sustainable growth.
Channel Expansion Can Put Pressure On Profitability
As D2C brands expand beyond their own websites, maintaining profitability becomes more complicated. Each channel comes with its own pricing, discounting, customer behaviour and unit economics. A product that works well on D2C may not necessarily be profitable on a marketplace or quick commerce platform.
Jain of Nutrabay noted that brands need to evaluate “category-channel fit” rather than assuming that product-market fit on D2C will translate across channels.
As brands add marketplaces, quick commerce, modern trade and offline stores, channel teams may also push for different product mixes, making it important to align channel requirements with the broader brand strategy.
Barosi’s Syed Shamoail Haque approaches this equation from the customer’s side. Barosi uses trial subscriptions to reduce the friction of getting customers to try its products and tracks two points in the customer lifecycle, 30 and 90 days, to understand feedback and retention. Haque said the data showed that customers who stayed for 90 days were likely to remain with the brand for much longer.
Together, these factors make channel selection as much a profitability decision as a growth decision. Instead of expanding everywhere at once, brands need to assess whether each channel can support the right assortment and pricing.
They also need to consider how much it costs to acquire and retain customers before committing significant marketing capital. This is particularly important as even channels that already work for a brand become increasingly expensive to scale. Managing that complexity then becomes a challenge in its own right.
Building Systems That Keep Growth In Check
As D2C businesses expand, the founder’s role inevitably changes. In the early stages, it is possible to stay close to everything from pricing and inventory to dispatch and customer experience. But as teams, products, and channels multiply, maintaining the same level of direct oversight becomes difficult.
Harshit Vij of FREECULTR sees this as a natural part of scaling.
“Maybe when you start, the founder has visibility on everything. As you scale, you build systems, you build control measures, and you hire high-calibre people,” he said.
Therefore, the shift is not about keeping every decision with the founder. It is about building enough structure so the founder knows what is happening, even when decisions are distributed across teams and functions.
Jain emphasises keeping processes in step with growth. “At Nutrabay, this includes building a product-classification framework that groups SKUs based on factors such as revenue, gross margin and potential, with decisions then made according to where each product sits within the framework.”
The need for stronger systems becomes even more apparent when brands enter new channels. Bhagchandka of M.O.M Meal of the Moment described how operating across airlines, railways, general trade, modern trade, ecommerce and quick commerce requires businesses to adapt to very different operating environments.
What works in one channel cannot simply be replicated in another, making execution capabilities increasingly important as the business expands.
Ultimately, losing control at scale does not mean a founder has stopped knowing every detail. It can also mean that the systems that once gave founders visibility are no longer enough as the business becomes more complex.
For brands, the goal is not necessarily more oversight, but enough systems, people and processes to make the right information available when it matters.
The roundtable, organised by Inc42 in collaboration with PhonePe Payment Gateway, came back to a key question for D2C founders: how do you know what is actually working as the business grows? The answer is to have clear visibility into your products, channels, customers and operations.
The post How Can D2C Founders Scale Business Without Losing Control? appeared first on Inc42 Media.

items.author: Staff
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Finding the ideal balance between physical ergonomics and advanced processing power remains an ongoing challenge in the smartphone industry. Many devices either bulk up to accommodate larger batteries or adopt harsh geometric shapes that hinder long-term comfort. The vivo V80 Lite enters the market with a distinct objective: providing a refined, highly capable handset for active professionals and content creators. Integrating the vivo V80 Lite into our daily routines over the past few weeks has provided ample opportunity for a comprehensive, real-world assessment of its hardware and software. Through rigorous testing of its unique curved architecture and processing capabilities, it becomes evident that vivo has engineered a competitive device. By emphasizing a comfortable form factor alongside rapid operational speeds and consistent imaging, the V80 Lite offers a practical balance for daily use.
Design and In-Hand Comfort
Because mobile devices are handheld for hours each day, physical ergonomics play a critical role in overall user satisfaction. The V80 Lite stands out immediately in this category, capturing attention through its construction. Guided by the “Slay Every Edge” design language, vivo has actively steered away from the sharp, flattened borders that characterize many contemporary handsets.
Turning to the back, the V80 Lite showcases the Skyline Camera Design, a horizontally aligned module inspired by the outstretched wings of a bird. In practical use, its symmetrical arrangement helps keep fingers away from the camera lenses when the phone is held in landscape orientation for media viewing or gaming.
The foundation of this structural approach is the Easy-Grip Curved Display. Measuring 6.83 inches this 3D dual-curved screen achieves a 93.82% screen-to-body ratio. During extended usage, such as reviewing corporate documents during a morning commute or browsing digital content in the evening, the contoured glass significantly minimizes hand strain. The smartphone’s edges transition smoothly into the back panel, bypassing the rigid pressure points inherent to flat-sided alternatives. Gripping the handset firmly does not trigger unwanted screen interactions.
Smoothness and Everyday Performance
vivo has equipped this model with highly capable silicon. Driven by the 4nm MediaTek Dimensity 7360-Turbo chipset, the V80 Lite registered an AnTuTu benchmark score exceeding 970,000ii during our independent testing. This processing power translates into consistent responsiveness for complex multitasking.
Featuring four high-performance Cortex-A78 cores paired with four energy-efficient Cortex-A55 cores, the device manages professional workloads with ease. Toggling rapidly between video conferencing software, heavy spreadsheet applications, and cloud storage drives happens without delay. Aided by Extended RAM technology, the V80 Lite demonstrates excellent memory management, consistently keeping upwards of 25 applications active simultaneously without forcing them to reload. Once professional tasks are completed, the chipset proves also capable at handling entertainment. We observed a stable 90 FPS while running popular MOBA titles, and the handset remained comfortably cool thanks to an integrated 3800mm² vapor chamber cooling system.
1.5K AMOLED Display Experience
High-tier processing requires an equally capable visual interface, and the V80 Lite delivers with its 1.5K Ultra Clear AMOLED Display. Boasting a crisp 449 PPI pixel density and a fluid refresh rate up to 120 Hz, the screen ensures animations and text scrolling are smooth. Outdoor visibility is strong; the panel utilizes a 2000 nits High Brightness Mode (HBM) and can reach 3000 nits local peak brightness, cutting through harsh afternoon glare to keep text fully legible. The display renders multimedia with accurate color accuracy and deep contrast ratios, creating a highly immersive viewing environment.
Real-World Battery Endurance
Battery longevity remains a paramount concern for intensive users, and the V80 Lite addresses this directly with its 7050 mAh All-Day Battery. To measure its limits, we ran a demanding, simulated daily routine. After 10 continuous hours of heavy utilization, encompassing GPS navigation, WhatsApp video calling, 4K video recording, music streaming, and over four hours of dedicated gaming and social media browsing, the battery indicator still displayed a comfortable 30% charge remaining. Under more typical usage conditions, this capacity easily stretches across multiple days, providing additional flexibility.
Imaging Experience
32 MP Group Selfie Camera Test
Reliable front-facing optics are essential for both digital communication and social sharing. The V80 Lite tackles standard framing constraints by incorporating a specialized 32 MP Group Selfie Camera. Featuring an 84° ultra-wide field of view, the lens effortlessly fits large gatherings of friends and expansive background scenery into the shot. The camera software effectively corrects edge distortion, maintaining natural facial proportions while accurately capturing skin tones and fine textures.
50 MP Sony Night Portrait Test
Low-light environments frequently expose the limitations of mid-range optics, yet the 50 MP Sony Clear Night Portrait system excels under these exact conditions. When photographing subjects in dimly lit restaurants or during evening outdoor events, the sensor captures a high volume of light while its algorithms reduce grain and noise. The resulting nighttime portraits are sharply defined and vibrant. Additionally, the rear camera supports 4K video recording at 30 FPS, offering clear detail for evening vlogs and cinematic clips.
Final Verdict
The vivo V80 Lite presents a well-rounded package for active professionals and digital creators. items.author: Meha Agarwal
items.content:
A pair of heels, a saree or a kurta bought for Diwali could easily be worn again at a wedding or a family function. Similarly, a skin or haircare product picked up during a festive sale may end up becoming part of the shopper’s daily routine.
But there is no guarantee that the shopper that stumbled upon new brands during the festive season sale will return to that same brand again and again.
So brands often find themselves back at day zero, fighting for attention all over again and spending money to reacquire users after the festive season bows out. This raises a simple question: how can brands retain users beyond the festive season?
Making Customers Reopen Their Wallets
Inc42’s conversations with D2C brands around this year’s festive marketing playbook point to a broader shift in how companies are thinking about growth beyond the festive season. Retention and remarketing are emerging as critical levers for brands looking to turn festive shoppers into repeat customers.
Brands need to track what the shopper bought and what they might need next. Most brands we spoke with see smart product recommendations and discovery as a key way to drive repeat purchases and build. The first step is communication and messaging.
Having scaled up to ₹270 Cr in operating revenue over the past nine years, Bengaluru-based The Bear House is now seeking a larger contribution from denim, trousers and complete outfits. The brand’s scale thus far has come from building a business weighted towards topwear or shirts.
Cofounder Harsh Somaiya said this journey to selling more jeans starts as a communication challenge.
“For example, if someone comes to us for shirts, the next conversation shouldn’t be, ‘Here is another shirt.’ It could be, ‘If you liked this, here’s how you can complete the look,’” he told Inc42.
Libas founder and CEO Sidhant Keshwani takes this one step further and added that personalisation in communication greatly improves the chances of getting the second purchase. According to him, customer segmentation is vital to enable personalisation at scale.
The brand separates customers by product interests, age, location and season, which allows the marketing team to tailor WhatsApp messages and other communication accordingly.
Escaping The Discount Trap
Personalisation allows brands to retain new customers at higher margins rather than a discount-driven play. This is also why most brands are constantly experimenting with low discount phases even during peak season.
The real test of festive retention is not whether customers buy again but whether they come back without another discount. A customer who returns only when the brand cuts prices is boosting repeat orders but doing little for profitability.
Higher purchase frequency may therefore conceal a risk in which the brand keeps surrendering margin to secure the next order.
Women’s occasion wear brand Koskii encountered that pressure while expanding online. Cofounder Umar Akhtar recalled that its stores had largely sold at full price, but last year’s online push involved more discounting than the company wanted.
“You have some brands where they launch at a 70% discount. Nobody will buy them at 50% because 70% is a standard discount,” said Akhtar.
In 2026, the startup plans to control incentives more closely and focus on sharper product pricing, rather than become associated with a permanent sale.
The risk also extends to how customers perceive the original price. Speaking to Inc42 earlier, Aukera founder Lisa Mukhedkar highlighted how large markdowns can raise doubts about pricing and quality.
This is why separating repeat demand from festive purchases requires a clear starting point. Segmentation has to cover each stage of the customer journey from registering interest to placing the first order to finally returning for another purchase. Each of these has to be treated as a different stage and requires specific processes to help grow retention.
Akhtar recalled that Koskii’s September 2025 bridal campaign attracted approximately 10,000 registrations, of which 864 participants subsequently bought. At an average order value of about ₹17,000, the campaign generated roughly ₹1.5 Cr in directly attributable revenue, with purchases continuing into August 2026.
But this success only captures prospective customers becoming buyers, not buyers returning for repeat purchases. Assessing the campaign immediately after the festive season would have missed revenue arriving later through repeat purchases, and there is the risk that some of the delayed conversions would be treated as retention and this would overstate repeat customer data and behaviour.
This is why a 90-day repeat-purchase assessment should trigger after the customer places their first order. Each category’s buying cycle can then inform how such an assessment should be interpreted.
Don’t Bet Before You Test
But simply following customers throughout this phase is not for every brand. Only brands that can afford a large campaign to stay visible through this 90-day assessment period should look to formalise such a process.
The choice entirely depends on how much capital is available to stay on the customer’s radar and how quickly the business needs evidence that its retention strategy is working.
Koskii’s Akhtar highlighted this distinction when discussing the limits of broad offline advertising. He recalled that roughly 60% of Koskii’s media budget once went towards non-digital channels, even though an overwhelming majority of customers identified online channels as a discovery source. This feedback gave the company a reason to reconsider its allocation.
That does not mean low-cost experiments will not work. They offer a different proposition.
Akhtar added that Koskii is testing pop-up shops in apartments and corporate parks to improve visibility. While these experiments are early, their appeal is partly rooted in the limited budgets required to execute this given the high visibility the brand will get in return.
The same test-before-expansion approach worked for cosmetics brand RENEE. Cofounder Ashutosh Valani recalled that a television campaign targeting selected regions and programmes last year did not deliver the expected results. But since it was a pilot, the company could reevaluate its approach after the initial response and avoided committing to a larger campaign.
A message, an ad or a reminder can bring a shopper back, but it cannot fix the reason they left your shop without buying in the first place, said Valani. Product performance, education and satisfaction are foundations of retention and RENEE’s subsequent campaigns introduced related products.
All this comes to nought if the product experience is poor. Brands can identify where that experience falls short by integrating data from various channels (online and offline) as well as customer touchpoints.
Having spent the first few years of their lifetimes trying to bring in new users, mature D2C brands are today putting more money into keeping customers beyond the temporary peak and bringing them back to their storefronts multiple times.
Shoppers are easy to win over during the festive season but retention is a tough nut. So, who’s up for the challenge?
Spotlight | Inside Japam’s Bet To Build A Modern Spiritual Accessories Brand
The spiritual tech D2C startup retails a wide range of spiritual wearables and accessories, with its portfolio centred on Rudraksha bracelets and malas, Karungali wearables, gemstone and crystal bracelets, spiritual jewellery, pendants and religious products. 
The startup operates primarily through its D2C website, while also selling through Amazon and offering bulk/wholesale orders. Positioned as everyday spiritual accessories, its over 500 SKUs range from below-₹500 bracelets to premium Rudraksha and gemstone products. Japam also sells internationally through its global storefront. 
As per Japan, its Rudraksha products are lab-tested, while select “Siddh” products are delivered with a Siddhi Prakriya Report and QR code showing the energisation ceremony.
The Deep Dive
Ecommerce Buzz
Satvacart, The Ayurveda Co Shut Down: Online grocery startup Satvacart has shut down after a 12-year run, failing to secure fresh funding or an acquisition deal. Meanwhile, D2C beauty and personal care brand The Ayurveda Co (TAC) has also shuttered down after overexpansion across channels and a cost-heavy business model derailed its operations.
PSL’s Muted Market Debut: The luxury fashion platform’s parent Purple Style Labs listed at ₹535 on the NSE, nearly 7% below its ₹575 IPO price, after its ₹680 Cr issue was subscribed just 1.29X. Its loss widened 51.5% YoY to ₹285.4 Cr in FY26 while operating revenue rose nearly 14% to ₹557.8 Cr.
D2C Funding Boom Gathers Pace: D2C brands Nua, Mokobara and Comet have raised fresh capital this week, with women’s wellness brand Nua bagging $50 Mn, travel accessories brand Mokobara ₹170 Cr and sneaker brand Comet $10.6 Mn to fuel expansion, offline growth and category bets. Meanwhile, SUGAR Cosmetics raised ₹145 Cr at an 80% valuation cut.
RentoMojo Sets IPO In Motion: The furniture and appliance rental startup has set a ₹384-₹404 price band for its ₹1,256 Cr IPO, valuing the company at around ₹4,206 Cr. Its FY26 revenue jumped 45.5% to ₹387 Cr, while profit surged 142% to ₹104 Cr, aided by a ₹36.6 Cr tax credit.
The post The 90-Day Festive Season Marketing Test appeared first on Inc42 Media.

items.author: Anne Florentyna
items.content:
Healthtech-focused VC firm W Health Ventures has closed its second fund at ₹700 Cr (about $84 Mn), sailing past its original target corpus of ₹630 Cr. A combination of family offices and institutional investors from India and the US were the limited partners (LPs) that backed the fund.
Launched in July 2025, the fund marked its first close in February at ₹550 Cr ($60.6 Mn), it targeted to back eight to ten early stage healthtech startups over the next four years, from pre-idea stage to growth stages startups in India and the US.
W Health Ventures’ managing partner Pankaj Jethwani told Inc42 that the firm looks to identify concepts at a very early age and then spends a fairly large amount of time pressure-testing these ideas.
“Once we pick the area we’re most excited about, we build a founding team around it and surround that team with resources. We have about a 50-person in-house team of technologists, entrepreneurs, and clinicians. From there, it’s a collaborative build to bring these companies to scale — we act as co-founders of the business,” he added.
Via the second fund, the firm has established two startups and has poured in capital so far. Firstly, it partnered with Narayana Health to set up Everhope Oncology, a cancer care platform and infused $10 Mn (about ₹86 Cr) in March 2025. It launched Everbright Health in the US and infused $7 Mn, along with Sanos Capital, in October 2025.
Founded in 2020 by Sunil Wadhwani and headquartered in Mumbai, W Health Ventures builds healthcare companies from pre-idea to category leader across India and the US-India corridor. The fund typically writes cheques in the range of ₹30 Cr to ₹50 Cr, and has backed 12 startups in India and the US via its first fund, including Wysa, BeatO, Mylo, Reveal, and BabyMD.
W Health’s fund close comes at a time when India’s healthtech funding market is undergoing a reset, with investors becoming more selective about digital-health business models.
The firm is also part of a broader shift among venture investors towards company creation, as funds increasingly look to participate earlier than the traditional pre-seed or seed stage.
Instead of waiting for founders to build businesses around identified opportunities, these firms are identifying problems themselves, validating the opportunity and assembling founding teams.
