items.title: University of the Punjab and Sustainadility Launch HEC Compliant Managed Remote Internship Pilot
items.summary:
The Faculty of Commerce, University of the Punjab (PU), has entered into a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Sustainadility LLC to pilot a fully managed remote internship model for its students. The MoU was signed by Prof. Dr. Hafiz Zafar Ahmad, Dean, Faculty of Commerce, University of the Punjab, and Sajjeed Aslam, Partner, Sustainadility LLC.
The collaboration responds to a set of reforms by the Higher Education Commission (HEC) that have reshaped what an undergraduate degree in Pakistan requires. HEC’s Undergraduate Education Policy 2023 first made a minimum of three credit hours of supervised internship mandatory for undergraduate degree programs, with flexibility for both on-site and remote/virtual formats. In September 2025, HEC reinforced that internship requirement and additionally made industry-relevant certifications a mandatory component of undergraduate degrees, in priority sectors including computing/IT, healthcare, construction, and finance.
That shift matters
items.author: Publishing Partner
items.content:
The Faculty of Commerce, University of the Punjab (PU), has entered into a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Sustainadility LLC to pilot a fully managed remote internship model for its students. The MoU was signed by Prof. Dr. Hafiz Zafar Ahmad, Dean, Faculty of Commerce, University of the Punjab, and Sajjeed Aslam, Partner, Sustainadility LLC.
The collaboration responds to a set of reforms by the Higher Education Commission (HEC) that have reshaped what an undergraduate degree in Pakistan requires. HEC’s Undergraduate Education Policy 2023 first made a minimum of three credit hours of supervised internship mandatory for undergraduate degree programs, with flexibility for both on-site and remote/virtual formats. In September 2025, HEC reinforced that internship requirement and additionally made industry-relevant certifications a mandatory component of undergraduate degrees, in priority sectors including computing/IT, healthcare, construction, and finance.
That shift matters most for students outside Pakistan’s largest cities. A commerce student in Jhelum or Gujranwala has historically had a smaller pool of internship opportunities than a peer in Lahore or Karachi, not for lack of ability, but for lack of address. By formally permitting remote placements, HEC turned a compliance requirement into an instrument of opportunity.
(L to R) Front: Sajjeed Aslam (Partner, Sustainadility), Prof. Dr. Hafiz Zafar Ahmad (Dean, Faculty of Commerce, University of the Punjab)
Prof. Dr. Hafiz Zafar Ahmad, Dean, Faculty of Commerce, University of the Punjab, commented: “HEC has given Pakistani universities a clear and welcome instruction: that our graduates must leave us with experience, not only with degrees. Our responsibility is to meet it with substance rather than paperwork. This pilot lets us extend supervised industry exposure to students across all four participating campuses, while the faculty retains complete authority over supervision, assessment, and credit.”
This program is the brainchild of Dr. Shahid Mahmud, Honorary Senior Advisor, COMSTECH – OIC Standing Committee on Scientific and Technological Cooperation, Chairman and CEO, Interactive Group of Companies, Senior Advisor, DEC40 (Digital Economy Cities 40. Dr. Mahmud has long argued that credible, genuine talent development is central to mobilizing both domestic and foreign direct investment in Pakistan. He believes that by taking an integrated approach across Pakistan’s current regulatory regimes, HEC’s requirements for internships, SECP’s ESG disclosure framework, and the State Bank of Pakistan’s green financing and green taxonomy directives, the country can deliver real value to the next generation of talent, to universities, to employers, and to investors alike. As he puts it: with the right intent, the right team, and the right partnerships, mountains can be moved.
Pakistan’s sustainability and disclosure landscape is also shifting. SECP’s ESG Disclosure are mandated for listed companies since financial year ending 2026, partnerships in such programme further strength their inclusion, women empowerment, community development and implementation of ESG mandates backed by audit-ready data.
Under the pilot, Sustainadility working with employer across Pakistan and the Middle East, converts live business requirements into structured internship roles and competency maps, and provides ARC, its digital platform for students, supervisors, and administrators, while the University retains full authority over academic supervision, assessment, and credit. Placements run year-round, typically 8 to 16 weeks, delivered remotely or on a hybrid basis, across Hailey College of Commerce, Hailey College of Banking & Finance, and the Departments of Commerce at the University’s Gujranwala and Jhelum campuses.
The University retains sole authority over its curriculum, Program Learning Outcomes (PLO) and Course Learning Outcomes (CLO) mapping, assessment, and the award of credit. Supervision is joint: an academic supervisor nominated by the faculty and a site supervisor from the host organization both retain visibility over the student’s work. Weekly logs, deliverables, and supervisor reviews are generated on the platform, producing a verified record that supports HEC reporting and accreditation. Transparency and academic control, in this design, are not constraints on opportunity, they are what make it credible.
Sajjeed Aslam, Partner, Sustainadility LLC, commented: “The constraint in Pakistan has never been talent, and after HEC’s reforms it is no longer policy either, it is infrastructure. Someone must do the sourcing, the matching, the supervision records, and the reporting, and that is the work we have taken, and the academic judgment stays exactly where it belongs.”
The post University of the Punjab and Sustainadility Launch HEC Compliant Managed Remote Internship Pilot appeared first on ProPakistani.

items.author: Onsa Mustafa
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
OpenAI has introduced GPT-6 Astra, a new AI model designed to handle complex tasks with greater accuracy, speed, and reliability. The company says Astra is its most intelligent and aligned model so far, with major improvements in computer use, coding, scientific research, cybersecurity, and professional work.
GPT-6 Astra combines advances in pre-training, reinforcement learning, and alignment research. It is built to do more than simply answer questions. The model can interact with computers, browse the web, work with software, analyze data, and complete multi-step tasks with less human involvement.
GPT-6 Astra: OpenAI Introduces Its Most Advanced AI Model Yet
The model has also achieved strong results across several demanding benchmarks. OpenAI says Astra scored 98% on FrontierMath Tier 4 and 99.9% on ARC-AGI-3. It also achieved a perfect 100% score on ExploitBench. These results show the model’s focus on solving difficult problems rather than only improving traditional language-based performance.
Better Computer Use
One of the biggest improvements in GPT-6 Astra is its ability to use computers. The model can fill out online forms, update customer records, organize calendars, conduct online research, and prepare summaries in documents or email.
It can also work with technical software. For example, Astra can analyze scientific data, create charts, build websites, test frontend features, and troubleshoot software problems. OpenAI says these capabilities make the model more useful for tasks that normally require several manual steps.
On the OSWorld 2.0 benchmark, Astra achieved a score of 72.6%, compared with 65.7% for GPT-5.6 Sol. OpenAI also says Astra can complete similar computer-use tasks in significantly less time.
Stronger Professional and Coding Skills
GPT-6 Astra is also aimed at professional users. It can create and edit documents, spreadsheets, presentations, and other work-related files. The model is designed to follow existing templates and understand the style and structure of business documents.
Coding is another major focus. On Terminal-Bench 4.0, Astra achieved 57.9%, compared with 37.3% for GPT-5.6 Sol. The model can work with codebases, run tests, use terminal tools, and handle complicated software engineering tasks.
Astra also introduces improved context handling in Codex. Instead of repeatedly compressing older information into summaries during long sessions, it can preserve notes and search earlier context when needed.
Advances in science and cybersecurity
OpenAI says Astra can assist researchers with scientific workflows. It can use specialized software, inspect datasets, run simulations, and help researchers decide what to investigate next. It achieved 96% on the GPQA Diamond benchmark for graduate-level scientific reasoning.
Cybersecurity is another area where Astra has made major progress. OpenAI reports a 100% score on ExploitBench and stronger performance on several security evaluations. Because these capabilities can also create risks, the company says additional safeguards are being used to prevent misuse.
Availability
GPT-6 Astra is initially being released to a limited group of organizations. OpenAI plans to expand access to ChatGPT Plus, Pro, Business, and Enterprise users. The model will also be available through the OpenAI API, Microsoft Azure, and Amazon Bedrock.
For developers, the API model is available as gpt-6-astra. Standard API pricing starts at $10 per million input tokens and $50 per million output tokens.
Overall, GPT-6 Astra represents a shift toward AI systems that can not only understand information but also act on it. Its stronger computer use, coding, research, and professional abilities could make it a more practical tool for everyday and advanced workflows.

items.author: Onsa Mustafa
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Google’s new Tensor G6 chipset brings major changes compared with previous Tensor processors. It focuses heavily on artificial intelligence, photography, and power efficiency. However, when it comes to raw performance, Qualcomm’s Snapdragon 8 Elite still has a clear advantage. In this vs article, we have done a brief comparison of Tensor G6 and Snapdragon 8 Elite.
Both chipsets are built using TSMC’s 3nm process, but they follow different approaches. The Tensor G6 uses a seven-core CPU with one C1-Ultra core and six C1-Pro cores. The Snapdragon 8 Elite, meanwhile, has eight custom Oryon cores with higher clock speeds.
Tensor G6 vs Snapdragon 8 Elite: Which Chipset Is More Powerful?
The Tensor G6 also comes with a fifth-generation Tensor Processing Unit (TPU), while Qualcomm uses its Hexagon NPU for AI tasks. Google’s approach puts more emphasis on running AI features directly on the phone, while Qualcomm focuses more strongly on overall performance.
Benchmark Performance
Geekbench 6 results show the Snapdragon 8 Elite ahead in both CPU tests. The Tensor G6 records 2,671 points in single-core performance and 6,802 points in multi-core performance. The Snapdragon 8 Elite scores 3,008 and 9,730 points, respectively.
This gives Qualcomm’s chip a 12% lead in single-core performance and a much larger 43% advantage in multi-core performance. The difference should be noticeable during demanding tasks such as heavy multitasking, video processing, and other CPU-intensive workloads.
The gap becomes even larger in AnTuTu. The Tensor G6 scores 1,857,406 points, while the Snapdragon 8 Elite reaches 3,162,650 points. Qualcomm’s chip records a 22% higher CPU score, but its GPU score is dramatically higher.
The Snapdragon 8 Elite achieves 1,200,291 points in the GPU test compared with 432,908 for the Tensor G6. That represents an advantage of around 177%. Its memory and UX scores are also considerably higher.
Gaming performance tells a similar story. In the 3DMark Wild Life Extreme Stress Test, the Tensor G6 scores 3,386, while the Snapdragon 8 Elite reaches 6,612. The Qualcomm chip also averages 39.48 frames per second compared with 20.31 FPS on the Tensor-powered device.
AI and Camera Features
The Tensor G6 is not designed simply to compete in benchmark charts. Google has given the chipset a much larger role in AI processing. Its fifth-generation TPU is designed to handle advanced on-device AI features and support Google’s latest Gemini Nano capabilities.
The chipset also focuses on computational photography. It supports features such as real-time semantic segmentation, 4K portrait video, 8K recording at 30fps, and up to 120x Pro Zoom support.
The Snapdragon 8 Elite has a powerful camera system of its own. Its Spectra ISP supports cameras of up to 320MP and 8K video recording at 60fps. It also includes AI-powered image processing and gaming-focused GPU technologies.
Connectivity and Efficiency
Both processors support modern connectivity, including Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6.0. The Tensor G6 has a MediaTek M90 modem with peak download speeds of up to 12Gbps, while the Snapdragon 8 Elite can reach up to 10Gbps.
Google has also improved power efficiency with the Tensor G6. Its newer CPU design and 3nm manufacturing process help reduce power consumption while improving everyday responsiveness.
Which one Should You Choose?
The Snapdragon 8 Elite is the better choice if you want maximum performance, stronger gaming results, and better sustained power for demanding workloads.
The Tensor G6 makes more sense for users who value Google’s AI features, computational photography, and efficient everyday performance. Its benchmark numbers may not match Qualcomm, but raw speed is not its only goal.
In short, Snapdragon 8 Elite wins the performance battle, while Tensor G6 focuses more on AI and Google’s smart software features.

items.author: Business Desk
items.content:
The Ministry of Information Technology has issued a practical cybersecurity guide for employees, officers, officials, and technical staff working across the federal and provincial governments and public sector organizations.
The National Cyber Emergency Response Team of Pakistan (PKCERT), under the Government of Pakistan, prepared and published the National Cybersecurity Handbook.
The handbook provides practical guidance on adopting secure cyber practices in daily government operations. It aims to help personnel prevent cyber incidents, protect sensitive information, and strengthen the security of government systems.
The ministry said the guidelines are based on Pakistan’s national laws, regulations, government directives, and international cybersecurity standards and best practices.
The handbook translates the requirements of the Pakistan Information Security Framework (PISF) 2026, National Cyber Security Policy 2021, CERT Rules 2023, and other applicable regulations into practical instructions for government personnel.
It covers eight key cybersecurity areas and outlines recommended practices and user responsibilities for protecting government information and systems.
The handbook also emphasizes that cybersecurity is a shared responsibility. As government services become increasingly digital and interconnected, the actions of individual users can affect the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of government information.
The guidelines are intended to significantly reduce cyber risks, but the government clarified that following the handbook does not provide complete protection against sophisticated cyber threats.

items.summary:
The Punjab Communication and Works Department will begin construction of two underpasses worth Rs. 8 billion on Peshawar Road in Rawalpindi from September 7, with work planned at Race Course Park and Charing Cross.
The Frontier Works Organisation (FWO) has secured the construction contract and completed alternate service roads to keep traffic moving during construction.
Traffic on Peshawar Road will be diverted to the newly constructed service roads once work begins. The alternate routes run from Qasim Market to Radio Pakistan and from Maryam Hospital to Rafay Mall.
A senior district administration official told Dawn that authorities had initially planned three underpasses at Race Course Park, Army Graveyard and Charing Cross. The plan was later revised to include only two underpasses, while the Army Graveyard site will receive an at-grade road.
Utility shifting work, including electricity pylons, water supply lines, telephone connections and cable networks, has already been completed.

items.content:
The Punjab Communication and Works Department will begin construction of two underpasses worth Rs. 8 billion on Peshawar Road in Rawalpindi from September 7, with work planned at Race Course Park and Charing Cross.

Traffic on Peshawar Road will be diverted to the newly constructed service roads once work begins. The alternate routes run from Qasim Market to Radio Pakistan and from Maryam Hospital to Rafay Mall.
A senior district administration official told Dawn that authorities had initially planned three underpasses at Race Course Park, Army Graveyard and Charing Cross. The plan was later revised to include only two underpasses, while the Army Graveyard site will receive an at-grade road.

The corridor aims to reduce travel time between the two points to 15 to 20 minutes. Construction on the two underpasses is expected to take around two to three months. The General Post Office Chowk project was completed last year, while the Kutchery Chowk remodeling project was completed in May.

Peran akal imitasi alias AI dalam keseharian masyarakat bisa dibilang semakin mendominasi, berkat kemampuannya yang semakin andal untuk menjawab semua pertanyaan hingga kebutuhan, baik demi mendukung produktivitas maupun sekadar aktivitas harian. Di tengah dominasi tersebut, Indosat Ooredoo Hutchison (IOH) mencoba kembali menekankan peran manusia sebagai pusat utama. Salah satunya melalui instalasi seni “Peran-Tara” di gelaran IdeaFest 2026.
Dalam menghadirkan instalasi tersebut, Indosat membawa gagasan yang sesuai dengan tema besar IdeaFest tahu ini, yakni “Heartware Inside the Hardware” sebagai pengingat bila peran manusia tidak dapat digantikan baik oleh AI, sistem, maupun algoritma. Lewat hal-hal seperti rasa ingin tahu, kreativitas, imajinasi, nilai, hingga kebijaksanaan dalam menentukan arah.
Bersama seniman Indonesia, Sarkodit, Indosat menampilkan sebuah karya instalasi spesial nan interaktif di tengah-tengah keramaian acara IdeaFest 2026, yang dibangun berdasarkan gagasan tersebut. Nama “Peran-Tara” sendiri merupakan sebuah permainan makna yang menyatakan bila instalasi tersebut berbicara mengenai peran manusia dengan akal dan kebijaksanaannya yang digunakan untuk memilih, menentukan arah, hingga memberi makna.
Baca juga: Indosat Hadirkan IM3 Istimewa, Paket Prabayar Fleksibel dan Relevan
“Peran-Tara” Hadirkan Konsep Interaktif, Juga Gelar Podcast Menarik
Lebih lanjut terkait instalasi “Peran-Tara”, Sarkodit mengatakan bila ia juga ingin menampilkan perjalanan Indosat dari waktu ke waktu, menghadirkan konektivitas yang terus berkembang. “Teknologi bisa terus berubah dan semakin canggih, tetapi selalu ada manusia di baliknya yang memiliki ide, membuat pilihan, memberikan makna, dan menentukan akan dibawa ke mana teknologi tersebut. Dari situlah Peran-Tara lahir sebagai interpretasi saya terhadap gagasan tersebut.”
Dalam instalasi tersebut, pengunjung dapat melakukan eksplorasi terkait perkembangan teknologi termasuk era di mana AI belum hadir. Mulai dari simulasi panggilan telepon jaman dulu, hingga mesin game arcade yang sangat populer di masanya. Sebelum kini digantikan ke dalam berbagai bentuk, termasuk dengan augmented reality maupun virtual reality.
Tidak hanya itu, Indosat juga turut menghadirkan sesi diskusi menarik dalam format podcast, yang digelar setiap hari selama Ideafest 2026 berlangsung. Membawa tema AI dan humanity, Indosat menggandeng Podcast Salmon, Maknatalks, hingga Podcast Dvet.
Meneruskan Semangat Indosat Untuk Pemanfaatkan Teknologi Lebih Luas
Melalui partisipasi Indosat dalam Ideafest 2026, pengunjung diharapkan untuk tidak hanya dapat melihat karya dari Sarkodit, namun juga turut menjelajahi perjalanan teknologi Indosat. Sekaligus berinteraksi dengan berbagai pengalaman yang dihadirkan, mengajak mereka untuk melihat teknologi dalam perspektif yang lebih manusiawi.
Odivia Nomia, SVP-Head of Corporate Communications IOH mengatakan, hadirnya Peran-Tara selaras dengan peran IOH sebagai penghubung antara teknologi terbaik dengan kebutuhan dan aspirasi masyakat. “Bagi kami, teknologi, termasuk AI, akan lebih berarti ketika membawa manfaat yang nyata bagi kehidupan manusia. Semangat ini sejalan dengan #LebihBaikIndosat, bahwa kemutakhiran teknologi pada akhirnya harus membuka lebih banyak kemungkinan bagi manusia.”

items.author: Team Inc42
items.content:
Dalal Street emerged as a founder’s paradise in 2025, with 18 Indian startups listing on the bourses and collectively mopping up a record ₹41,248 Cr from the public markets.
The surge was driven by a combination of macroeconomic tailwinds and regulatory support. While robust GDP growth projections helped revive investor appetite, SEBI’s reforms played a key role. Measures such as simplified DRHP filings reduced red tape, while more flexible ESOP rules allowed founders to retain meaningful ownership.
Retail investors also fuelled the frenzy as demat accounts crossed the 20 Cr mark. The OFS component dominated public issues last year, providing liquidity to the early backers of the new-age tech companies. Post-listing performance also followed the usual curve, with investors rewarding companies that prioritised profits, sustainable growth and governance over hype.
“⁠Besides the readiness that startups showed in their unit economics, there is also an increase in the founders committing to their businesses for next couple of decades and grow their businesses by adding adjacent profit pools – something that the public markets reward handsomely,” said Ashish Kumar, cofounder and general partner at Fundamentum Partnership.
Building on the momentum, eleven new-age tech companies have already made their D-Street debut so far this year. Of these, ESDS Software Solution, Klassroom, SEDEMAC, Kissht, LEAP India and Shiprocket made a bumper debut on the bourses.
Nevertheless, the IPO pipeline remains strong. Twenty four startups have already filed their DRHPs with SEBI, while over 25 are in various stages of finalising their IPO plans. Unicorns like OYO, Razorpay and Zetwerk alone could raise over ₹34,000 Cr in 2026, making it one of the biggest years for startup IPOs.
However, recalibration is likely to define 2026 as investors are expected to prioritise strong fundamentals, profitability and low cash burn when backing new-age tech companies.
“IPO-bound startups in 2026 will be increasingly defined by their ability to demonstrate predictable cash flows, sustainable unit economics, and operational discipline rather than headline growth alone. Public market investors will place greater emphasis on governance, capital efficiency and long-term value creation, favouring companies that balance scale with financial prudence,” Orios Venture Partners’ managing partner Rehan Yar Khan told Inc42.
There are other challenges as well. Average retail subscription levels are moderating, while foreign institutional investors (FIIs) are pulling back in droves, reflecting caution amid geopolitical tensions and muted secondary market performance. The ongoing conflict in West Asia has further complicated the situation.
Yet, the overall outlook remains bullish for new-age tech IPOs. Maturing business models, deeper domestic capital pools and an evolving regulatory framework favouring transparency position India as a leading startup IPO hub.
With much on the anvil, we have compiled a list of Indian new-age tech companies eyeing a Dalal Street debut later this year. But before we dive into the list, here are the latest developments from India’s IPO landscape:

SaaS startup NoPaperForms has filed its updated DRHP with SEBI for its IPO, which will comprise a fresh issue of shares worth ₹375 Cr and an OFS of up to 3.8 Cr shares
Data centre company ESDS Software Solution made a stellar debut on bourses as its shares listed at ₹757 on the NSE, a premium of 76.5% over the issue price of ₹429
Furniture rental startup RentoMojo has set a price band of ₹384-₹404 per share for its IPO, which comprises a fresh issue worth ₹150 Cr and an OFS worth ₹1,106 Cr
