items.author: Abbas Naqvi
items.content:
The Sindh High Court (SHC) on Wednesday rejected a plea seeking the formation of a Joint Investigation Team (JIT) in the Mir Raza murder case, dismissing the family’s concerns over an alleged “botched probe”.
Raza’s family, through lawyer Jibran Nasir, sought the formation of a JIT, alleging serious lapses in the original probe, including mishandling and destruction of evidence and failure to preserve CCTV footage. The Sindh government opposed the request, saying a judicial commission had already been formed to investigate the death. On Monday, the court reserved its verdict on a petition after the investigating officer (IO) probing the death of Raza told the SHC that investigators were clear that the case was one of murder and not suicide.
According to the written order available to The Express Tribune, the court said that the investigating officer had assured it that the investigation would be completed in accordance with the law and if deemed necessary, assistance would also be sought from other investigative and law-enforcement agencies.
The court further said that the Supreme Court judgment cited by the petitioner dealt with a different set of circumstances and directed the relevant authorities to conduct the investigation into the Raza case “impartially, fairly and expeditiously”.
The court further observed that the petitioner can avail all available legal remedies to ensure a transparent and fair investigation.
{{pdf}}
Read: Mir Raza death was not suicide, says IO as SHC reserves JIT plea verdict
During the hearing, the court also questioned the lawyers about its authority to supervise an ongoing investigation and order the formation of a JIT.
In response, public prosecutors argued that the court had no authority to interfere in or supervise an ongoing investigation, particularly since the police had not yet submitted the challan in the case.
The court ultimately dismissed the petition and directed the investigating officer to complete the investigation in a transparent, fair and expeditious manner.
Speaking to The Express Tribune, Advocate Nasir said he would appeal against the SHC decision announced today, clarifying that his petition had asked for a judicial review into documented failures in the investigation to determine whether they met the threshold for an independent, multidisciplinary JIT in the Raza case.
“With utmost respect for the Honourable SHC, we respectfully disagree with the judgment in our petition to form a JIT in the Raza case and reserve our right to appeal,” he said.
“We never asked the court to investigate Raza’s murder, identify his killers or determine criminal liability. We asked it to judicially review documented failures in the investigation and determine whether they met the threshold for an independent, multidisciplinary JIT,” he added.
He explained that the judgment, as per his understanding, conflated two very different exercises: deciding disputed questions of fact under Article 199, and examining admitted, documented or officially established facts to determine whether an investigation has been compromised.
He argued that after the binding judgment in the case of Sultan Ali recognised “institutional sabotage” as a relevant consideration, he questioned, “how could that question be answered without testing the material placed before the court against that very parameter? Merely distinguishing Sultan Ali on its facts does not answer the principle relied upon.”
He said the “several” highlighted failures were not mere allegations but facts.
“Yet no distinction was drawn between genuinely disputed allegations and admitted or documented facts,” he protested.
“There is a fundamental difference between a Constitutional Court supervising an investigation and judicially reviewing whether the investigation itself has become compromised. The former may be impermissible; the latter is precisely what constitutional judicial review exists for,” the legal counsel for Raza’s family said.
Also Read: Judicial commission grills doctor over errors in Mir Raza's first post-mortem report, calls it 'criminal negligence'
He added the judgement relied on the investigating officer's (IO) assurance that the investigation would be fair and left remedies open after its conclusion.
“But evidence lost, destroyed or compromised today may never be recovered tomorrow.”
He highlighted that constitutional relief should be effective and “not merely available” when it is already too late.
Case developments
A judicial commission was formed on the request of the Sindh government to probe the death of Raza, who was allegedly kidnapped from PECHS before his body was found in bushes near a wedding hall in Karachi's Gulistan-e-Johar on July 29. The case had initially been surrounded by uncertainty over whether he had been murdered or died by suicide. The first post-mortem findings contained discrepancies and omissions, leading to a second post-mortem that confirmed his murder. Consequently, considering the probe "botched", the family filed a petition in the SHC seeking the formation of JIT.
During earlier hearings regarding the formation of JIT, the investigating officer probing the death of Raza told the SHC that investigators were treating the case as murder and had ruled out suicide based on the post-mortem findings. DSP Siraj Lashari said the investigation had restarted “from zero” on August 13 and was being conducted using digital evidence, including CCTV footage. Investigators had recovered a bullet casing but had yet to find the weapon, while final post-mortem and forensic reports were still awaited.
Separately, the judicial commission convened its second hearing on Monday, September 1, wherein it grilled Medico-Legal Officer Dr Usama Sheikh over discrepancies in the first post-mortem report filed by him. The commission also recorded the statements of the victim's family and Edhi volunteers who shifted his body during the hearing. After the conclusion of the second hearing, Advocate Nasir said the first account of the MLO proved that he was correct about the "botched probe" and, since the commission is not tasked with the probe and can only oversee it, he reiterated that a JIT was crucial for a transparent investigation into the case. The next hearing by the commission is scheduled for tomorrow.

items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Pakistan’s plans to accelerate fiber deployment and expand next-generation 5G services could face delays after the government withdrew the Pakistan Telecommunication (Reorganization) (Amendment) Bill, 2026, which was intended to address long-standing issues surrounding Right of Way charges and approvals.
The proposed legislation was designed to reduce financial and administrative barriers faced by telecom operators while laying optical fiber cable, or OFC, across the country. Fibre infrastructure is considered essential for improving broadband quality and ensuring that recently auctioned spectrum can be used effectively.
With the bill now withdrawn and fresh legislation expected, uncertainty over RoW charges and approval procedures may continue at a time when telecom companies are under pressure to expand fiber networks, improve service quality, and prepare infrastructure for wider 5G deployment.
Minister for Information Technology and Telecommunication Shaza Fatima Khawaja had earlier said the proposed amendment would provide a legal framework for rationalizing RoW fees and reduce both the cost and time involved in fiber deployment.
According to the minister, lower RoW charges could help operators expand network coverage more rapidly, improve broadband affordability, and extend high-speed connectivity to remote and underserved areas.
Fiberization Remains Critical for 5G
The government has linked RoW reforms directly with its broader 5G strategy.
Pakistan auctioned an additional 480 MHz of spectrum in March 2026, taking the country’s total available spectrum to 754 MHz. The additional spectrum is expected to support higher network capacity and next-generation mobile services.
However, spectrum availability alone may not be enough to deliver the full benefits of 5G. Modern mobile networks require extensive fiber links between cellular sites and the wider telecom backbone, making faster OFC deployment a key part of network expansion.
High RoW charges, delays in approvals and varying procedures across authorities can increase deployment costs and slow infrastructure projects. The government had hoped the proposed reforms would create a more predictable regulatory environment and encourage greater private-sector investment.
The economic implications are also significant. Citing World Bank estimates, the IT minister said every 10 percent increase in broadband penetration could contribute between 0.9 percent and 2 percent to GDP growth, potentially adding nearly $30 billion to Pakistan’s economy over five years.
She also cited research suggesting that a 10 percent rise in broadband access could increase employment by between 3.1 per cent and 13.2 per cent, potentially creating more than two million jobs.
Attention will now turn to the replacement legislation and whether it preserves the original objective of rationalizing RoW charges while addressing concerns surrounding the withdrawn bill.
Any prolonged delay could slow fiber deployment at a time when telecom operators are preparing to make greater use of newly acquired spectrum, potentially affecting broadband quality, network expansion, and the pace of 5G rollout across the country.

items.summary:
Apple baru saja merilis iOS 27 Beta 8 untuk pengembang pada 31 Agustus 2026, dengan nomor build 24A5430a. Versi sama juga sudah tersedia untuk pengguna program public beta.
Rilis iOS 27 Beta 8 ini datang 9 hari sebelum Apple Event pada 9 September atau 10 September di Indonesia, sehingga Beta 8 kemungkinan besar jadi salah satu build terakhir sebelum versi Release Candidate (RC) dirilis.
Update iOS 27 kali ini memang tidak ada fitur baru diumumkan secara khusus untuk Beta 8. Menurut laporan 9to5Mac, Rabu (2/9/2026), update iOS 27 Beta 8 lebih fokus pada stabilitas, perbaikan bug, dan penyempurnaan jelang rilis final OS untuk perangkat Apple tersebut.

items.author: Yus Lianson
items.content:
Apple baru saja merilis iOS 27 Beta 8 untuk pengembang pada 31 Agustus 2026, dengan nomor build 24A5430a. Versi sama juga sudah tersedia untuk pengguna program public beta.
Rilis iOS 27 Beta 8 ini datang 9 hari sebelum Apple Event pada 9 September atau 10 September di Indonesia, sehingga Beta 8 kemungkinan besar jadi salah satu build terakhir sebelum versi Release Candidate (RC) dirilis.
Update iOS 27 kali ini memang tidak ada fitur baru diumumkan secara khusus untuk Beta 8. Menurut laporan 9to5Mac, Rabu (2/9/2026), update iOS 27 Beta 8 lebih fokus pada stabilitas, perbaikan bug, dan penyempurnaan jelang rilis final OS untuk perangkat Apple tersebut.
Selain iOS, raksasa teknologi berbasis di Cupertino tersebut juga merilis versi beta untuk iPadOS 27, watchOS 27, tvOS 27, dan visionOS 27.
Baca Juga: Apple Disebut Sudah Siapkan iPhone Ultra Generasi Kedua dan Ketiga
iPhone apa saja yang kebagian iOS 27?
Hingga saat ini, dukungan iOS 27 masih bisa dinikmati oleh pengguna iPhone sebagai berikut:
iPhone SE generasi kedua
iPhone 11
iPhone 12
iPhone 13
iPhone 14
iPhone 15
iPhone 16
Keluarga iPhone 17
Walau kompatibel dengan iOS 27, bukan berarti iPhone versi lama bisa mendapatkan seluruh fitur. Apple Intelligence, misalnya, hanya berjalan di iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 15 Pro Max, dan iPhone 16 ke atas.
Siri AI jadi Sorotan di iOS 27 Beta 8, Kenapa?
Siri AI iOS 26 di iPhone 17e
Siri AI menjadi salah satu perubahan paling signifikan yang akan tampil di iOS 27 Beta 8. Diperkenalkan pada WWDC 2026 sebagai versi Siri ditenagai Apple Intelligence, Apple merancang AI ini agar mampu memahami percakapan secara lebih natural, termasuk konteks pribadi pengguna dan informasi yang tampil di layar.
Tak hanya itu, pembuat iPhone ini juga menambahkan aplikasi Siri terpisah agar pengguna bisa melihat kembali riwayat percakapan mereka.
Apple Intelligence tidak berhenti di Siri saja, aplikasi Photos, Safari, Image Playground, dan sejumlah aplikasi lain juga menjadi bagian dari generasi baru fitur AI di iOS 27 nanti.
Siri AI sudah Dukung Bahasa Indonesia?
Sayangnya, Siri AI hingga saat ini masih belum tersedia atau mendukung bahasa Indonesia. Dalam daftar bahasa yang diumumkan Apple, Bahasa Indonesia tidak tercantum sebagai bahasa didukung Apple Intelligence.
Siri AI akan tersedia dalam tahap beta untuk pengguna dengan perangkat didukung dan menggunakan bahasa Inggris. Karena itu, dukungan bahasa lain, termasuk kemungkinan Bahasa Indonesia, baru menyusul setelahnya. 
Artinya, pengguna di Indonesia yang sudah punya iPhone 15 Pro ke atas pun belum tentu bisa menjajal fitur ini di gelombang pertama.
Kapan iOS 27 Versi Final Dirilis?
Apple belum mengumumkan tanggal pasti. Tapi dengan Beta 8 yang hadir jelang Apple Event 9 September, dan siklus beta yang sudah masuk build kedelapan, langkah berikutnya diperkirakan bergerak ke RC sebelum rilis publik. 9to5Mac memperkirakan peluncuran iOS 27 akan berlangsung bulan ini.
Rencananya, perusahaan akan mengumumkan sejumlah lini produk baru mulai dari iPhone 18 Pro dan iPhone 18 Pro Max. Selain kedua model ini, banyak pihak menanti kehadiran iPhone lipat pertama Apple yaitu iPhone Ultra.
Bocoran Kapasitas Baterai iPhone Ultra Muncul
Rumor mengenai iPhone Ultra, yang disebut-sebut sebagai ponsel lipat pertama Apple, kembali mencuat menjelang peluncurannya yang diperkirakan berlangsung pada September 2026. Kali ini, perhatian tertuju pada kapasitas baterai perangkat tersebut setelah muncul laporan mengenai sertifikasi dua unit baterai yang diduga ditujukan untuk perangkat lipat Apple.
Informasi tersebut berasal dari pembocor Digital Chat Station di Weibo yang menyebut salah satu pemasok baterai Apple baru saja mendapatkan sertifikasi untuk sepasang baterai. Konfigurasi seperti ini umum ditemukan pada smartphone lipat karena desain perangkat mengharuskan baterai dibagi ke dalam dua bagian agar dapat menyesuaikan mekanisme engsel dan lipatan layar.
Meski Apple belum memberikan informasi resmi terkait perangkat tersebut, kemunculan sertifikasi baterai sering kali menjadi salah satu petunjuk awal menjelang peluncuran produk baru. Jika laporan ini akurat, iPhone Ultra berpotensi menjadi salah satu perangkat lipat dengan kapasitas baterai terbesar yang pernah dirilis Apple.

items.author: Shrishti Bisht
items.content:
Pune-based deeptech company Aeron Systems has raised ₹45 Cr (about $4.7 Mn) in a pre-Series B funding round jointly led by Riverwalk Holdings and MGF-Kavachh (MountTech Growth Fund).
The company plans to use the fresh capital to expand its manufacturing capacity for advanced inertial navigation systems, accelerate R&D, meet growing customer demand, and strengthen its presence in international markets.
Founded in 2008 by Ashvani Shukla and Abhijeet Bokil, Aeron designs and manufactures inertial navigation and industrial IoT-based weather-monitoring systems for aerospace, defence, renewable energy, and other industrial applications.
Its navigation systems help aircraft, drones, missiles, military vehicles, and ships determine their position, direction, orientation, and movement, including in situations where satellite navigation signals are unavailable or disrupted. Its weather-monitoring systems collect environmental data for renewable energy, agriculture, and other industries.
Its product portfolio includes inertial navigation systems, air data computers, weather and environmental sensors, flight-test instrumentation, avionics, and resilient positioning, navigation and timing (PNT) technologies.
Aeron’s technologies are deployed across aircraft, helicopters, unmanned platforms, missiles, armoured vehicles, and naval platforms. It counts Hindustan Aeronautics, Bharat Electronics, DRDO, the Indian Army, and the Indian Navy among its customers.
The company claims to have deployed more than 10,000 inertial systems and over 2,500 weather stations globally. Its systems operate in environments ranging from high-altitude cold deserts to tropical regions, it said in a statement.
Deeptech Funding Gathers Pace
The funding comes amid growing demand for aerospace and defence technologies that can operate in increasingly complex and contested environments. Electronic warfare and disruption of satellite navigation signals have increased the need for navigation and sensing systems that can provide reliable data under demanding conditions.
Investor interest in the sector is also rising, with capital flowing into areas such as space-based intelligence, autonomous systems, avionics, and defence electronics.
For instance, Bengaluru-based spacetech startup Kepler Aerospace yesterday raised $8 Mn in a seed round led by Blue Ashva Capital to develop space-based intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance (ISR) capabilities.
Meanwhile, aerospace startup Alteon raised $2.5 Mn in a pre-seed round led by Lachy Groom, with participation from Together Fund, to develop autonomous aircraft designed to remain airborne for months without landing.
India’s overall deeptech market is estimated to have been worth $9 Bn to $12 Bn in FY25 and is expected to grow to $27 Bn to $33 Bn by 2030, registering a CAGR of around 20%–30%, according to Redseer Strategy Consultants

items.author: Onsa Mustafa
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Xiaomi is preparing to launch its new foldable smartphone, the Xiaomi 18 Fold, later this month. The company has already confirmed that the Xiaomi 18 Fold will use its self-developed Xring O3 chipset. Now, a benchmark listing has revealed more details about the upcoming phone.
The Xiaomi 18 Fold was spotted in the Geekbench AI database after a prototype was tested. The listing confirms that the foldable will be powered by the Xring O3 processor. It also shows that the tested model came with 16GB of RAM. Xiaomi could still release the phone in other memory configurations.
Xiaomi 18 Fold Appears in Benchmark With Xring O3 Chip and 16GB RAM
The benchmark listing also confirms that the Xiaomi 18 Fold will run Android 17 out of the box. This will give the device access to Google’s latest Android features and improvements when it launches.
In the Geekbench AI test, the prototype recorded a score of 629 in the Single Precision test. It achieved 799 in the Half Precision test and 634 in the Quantized test. These results provide an early look at the phone’s AI performance, although benchmark scores from a prototype may not represent the final retail version.
The listing also provides some information about the Xring O3’s CPU configuration. The chipset was detected with two cores running at up to 4.36GHz. Four additional cores reached speeds of up to 3.69GHz, while another four cores were clocked at up to 3.15GHz.
For graphics, the Xring O3 appears to use a Mali-G2-Ultra-NX MC16 GPU. The combination of the new processor, large amount of RAM, and powerful graphics hardware suggests that Xiaomi is positioning the 18 Fold as a high-end foldable.
See Also: Xiaomi 18 Fold to Become First Smartphone With CXMT’s New LPDDR6 Memory
The Xring O3 is particularly important because it is Xiaomi’s own chipset. The company has been developing its in-house silicon to compete more directly with processors from major chipmakers. Xiaomi has also highlighted the efficiency and performance improvements of the new chip.
The Xiaomi 18 Fold is expected to be officially introduced in September. More details about its display, cameras, battery, and pricing should become available as the launch gets closer.
For now, the Geekbench AI listing gives us a clearer picture of the phone’s hardware. The 16GB RAM configuration, Android 17, and Xring O3 chipset make the Xiaomi 18 Fold an interesting device to watch in the growing foldable smartphone market.

items.author: Shrishti Bisht
items.content:
BYJU’S founder Byju Raveendran has proposed relinquishing his claimed beneficial interest in 17.89 Mn shares of Aakash Educational Services to settle Qatar Holding’s arbitration claim of more than $235 Mn against him.
However, the precise structure of the proposed settlement and the value assigned to the shares could not be ascertained, ET reported, citing sources.
A person familiar with Qatar Holding’s position told the publication that the fund would continue to pursue repayment of the debt and enforcement of the arbitral award in its favour.
Inc42 has reached out to Qatar Investment Authority (QIA) for a comment on the development. The story will be updated if a response is received. Raveendran could not be reached for a comment despite repeated attempts.
The 17.89 Mn shares are held through Singapore-based Beeaar Investco Pte and currently represent about 5.7% of Aakash’s equity, the report said.
The shares were acquired in 2022 using $150 Mn in financing extended by QIA-owned Qatar Holding to Raveendran’s Singapore-based investment vehicle, Byju’s Investments Pte Ltd (BIPL). Raveendran personally guaranteed the financing.
The arrangement subsequently broke down after Qatar Holding alleged breaches of the financing agreement and defaults by BIPL. It terminated the agreement and demanded more than $235 Mn, including early termination fees and penalties.
Qatar Holding also alleged that the Aakash shares were transferred to Beeaar, which it claims is beneficially owned by Raveendran, in breach of the agreement. The fund has sought to prevent the shares from being transferred, sold, or pledged while it pursues recovery of its dues.
Qatar Holding’s Legal Battle
The proposed settlement comes amid legal proceedings against Raveendran and BIPL in India and Singapore.
In July 2025, a Singapore arbitration tribunal directed Raveendran and BIPL to pay Qatar Holding more than $235 Mn, along with interest of 4% a year, compounded daily from February 28, 2024.
Qatar Holding subsequently approached the Karnataka High Court to enforce the award. In September 2025, the court restrained Raveendran and BIPL from disposing of their assets while the enforcement proceedings continued.
In July 2026, Qatar Holding secured another arbitration award directing Raveendran and BIPL to pay SGD 7.2 Mn, or about ₹53 Cr, towards arbitration costs. The award, dated July 21, also carries simple interest of 5.33% a year until payment.
Last month, the Karnataka High Court admitted Qatar Holding’s fresh plea seeking enforcement of the SGD 7.2 Mn award. The fund also sought protection over assets worth more than $235 Mn while it pursues enforcement of both awards.
Qatar Holding has asked the court to direct Raveendran to disclose his assets, including their location, value, and beneficial ownership. It has also sought the appointment of a receiver over the assets and properties of Raveendran and BIPL.
The High Court issued notices to Raveendran and BIPL and clubbed the fresh plea with the related proceedings. The matter is scheduled to be heard on September 21.
Aakash At Dispute’s Centre
Aakash has emerged as one of the most important assets in the wider battle among BYJU’S creditors.
BYJU’S parent Think & Learn has been undergoing insolvency proceedings since 2024 after defaulting on a ₹158 Cr payment to the Board of Control for Cricket in India under a sponsorship agreement.
In July, the NCLT’s Bengaluru bench paused the next stage of the bidding process until its August 31 hearing. It directed the resolution professional not to issue Form G inviting expressions of interest or finalise the list of prospective resolution applicants during this period.
However, the Tribunal did not halt the insolvency proceedings themselves.
The order followed a challenge by Byju and Riju Raveendran to a ₹11,433 Cr claim filed by GLAS Trust, the trustee representing BYJU’S US term loan lenders.
Meanwhile, Raveendran is facing a six-month civil contempt sentence in Singapore in connection with the Qatar Holding dispute.
Creditors have been separately exploring a broader settlement centred on Aakash.
The latest proposal further places Aakash at the centre of overlapping disputes over ownership, creditor recoveries, and the future of the Byju’s group.

items.author: Rizwana Omer
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
vivo’s camera teaser campaign for the X500 Pro Series has become a slow drip of specs, and the latest reveal is aimed squarely at video shooters. The company has now shown off just how far it’s pushing slow-motion recording on its next flagship.
The X500 Pro and X500 Pro Max will support 4K recording at up to 960 frames per second, an extraordinary frame rate for a phone camera, alongside two other slow-motion tiers below it.
What vivo Has Confirmed So Far
vivo confirmed last week that the X500 Pro and Pro Max will shoot 4K video at 240fps, and the company has now published a short clip on Weibo showing that mode in action. Beyond the headline number, vivo also confirmed 4K recording at 480fps and 960fps, reaching those higher frame rates through what it describes as 4K frame interpolation and variable speed mapping algorithms rather than pure sensor readout speed alone.
That distinction matters for anyone judging the claim on its face. Frame interpolation software fills in additional frames between what the sensor actually captures, which is a different technical approach than a sensor natively reading out 960 frames every second. It’s a common technique in professional cinema cameras too, so it isn’t a red flag on its own, but it does mean the 960fps figure reflects processed output rather than raw sensor throughput.
https://www.phoneworld.com.pk/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/vivo-X500-Pro-Series.mp4
The Hardware Behind The Video Claims
Driving these video modes is a new primary rear camera built around a custom Phantom 900 sensor, co-developed by Sony and vivo’s in-house Blueprint Imaging team. vivo says the sensor delivers up to 17EV of dynamic range along with 3-axis optical image stabilization, a combination aimed at keeping footage steady and detail intact in both bright highlights and shadows during fast motion capture.
For context, most flagship phone cameras today sit somewhere in the 13-14EV dynamic range. A jump to 17EV, if it holds up under independent testing, would put the X500 Pro’s sensor closer to what dedicated mirrorless cameras achieve, a meaningful claim if vivo can back it up once review units are in hand.
vivo has branded the setup the “ZEISS Ultra Dynamic Main Camera”, continuing its long-running optics partnership with the German lens maker, and vivo Product Manager Han Boxiao has said the X500 Pro Max’s version of this camera adds CIPA 7.0-grade stabilization on top of the 3-axis OIS.
Where Video Fits Into The Bigger X500 Picture
Video is only one part of what vivo is building toward with this launch. The series carries the internal codename “Thanos 500”, a nod to the telephoto reputation the X100 Ultra built two generations ago, and vivo has said the X500 lineup is targeting five upgrade areas at once: video, photography, performance, display and software.
On the photography side, the Pro Max is expected to pair the new main sensor with a 200 MP periscope telephoto camera, continuing vivo’s pattern of pushing periscope resolution well beyond what most competitors offer. Performance-wise, the Pro models are widely expected to run MediaTek’s Dimensity 9600 Pro, built on a 2nm process, which would make the X500 Pro among the first phones on the market with 2nm silicon if the chip ships as expected.
A Launch Window Getting Crowded Fast
vivo has confirmed the X500 series will launch in China later this month, succeeding the X300 lineup that debuted in October 2025. No specific date within September has been announced yet, and vivo hasn’t detailed pricing or confirmed markets beyond China so far.
The timing puts vivo in the middle of an unusually stacked flagship season. September 2026 is also expected to bring the Xiaomi 18, Oppo Find X10 and Apple’s iPhone lineup to market, meaning vivo’s video-first pitch will need to stand out fast in a month already crowded with competing camera claims.
Why This Matters Beyond The Spec Sheet
Slow-motion frame rates make for eye-catching marketing, but they’re also a genuine differentiator in a market where most flagship camera upgrades have started to feel incremental year over year. A 17EV dynamic range claim and a 960fps mode, even a software-assisted one, give vivo something concrete to lead with heading into launch, rather than another round of megapixel or zoom-range bragging rights.
Whether the video quality holds up outside controlled teaser clips is the real question review units will answer. For now, vivo is betting that video, not just photography, is where it can differentiate the X500 Pro series in an increasingly saturated flagship camera race, and the frame rate numbers alone are enough to make that a story worth watching once the phones actually launch.

items.content:
John Ternus jadi CEO Apple mulai 1 September 2026, menggantikan Tim Cook yang telah memimpin perusahaan selama 15 tahun lamanya.
Keputusan menunjuk John Ternus jadi CEO Apple menandai perubahan kepemimpinan pertama perusahaan dalam 15 tahun, dan publik menyoroti bagaimana arah raksasa teknologi ini di bawah nakhoda baru.
Hanya dalam hitungan beberapa hari mendatang, mantan bos hardware Apple tersebut akan menghadapi agenda besar pertamanya, yaitu Apple Event pada 9 September atau 10 September waktu Indonesia.
Baca Juga: Apple Event 2026 Digelar 10 September, iPhone Lipat Debut?
Berperan sebagai CEO, Ternus langsung mengirim memo ke seluruh karyawan Apple di hari pertamanya. Selain berterima kasih kepada Tim Cook, ia juga menggoda adanya peluncuran besar yang telah dipersiapkan perusahaan pekan depan.
“Kami ada peluncuran besar minggu depan yang akan menjadi sesuatu fenomenal,” ujar John Ternus di dalam memo, sebagaimana dikutip dari 9to5Mac, Rabu (2/9/2026).
Tim,
Hari ini, di hari pertama saya menjabat sebagai CEO, saya ingin menyampaikan pesan singkat untuk berterima kasih kepada Anda semua atas ucapan selamat yang hangat. Saya juga ingin menyampaikan apresiasi yang mendalam kepada Tim karena telah berbagi begitu banyak pengetahuan dan pengalamannya selama masa transisi ini, dan yang lebih penting lagi, atas segala kontribusinya bagi Apple selama bertahun-tahun. Kita sangat beruntung pernah memiliki CEO yang memimpin dengan berlandaskan nilai-nilai serta sikap yang begitu santun dan manusiawi. Kita semua menjadi lebih baik karenanya, dan saya sangat bersyukur beliau akan menjabat sebagai ketua eksekutif kita.
Saya merasa terhormat dapat mengemban peran ini di perusahaan yang sungguh merupakan perusahaan terbaik di dunia, dan saya sangat antusias menyambut segala hal yang telah kita siapkan ke depannya. Pekan depan, kita akan mengadakan peluncuran besar yang pastinya akan luar biasa. Terima kasih atas segala upaya Anda semua yang telah mewujudkan hal ini.
Saya juga sama antusiasnya dengan apa yang menanti setelah itu, termasuk produk-produk luar biasa yang sedang dalam tahap pengembangan serta produk-produk yang bahkan belum kita bayangkan saat ini—yang akan kita rancang dan wujudkan bersama. Tidak ada tim lain di dunia ini yang lebih saya inginkan untuk membangun masa depan bersama.
Akan ada kabar lebih lanjut nanti. Untuk saat ini, terima kasih atas kerja keras Anda yang luar biasa!
John
Apple memang berencana untuk menggelar ajang besar minggu depan, 9 September atau 10 September di Indonesia. Bertajuk “Surprise and Shine”, acara tahunan ini akan digelar di Apple Park, Cupertino.
Resmi menjabat CEO Apple, postingan John Ternus di akun media sosial (medsos) pribadinya di X (dulunya bernama Twitter) langsung menjadi sorotan. Dalam waktu singkat, cuitan “hello” di akun Ternus pun sudah menyedot views lebih dari 50 juta.
Selain itu, postingan ini juga sudah mengantongi 50 ribu lebih komentar dan sudah di like lebih dari 410 ribuan.
John Ternus Jadi CEO Apple, Siapa Sosoknya?
CEO Apple John Ternus gantikan Tim Cook. (Doc: Apple)
John Ternus bukan sosok baru di balik berbagai perangkat Apple. Ia bergabung dengan tim Product Design Apple pada 2001, kemudian menjadi Vice President Hardware Engineering pada 2013 dan Senior Vice President Hardware Engineering pada 2021.
Selama berada di Apple, Ternus memimpin engineering hardware untuk berbagai produk seperti iPhone, iPad, Mac dan AirPods. Ia juga menjadi salah satu sosok penting dalam transisi Mac dari prosesor Intel menuju Apple silicon.
Latar belakang hardware tersebut membuat kepemimpinan John Ternus berbeda dengan Cook, yang dikenal kuat dalam operasi dan supply chain.
Cook sendiri tidak meninggalkan Apple. Ia kini menjabat sebagai Executive Chairman, dengan salah satu tugas membantu perusahaan dalam hubungan dengan pembuat kebijakan di berbagai negara.
Apa Tantangan Terbesar John Ternus Jadi CEO Apple?
Sebagai CEO, Ternus mewarisi hal jauh lebih besar dibanding ketika Cook menggantikan Steve Jobs pada 2011.
Reuters mencatat, pendapatan tahunan Apple meningkat dari sekitar USD 108 miliar menjadi USD 416 miliar selama kepemimpinan Cook, sementara perusahaan juga membangun bisnis Services dan kategori perangkat baru seperti Apple Watch dan AirPods.
Namun, John Ternus jadi CEO Apple juga menghadapi sejumlah tantangan.
Salah satu yang terbesar adalah kecerdasan buatan. Apple menghadapi tekanan untuk mempercepat kemampuan AI setelah pengembangan Siri generasi baru mengalami sejumlah hambatan.
Ternus juga harus menghadapi diversifikasi rantai pasok Apple dari China serta tekanan terhadap margin akibat biaya komponen. Ujian publik pertama Ternus akan datang hanya delapan hari setelah ia resmi menjadi CEO.
Apple Event pada 9 September diperkirakan menjadi panggung berbagai perangkat baru. Namun, produk seperti iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone lipat, Apple Watch Series 12 hingga AirPods 5 masih berdasarkan laporan dan rumor hingga diumumkan langsung oleh Apple.

items.author: Sports Desk
items.content:
Pakistan cricket has entered one of the most embarrassing phases in its history, with the ongoing 2026 England Test series exposing not only the team’s weaknesses on the field but also creating alarming instability in the boardroom.
The latest controversy erupted after Pakistan suffered a heavy 194-run defeat to England at Lord’s. With the Pakistan Cricket Board’s top hierarchy present, the defeat was followed almost immediately by news that seven players would be sent home and replaced for the remaining tour. The PCB subsequently confirmed the decision through an official press release.
The timing and manner of the move have raised serious questions.
Changes to a squad during an overseas Test series are not unprecedented, but the scale and the abrupt manner in which this decision was taken has left Pakistan cricket looking directionless. If the selectors and team management had lost faith in certain players, the changes could have been made after the conclusion of the series.
Instead, the PCB has once again created a controversy that has overshadowed cricket itself.
For several years, only a handful of individuals have appeared to control the direction of Pakistan cricket. Their repeated administrative experiments and sudden decisions have increasingly given the impression of a system searching for scapegoats rather than solutions.
The treatment of Mohammad Rizwan is perhaps the most striking example.
Rizwan, who has also captained Pakistan, played a key role when Pakistan secured series victories in Australia and South Africa. Yet after struggling with the bat in England, he was among those sent home. His batting form certainly requires improvement, but there is little doubt that he remains Pakistan’s premier wicket-keeper.
His selection for the England and West Indies tours was hardly surprising. In Sylhet against Bangladesh in May, Rizwan had produced a fighting 94 when Pakistan’s batting line-up struggled against the hosts’ bowling attack. He also scored 59 in the first innings of the Mirpur Test. On that evidence, dropping him from the touring squad altogether was difficult to justify.
Imam-ul-Haq’s case is different. The left-hander suffered a calf injury and missed both innings at Lord’s. His fitness should be assessed carefully rather than becoming another subject of speculation.
The controversy deepened when the PCB bureaucracy sought an explanation from the selection committee over the inclusion of Rizwan and Imam for the England and West Indies tours. Senior selector Misbah-ul-Haq subsequently resigned, adding another layer of uncertainty to an already troubled system.
Aaqib Javed, who holds multiple important responsibilities within Pakistan cricket, has emerged as one of the most influential figures in the current set-up. The concentration of authority in the hands of a few individuals has become a growing concern.
The humiliation has not been limited to players. Head coach Sarfaraz Ahmad, who led Pakistan to Champions Trophy glory, and bowling coach Umar Gul, a former Pakistan pace spearhead who has rendered distinguished services to the country, have also found themselves caught in the turmoil.
PCB chairman Mohsin Naqvi now faces a defining challenge. His position gives him enormous authority, and his role in cricket administration can still help Pakistan cricket recover but only if he is willing to make difficult decisions.
The PCB needs people of integrity, experience and cricketing credibility. Former cricketers with strong reputations should have a greater voice in decision-making, while arbitrary mid-tour interventions must end.
Pakistan cricket does not need another turmoil. It needs stability, accountability and a clear cricketing vision.
Sending seven players home in the middle of an overseas Test series has left Pakistan cricket embarrassed on the international stage. The question now is whether the PCB will learn from the fiasco, or simply prepare for the next one.
Following such a high disgrace players now should think for forming Players' Association, a representative body, which could safeguard their interests. Such step will leave a good impact on players’ future. But who will take this step is a difficult question to answer.

items.title: ADB praises Pakistan's economic progress, backs shift towards private-sector-led growth
items.summary:
The Asian Development Bank (ADB) praised Pakistan’s progress in macroeconomic stabilisation and said it was ready to expand support for private-sector development, small and medium enterprises (SMEs) and export-led growth, the Ministry of Finance said on Wednesday.
According to a statement, ADB Vice President for South, Central and West Asia Yingming Yang congratulated Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb and the government on Pakistan’s “progress in macroeconomic stabilisation” and commended improvements in “fiscal management, the external account and overall economic stability”.

items.content:
The Asian Development Bank (ADB) praised Pakistan’s progress in macroeconomic stabilisation and said it was ready to expand support for private-sector development, small and medium enterprises (SMEs) and export-led growth, the Ministry of Finance said on Wednesday.
According to a statement, ADB Vice President for South, Central and West Asia Yingming Yang congratulated Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb and the government on Pakistan’s “progress in macroeconomic stabilisation” and commended improvements in “fiscal management, the external account and overall economic stability”.
Finance Minister, ADB Vice President Discuss Expanded Cooperation on Reforms, Access to Finance for SMEs and Export-Led Growth
ADB Commends Pakistan’s Macroeconomic Progress, Sovereign Rating Upgrades and Reform Momentum
Federal Minister for Finance and Revenue, Senator… pic.twitter.com/D7OaJl2ZVj
— Ministry of Finance, Government of Pakistan (@Financegovpk) September 2, 2026
During a meeting with Yang, Aurangzeb said the government’s focus was shifting “from macroeconomic stabilisation towards sustainable and inclusive growth”, with greater emphasis on “investment, exports, employment generation and private-sector participation”.
He welcomed ADB’s “expanding engagement beyond sovereign financing”, including support for “private-sector operations and public-private partnerships”.
The meeting discussed access to finance for SMEs, which the minister said was an important part of Pakistan’s “growth and export strategy”.
The finance minister highlighted efforts to “expand financing for SMEs” and strengthen their capacity to contribute to “employment, investment and exports”.
The two sides also underscored the importance of integrating SMEs into “global value chains” and improving their competitiveness.
Read: Govt signs two export financing deals
Yang reaffirmed the ADB’s “commitment to supporting Pakistan’s development priorities” and said there was “strong alignment” between the bank’s strategic priorities and the government’s reform agenda.
He expressed readiness to provide further support for “private-sector development, SME value chain financing” and other priority areas.
The ADB vice president also commended positive developments in Pakistan’s sovereign credit ratings, describing them as evidence of the country’s “continued reform efforts and improved economic fundamentals”.
The ADB vice president, however, stressed the importance of maintaining “fiscal prudence” as Pakistan transitioned towards sustainable growth.
Aurangzeb, meanwhile, stressed the need to “institutionalise reforms” in domestic resource mobilisation, public finance, energy, insurance and pensions to establish a “sustainable growth trajectory”.
The meeting also reviewed the government’s insurance transformation programme, public-private partnership initiatives and efforts to improve “project readiness and implementation capacity”.
Read More: Govt taps HK expertise for virtual assets
The finance minister called for greater mobilisation of “domestic and private capital”, including through “innovative financing structures, co-financing” and stronger participation by international development and financial institutions.
He also highlighted opportunities to expand cooperation in “infrastructure, transport, clean energy, water resource management, climate resilience” and other priority sectors.
The two sides also discussed pension reforms, institutional strengthening and ongoing and pipeline policy-based operations, recognising their role in supporting “key structural reforms and long-term economic transformation”.
Aurangzeb said future ADB support should align with the government’s priorities of “private-sector-led growth, export competitiveness, access to finance, infrastructure development, climate resilience and social protection”.
The meeting came days after Pakistan strengthened its export financing framework through two agreements aimed at improving access to finance and insurance for exporters and SMEs.
On Aug 31, the Export-Import Bank of Pakistan (Pak EXIM) and the Islamic Corporation for the Insurance of Investment and Export Credit (ICIEC) signed a reinsurance partnership, while the Export Development Fund (EDF) and Pak EXIM established an approximately Rs3 billion SME Risk Pool to expand SMEs’ access to export credit insurance against non-payment risks.

items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Samsung appears set to continue with its cautious approach to smartphone charging, as new certification details suggest the upcoming Galaxy S27 and Galaxy S27+ will retain charging speeds already familiar to users of recent Galaxy flagships.
The two devices have reportedly appeared on China’s 3C certification database, offering an early look at Samsung’s charging plans ahead of the expected launch of the Galaxy S27 series.
According to the listing, the standard Galaxy S27, carrying model number SM-S9520, will support 25W wired charging. That is unchanged from the Galaxy S26 and continues a charging limit Samsung has maintained on its base Galaxy S models for several generations.
The Galaxy S27+, identified as SM-S9560, is listed with support for 45W wired charging. While faster than the standard model, it also represents no major improvement over Samsung’s previous Plus-series flagships.
The certification suggests Samsung is once again choosing consistency over aggressive charging upgrades.
Several rival Android manufacturers have pushed charging speeds significantly higher in recent years, but Samsung has continued to rely on relatively conservative power limits across much of its premium smartphone range.
For users hoping the Galaxy S27 generation would finally bring a noticeable charging boost, the latest filing may therefore come as a disappointment.
Samsung’s approach could still reflect a broader focus on battery longevity, thermal management, and overall device reliability rather than headline charging figures.
No Charger Expected in the Box
The 3C information also indicates that both the Galaxy S27 and Galaxy S27+ are expected to ship without a wall charger.
A USB Type-C cable is likely to be included in the retail package, continuing Samsung’s current practice across its flagship lineup.
The certification does not reveal the full specifications of the upcoming phones, leaving key details such as battery capacity, chipset, cameras, and display upgrades unconfirmed for now.
Still, the appearance of the Galaxy S27 and S27+ in a regulatory database suggests development is progressing, and further leaks and certifications are likely to emerge in the months ahead.

Google has announced a new Android update as part of its September Android Drop. The update focuses on making everyday tasks easier, improving accessibility, reducing motion sickness, and giving users more ways to personalize their phones.
One of the most useful additions is a new way to remember where important items are stored. Users will soon be able to ask Gemini to remember the location of items that do not have a tracking tag. For example, users can tell Gemini that they placed their passport in a bedroom drawer or kept spare keys in a particular location.
September Android Update Gets 5 New Features to Make Your Phone More Useful
Gemini will save this information in Find Hub. Users can later ask Gemini where they placed the item or check their remembered items in Find Hub. They can also add a photo when saving an item. The feature will be available on devices running Android 16 or later in supported countries.
Google is also introducing Motion Assist to help people who experience motion sickness while using their phones during a journey. The feature places a small bubble overlay on the screen that moves with the vehicle. This is designed to reduce the mismatch between what the eyes see and what the body feels.
Motion Assist will be available on phones running Android 17. Users can turn it on automatically or add it to Quick Settings. They can also customize the bubble’s appearance, including its shape, color, and opacity.
Another major addition is Guided vision in Gemini Live. The feature is designed with blind and low-vision users in mind. It allows users to share their phone camera with Gemini and receive spoken descriptions of what is around them.
See Also:Android Pulse: What Is the New Google App in the Play Store?
Guided vision can help users read small text, understand menus, or identify objects. Gemini can also provide voice instructions if the camera is not positioned correctly. It can tell users to move the camera, reframe the view, or center an object. The feature is coming to phones running Android 9 and newer in regions where Gemini is available.
Google is also making collaboration easier through Google Keep and Google Messages. Users can create or edit notes and lists directly inside a conversation. This can be useful for grocery lists, travel plans, and other shared tasks. People in the chat can view, edit, and add information without switching between apps. The rollout has started in Google Messages.
Finally, Google Messages is getting more customization options through Chat themes. Users can choose different backgrounds, including their own photos, and customize the colors of their conversations. The text bubbles can automatically match the selected background, or users can choose their own colors.
These new features show Google’s focus on making Android more useful in everyday situations. The September Android Drop combines practical tools, accessibility improvements, and personalization options to give users more control over how they use their devices.

items.author: JEHANZEB ABBASI
items.content:
Dr Uzma Khan on Wednesday filed a second contempt of court petition before the Supreme Court over alleged noncompliance with its August 18 order allowing former prime minister Imran Khan to communicate digitally with his sons and meet his sisters weekly.
The petition named Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and four other officials as respondents, alleging that the court’s directives had once again not been implemented. According to the petition, Imran had been denied a meeting with his sisters on September 1 and had been unable to communicate with his sons since March.
The petition was filed by Dr Uzma, sister of the incarcerated former premier, through SC Advocate Uzair Karamat Bhandari under Articles 187 and 204 of the Constitution. It sought contempt proceedings against the respondents and implementation of the apex court’s August 18 order.
The petition argued that, according to a Supreme Court judgment, responsibility for ensuring compliance with a court order rested with the chief executive, namely the Prime Minister’s Office. It asked the court to apply the principle laid down in the Yousuf Raza Gilani contempt of court case to the present matter and ensure implementation of its August 18 order.
The respondents included Rawalpindi Central Jail (Adiala) Superintendent Sajid Baig, Punjab Inspector General of Prisons Mian Salik Jalal, Ministry of Interior Secretary Ahmed Sarwar Raza and Islamabad Capital Territory Chief Commissioner Sohail Ashraf.
The petition alleged that Imran’s sisters — Dr Uzma Khan, Noreen Niazi and Aleema Khan — and his cousin Qasim Zaman had been barred from meeting him despite the Supreme Court’s directions.
It further alleged that no arrangements had been made to facilitate telephone conversations between Imran and his sons, Kasim Khan and Sulaiman Khan, twice a week as directed by the court.
Also Read: SC rejects second plea for early hearing of Imran’s hospital transfer contempt case
The petition asked the Supreme Court to “direct and/or take all appropriate steps” to implement its August 18 order, particularly the directions concerning weekly meetings between Imran and his sisters and cousin, as well as twice-weekly phone calls with his sons.
Two separate miscellaneous applications were also filed seeking permission to place additional documents on record in support of the contempt petition.
The latest petition followed an earlier contempt case over the government’s failure to comply with the Supreme Court’s August 18 order concerning Imran’s medical treatment.
The SC had ordered that Imran be transferred to Shifa International Hospital for examination and treatment by a multidisciplinary medical board. It had also directed the government to facilitate weekly meetings between him and his family.
Instead, Imran had been taken to the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences on August 21 for a medical examination and had later been returned to Adiala Jail after doctors declared him “medically fit”.
Information Minister Attaullah Tarar had said the decision to take Imran to the government-run hospital had been prompted by the security situation involving Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) workers outside the facility and along the route to Shifa International Hospital. The move had prompted the PTI to file a contempt petition before the Supreme Court on August 22.
The petition had been filed by Dr Uzma, Advocate Uzair Bhandari and PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja. PTI had later resubmitted it after addressing objections raised by the Supreme Court registrar, with the apex court fixing September 16 for its hearing.

Pakistan Signs Key Cybersecurity Agreement with Saudi Arabia
The agreement aims to improve cooperation between Pakistan and Saudi Arabia in protecting cyberspace and safeguarding the critical interests of both countries. It will also create opportunities for the two countries to work together against growing cyber threats.

Cybersecurity has become an increasingly important area of cooperation as governments, businesses and public services rely more heavily on digital systems. Stronger coordination can help countries respond more effectively to cyberattacks and other digital security risks.

The agreement also reflects Pakistan and Saudi Arabia’s efforts to expand their cooperation in the technology sector. Through closer collaboration, the two countries aim to contribute to stronger cybersecurity practices and promote international cooperation in protecting digital infrastructure.
The new partnership will provide a framework for continued engagement between the relevant cybersecurity authorities of Pakistan and Saudi Arabia. It could also help both sides build stronger technical capabilities and prepare for future cyber threats.

items.author: Anjali Jain
items.content:
Bharti Group-backed satcom services provider Eutelsat OneWeb has sought the immediate grant of security approval for its low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite constellation, which would take it closer to commercially launching its services in India.
Many of OneWeb’s satellites are nearing the end of their operational lives and could become useless if there are further delays in launching its services in India, the Economic Times reported, citing sources.
The company has been awaiting security approval for more than 18 months after conducting its security compliance demonstration in January 2025.
OneWeb has informed the DoT that it submitted all the required data and information related to the security demonstration and responded to additional queries raised by law enforcement agencies. However, the approval is yet to come, the report said.
Questions sent to OneWeb remained unanswered till the time of publication. The story will be updated on receiving a response.
The clearance covers requirements related to lawful interception, network monitoring, and the localisation of critical network functions.
OneWeb’s Long Wait
OneWeb was the first satcom operator to secure a GMPCS licence in India, receiving the permit from the DoT in August 2021. The company was initially looking to launch its services in the country in 2022.
However, its rollout has faced repeated delays due to the Russia-Ukraine war, which disrupted the launch of its satellites, and the wait for approvals from Indian authorities, the report said.
The company subsequently received authorisation from IN-SPACe in November 2023 to provide the capacity of its satellite constellation in India.
OneWeb has established the necessary ground infrastructure, including gateways in Mehsana, Gujarat, and Thoothukudi, Tamil Nadu, as well as two points of presence in Mumbai and Chennai.
The gateways will connect with OneWeb’s global LEO satellite constellation and enable the delivery of satellite broadband services in India.
OneWeb operates a global constellation of more than 600 LEO satellites. ISRO launched 72 OneWeb satellites across two dedicated LVM3 missions in October 2022 and March 2023.
The report said OneWeb is replacing some satellites that have completed their operational lives. However, the number of operational satellites in its existing constellation could decline as more reach the end of their lives.
Even after securing security approval, OneWeb will require spectrum assignment before it can commercially launch services in India.
India’s Satcom Race
Elon Musk-led Starlink and Jio Satellite are also awaiting security clearance to commercially launch their satcom services in India.
However, the three companies are targeting different customer segments. OneWeb plans to cater primarily to businesses, while Starlink intends to offer services directly to retail consumers. Jio Satellite, meanwhile, plans to offer services through Reliance Jio’s joint venture with Luxembourg-based SES, which operates a medium Earth orbit satellite constellation.
Reliance Industries is also said to be evaluating a multi-billion-dollar investment in its own LEO satellite constellation. The conglomerate is exploring both organic and inorganic expansion opportunities, including possible acquisitions of satellite companies with existing orbital slots and infrastructure.
Last month, Starlink reapplied to IN-SPACe for authorisation for its second-generation constellation comprising nearly 30,000 satellites, which will include direct-to-device connectivity capabilities.

items.title: Volume Transaksi INDODAX Naik ke Rp8,7 Triliun di Tengah Aktivitas Pasar Kripto yang Menguat
items.summary:
Aktivitas perdagangan aset kripto di Indonesia mulai kembali meningkat pada Agustus 2026. Volume transaksi INDODAX tercatat mencapai sekitar Rp8,7 triliun, naik sekitar 16 persen dibandingkan Juli yang berada di kisaran Rp7,5 triliun. Kenaikan tersebut terjadi ketika pasar kripto global menunjukkan penguatan di sejumlah aset utama.
Di sisi lain, pertumbuhan volume transaksi INDODAX terjadi ketika nilai transaksi aset kripto nasional pada Juli justru mengalami penurunan. Berdasarkan data yang disampaikan INDODAX, nilai transaksi kripto nasional pada Juli mencapai Rp20,52 triliun, turun 28,2 persen dari Rp28,58 triliun pada Juni. Pada periode yang sama, jumlah konsumen aset keuangan digital Indonesia meningkat menjadi 22,93 juta akun.
Dengan volume sekitar Rp7,5 triliun pada Juli, transaksi INDODAX menyumbang sekitar 36,5 persen dari nilai transaksi kripto nasional pada bulan tersebut. Memasuki Agustus, peningkatan menjadi Rp8,7 triliun menunjukkan aktivitas di platform tersebut kembali
items.author: Christopher Louis
items.content:
Aktivitas perdagangan aset kripto di Indonesia mulai kembali meningkat pada Agustus 2026. Volume transaksi INDODAX tercatat mencapai sekitar Rp8,7 triliun, naik sekitar 16 persen dibandingkan Juli yang berada di kisaran Rp7,5 triliun. Kenaikan tersebut terjadi ketika pasar kripto global menunjukkan penguatan di sejumlah aset utama.
Di sisi lain, pertumbuhan volume transaksi INDODAX terjadi ketika nilai transaksi aset kripto nasional pada Juli justru mengalami penurunan. Berdasarkan data yang disampaikan INDODAX, nilai transaksi kripto nasional pada Juli mencapai Rp20,52 triliun, turun 28,2 persen dari Rp28,58 triliun pada Juni. Pada periode yang sama, jumlah konsumen aset keuangan digital Indonesia meningkat menjadi 22,93 juta akun.
Dengan volume sekitar Rp7,5 triliun pada Juli, transaksi INDODAX menyumbang sekitar 36,5 persen dari nilai transaksi kripto nasional pada bulan tersebut. Memasuki Agustus, peningkatan menjadi Rp8,7 triliun menunjukkan aktivitas di platform tersebut kembali meningkat, meski angka tersebut belum dapat menggambarkan keseluruhan kondisi pasar kripto Indonesia.
Baca Juga: SK hynix Prediksi Krisis Memori Berlanjut hingga 2030, Harga Tetap Tinggi
Bitcoin Menguat, Altcoin Ikut Bergerak
Chief Marketing Officer INDODAX Aloysia Dian menilai peningkatan volume transaksi pada Agustus mencerminkan aktivitas pasar yang mulai kembali menguat. Menurutnya, pergerakan Bitcoin turut menarik perhatian investor, sementara pertumbuhan jumlah investor menunjukkan minat terhadap aset kripto masih bertahan.
Data CoinMarketCap yang dikutip INDODAX menunjukkan Bitcoin menguat 24,36 persen dalam satu bulan. Sejumlah aset lain bahkan mencatat kenaikan lebih tinggi, seperti Ethereum sebesar 32,01 persen, XRP 28,22 persen, Solana 41,33 persen, dan Hyperliquid (HYPE) 61,53 persen. Namun, kenaikan tersebut juga menunjukkan bahwa pemulihan sentimen tidak berarti tingkat risiko setiap aset menjadi sama.
Aktivitas Naik Bukan Berarti Risiko Menurun
Peningkatan volume perdagangan dapat menjadi indikasi pasar yang lebih aktif, tetapi tidak otomatis menunjukkan kondisi yang sepenuhnya positif bagi investor. Pergerakan harga kripto tetap sangat dipengaruhi volatilitas, likuiditas, kondisi ekonomi global, serta arah kebijakan moneter.
Aloysia juga mengingatkan bahwa penguatan pasar dapat berubah mengikuti perkembangan ekonomi dan kebijakan global. Karena itu, kenaikan aktivitas transaksi pada Agustus sebaiknya tidak langsung diterjemahkan sebagai sinyal untuk meningkatkan eksposur. Investor tetap perlu mempertimbangkan karakteristik masing-masing aset, melakukan riset, serta memahami risiko sebelum mengambil keputusan.

items.author: Rizwana Omer
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Khyber Pakhtunkhwa has launched an International Skills Certification Programme, described by officials as the province’s first initiative built specifically to equip young people with internationally recognized skills certifications, aimed at improving job prospects both inside Pakistan and abroad.
The programme, run under the NH-P Tobacco Cess Development Programme, was formalized through a Memorandum of Understanding signed with Pak-Austria Fachhochschule Institute of Applied Sciences and Technology in Haripur.
What The Programme Actually Covers
The training list is broad, spanning cybersecurity, artificial intelligence, mobile phone repair, plumbing, general technical skills, solar panel installation, e-commerce, and international languages. It also includes IOSH, NEBOSH and OSHA certifications, three globally recognized occupational health and safety qualifications commonly required for construction, industrial and overseas employment roles.
That mix matters because it spans two very different labour markets at once. Cybersecurity and AI training targets Pakistan’s growing digital economy and remote-work opportunities, while trades like plumbing, solar installation and the OSHA-style safety certifications are aimed squarely at overseas employment, particularly in Gulf countries where such certifications are frequently prerequisites for skilled labour visas.
Project Director Hashmat Ali said more than two dozen technical, digital and health-related courses are being introduced under the initiative, positioning it as a considerably wider offering than typical single-sector vocational programmes run in the province before.
Scholarships Tied To Germany And Austria
A specific component of the programme offers scholarships in robotics and cybersecurity in collaboration with Germany and Austria. Neither the scale of these scholarships nor the number of seats available was disclosed at the signing ceremony, so it’s not yet clear how many students will actually benefit from this component versus the broader certification training.
The European connection isn’t incidental. Pak-Austria Fachhochschule was itself established through a Rs250 billion government initiative to build technology-focused universities in partnership with China and several European countries, with a founding mandate centered on artificial intelligence, engineering and applied sciences. The institute has run on a campus in Haripur since 2020 and currently serves around 5,000 students, giving it existing infrastructure and academic partnerships to draw on for a programme like this one.
Who’s Backing The Initiative
Former National Assembly Speaker Asad Qaiser, speaking at the MoU-signing ceremony, said global-standard training and international education opportunities would help empower youth and support regional economic development. MPA Rangez Khan said the initiative would promote quality education, practical skills and improved employment outcomes.
Neither official’s remarks included specific targets, such as how many students the programme aims to train in its first phase or what employment outcomes will be tracked to measure success. That’s a common gap in programme launch announcements generally, and it means the real test of this initiative’s impact will come from data released once training cohorts actually begin completing courses.
Starting In Swabi, With Provincial Expansion Planned
The programme has initially launched in Swabi, with plans to expand across Khyber Pakhtunkhwa over time, according to Hashmat Ali. No timeline was given for what that expansion would look like or which districts would be next in line.
Starting in a single district before scaling is a reasonably standard approach for vocational programmes of this size, allowing implementers to work out logistics and course delivery before committing resources province-wide. Whether that expansion happens on schedule, and how quickly, will be the clearest early signal of whether this programme has the institutional backing to match its ambitious course list.
How This Fits Into KP’s Broader Skills Landscape
This isn’t the first skills initiative aimed at KP’s youth. The UNDP, working with Japan’s government and the Sarhad Rural Support Programme, ran a separate three-month vocational training programme in 2024 that equipped 700 young people, including 375 women, from Kurram and Orakzai districts with skills like cell phone repair, electrical work, plumbing and solar and UPS installation.
That earlier programme shares some overlap in subject matter, particularly around technical trades, but ran at a smaller scale and without the international certification and university partnership structure this new initiative is built around. The distinguishing feature of the NH-P programme is its pairing of vocational trades with globally recognized certifications and a formal academic institution, rather than standalone skills training delivered through an NGO partnership.
What Determines Whether This Programme Delivers
The ambition here is clear: cover a wide span of in-demand skills, attach internationally recognized certifications to them, and use tobacco cess revenue, a funding source tied to the province rather than dependent on federal allocation, to sustain it. That funding structure is worth noting on its own, since programmes reliant on provincial cess revenue tend to have more predictable continuity than those dependent on annual federal budget approval.
What isn’t yet clear is capacity. Running two dozen distinct courses, several of them requiring specialized instructors and equipment, such as cybersecurity labs or solar installation training, is a significant operational undertaking for a programme just getting off the ground in one district. How quickly Pak-Austria Fachhochschule can scale that capacity, and how many students actually complete courses and go on to secure jobs locally or abroad, will determine whether this becomes a genuine employment pipeline or another well-intentioned announcement that struggles to scale past its pilot phase.
