items.author: Dr Fahd Rehman
items.content:
A household is said to be financialised when it depends on cedit. Credit is advanced to households in the form of personal loans, auto loans, home loans, mortgages, etc. Credit advancement to households promotes consumption which, in turn, increases the import bill.
Credit advancement to households increased in the advanced economies during the 1970s and 1980s while credit expansion in the developing economies started in the 1990s and gathered pace in the early 2000s. This expansion increased the household debt-to-income ratio.
For instance, the US household debt-to-income ratio was around 100% in 2000 and it grew to 130% in 2008. Similarly, the Turkish household debt-to-income ratio grew from 7.5% in 2002 to 29.5% in 2007. Aggressive household lending contributed heavily to increase this ratio. In addition, South Korea, Malaysia, Mexico, Brazil and many East European countries experienced a growth in the household debt-to-income ratio during this time period.
Similarly, credit card loans were made easy in Pakistan in 2002. It was the beginning of a credit card culture. A new middle-class market was tapped through the relaxation of rules by the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP). As a result, the emerging middle class started to take personal loans and use credit cards to fulfil their wants. Auto loans grew around 320% from 2002 to 2007, though comparable figures of household debt-to-income ratio are not available for Pakistan.
The financialisation of household is also marked by market-based pension schemes. Market-based provision of pension replaces government-provided pension schemes. Governments used to adopt pay-as-you-go (PAYG) pension where pensioners do not contribute towards pension. When a public servant reaches the age of superannuation, he will become eligible and get pension for the rest of his/her life.
In Pakistan, the federal expenditure on pension under the PAYG scheme reached around Rs1,000 billion in FY 2026. These expenditures were around 4.2% of the total expenditure and 0.8% of GDP in FY 2026. These expenditures do not include the pension expenditure of provincial governments.
On the other hand, market-based pension requires contribution from public servants. A certain percentage is deducted from the salary of public servants and governments match same amounts in the accounts of their employees. Both of these contributions become part of employees' accounts. All these accounts are part of the pension fund managed by a team of professionals working in a pension fund company.
Such contributory pension schemes have been adopted by the governments of developed and developing economies alike. In Latin America, Chile was the forerunner in privatising the pension system. It adopted a contributory pension scheme for public servants. This scheme turned out to be costly for public servants. Fund managers used to charge around one-third of contributions as consulting, advising and asset managing fee.
Taking stock of the situation, the Chilian government has to reform the pension system to safeguard the interests of elderly and low-income individuals. Such pension schemes are relatively successful in developed countries. However, the performance of contributory pension schemes in developing countries is less than satisfactory.
In a nutshell, the financialisation of household promotes consumption through the extension of credit in various forms. Households fulfil their desires and/or wants which, in turn, creates demonstration effect. Through this effect, individuals tend to copy the spending patterns and lifestyles of the privileged class.
The demonstration effect tends to reduce savings in the economy. Hence, the financialisation of household gives rise to a long-term trend of consumption in an economy.
The writer is an independent economist and authored a book: Pakistan's Structural Economic Problems in the era of Financial Globalization

items.author: SHAMSUL ISLAM KHAN
items.content:
In the FY2026-27 budget, the government has set an ambitious tax revenue target of Rs15.264 trillion, alongside a non-tax revenue target of Rs5.336 trillion.
After the 18th Amendment, agriculture is devolved to the provinces. However, the federal government continues to maintain the Ministry of National Food Security and Research. Its record has been far from reassuring. Pakistan has repeatedly faced crises in staple commodities such as wheat and sugar, agricultural research has stagnated, food import dependence has increased, and the country is steadily shifting away from indigenous heirloom seeds towards reliance on imported seed varieties. This is alarming for national food security if other international sea chokepoints, particularly the Strait of Malacca, disrupt supplies after the Strait of Hormuz.
Pakistan's agricultural income tax regime was hailed as a landmark reform to broaden the tax base, promote tax justice and fulfil commitments under the International Monetary Fund (IMF) programme. Yet its first year has exposed a familiar reality: Pakistan's tax problem is not a shortage of laws but a chronic failure of enforcement against the ruling elites and powerful well-connected interests.
During FY2025-26, nearly 445,000 taxpayers declared Rs306 billion in agricultural income. However, provincial governments collected only Rs5.62 billion in agricultural income tax – barely 2% of the declared income. Punjab alone accounted for around 396,000 taxpayers declaring Rs293 billion, underlining the enormous untapped revenue potential. These figures expose a fundamental weakness in Pakistan's tax system. The country continues to squeeze salaried employees, documented businesses and existing taxpayers while large segments of wealth and income remain outside the effective tax net. True tax reform is not about imposing more taxes on those already paying; it is about ensuring every sector contributes according to its ability.
Politics, not policy
Agriculture contributes substantially to Pakistan's economy, yet effective taxation remains elusive because the challenge is political as much as administrative. Large landowners continue to wield significant influence in provincial assemblies, parliament and the Senate. Many absentee landlords lease out their land while continuing to benefit from government incentives intended for genuine growers.
This political economy explains why successive governments have announced reforms but struggled to implement them. Passing legislation is relatively easy; collecting taxes from influential constituencies is the real test of political will.
Protect small farmers, tax commercial agriculture
The debate has wrongly been framed as agriculture versus farmers. It is neither fair nor economically sensible to burden small cultivators already struggling with rising input costs, water shortages and climate shocks. Agricultural holdings of up to 20 acres should remain exempt from agricultural income tax. This would protect the overwhelming majority of small farmers while allowing tax authorities to concentrate on medium and large landholders, commercial farms, absentee landlords and corporate agriculture where the real revenue potential exists. Pakistan needs tax justice, not blanket taxation.
Digital enforcement instead of paper compliance
The disappointing first-year performance reflects fragmented provincial implementation, weak enforcement and outdated tax administration. Provincial governments should fully integrate digitised landholders' records with agricultural taxation. Ownership records, irrigation water usage footprints, databases, crop reports, procurement records, banking data and satellite imagery can all be cross-checked to identify discrepancies between the declared income and actual agricultural production. Risk-based audits should replace indiscriminate inspections, focusing only on taxpayers whose declared income is inconsistent with their landholding size or crop output.
Collect tax at the first point of sale
Instead of relying entirely on the Patwari system and voluntary declarations, provincial governments should strengthen compliance through adjustable withholding tax at the first point of sale.
Cotton ginning factories, sugar mills, rice shellers, modern rice mills, tobacco companies, grain procurement agencies, fruit and vegetable arrivals in mandis, exporters, feed manufacturers and other major buyers should deduct a modest adjustable withholding tax against future agricultural income tax liabilities. Such a system would significantly reduce evasion while simplifying tax collection without increasing rates.
Visible benefits build compliance
Tax compliance improves when taxpayers see where their money is spent. A fixed share of agricultural income tax collected in each district should remain there to finance rural roads, waterways, irrigation infrastructure, schools, healthcare facilities, agricultural research and extension services. Farmers are far more willing to pay taxes when they witness direct improvements in their own communities rather than lavish spending on provincial chief ministers.
Recognition also matters. Every district should publish an annual roll of honour recognising the highest compliant agricultural taxpayers, awarding medals through chief ministers, ministers and commissioners. Public acknowledgement reinforces the principle that paying taxes is responsible citizenship rather than a penalty.
Unified taxation means fairness
Pakistan's fragmented tax system has created deep inequities. The country's documented sectors continue to shoulder a disproportionate burden while politically influential groups remain lightly taxed. Unified taxation and tax justice are far more important for widening the tax base than repeatedly squeezing already compliant sectors, exporters and the salaried class. Income tax reform must focus on ending unjustified exemptions, strengthening enforcement and bringing the "big fish" into the tax net. Agriculture cannot remain an exception indefinitely if Pakistan hopes to restore fiscal sustainability.
The real reform
The first year of the unified agricultural income tax regime has shown that Pakistan's challenge is not designing tax policy but enforcing it fairly. A system that protects small farmers, targets large landholdings, leverages digital technology, collects taxes efficiently through market transactions, and ensures visible local benefits offers a practical path forward. The government must now answer a difficult question: will it continue taxing those who are the easiest to tax, or will it finally demonstrate the political courage to tax those with the greatest capacity to pay? The credibility of Pakistan's tax reforms – and the promise of genuine tax justice – depends on that answer.
THE WRITER IS A FORMER VICE PRESIDENT OF KCCI, FORMER BOARD MEMBER OF REAP AND AN INTERNATIONAL TRADE EXPERT

“The notification issued by the Sindh Building Control Authority in pursuance of the Order dated 22.01.2019, regarding the immediate ban on conversion (change of land use), is hereby withdrawn with immediate effect,” said the notification.

items.author: Muhammad Saleem Jhandeer
items.content:
The Sindh Master Plan Authority has lifted a seven-year ban on the conversion of residential plots for commercial use following recent court decisions, while a new formula for distributing infrastructure fees collected on changes in land use has also come into effect.
In light of recent decisions of the Supreme Court and the Federal Constitutional Court, the Authority has withdrawn the notification imposing the ban on conversion of residential plots for commercial purposes across the province, including Karachi and Hyderabad, since 2019.
“The notification issued by the Sindh Building Control Authority in pursuance of the Order dated 22.01.2019, regarding the immediate ban on conversion (change of land use), is hereby withdrawn with immediate effect,” said the notification.
Read: SC places ban on conversion of residential, amenity plots
The process of changing land use, which had remained suspended for seven years, has consequently been restored with immediate effect.
According to the notification, the Court’s decisions of 2018 and 2019, as well as the Sindh Building Control Authority’s restraining notification, have been declared void and withdrawn. All relevant institutions have been directed to implement the court orders in letter and spirit.
Officials clarified that withdrawal of the ban did not mean that every residential plot would automatically become commercial, adding that any change in land use would still require compliance with relevant laws, zoning rules and the master plan, as well as a formal no-objection certificate and approval from the competent authority.
Senior Director of the Sindh Master Plan Authority Shakeel Siddiqui said commercialisation would be allowed on Beach Avenue Road, Khayaban-e-Saadi, Khayaban-e-Rumi, Nishtar Road/Dhoraji Road, Alamgir Road, Shahrah-e-Noor Jehan, Stadium Road, Shahrah-e-Usman, Tipu Sultan Road, Shahrah-e-Humayun, Shahrah-e-Faisal, Tariq Road, Rashid Minhas Road, University Road, Shahrah-e-Pakistan, Nazimabad A Road, North Nazimabad 300-foot Road, Shahrah-e-Jahangir, Khayaban-e-Iqbal, Khayaban-e-Jami, Khalid bin Walid Road, Jamaluddin Afghani Road, Allama Iqbal Road, Sir Syed Ahmed Road, Shaheed-e-Millat Road and Chaudhry Khaliquzzaman Road.
The court has also made it clear that amenity plots, including parks, hospitals, schools, mosques, playgrounds and graveyards, cannot be used for commercial or residential purposes under any circumstances.
Also Read: KDA flouts top court ban on land commercialisation
The ban on commercial use of residential land in Karachi had left several projects of builders and the business community pending for several years.
New fee-sharing formula
Alongside lifting of the ban, a new formula for distributing infrastructure fees collected for changes in land use has also been introduced and a notification issued.
Siddiqui told Express Tribune that the Local Government and Housing, Town Planning Department had prepared the new formula for distributing infrastructure fees collected by the Sindh Master Plan Authority among various local government bodies and authorities.
Under the notification, all previous orders and notifications regarding the distribution of the fees have been cancelled.
According to the formula, districts and divisions across the province have essentially been divided into three categories for the collection and distribution of the fees.
In Karachi division and Hyderabad district, 45 per cent of the infrastructure fee collected for a change in land use will go to the relevant Town Municipal Corporations, 25pc to the Sindh Master Plan Authority, 20pc to the Water and Sewerage Corporation and 10pc to the metropolitan or municipal corporation.
A separate mechanism has been devised for urban and rural areas of the other divisional headquarters — Mirpurkhas, Shaheed Benazirabad, Sukkur and Larkana.
Within the jurisdiction of a municipal corporation, the fee will be distributed according to the same pattern as in Karachi and Hyderabad: 45pc to Town Municipal Corporations, 25pc to the Sindh Master Plan Authority, 20pc to the Water and Sewerage Corporation and 10pc to the relevant municipal corporation.
In areas where there is no corporation jurisdiction, 75pc of the total fee will go to the relevant municipal committee, town committee or district council, while the remaining 25pc will be transferred to the Master Plan Authority.
Chairman of the Association of Builders and Developers (Abad) Hassan Bakshi welcomed the decision, saying the real estate sector had breathed a sigh of relief.
“I welcome this decision,” he said, adding that allowing commercialisation indiscriminately without proper planning and improvements in infrastructure could further affect Karachi’s traffic, water, sewerage and other civic services.
He said commercialisation had been suspended in Karachi at a time when it was allowed across the rest of the country.
“Commercialisation on the 26 declared roads will create employment opportunities and increase options for ordinary buyers,” he added.

items.author: M Yasir
items.content:
Pakistan has nearly 3 million full-time and part-time freelancers who earned more than $1.76 billion through digital services during the last financial year, Governor Sindh Syed Muhammad Nehal Hashmi said.
Addressing the first National Recognition Ceremony organised by the Pakistan Freelancers Association (PAFLA), Hashmi described freelancers as an emerging digital workforce and an important source of foreign exchange for Pakistan.
He said Pakistan’s large youth population could play a major role in the country’s economic future if equipped with modern IT skills, entrepreneurship and market-oriented training.
Hashmi said the federal government, in collaboration with the Governor House, was implementing skill-development initiatives for Sindh’s youth to improve their employment and entrepreneurial opportunities.
He also highlighted the government’s target of increasing Pakistan’s IT exports to $25 billion by 2030. He urged young people to develop skills aligned with emerging technologies and compete in international markets.
The governor also urged youth to use the Digital Youth Hub, launched under the Prime Minister’s Youth Program, for opportunities in education, skills, employment and entrepreneurship.
Minister of State and Special Assistant to the Prime Minister Fahd Haroon said the government was supporting initiatives aimed at expanding freelancing and increasing youth participation in the digital economy.
PAFLA President and CEO Dr. Imran Batada said skills in areas such as artificial intelligence, data analytics and cybersecurity would become increasingly important as technology changes the nature of work.
At the ceremony, Governor Hashmi presented shields to 45 Pakistani freelancers in recognition of their international work and contribution to the country’s digital economy.

items.author: Business Desk
items.content:
The textile industry has welcomed a Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) crackdown on importers misdeclaring fabric to obtain duty and tax exemptions under the Export Facilitation Scheme (EFS).
The All Pakistan Textile Mills Association (APTMA) said Pakistan Customs has started stricter physical inspections and laboratory testing of fabric consignments imported under the scheme.
APTMA said greige fabric was removed from the EFS in August 2025, but such imports had continued through alleged misdeclaration, depriving the government of revenue and hurting local fabric manufacturers.
According to APTMA, laboratory tests of some consignments reportedly found food colouring instead of proper dyeing, leading Customs to record violations.
The association urged the FBR to apply physical inspections and laboratory testing to all fabric consignments imported under the EFS across the country, including through dry ports.
APTMA also called for verification of importers’ manufacturing facilities. It said some firms allegedly lack the machinery needed to process fabric and may instead be diverting imported material into the domestic market.
The association urged authorities to suspend the licenses of companies found violating the rules and initiate legal proceedings where required.
APTMA Chairman Kamran Arshad said continued enforcement was necessary to prevent the EFS from being misused for tax evasion and to protect local manufacturers that have invested in production and employment.
The association said it supports further FBR and Customs action to ensure the scheme remains focused on genuine export-related activity.

items.author: Business Desk
items.content:
The Central Development Working Party (CDWP) has approved or recommended five development projects worth Rs. 60.259 billion, covering health, roads, science and technology, housing and water supply.
The biggest project discussed was the Rs. 29 billion water supply scheme for Gwadar Town from Mirani Dam. It was also referred to ECNEC.
Ahsan Iqbal directed the Balochistan government to study wastewater treatment in Gwadar to prevent sewage from polluting the sea. He allowed the project to move to the bidding stage but said no contract should be awarded until ECNEC approval.
The meeting approved three projects worth Rs. 11.714 billion, while two projects worth Rs. 48.545 billion were referred to the Executive Committee of the National Economic Council (ECNEC).
The approved projects include the establishment of a Medical and Nursing College in Gilgit at a revised cost of Rs. 4.924 billion. Ahsan Iqbal stressed the need to complete the project, which was initiated in 2017 but faced delays due to funding constraints.
The CDWP also approved the establishment of a National Defence University (NDU) FCS Campus at Defence Complex Islamabad at a cost of Rs. 2.753 billion.
Another approved project is the 53.4-kilometre road from Zera to Daboori in Orakzai District, costing Rs. 4.037 billion. The planning minister directed authorities to release the remaining funds before winter to help complete the long-delayed project, which dates back to 2016.
The Rs. 19.545 billion Karachi Neighborhood Improvement Project was referred to ECNEC. The project will be financed through foreign funding and the Sindh government’s development program.

At least ​seven people died and 23 were missing after a ferry carrying around 270 passengers and crew capsized ‌off North Cyprus on Sunday, leaving survivors clinging to its overturned hull.
The privately owned ferry left the port of Kyrenia at 12:30pm (0930 GMT) and immediately started taking on water for an unknown reason, authorities said. It was heading for the Turkish port of Tasucu in Mersin province ​in the eastern Mediterranean.
The disaster occurred just off the coast of Kyrenia, a popular holiday resort for both ​locals and tourists. The ferry involved, a catamaran, was one of several shuttle sea services that ⁠link North Cyprus with Turkey daily.
Turkish Cypriot leader Tufan Erhurman said 237 people had been rescued alive, while seven people ​had died and 23 people were still being sought.
“We have reached 237 people alive. However, we have also recovered seven ​people who lost their lives. We are deeply saddened by this,” Erhurman told CNN Turk in a live broadcast.
Video footage showed people in red life jackets sitting or standing on top of the overturned vessel as authorities scrambled coastguard and private vessels for assistance to bring them to ​shore.
"We have still not been able to reach 23 people. Search and rescue teams are working very intensively to find ​them," Erhurman said.

"If there are people still inside the vessel, reaching them does not appear easy at the moment. Efforts are being made ‌using ⁠other technologies to reach them as well."
Major rescue operation underway
Cyprus was battered by fierce storms on Saturday, with one person dying after his sailboat crashed onto rocks in rough seas in the island's south-east.
Asked about the cause of the capsize, Erhurman noted the storm on Saturday, but said the weather was considered suitable for travel.
"There is a great sense of shock here. ​This is not something we ​have experienced before... we ⁠are extremely saddened. Everyone is doing everything they can and making every effort," he said, speaking from the crisis centre set up in the area.
Turkish Cypriot Prime Minister Unal Ustel said ​a major rescue operation was underway.
"Our sole priority right now is human life. All institutions ​of our state, ⁠our security forces, our health teams and our search and rescue elements are on the ground in full coordination," he told reporters after chairing a crisis management committee.
The Turkish Cypriot Interior Ministry said the passenger ferry 'FILOJET' was carrying 259 passengers and eight crew, ⁠and it ​began taking on water about four nautical miles off Kyrenia while sailing ​from Kyrenia to Tasucu in Turkey.
Four Turkish Cypriot coast guard vessels and a civilian passenger boat were deployed to the scene, along with five Turkish coastguard ​vessels and two helicopters, the ministry statement said.

items.author: Business Desk
items.content:
The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has pushed Pakistan to sharply restrict the practice of government agencies directly awarding contracts to state-owned companies.
The lender says such deals should only be allowed in limited and clearly justified circumstances.
The dispute has delayed Pakistan’s new public procurement rules, which are meant to replace the Public Procurement Rules 2004.
Under its Governance and Corruption Diagnostic Assessment action plan, Pakistan was required to approve and notify the Public Procurement Regulatory Authority (PPRA) Rules 2026 by June 2026.
The deadline was missed as the government and IMF differed over provisions dealing with direct contracts to state-owned enterprises (SOEs).
Contractors, beneficial owners, owners and directors facing certain court proceedings that could lead to bankruptcy, as well as those with previous convictions, could be disqualified from bidding for government procurement.
The biggest disagreement is over Rule 32-F, which governs direct contracting between government bodies and SOEs.
The IMF has proposed that government procuring agencies should not normally award contracts directly to state-owned professional, autonomous or semi-autonomous organisations for goods, works, services or consultancy.
It wants such contracts limited to exceptional cases, including projects involving urgent, geographically scattered or remote works and services where a direct award is considered to be in the public interest.
Where specialised portions of a project need outside assistance, the IMF has suggested that subcontracting should not exceed 40% of the total work.
Pakistan has accepted the 40 percent ceiling but has proposed allowing the relevant authority to change financial limits under the rule from time to time.
Under the IMF’s proposed framework, exceeding the permitted subcontracting limit would be considered a material deviation and could fall under rules dealing with collusive, coercive, corrupt, fraudulent and obstructive conduct.
The IMF has also called for greater disclosure when a direct contract is approved.

items.author: Business Desk
items.content:
The Pakistan Telecommunication Access Providers Association (PTAPA) has warned that expanding direct government contracts to state-owned companies could weaken the private sector and eventually create more loss-making entities like Pakistan International Airlines (PIA).
PTAPA represents 26 companies, including Cybernet, Nayatel, PTCL, Wateen and Multinet. PTAPA President Dr Shahid Farooq raised the issue in a letter to Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb, Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal and IT and Telecom Minister Shaza Fatima Khawaja.
The association wants the government to remove Clause 42(f) of the Public Procurement Rules 2004, which allows government-owned organizations and state-owned enterprises (SOEs) to contract directly with other government entities without competitive bidding.
PTAPA said the arrangement has enabled SOEs to secure a growing number of IT and telecom projects over the past five years. Private firms have invested heavily in telecom infrastructure and digital services over the past two decades, but direct government contracting is now creating an uneven playing field.
It also warned that state-backed entities can have advantages that private companies do not, including government support, regulatory concessions and preferential treatment. The president said the reduced competition can also weaken incentives for companies to improve efficiency, develop new technologies and invest in research and development.
PTAPA is of the view that organizations operating without sufficient competitive pressure can become inefficient and eventually turn into financial burdens on the state.
It pointed to PIA, Pakistan Steel Mills and distribution companies as examples of state entities that have struggled financially and operationally.
PTAPA also alleged that some SOEs subsequently subcontract projects to private companies without competitive bidding. The association has therefore called for SOEs to compete with private companies on equal terms for government-funded IT, telecom and digital projects.
It said restoring open competition would help protect private-sector investment, encourage innovation and prevent the government from crowding out businesses that contribute through taxes, employment and investment.

The firing took place in village Sheikh Gulab, within the limits of Jalhu police station, police said.
Following the incident, a heavy contingent of police was dispatched to the area on the directives of Dadu SSP retired Capt Saddam Hussain Khaskheli. Police cordoned off the area and brought the situation under control.
Khaskheli described the incident as a result of an old personal enmity. He said weapons used in the incident had been recovered and police were conducting raids to apprehend those involved.
Read: Five killed in clan clash as Junejo feud turns deadly
He said the eight people killed in the firing were identified as Fida Hussain, Zulfiqar alias Watni, Mohammad Bachal, Sultan, Manzoor, Irshad alias Hajin, Gulbahar and Didar Chandio.
Khaskheli added that two other people, Ghulam Qadir Chandio and Mumtaz Chandio, were injured and shifted to hospital after being rescued from the scene. The bodies of the deceased were also taken to hospital for the required legal formalities.
Hyderabad DIG Tariq Razzaq Khan Dharejo and the Dadu SSP directed a heavy police contingent to remain deployed in the area. Police said the area had been cordoned off and the situation brought under control.
Further action was underway, with police saying strict legal action would be taken against those involved in the incident.
Meanwhile, Sindh Chief Minister Syed Murad Ali Shah took notice of the killings in village Dano Chandio in Dadu and expressed grief over the loss of lives and sympathy with the bereaved families.
He sought a report from the inspector general of police and ordered immediate investigations into the incident and the arrest of those responsible.
“Law cannot be allowed to be taken into one’s own hands. The culprits must be brought to justice at all costs,” Shah said while directing the police to ensure indiscriminate action against all those involved.
Also Read: Cop among 18 killed in armed clash between bandit gangs in Sindh’s Katcha area
Separately, Sindh Home Minister Ziaul Hasan Lanjar also took notice of the clash between the two groups and sought an immediate report from the Hyderabad DIG.
He directed the police to maintain law and order in the area and bring the situation under control.
Lanjar also directed authorities to ensure immediate medical treatment for the injured and hand over the bodies of the deceased to their heirs after completion of legal formalities.

items.author: ProPK Staff
items.content:
Suzuki has launched the Pakistan-made Alto and Every in Brunei, marking the first time the Japanese automaker has exported mini-vehicle models from an overseas production base with the same body size and engine displacement specifications as its kei cars in Japan.
The two vehicles are produced by Pak Suzuki Motor Company and will be sold in Brunei through Boustead Sdn. Bhd., Suzuki’s local distributor.
Boustead announced the launch on August 27 during an event celebrating the 50th anniversary of its appointment as a Suzuki distributor.
The ceremony was held at the Airport Mall Atrium in Bandar Seri Begawan, the capital of Brunei.
Pakistan-Made Alto and Every Join Suzuki Brunei Lineup
The introduction of the Alto and Every expands Suzuki’s passenger vehicle range in Brunei.
Both models follow the compact dimensions and engine displacement specifications associated with Japanese mini-vehicles.
Suzuki said this is the first time it has exported vehicles with these specifications from one of its production bases outside Japan.
Pak Suzuki will manufacture the vehicles in Pakistan before exporting them to Brunei.
Suzuki Motorcycles Also Coming to Brunei
Boustead also announced plans to begin selling Suzuki motorcycles in Brunei.
Motorcycle sales are expected to start around autumn 2026.
Suzuki plans to introduce several of its larger motorcycles aimed mainly at touring and recreational riders.
The planned lineup includes the Hayabusa, GSX-S1000GX and GSX-8R.
Senior Officials Attend Launch Ceremony
Around 120 people attended the anniversary and launch event.
The guests included Yutaka Kikuta, Ambassador of Japan to Brunei, and Lim Jin Lee, Executive Manager of Boustead.
Suzuki was represented by Masafumi Harano, Managing Officer and Executive General Manager for Automobile Marketing in Asia, Latin America and Oceania.
Takashi Ise, Managing Officer and Executive General Manager of Motorcycle Operations, also attended.
Representatives from distributors and business partners were present as well.
Brunei Has High Vehicle Ownership
Brunei has a high rate of vehicle ownership per person, while cars remain an important part of daily life.
Residents widely use private vehicles for commuting to work, travelling to school and other routine transportation needs.
Boustead already imports and sells several Suzuki models in the country.
Its current lineup focuses mainly on compact and easy-to-drive vehicles, particularly SUVs.
These include the Jimny 3-Door, Jimny 5-Door, Ertiga and Fronx.
Via: Suzuki Global

items.author: Reuters
items.content:
NASA's new flagship astronomical observatory was launched into space from Florida on Sunday on a mission to probe some of the biggest ​mysteries in astrophysics and cosmology.
The Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope, a roughly $4 billion project, was carried aloft from NASA's Kennedy Space Center aboard a SpaceX  Falcon ‌Heavy rocket.
The telescope is designed to investigate cosmic enigmas such as dark energy and dark matter, while also testing gravity at vast scales and searching for exoplanets, as planets beyond our solar system are called.
There were some weather concerns ahead of the launch but the rocket carried the telescope into space through blue skies and some scattered clouds.
Roman will travel through space toward an orbital location called Lagrange Point 2, situated about a million miles (1.6 million km) ​from Earth. Its mission is planned for five years, though the U.S. space agency said the telescope may have enough fuel for five additional years.
Roman will build on ​the capabilities of other orbiting observatories such as the James Webb Space Telescope, launched in 2021, and the Hubble Space Telescope, launched in 1990.
"It will be ⁠as if Hubble and James Webb kind of peered through a keyhole at the universe, while Nancy Grace Roman will kick the door down," Nicola Fox, chief of NASA's Science Mission ​Directorate, told reporters on Saturday.
Read More: New NASA telescope to probe dark energy, dark matter and exoplanets
"Roman has broadly the same sensitivity and sharpness of vision as Hubble, but we survey the sky much faster," Julie McEnery, Roman's senior project scientist at NASA's Goddard ​Space Flight Center in Maryland, told reporters at a briefing in July.
McEnery said one month of Roman observations can survey our entire home galaxy.
"One month of observations to survey our Milky Way galaxy would take about a century with Hubble," McEnery said.
Wide angle and zoom lenses
Webb has provided a new understanding of the early history of the universe, finding among other things that primordial galaxies formed sooner and were bigger than previously known. ​Webb is capable of looking across vast distances and back into deep time, because of the time it takes light to travel.
Roman instead is able to take panoramic views. NASA likens ​Roman to a camera's wide-angle lens and Webb to a zoom lens.
"Webb is designed to be able to probe very deeply and with exquisite sensitivity into the universe, so we can find rare things in ‌the early ⁠universe," McEnery said, while Roman offers "the large vision that complements the deep views that Webb provides."
Roman will help in the understanding of two mysterious cosmic components — dark energy and dark matter — by creating the most comprehensive 3D map of the universe to date. Its main survey, to take more than a year to complete, will cover more than two billion galaxies.
The Big Bang event roughly 13.8 billion years ago initiated the universe, and it has been expanding ever since. Scientists in 1998 disclosed that this expansion was actually accelerating, with an invisible force called dark energy as the ​hypothesized reason.
The universe's contents include ordinary matter — stars, ​planets, gas, dust and all the familiar ⁠stuff on Earth — as well as dark matter and dark energy. Ordinary matter represents perhaps 5% of the contents. Dark matter, known through its gravitational influences on galaxies and stars, may represent about 27%. Dark energy may represent about 68%.
Using Roman to gauge dark matter's pull and ​dark energy's push across the universe will bring scientists closer than ever before to solving both mysteries, according to NASA.
Roman also will conduct ​one of the most ⁠comprehensive searches ever for exoplanets. It is expected to discover thousands of new ones and provide the first statistical census of planetary systems similar to our own.
"One of the most exciting aspects of Roman is its discovery potential. Historically, major astronomical observatories have often made their most important breakthroughs in areas that scientists did not anticipate before launch," cosmologist Mustapha Ishak of the University of Texas at ⁠Dallas, a member ​of Roman's scientific collaboration, told Reuters.
President Donald Trump's administration tried during both his first and second terms to reduce or ​eliminate funding for Roman, but Congress preserved it. Roman's launch comes nine months ahead of schedule, according to NASA.

items.author: Web Desk
items.content:
Defence Minister Khawaja Asif on Sunday rejected claims that the sons of Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) founder Imran Khan had been denied visas to enter Pakistan, saying they could visit the country on their National Identity Cards for Overseas Pakistanis (NICOPs).
"The children of the founder of PTI last travelled to Pakistan on these NICOPs in 2022. And today, if they want, they can visit Pakistan. Both NICOPs are valid. It is wrong for the family or PTI to give the impression that the government is not giving them visas," the defence minister said in a post on X.
The statement came in response to reports that Imran’s sons had been barred from travelling to Pakistan. A day earlier, the Information Ministry had also rejected similar claims, saying that both held valid NICOPs. According to the ministry, a valid NICOP is a recognised travel document for entry into Pakistan and can be used by the two men to travel to the country.
Asif further said in his statement that, with valid NICOPs, the two could travel to Pakistan whenever they wanted and did not require visas.
He also shared the details of the NICOP for both of Imran's children: "Sulaiman Khan: NICOP (35202-273-22XX-1) is available, which is valid until January 6, 2030", and "Kasim Khan: NICOP (35202-782-76XX-1) is available, which is valid until November 8, 2032".

items.author: Prasetyo Herfianto
items.content:
Selain kehadiran iPhone 18 Pro Series dan smartphone lipat Apple perdana, yang tidak kalah dinantikan kehadirannya pada gelaran Apple Event awal September nanti, adalah aksesori wearables pelengkap smartphone Apple generasi terbaru. Ya, apalagi kalau bukan Apple Watch. Dan tahun ini dirumorkan bila spesifikasi Apple Watch Series 12 maupun Apple Watch Ultra 4 bakal bawa upgrade yang signifikan dibandingkan generasi sebelumnya.
Ya, seperti yang Gizmo friends ketahui, tahun lalu Apple merilis Apple Watch Series 11 serta Ultra 3. Dan untuk pertama kalinya dalam sejarah Apple, cip yang digunakan untuk kedua jam tangan pintar tersebut, masih sama seperti generasi sebelumnya. Yang mendapatkan upgrade lebih signifikan justru Apple Watch SE 3, di mana akhirnya sama-sama gunakan cip Apple S10 yang lebih kencang sekaligus efisien daya.
Dari rumor yang terus beredar dalam beberapa pekan terakhir, disebutkan bila Apple Watch Series 12 maupun Ultra 4, bakal mendapatkan peningkatan signifikan pada sektor performa—dengan kata lain, siap mendapatkan cip generasi terbaru. Hal ini tentu bakal terasa sangat pas ketika Siri AI akan hadir lebih matang melalui watchOS 27. Sehingga siap bersaing dengan smartwatch rilisan Samsung yang juga mengedepankan AI Google Gemini.
Baca juga: iPhone 17 Pimpin Penjualan Smartphone Paling Laris di Q2 2026
Cip Baru Apple Watch Series 12 Siap Bawa Performa Lebih Ngebut
Dikutip dari 9to5Mac, Apple memang tidak menaikkan performa cip smartwatchnya dari tahun ke tahun. Cip Apple S10, misalnya, memiliki performa CPU yang setara dengan Apple S9, hanya saja dirancang lebih kompak agar muat ke dalam bodi Apple Watch generasi berikutnya yang dirancang lebih tipis. Dengan kata lain, performa Apple Watch Series 11 tak jauh berbeda bila dibandingkan dengan Series 9 yang rilis 2023 silam.
Menariknya, Mark Gurman dari Bloomberg yang dikenal selalu akurat dalam membocorkan informasi terbaru terkait Apple, baru saja sebutkan bila Apple Watch Series 12 maupun Ultra 4 siap debut dengan cip terbaru, yang kemungkinan bakal disebut sebagai cip Apple S11 atau S12. Ia menambahkan, model rilisan tahun ini siap mendapatkan peningkatan signifikan pada sektor performa.
Sementara cip Apple S9 sendiri tidak sepenuhnya membawa peningkatan pada aspek performa CPU, bila dibandingkan dengan generasi Apple S8. Namun performa perangkat tetap terasa lebih mulus, berkat GPU yang dibuat 30% lebih kencang, hingga empat inti neural engine yang juga dua kali lebih instan untuk melakukan tugas seperti saat menerima input perintah suara.
watchOS 27 sendiri membawa dukungan Siri AI yang tergolong jauh lebih komplit—menjadi salah satu alasan mengapa Apple tidak membawa semua fitur terbaru ke smartwatch rilisan terdahulu. Sehingga wajar saja bila pengalaman akses Siri AI pada Apple Watch Series 12 bakal terasa jauh lebih mulus dibandingkan generasi sebelumnya, meski hanya terpaut satu generasi.
Apple Disebut Siap Kembali Hadirkan Opsi Keramik Sejak Terakhir 2019
Selain chipset baru yang siap berikan peningkatan performa, rumor terbaru juga menyebutkan bila akhirnya Apple siap kembali menawarkan smartwatch terbarunya dalam edisi keramik. Rumor yang satu ini sempat disampaikan oleh Mark Gurman sejak bulan Juli lalu, yang kemudian turut dikonfirmasi oleh pembocor informasi lainnya, yakni Kusotami lewat akun X pribadinya.
Bila hal ini benar, berarti Apple Watch Series 12 Ceramic Edition bakal jadi penerus yang sebenarnya, dari varian yang sama dirilis dalam generasi kelima, yang sudah terpaut 7 tahun lamanya. Benefit menggunakan material premium tersebut, tidak lain selain terlihat premium, juga memiliki nilai durabilitas yang lebih tinggi.
Saat pertama kali Apple menghadirkan Apple Watch edisi keramik, material yang digunakan pada bodi perangkat disebut empat kali lebih kuat dari stainless steel, sehingga lebih tahan baik dari goresan maupun risiko penyok. Namun juga dibanderol jauh lebih mahal, yakni mencapai USD1299 atau sekitar Rp22,9 jutaan, dan harga tersebut merupakan harga Apple Watch edisi keramik rilisan 2019 silam. Apakah Gizmo friends menantikan Apple Watch Series 12 varian lebih premium satu ini?

items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Apple is preparing to unveil its next generation of iPhones, and the iPhone 18 Pro Max is expected to be one of the biggest launches of the year. Samsung, meanwhile, already has the Galaxy S26 Ultra on the market. Both phones target users who want a large display, powerful performance, and advanced cameras. While the Galaxy S26 Ultra is already available, most details about the iPhone 18 Pro Max are still based on leaks and rumors. In this article, we do a brief comparison of the iPhone 18 Pro and the Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra.
iPhone 18 Pro Max vs Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra: Which Flagship Could Win?
Here is how the two flagship phones could compare.
Display and Design
The iPhone 18 Pro Max is expected to feature a 6.9-inch OLED display with a 1-120Hz adaptive refresh rate. Its screen could offer a resolution of 2,868 x 1,320 pixels and around 460 pixels per inch.
The phone is not expected to receive a major design change compared with the iPhone 17 Pro Max. However, reports suggest that Apple could make it slightly thicker and heavier to accommodate a larger battery. The Dynamic Island may also become around 35% smaller.
The Galaxy S26 Ultra also has a 6.9-inch OLED display with a 120Hz refresh rate. Samsung offers a higher resolution of 3,120 x 1,440 pixels, resulting in 505ppi. The phone can also reduce its resolution to save battery.
Samsung has another advantage with its Privacy Display feature. It limits the viewing angle of the screen, making it harder for people nearby to see private information. The Galaxy S26 Ultra also includes an integrated S Pen, which gives it an advantage for note-taking and drawing.
Performance
The Galaxy S26 Ultra uses Qualcomm’s Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 for Galaxy processor. Depending on the model, it comes with 12GB or 16GB of RAM. Samsung also uses a vapor chamber to help control heat during demanding tasks and gaming.
The upcoming iPhone 18 Pro Max is expected to use Apple’s A20 Pro chip. Rumors suggest that Apple could build the processor using a 2nm manufacturing process. This could improve both performance and power efficiency.
Reports suggest the A20 Pro could deliver an 18% performance improvement and around 30% better power efficiency. However, Apple has not confirmed these figures yet.
Battery life
Battery life could become another major advantage for the iPhone 18 Pro Max. Reports indicate that Apple may increase the battery capacity compared with the previous generation.
The rumored capacity is around 5,567mAh for models without a physical SIM tray and about 5,491mAh for versions with one. Combined with the more efficient A20 Pro chip, this could give the iPhone longer battery life.
The Galaxy S26 Ultra has a 5,000mAh battery. It already delivers strong endurance, but the rumored iPhone 18 Pro Max could have an advantage if Apple’s larger battery and new processor perform as expected.
Cameras
Samsung currently has the stronger camera setup on paper. The Galaxy S26 Ultra features a 200MP main camera, a 50MP ultrawide camera, a 10MP telephoto lens with 3x optical zoom, and another 50MP telephoto camera with 5x optical zoom.
The iPhone 18 Pro Max is rumored to use three 48MP cameras, including the main, ultrawide, and telephoto sensors. These numbers may not match Samsung’s specifications, but Apple could introduce an important camera upgrade.
The main camera is expected to feature a variable aperture. This would allow users to control how much light enters the lens. It could give experienced photographers more control over images and creative compositions.
Price and availability
Apple is expected to announce the iPhone 18 Pro Max at its September 9 event. The regular iPhone 18 is reportedly being delayed until 2027, but the Pro models are expected to arrive this year.
The iPhone 18 Pro Max could start at around $1,299 for the 256GB version. Higher storage options could push the price to $1,499 for 512GB, $1,699 for 1TB, and $2,099 for 2TB.
The Galaxy S26 Ultra originally started at $1,299 for 256GB. Its 512GB model launched at $1,449, while the 1TB version cost $1,799.
Which Phone Could Be Better?
The Galaxy S26 Ultra already offers a powerful package with a high-resolution display, a flexible camera system, the S Pen, and a Privacy Display. It is also available now and may cost less through current deals.
The iPhone 18 Pro Max, however, could have an advantage in performance and battery life if the current rumors prove accurate. Its variable-aperture camera could also appeal to photography enthusiasts.
Still, Apple has not officially confirmed most of the iPhone 18 Pro Max specifications. The final comparison will become clearer after Apple’s September 9 event.
For now, the Galaxy S26 Ultra remains the safer choice because it is already available and its specifications are confirmed. The iPhone 18 Pro Max could become the more exciting option for users willing to wait for Apple’s latest flagship.

Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Rockstar Games has confirmed that Grand Theft Auto 6 (GTA 6) will not include microtransactions or generative AI when the game launches later this year. The announcement gives players some positive news ahead of one of the most highly anticipated game releases in years.
Rockstar shared the details during a recent conversation with Kinda Funny Games. According to the discussion, the studio was directly asked whether players would be able to spend real-world money on items or content inside GTA 6.
Rockstar Confirms No Microtransactions or Generative AI in GTA 6
Rockstar reportedly responded that there will be no monetization in the game at launch. This means players should not expect the usual microtransaction systems that allow users to buy virtual items, currency, or other content using real money.
The decision could be particularly welcome for players who have been waiting more than a decade for the next main entry in the Grand Theft Auto series. Microtransactions have become common in many major games, but their inclusion can also attract criticism from players.
No Generative AI in GTA 6
Rockstar was also asked about the use of generative artificial intelligence during the game’s development. Greg Miller of Kinda Funny reportedly asked the studio directly whether GTA 6 uses generative AI.
The response was simple: Rockstar said there is no AI used in the game.
Generative AI has become a controversial subject across the gaming industry. Some developers have used AI tools during development, while others have faced criticism from players and industry professionals over their use.
Players who prefer traditionally developed game content welcome Rockstar’s decision to avoid generative AI.
Ultimate Edition Still Offers Extra Content
While GTA 6 will not have traditional microtransactions at launch, Rockstar will still offer additional content through the game’s Ultimate Edition.
The Ultimate Edition will cost $99.99, while the standard version costs $79.99. The more expensive edition includes several exclusive items and bonuses connected to the game’s characters, Jason and Lucia.
These bonuses include cosmetic content, vehicles, weapons and access to certain locations. Some of the exclusive content includes the Electric Fang tattoo parlor and Stock 305 clothing store.
Rockstar has also confirmed that players who purchase the standard edition will be able to buy an upgrade to the Ultimate Edition separately.
This means GTA 6 will still have premium content, but it will not use the same type of ongoing microtransaction system seen in many online games.
GTA 6 Release Date
Grand Theft Auto 6 will launch on November 19, 2026, for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S.
Rockstar has already shown more details about the game, but fans can expect additional information before launch. The game will take players back to Vice City and introduce protagonists Jason and Lucia as they become involved in a criminal story.
For now, the confirmation about microtransactions and generative AI gives players two fewer concerns to think about. However, questions remain about the future of Grand Theft Auto Online and whether Rockstar will introduce a new online experience after GTA 6 arrives.

Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
WhatsApp has announced several new security features for its iOS and Android apps. The latest changes focus on protecting accounts, making unknown calls easier to understand, and giving users more secure ways to sign in.
The biggest update is an improvement to WhatsApp’s two-step verification system. Users can now protect their accounts with a password instead of relying only on a PIN. The password must contain at least eight characters, including at least one letter and one number.
WhatsApp Adds New Security Features for iOS and Android Users
A password gives users more combinations than a short PIN. This can make it harder for someone to guess the security credential and gain unauthorized access to an account. Users who have received the feature can find the new password option in their account settings.
WhatsApp is rolling out the feature gradually on the latest versions of its iOS and Android apps. If the password option does not appear yet, users may need to wait for a future update.
More information about Unknown Callers
WhatsApp is also adding more information about unknown calls on Android. The app can now provide additional context when a user receives a call from an unfamiliar number.
For example, users may see if the caller is using a number from another country. WhatsApp can also show how many groups the user and the caller have in common.
This information could help users decide whether they should answer an unknown call. It may also help them identify suspicious calls and avoid potential scams.
Multiple Passkeys are now Supported
Another important security improvement allows users to add more than one passkey to their WhatsApp account.
Passkeys offer a more secure way to sign in without depending on traditional passwords. Supporting multiple passkeys also gives users greater flexibility when accessing their accounts from different devices.
Together, these changes give WhatsApp users more options to protect their accounts and reduce the risk of unauthorized access.
WhatsApp is Also Testing Scam Alert
Alongside the announced security updates, WhatsApp is testing a Scam Alert feature with a limited number of Android beta users.
The feature uses an on-device machine learning system to examine messages from unknown contacts and look for patterns associated with scams. According to the information provided, the analysis happens on the device, so the message content is not sent to WhatsApp or Meta for this process.
If the system detects a possible scam, WhatsApp can display a warning. Users can then block or report the contact or mark the conversation as trusted.
Scam Alert is optional and is turned off by default. Users can also disable it whenever they want.
See Also: WhatsApp Starts Rolling Out Admin Profiles for Channels
Other WhatsApp Features in Development
WhatsApp is working on several other changes beyond security. The company is preparing a new payment section that could allow users to manage cards, billing details and shipping information. It is also exploring the option to send payments directly to contacts in supported markets.
The messaging platform is also rolling out admin profiles for channels. Channel administrators can create a separate name and profile photo, helping followers identify which admin published a particular update.
On iOS, WhatsApp is introducing new categories for chat themes, including Featured, Nature, Live, Minimal and Doodle. The app will automatically adjust chat bubble colors to maintain readable text.
Another feature in development is a smart chat filter called “To You.” It will collect conversations where users have been mentioned or received replies, making it easier to find important interactions in busy chats.
WhatsApp is rolling out these features at different times. Some are already reaching users, while others remain limited to beta testing or are still under development.

items.author: Anadolu Agency
items.content:
Russian Ambassador-at-large Andrey Belousov on Sunday accused the United States of viewing Europe as a potential nuclear battlefield.
Speaking in an interview with the Russian RT TV channel, Belousov said the persistence with which Washington is trying to initiate discussions on Russian non-strategic nuclear weapons suggests that the US is seriously considering the possibility of using nuclear weapons in the European theatre of operations.
"And, essentially, they view Europe as such a potential military theatre," he said.
Belousov argued that by urging Russia to engage in a dialogue on non-strategic nuclear arsenal, the US is trying to divert international attention from the risks posed by American nuclear weapons deployed in Europe and Washington’s broader missile and nuclear programs.
Read: Revolver gift leaves NATO leaders with dilemma
The official said obtaining information about Russia’s non-strategic nuclear weapons through greater transparency measures, or reducing or eliminating the arsenal, could increase the likelihood of a nuclear-use scenario involving the US and its European allies.
“I hope that Europe will recognise the danger of Washington’s purely operational-military approach to the territory of its allies,” he said.
According to Belousov, the deployment of US nuclear weapons in European NATO countries and NATO’s “nuclear sharing” arrangements have long been a concern for Moscow.
The expansion of such arrangements, including the involvement of additional NATO members in exercises related to the potential use of nuclear weapons, was increasing risks to Russia’s security, he said.
Belousov said Russia had reduced its non-strategic nuclear arsenal by four times in the early 1990s and moved the remaining weapons to centralised storage facilities, saying Moscow had expected reciprocal steps from Washington.
The diplomat argued that subsequent US moves had not fundamentally changed the military-political situation in Europe.
Read More: Alliance by footnote
He also said the collapse of arms-control and nuclear-disarmament agreements, combined with US plans to develop a multilayered missile-defence system under the “Golden Dome” program and modernise its nuclear forces, had significantly worsened the strategic environment.
Belousov said Russia was seeking to initiate an international discussion on what it considers the destabilising nature of NATO’s nuclear-sharing arrangements and to encourage the US to withdraw its nuclear weapons from Europe.
At the same time, Moscow remained open to resuming a strategic dialogue with Washington, although prospects for mutually acceptable agreements currently appeared limited, he stressed.
Belousov emphasised that any such negotiations should be based on equal and indivisible security and address the broader range of factors affecting strategic stability rather than focusing on individual issues.
Belousov also said Russia would respond to developments in the strategic-arms sphere through a combination of political, diplomatic, and military-technical measures aimed at maintaining strategic balance and addressing potential additional threats to its security.
Belousov’s comments come as the US continues to maintain nuclear weapons in Europe as part of NATO’s nuclear deterrence arrangements.
Also Read: UN chief says nuclear tests 'shatter trust,' wants global test ban
The Pentagon has said Washington remains committed to nuclear deterrence while urging European NATO members to assume greater responsibility for the alliance’s conventional defence.
US President Donald Trump said this week that he was not concerned about the possibility of Russia attacking NATO territory, amid growing European concerns over a potential Russian military challenge to the alliance.
Meanwhile, NATO has criticised Russia’s expansion and modernisation of its non-strategic nuclear capabilities, while Moscow views its nuclear arsenal as the only means capable of deterring an attack from NATO, which significantly outnumbers its forces.
The issue of non-strategic, or tactical, nuclear weapons has long been a contentious subject in US-Russian arms-control discussions. The two countries maintain significant tactical nuclear arsenals, while the US also deploys nuclear weapons in Europe under NATO arrangements.
Belousov’s remarks come amid broader tensions over European security and the future of arms control following the expiration of the New START treaty in February, which had been the last remaining treaty limiting US and Russian strategic nuclear arsenals.

items.author: APP
items.content:
Pakistan and Saudi Arabia agreed to work towards increasing Pakistan's agricultural and food exports to the Kingdom to $3 billion within the next two years, as the two countries seek to deepen cooperation in food security and agriculture, according to a joint statement released by the Prime Minister's Office (PMO) on Sunday.
The statement noted that significant progress in agricultural cooperation between Pakistan and Saudi Arabia was achieved due to Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif’s patronage and personal interest.
PMO said that at the government's invitation, a Saudi delegation led by Eng Abdulrahman A. Alfadley, Minister of Environment, Water and Agriculture, and comprising senior officials from the Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture, the General Food Security Authority, and related entities, visited Islamabad from August 26 to 28.
According to the joint statement, the Pakistani side was led by Minister for National Food Security & Research (MNFSR), Rana Tanveer Hussain and included senior government officials and private-sector representatives, including Secretary Commerce Jawad Paul, Secretary Ministry of MNFSR Amer Ali Ahmed, PM’s Coordinator on Agriculture & Food Security Ahmad Umair, and private-sector representatives of Pakistan’s rice, red meat processed-food/fruit-concentrate, and green fodder sectors.
The statement also noted that PM Shehbaz met the Saudi delegation and discussed potential areas of bilateral cooperation.
According to a joint statement issued after the visit, rice, red meat, fruits and fruit concentrates, green fodder and water-efficient agricultural technologies had been identified as priority areas for expanding trade and investment, particularly through cooperation with Saudi Arabia’s private sector.
وزیراعظم کی سرپرستی میں پاکستان اور سعودی عرب کے درمیان زرعی شعبے میں اہم پیش رفت.
وزیراعظم کی ذاتی دلچسپی سے سعودی وزیرِ ماحولیات، پانی و زراعت اور وزارتِ قومی غذائی تحفظ و تحقیق کے درمیان کامیاب مذاکرات ہوئے.
مشترکہ اعلامیہ:
اسلامی جمہوریہ پاکستان اور مملکتِ سعودی عرب کے… pic.twitter.com/Alv2M6JTT1
— Prime Minister's Office (@PakPMO) August 30, 2026
PMO stated that Pakistan supplied about 169,000 tonnes of rice worth $163 million to Saudi Arabia in 2025, adding that the Saudi side expressed interest in further increasing imports of rice.
The statement noted that the two sides also reviewed Pakistan’s annual exports of around 30,000 tonnes of red meat valued at approximately $167 million, adding that the Saudi side expressed interest in gradually doubling its imports of Pakistani red meat.
Read: PM Shehbaz urges Pakistan, Saudi Arabia to deepen economic, agricultural ties
PMO said that both countries agreed to facilitate business-to-business linkages and matchmaking in the fruit and fruit concentrate sectors and encouraged steps towards mutual recognition of quality certifications.
The press release stated that green fodder was also identified as a promising sector for expanding trade and establishing long-term supply partnerships.
It added that the two sides welcomed the completion of the first phase of a water-efficient irrigation programme in Bhakkar, Punjab, and expressed interest in a second phase aimed at small farmers.
PMO said that the Saudi delegation also encouraged Pakistan to join the International Dates Council, a proposal welcomed by Islamabad.
According to the press release, the two sides reviewed investment proposals from Pakistan’s private sector in livestock, agri-food processing and the rice value chain, agreeing to maintain coordination to advance the projects.
PMO said that the Saudi delegation also visited the National Agricultural Research Centre (NARC) and held meetings with the authorities of the Special Investment Facilitation Council (SIFC), Fauji Foundation and the Pakistan-Saudi Arabia Agri Business Forum and were briefed in detail.
The joint communique said that both countries reaffirmed their longstanding strategic and fraternal ties and highlighted the alignment between Saudi Arabia’s Vision 2030 food-security priorities and Pakistan’s agricultural export potential.
Read More: Saudi Vision 2030 opens new trade avenues
The statement noted that Pakistan was also invited to participate in the 43rd Saudi Agriculture Exhibition, scheduled to take place in Riyadh from October 19 to 22, 2026.
PMO said that both sides expressed satisfaction with the outcome of the visit and agreed to continue coordination to translate the agreements into practical cooperation.

items.author: Prasetyo Herfianto
items.content:
TECNO sedang menyiapkan kehadiran smartphone gaming terbarunya di Indonesia, yakni POVA 8 Pro 5G yang sudah diumumkan lewat sejumlah teaser dari akun media sosial resminya. Namun lain di India, di mana TECNO Spark Go 3 Pro debut dalam desain yang kekinian. Menariknya, smartphone TECNO Rp2 jutaan terbaru ini mengedepankan daya tahan perangkat.
Sejak awal, lini TECNO Spark memang hadir sebagai opsi yang lebih terjangkau, terutama bila dibandingkan dengan lini POVA yang fokus pada aspek gaming alias performa, hingga CAMON yang membawa inovasi terbaik di segmennya untuk sektor kamera. Adanya embel-embel “Pro” seolah menunjukkan bila opsi baru satu ini bakal mengisi segmen yang sedikit lebih tinggi dibandingkan Spark Go 3 terdahulu.
Tidak dapat dipungkiri, harga TECNO Spark Go 3 Pro yang siap dijual perdana lewat e-commerce Amazon di India, tidak semenggoda generasi-generasi sebelumnya yang dibanderol mulai Rp1 jutaan. Meski memang, situasi ini dialami oleh semua brand, akibat kenaikan biaya komponen yang dilanda semua perusahaan secara global, setidaknya dalam satu tahun terakhir.
Baca juga: Spesifikasi TECNO POVA 8 Pro 5G, Siap Hadir Resmi dalam Edisi Eksklusif Lamborghini
Bawa Dua Sertifikasi Khusus Untuk Durabilitas
Dengan imbuhan pada bagian namanya, tentu spesifikasi TECNO Spark Go 3 Pro lebih tinggi dibandingkan varian Spark Go 3 standar yang debut Januari kemarin. Secara tampilan, desain TECNO Spark Go 3 Pro nampak mengikuti bagaimana Apple merancang iPhone seri Pro terbarunya, dengan modul kamera yang dibuat melebar dari tepi kiri ke kanan di sisi belakang atas perangkat. Bahkan lampu kilatnya juga diletakkan berjauhan dari sensor kamera, seperti iPhone 17 Pro Series. 
Bodi TECNO Spark Go 3 Pro sudah mengusung sertifikasi hingga IP69, sehingga tahan dari debu dan air baik dalam suhu maupun tekanan tinggi. Dan tak sampai di situ, juga membawa sertifikasi bintang lima dari SGS, yang menjamin tetap dapat berfungsi normal meski jatuh dari ketinggian hingga 1,7 meter. Layar perangkat juga dirancang agar tetap dapat digunakan secara normal meski di bawah guyuran air hujan, atau dengan jari berminyak sekalipun.
Layar TECNO Spark Go 3 Pro berukuran 6,78 inci, menggunakan panel IPS dalam resolusi HD+, dengan refresh rate maksimum sampai 120Hz. TECNO mengklaim angka refresh rate tersebut bersifat adaptif, dan dipasangkan bersama setup speaker stereo dengan fitur volume maksimum hingga 300%.
Keunggulan TECNO Spark Go 3 Pro lainnya ada pada sektor baterai. Di segmennya, kapasitas baterai 5200 mAh sudah tergolong cukup besar, diklaim sanggup digunakan untuk memutar video secara kontinyu hingga 11 jam. Mendukung fast charging 15W, baterai tersebut juga diklaim tetap memiliki kapasitas hingga 80% selama 4 tahun penggunaan.
Spesifikasi TECNO Spark Go 3 Pro Identik dengan Spark 50C
Mengingat smartphone TECNO terbaru satu ini menyasar segmen kelas entri, maka wajar bila aspek performa bukan jadi nilai jual utama. Performa TECNO Spark Go 3 Pro diperkuat cip Helio G81 octa-core dari MediaTek, dengan RAM LPDDR4x dan penyimpanan berjenis UFS 2.2. Sistem operasinya sendiri sudah menjalankan Android 16.
Meski begitu, tetap ada sejumlah fitur ekstra menarik yang disematkan. Selain sensor inframerah yang dapat digunakan untuk mengendalikan perangkat elektronik rumah, juga disematkan fitur AI yang bisa membantu meningkatkan kualitas panggilan suara. Dan bila ditilik ke situs resmi TECNO global, TECNO Spark Go 3 Pro punya spesifikasi hingga desain identik seperti seri Spark 50C. Mengindikasikan penamaan berbeda di luar India.
Di India, harga TECNO Spark Go 3 Pro dibanderol mulai INR15,999 atau sekitar Rp2,9 jutaan untuk varian 4+64GB. Sementara untuk varian 4+128GB, dibanderol INR16,999 (Rp3,1 jutaan). Ya, sayangnya dengan kenaikan biaya komponen global, harga smartphone kelas entri satu ini jadi naik derastis. Apakah bakal lebih terjangkau bila kelak dijual resmi di Indonesia? Kita nantikan saja kehadirannya ya.

items.title: PML-N leadership urges prioritising healthcare, education, infrastructure in meeting with new AJK PM Gilani
items.summary:
The Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz's (PML-N) senior leadership on Sunday stressed the need for the immediate resolution of problems faced by people in Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK), with a focus on healthcare, education and infrastructure, during a meeting with newly elected AJK Prime Minister Iftikhar Gilani and Speaker Tariq Farooq.
According to a statement issued by the PML-N, party President Nawaz Sharif, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif met Gilani and Farooq.
The statement said that the party's senior leadership “stressed the need for the immediate resolution of the problems faced by the people of Azad Kashmir”.
"پاکستان مسلم لیگ ن کے صدر محمد نواز شریف، وزیراعظم محمد شہباز شریف اور وزیر اعلیٰ پنجاب مریم نواز شریف سے آزاد جموں و کشمیر کے وزیر اعظم افتخار گیلانی اور سپیکر طارق فاروق کی ملاقات"

items.author: Web Desk
items.content:
The Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz's (PML-N) senior leadership on Sunday stressed the need for the immediate resolution of problems faced by people in Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK), with a focus on healthcare, education and infrastructure, during a meeting with newly elected AJK Prime Minister Iftikhar Gilani and Speaker Tariq Farooq.
According to a statement issued by the PML-N, party President Nawaz Sharif, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif met Gilani and Farooq.
The statement said that the party's senior leadership “stressed the need for the immediate resolution of the problems faced by the people of Azad Kashmir”.
"پاکستان مسلم لیگ ن کے صدر محمد نواز شریف، وزیراعظم محمد شہباز شریف اور وزیر اعلیٰ پنجاب مریم نواز شریف سے آزاد جموں و کشمیر کے وزیر اعظم افتخار گیلانی اور سپیکر طارق فاروق کی ملاقات"
🔸آزاد جموں و کشمیر کے وزیر اعظم افتخار گیلانی اور سپیکر طارق فاروق نے اظہار اعتماد پر پاکستان… pic.twitter.com/Bt0hspBX4x
— PMLN (@pmln_org) August 30, 2026
During the meeting, Nawaz shared a “100-day reform plan” with the AJK prime minister aimed at improving healthcare, education, sanitation, infrastructure and other sectors in the region, according to the post on X.
The PML-N said its leadership directed that “AJK be put on a path of modernisation and development along the lines of Punjab”.
AJK PM Gilani and Speaker Farooq thanked the PML-N leadership for “expressing confidence” in them, the party said.
Nawaz, PM Shehbaz Sharif and CM Maryam also extended their “best wishes and congratulations” to the AJK prime minister and speaker, according to the post.
At the beginning of the current week, on August 24, forty-six newly elected members of the AJK Legislative Assembly took the oath, formally marking the start of the new parliamentary term following the 2026 general elections, with the PML-N emerging as the dominant parliamentary force.
PML-N-backed Barrister Iftikhar Gillani was sworn in as the 17th prime minister of AJK on Friday, completing the parliamentary set-up of the newly elected assembly. PPP's Chaudhry Muhammad Yasin was appointed leader of the opposition.
In his maiden speech, Gillani said livelihood opportunities would be his government's top priority, alongside reforms in education and healthcare. He also pledged to “digitalise the economy” and improve internet access across AJK.
AJK elections conclude
The elections were held in three phases under a revised schedule announced by AJK Chief Election Commissioner Ghulam Mustafa Mughal on July 21. The first phase covered all 13 constituencies in Mirpur Division, while polling in Muzaffarabad Division and the 12 refugee constituencies was held on August 2, followed by Poonch (Rawalakot) Division on August 10.
The AJK Election Commission on August 7 announced that polling would proceed as scheduled in four constituencies — Bagh Central, Bagh East, Bagh West and Haveli — while voting in seven constituencies would be postponed due to security concerns.
The postponement came against the backdrop of deteriorating security conditions in Poonch Division, where tensions have persisted since late July. Violent clashes erupted in Rawalakot between police and members of the proscribed Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC) after the group attempted to enter the city during the first phase of the AJK elections.
Read More: AJK premier alleges PPP denied level playing field in recent elections
The first phase concluded with polling across Mirpur Division, while the second phase covered nine constituencies in Muzaffarabad Division and 12 refugee seats, bringing 21 constituencies to the polls. However, voting in LA-27 Muzaffarabad-I and LA-28 Muzaffarabad-II was postponed after heavy rain, landslides and adverse weather prevented election staff and polling material from reaching several polling stations.
Polling in the two delayed constituencies was held two days later under heightened security arrangements, with the PML-N winning LA-27 Muzaffarabad-I and the PPP securing LA-28 Muzaffarabad-II, formally bringing the second phase of the elections to a close. The Election Commission subsequently notified the results of all 21 constituencies contested in the second phase.

items.title: Zerodha’s Diversification Clock Is Ticking
items.summary:
Zerodha’s core business is no longer growing. Regulatory curbs and changing investor behaviour are cooling trading activity and squeezing brokerage revenue.
Broking revenue fell 10.4% from ₹3,066 Cr in FY25 to ₹2,738 Cr in FY26. Net transaction charges (income earned from exchange-related transaction fee rebates) also fell to zero from ₹400 Cr in FY25 due to SEBI’s true-to-label norm framework. In a blog post, CEO Nithin Kamath hinted that its overall top line remained almost flat in FY26 versus ₹8,847 Cr a fiscal year ago.
Despite the revenue squeeze, Zerodha kept its bottom line largely intact, with profit rising marginally to ₹4,283 Cr in FY26 from ₹4,231 Cr in FY25.
So, with its core revenue engine slowing, what is keeping Zerodha’s profits afloat? The answer: Zerodha is increasingly making money from sources other than brokerage.
Interest income (₹2,269 Cr): The discount broker earns interest on its cash balances and other interest-generating assets.
