Zerodha’s core business is no longer growing. Regulatory curbs and changing investor behaviour are cooling trading activity and squeezing brokerage revenue.
Broking revenue fell 10.4% from ₹3,066 Cr in FY25 to ₹2,738 Cr in FY26. Net transaction charges (income earned from exchange-related transaction fee rebates) also fell to zero from ₹400 Cr in FY25 due to SEBI’s true-to-label norm framework. In a blog post, CEO Nithin Kamath hinted that its overall top line remained almost flat in FY26 versus ₹8,847 Cr a fiscal year ago.
Despite the revenue squeeze, Zerodha kept its bottom line largely intact, with profit rising marginally to ₹4,283 Cr in FY26 from ₹4,231 Cr in FY25.
So, with its core revenue engine slowing, what is keeping Zerodha’s profits afloat? The answer: Zerodha is increasingly making money from sources other than brokerage.
Interest income (₹2,269 Cr): The discount broker earns interest on its cash balances and other interest-generating assets.
Delayed payment charges + MTF (₹448 Cr): It earns money when customers delay paying for trades and, through MTF, when customers borrow money to buy stocks.
AMC charges: Zerodha’s asset management business is also generating more fee income, though it is still relatively small.
In Q1 FY27, the discount broker said that nearly 40% of its gross revenue came from the businesses outside its core trading platform.
While these revenue streams are cushioning the impact of falling brokerage income, are they large enough to replace the core business entirely, especially when its arch-rival Groww now has an active client base almost twice the size?
Zerodha’s User Problem Is Bigger Than It Looks
Regulatory changes have added to the pressure on Zerodha’s core brokerage business, particularly by curbing derivatives and currency trading activity. SEBI’s derivatives clampdown and RBI’s tighter rules around currency futures and options (F&O), introduced in 2024, reduced trading activity across segments.
According to Zerodha, these regulatory changes led to a 20-30% drop in F&O activity across exchanges and brokers. INR currency F&O volumes fell 90% after the RBI introduced rules requiring trades to be backed by an underlying foreign currency exposure.
But regulations do not fully explain the divergence between Zerodha and Groww, which has almost twice as many clients as Zerodha.
In July, Groww added 70,119 active clients, taking its base to 13.12 Mn and its NSE market share to 28.88%. Zerodha lost 38,725 clients, leaving it with 6.76 Mn and a 14.88% share. The entire broking industry added only around 8,000 net active clients during the month.
The divergence is visible in revenue as well.
Groww’s operating revenue rose from ₹ 2,609 Cr in FY24 to ₹4,645 Cr in FY26, an increase of about 78%. Zerodha, by comparison, saw its revenue decline from nearly ₹9,994 Cr in FY24 to around ₹8,847 Cr in FY26.
However, according to Rahul Sharma, head of office research at Equity99, Groww and Zerodha are not competing for the same customer or the same kind of revenue.
While Groww has focused more on mass-market equity, mutual funds and SIPs, Zerodha continues to derive a significant portion of its revenue from active F&O traders. Even CEO Nithin Kamath argues that the active-client market is not the most important metric.
This, however, does not answer the fundamental question: if Zerodha is not trying to win on users, can it extract enough value from its existing base?
MTF Rescue Boat
Margin trading facility (MTF) is helping Zerodha build a new revenue stream, but it is not the only one trying to reduce its dependence on trading-led revenue. Angel One has been moving aggressively in the same direction, with client funding, wealth management, asset management and distribution becoming a larger part of its business.
Zerodha launched its MTF offering in December 2024, after years of debating whether to enter the segment. At the time, Zerodha said it made little business sense to remain the only large broker without the product.
The product has since scaled. Zerodha’s MTF book has reached around ₹9,000 Cr, with customers borrowing about ₹6,000 Cr. Per Kamath, MTF contributes roughly 10% of the startup’s revenue.
The financials show the change clearly. Delayed payment charges and MTF generated ₹448 Cr in FY26, compared with ₹22 Cr in FY25.
The reason this matters is simple: Brokerage revenue depends heavily on customers trading. MTF allows Zerodha to earn interest from customers who borrow to invest, creating a revenue stream that is less dependent on the number of trades.
The bigger issue is that MTF is being built against a business that remains heavily exposed to derivatives. Avinash Gorakhshar, founder of Avinash Mentor Research, said continued regulatory pressure on F&O could make Zerodha’s slower diversification into mass-market wealth products a growth constraint.
But MTF is not yet large enough to replace the revenue lost from Zerodha’s traditional business. It puts Zerodha in an interesting position. Angel One, which had a broadly similar active client base to Zerodha at the end of FY26, has also been building its client funding business; its average client funding book stood at ₹5,305 Cr for FY26 and rose to ₹6,783 Cr by June 2026. It is pertinent to note that Angel One’s client funding book includes MTF loans and period-end trade receivables, net of non-interest-bearing receivables.
Then there is also a limit to how aggressively Zerodha can push the product. Kamath has acknowledged the risks associated with leveraged investing and said the startup does not want to encourage customers to borrow simply because it generates revenue.
The Diversification Dilemma
Zerodha remains profitable, its AMC is scaling faster than Groww’s AUM, and its MTF book has grown rapidly. But the timing of some of these moves is tricky.
Zerodha had a significant first-mover advantage in digital broking, but MTF came only in late 2024, while it launched AMC in 2023. It is now bringing mutual fund transactions to Kite, after keeping the trading and mutual fund experience separate for years.
The gap is more visible in wealth management.
Groww has moved into the affluent investor segment through W, its wealth management platform, which offers access to Portfolio Management Services (PMS), Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs) and private market opportunities.
Lalit Keshre’s Groww entered the segment after acquiring Fisdom in October last year, a deal that brought wealth management and distribution capabilities into its business. Zerodha, by comparison, remains largely a self-directed investment platform through Kite and Coin. Its Zerodha Fund House gives it an asset management business, but that is different from offering personalised wealth management.
However, not everyone believes Zerodha’s slower customer growth means it has been slow to respond to changing market realities. Sharma of Equity99 argues that the startup is making a deliberate trade-off, prioritising profitability and capital efficiency over aggressive customer acquisition.
But with Groww moving faster into wealth and adjacent products, Zerodha risks falling behind if its diversification does not scale quickly enough.
All in all, Zerodha is not a troubled business. It remains highly profitable, has a strong brand, a sizeable customer base and growing businesses beyond brokerage.
But the economics of digital broking are changing, and the company can no longer rely on its traditional F&O-heavy model to drive growth. Therefore, it will have to diversify fast enough before its core business shrinks further.

items.author: Press Release
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Continuing its legacy of marketing excellence, Pakistan largest telecommunication and integrated ICT services provider, Pakistan Telecommunication Company Limited (PTCL) has secured five awards at the Dragons of Pakistan 2026, including one Silver, one Bronze and three Black Dragons, in recognition of its creative excellence and impactful brand campaigns.
The awards recognize a diverse portfolio of campaigns by PTCL that addressed themes ranging from national pride and social inclusion to women’s empowerment and education.
Among the winning campaigns, PTCL’s “Pakistan Ki Pehchan – Celebrating Pakistan’s Underrepresented Sports” received a Silver Dragon in the Brand Activation and/or Awareness category, recognized for bringing greater attention to Pakistan’s lesser-known sporting disciplines and the athletes whose talent and commitment often remain outside the mainstream spotlight. PTCL’s “Mother’s Day – More Support for Mothers” received two awards Black Dragon in the Marketing Discipline category and a Bronze in the Cause, Environment or Sustainability category, reflecting the campaign’s focus on the everyday realities and support systems that matter to mothers.
PTCL’s “Dil Se Ba-Ikhtiar” was also among the award-winning campaigns and received Black Dragon, earning recognition for using digital technology as a lever for women’s empowerment, while PTCL’s “World Education Day – Late Ho Gaye” received a Black Dragon in the Cause, Environment or Sustainability category for highlighting the physical and emotional burdens carried by children in Pakistan, including unrealistic expectations, responsibilities and the many challenges that often weigh on their childhood.
The latest recognition reinforces PTCL’s commitment to building a brand that connects with people through relevant ideas and purposeful communication. The latest recognition adds to a series of notable achievements for PTCL in the creative and marketing industry.

items.author: Prasetyo Herfianto
items.content:
Bila Gizmo friends ingat, POCO sempat menggelar sebuah acara peluncuran akbar untuk flagship-nya langsung dari pulau Bali, Indonesia. Dan ternyata belum genap satu tahun, POCO sudah menyiapkan flagship generasi penerusnya melalui POCO F9 Series. Dan spesifikasi POCO F9 Ultra sudah dibocorkan secara resmi, kembali andalkan performa sekaligus setup speaker superior.
Ya, generasi sebelumnya alias POCO F8 Ultra hadir dengan diferensiasi cukup menarik, menggandeng Bose untuk membawa setup speaker stereo simetris, memiliki woofer khusus yang disematkan secara langsung pada sisi bodi belakang perangkat. Nilai jual tersebut nampaknya berhasil menarik minat konsumen, sehingga kembali menjadi unggulan spesifikasi POCO F9 Ultra, hingga varian Pro yang lebih terjangkau.
Jelang peluncurannya pekan depan, tentu bocoran spesifikasi POCO F9 Ultra sudah mulai bermunculan. Menariknya, Xiaomi sendiri juga ikut membocorkan beberapa keunggulan yang siap ditawarkan. Sekaligus menampilkan desain POCO F9 Pro sebagai opsi lain yang juga tidak kalah menarik secara visual.
Baca juga: Redmi Note 17 Pro & Pro Max Debut Global, Kapasitas Baterai Sampai 10.000 mAh
Spesifikasi POCO F9 Ultra Masih Banyak yang Sama
View this post on Instagram
Sebelum membahas lebih jauh terkait spesifikasi POCO F9 Ultra, desain perangkat bisa dibilang menarik. Pasalnya, warna utamanya “Dark Cherry” seperti unggahan pada akun Instagram resminya—seolah “menyalip” Apple yang, dalam beberapa bulan terakhir, dirumorkan siap hadirkan iPhone 18 Pro Series dalam tampilan warna serupa.
Spesifikasi POCO F9 Ultra sendiri bisa dibilang identik dengan Redmi K100 Pro Max yang debut lebih dulu di negara asalnya. Hanya saja karena dirilis untuk pasar global, ada penyesuaian pada kapasitas baterai. Di mana baterai POCO F9 Ultra berukuran 8050mAh, yang sejatinya sudah signifikan lebih lega dibandingkan generasi sebelumnya.
Baterai tersebut dapat terisi secara instan lewat fast charging 100W, maupun fast wireless charging 50W. Sementara pada sektor performa, spesifikasi POCO F9 Ultra tetap jalankan cip Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5. Xiaomi mengklaim mampu mencetak skor Antutu hingga lebih dari 4,1 juta poin. Peningkatan lain juga ada pada sektor layar, di mana POCO F9 Ultra bisa berikan pengalaman bermain game hingga 185fps, lewat layar yang mendukung refresh rate hingga 185Hz.
Pihak resmi juga membocorkan bila POCO F9 Ultra kembali membawa Sound by Bose, untuk setup speaker stereo yang diperkuat subwoofer khusus pada bodi belakangnya, demi pengalaman mendengarkan musik atau bermain game lebih imersif. Namun dari bocoran yang ada, POCO bakal sematkan LED ring khusus pada sekitar subwoofer sebagai nilai tambah.
POCO F9 Pro Justru Bakal Punya Sensor Utama 200MP
Dari rumor yang sudah beredar sejak beberapa pekan lalu, spesifikasi POCO F9 Ultra disebut bakal masih relatif sama seperti generasi sebelumnya. Mulai dari layar AMOLED berukuran 6,9 inci, opsi RAM dan penyimpanan yang masih sama, hingga spesifikasi kamera yang juga masih identik. Sehingga jika memang benar, smartphone ini siap mengusung tiga sensor 50MP di sisi belakang. Terdiri dari sensor utama, ultra-wide, dan telefoto yang mampu berikan 5x optical zoom.
Sementara itu, POCO F9 Pro tampil dalam warna utama hijau cerah, dengan logo Bose yang kini memiliki aksen melingkar pada modul kamera belakangnya. Spesifikasinya juga diklaim bakal identik seperti Redmi K100 Pro dengan perbedaan pada sektor baterai, di mana varian global mengusung kapasitas 6330 mAh.
Kapasitas yang masih tergolong besar, mengingat dimensi layarnya lebih kompak di 6,59 inci, dengan panel AMOLED full HD+ dalam refresh rate hingga 185Hz. Varian yang lebih terjangkau dan lebih kecil ini siap mengusung cip Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5, kamera utama 200MP, telefoto 50MP dengan 2,5x optical zoom, dan 8MP ultra-wide. Apakah Gizmo friends menantikan kehadiran keduanya di Tanah Air?

The handmade piece featured embroidered birds and interconnected daisy chains, a fitting nod to the women-led festival's name and wider themes. Olivia paired the look with vintage Gucci Mary Jane heels and a silver pendant.

items.title: How to Recover Deleted Photos on Android: A Step-by-Step Guide
items.summary: Android allows users to recover their recently deleted photos for a specific period of time. Depending on the brand and the UI, Android handsets usually retain deleted images for 30 days. This allows users to restore the photos they deleted from their Android phone by mistake. When a user deletes an image, it is first moved to their phone's Recently Deleted folder. Similarly, users can also recover images that they recently deleted in Google's Photos app. Users can also choose to permanently delete photos from the Recently Deleted folder.

items.author: Emmanuel Okogba
items.content:
Uhuru, a Swahili word which means “freedom or independence” was popularized by Kenyan nationalist and leader Oginga Odinga who used it in the title of his 1967 autobiography, “Not Yet Uhuru “.
The phrase was used to express the fact that “a long-fought struggle or goal is incomplete, even if nominal independence or a milestone has been reached”.
That is the position of Nigeria’s most versatile former Green Eagles player and captain, Chief Olusegun Patrick Odegbami who is many things rolled into one.
His versatility as a football player, journalist, writer, businessman, football school proprietor, motivational speaker, radio and television analyst and a sports activist is a story for another day.
Odegbami has been in the forefront of those agitating that football administration should be open to all Nigerians who have a stake in the game in one way or the other.
This struggle which he has carried over the years as a solo crusader have always been frustrated by the aloofness of most stakeholders including the government which provides about 90 percent of the funds with which football survives in the country.
The struggle however, took a more vociferous dimension this year when those who have been aloof in the past suddenly discovered that the people managing the game everybody says is the only unifier of Nigerians across ethnic and religious divide are destroying it.
Why? Because for the first time since 1994, the Super Eagles missed two World Cups consecutively in 2022 and 2026 while the Super Falcons, Nigeria and Africa’s most successful national team, failed to qualify for the 2027 World Cup for the first since women’s World Cup began in 1991. This was the last straw that broke the proverbial camel’s back.
That was when the agitation became louder and several voices joined, saying enough was enough. I must mention a few people who added their voice to the campaign that the Ibrahim Gusau-led NFF board must go.
Former Director General of the National Broadcasting Commission, NBC, Dr Danladi Bako who was also a former chairman of the Sokoto state FA, former Secretary General of the NFA, Alhaji Sani Ahmed Toro, Sylvanus Okpalla, former assistant Super Eagles coach, Adokiye Amiesimaka, former Green Eagles winger and former chairman of Sharks Football Cub of Port Harcourt, former Green Eagles player, former Enyimba FC and Super Falcons coach, Kadiri Ikhana as well.
as Tony Ubani, Editor of Sporting Vanguard and president of the Guild of Sports Editors. 
Odegbami saw that if Nigerians shout till eternity, calling for Gusau and his cohorts to resign for failing the country and the doctored NFF Statutes wasn’t reviewed, the same people would
return to continue destroying football from where they stopped.
That was why he wrote, asking President Bola Tinubu to stop the NFF Elections scheduled for September 27, 2026, failing which he would head to court to halt the process. 
His prayer was answered as the government asked security agencies to investigate the NFF administrators, to find out how they spent the N17 billion it provided the federation to pay all
monies owed the various national teams’ players and officials.
They quickly resigned but the security agencies have affirmed that their resignation won’t stop the probe into the financial misappropriation and misapplication of funds meant for football they are facing.
Nigerians are happy with this development and pray that the NFF is sanitised for a fresh life to be breathed into the house. 
However, for Odegbami to be totally happy that he fought a good fight, he has said it is not Uhuru, stressing that going on with the election as planned without reviewing the manipulated NFF Statutes would amount to pouring of new wine into an old wine bottle.
As a result therefore, he wants a fundamental change to the NFF Statutes and the amendment of the electoral guidelines to end the monopoly of State FA chairmen and allow a broader, more inclusive group of stakeholders—such as club owners, coaches, referees, and players unions—to vote and be voted for.a
He equally advised that the rule which allows heavy financial costs tied to contesting elections, which holds back qualified candidates who do not have loads of money from contesting, should be removed.
As if the president was reading Odegbami’s mind, he said the reform the NFF needs “must respond to a long-standing need to strengthen governance, administration, stakeholder representation, development pathways, domestic competitions and accountability across Nigerian football.”
Reiterating why a new lease of life was necessary at the NFF, the president said that, “Football, Nigeria’s most popular sport and the greatest beneficiary of public support, investment and national attention, has continued to struggle basically due to structural deficits within the system.”
He has directed the Chairman of the National Sports Commission, NSC, to work with the NFF Secretariat and relevant football stakeholders to ensure continuity in essential football administration and facilitate a broad, consultative reform process.
The reform is expected to commence with a normalization committee, to be endorsed by FIFA and CAF, put in place pending when a new election is held. Meanwhile, Odegbami is already looking ahead, urging a break from the past as stakeholders look for the person to steer the new ship of football.
”This period provides an opportunity for serious interrogation of the subject, a clean sweep of the past failures, and a new start for Nigerian football administration”, he surmised.
The post ”Not Yet Uhuru”, by Patrick Omorodion appeared first on Vanguard News.

items.author: Emmanuel Okogba
items.content:
By Bunmi Sofola
As soon as Terry walked into his lavishly furnished home at his usual time of 8p.m. or thereabout, his wife was waiting for him. His best food was kept hot in the food warmer, his favourite bottle of wine nesting in the fridge. This was late last year when Covid-19 was virtually unheard of.
“Mide was here to see us,” Nina, his wife said after Terry’s had his meal.  “As a matter of fact, she left just before you came in.”  “Mide?  Who is Mide?”, she told him who Mide was.  “What was she doing out so late in the night”, Terry wanted to know.  “Shouldn’t she be in school?”
“She finished over two years ago at the university.  As a matter of fact, she is getting married and came to tell us specially before the cards are out.  She is now 25 years old”, Nina told her husband in her most patient voice.
“Already?”, Terry feigned surprise, “the last time I saw her, she was in secondary school.”  “Anyway, she wants you to be the chairman of the wedding”, continued his wife, “Chairman ke?”  Terry boomed.  “How many wedding receptions am I supposed to chair in a year?  I just did one last month.  Tell her to look for another sucker, you can tell her I wouldn’t be around on that day”.
“Actually”, Nina persisted “she’s left us to pick a day you’ll be free as the wedding date.  I don’t know why she’s bent on choosing you as the chairman.  If you’re not up to it, we could find a real excuse to let her down.”
Terry knew he’d gone too far.  Of course, he knew Mide would be in the house that day. The meeting had been well rehearsed between the two of them.  Not only was Mide, Terry’s girlfriend, so was her mother, and one of her sisters!  But Mide is the officially acknowledged ‘mistress’ by her mum and sister.
After grumbling a while further, Terry said, “I pretended to grudgingly agree to be the chairman at Mide’s wedding.  I had already paid for most of the things she would need and she had brought her fiancé to see me in my office.  The poor sucker was full of appreciation for all that I had done towards their having a successful wedding and to show how grateful he was, he prostrated, his chest touching the floor!  I’d already been introduced to him as Mide’s ‘uncle’.
“I smirked.  How many such gratitudes had I taken in the past from unsuspecting husbands-to-be, whom I was introduced to as an ‘uncle?’  And the poor chaps never suspect a thing.  Most of these “blushing brides,” I met through their mothers or older sisters.  As a result, we’ve all become firm family friends and even after the weddings, I still play my ‘uncle’ role.  I’m always there for them when the house keeping is short, when hospital bills couldn’t be met and even when the poor bride couldn’t get pregnant quickly enough.
“I don’t ask any questions and I don’t want to be lumbered with any paternity problems.  I love my wife and the home we’ve been able to create.  If it is within my means to make other young marriages stable, where is the harm?  I don’t want a second wife, all I want is to be the godfather of good marriages.  Even when our affairs get into the head of some of these “wives”, I have counselled them on the virtue of being tolerant, instead of being rebellious and lumbering me with unwanted responsibility.  I’m sure my wife suspects that these women mean more to me than mere acquaintances.  She has caught me a few times almost with my pants down.  She’s made the right noise but, she’s never threatened to leave.  I am a good husband and my children even relate to me better than they do to their mother, so why would she want to rock the boat?”
It is common belief these days that adultery no longer signified the end of a marriage.  It doesn’t even mean that a marriage is in trouble.  According to experts, “adultery falls into two categories.  There are those who cheat because there is something wrong in the relationship, and there are those who cheat because there is a fault within themselves.  If your partner falls into the first bracket, there is a good chance he won’t misbehave again, provided you identify and sort out your problems.”
“There may be times when an affair is a wake-up call”, says a psychologist, “it’s probably less to do with the other woman than with the state of your relationship.  In such cases, an affair fulfils a need that isn’t being met within the main relationship.  And for some people, it is easier to look outside their marriage for what they’re missing than to admit there are problems.
She explains: “your man feels he’s playing second fiddle to the kids, so he finds a woman who tells him he’s number one.  He feels you don’t appreciate his finer points, so he finds a woman who tells him he’s the best thing that has ever happened to her.
“Some people even use an affair as a strategy for maintaining their marriage.  It can be an act of preservation rather than distinction.  But, if the reasons behind the betrayal are more to do with your partner’s personality, you could be in trouble.
Some experts believe that this type of adulterer has a personality disorder, which means he will continue cheating no matter what.”
The post Escapades of a typical ‘area father!’ appeared first on Vanguard News.

items.author: Emmanuel Okogba
items.content:
Immediately after the 2023 general elections, many politicians began illegal electioneering campaigns for the next set of elections scheduled for 2027. All efforts to remind them that they were abandoning governance which is the real essence of democracy and which should naturally follow elections failed. The truth however is that those cosmetic gestures across the nation made up of political alignments and defections which are essentially self-seeking do not constitute proper campaigns. Politicians with great ideas of how to improve the living standards of the people ought to be better disposed. They ought not to jump the gun by engaging in premature campaigns just as whatever campaigns they choose to participate in at the appropriate time should be detailed enough to aptly enlighten the people to make informed choices. Now that campaigns have rightly begun, politicians must not be allowed to be sleepy, instead they are obliged to educate us all on their manifestoes and election promises. It is against this backdrop that we call on all politicians to embrace issue-based campaigns and also to put an end to the practice of taking our citizens for granted.
In the last one week, Atiku Abubakar, the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress ADC appears to have gained some traction even without supplying us with all the details concerning the political messages he has fired. First, Atiku says if elected, he would restore fuel subsidy. The loud applause which greeted the promise does not mean that people understood how the maker intends to fulfil the promise. Ordinarily, considering the high level of corruption which surrounded subsidy since 1999 when the same Atiku was the nation’s vice president, a persuasive analysis of how he intends to accomplish the goal is what should deserve an applause but many people are excited because the candidate’s message suits the emotions of the moment. Atiku and his principal, Olusegun Obasanjo were in power from 1999 to 2007; they could not defeat the oil thieves that were described as a cartel by government. From then till 2023, successive governments established beyond reasonable doubt that the cartel was invincible. If Atiku is elected in 2027 and he restores subsidy, the cartel and fuel scarcity may return but at this point only a few would bother about that because it concerns the future.
At the peak of the Obasanjo-Atiku presidency, fuel price moved to N49 per litre thereby raising huge inflation of prices across the board. The hard-fighting Nigerian Labour Congress NLC of those days tackled the government. Federal and state officials and indeed the national council of states came up with a solution for each state to provide N200million naira to which the federal government was to donate N100m per state for the purchase of buses to be given to transporters to bring down the high cost of transportation at the time. Whereas the federal government met its own side of the arrangement, I think it was only Lagos and Oyo states that released their own counterpart funding. In short, the lofty idea eventually failed making it clear that as soon as some truce is achieved on a subject, government has a way of giving up on its promises. What this suggests is that it is unwise to trust politicians concerning the people’s welfare. Now that people are clapping for the likely return of subsidy, we expect the ruling party to task Atiku to give details of his plan to return the nation to what hurt us before. Meanwhile, no one knows if what Atiku is championing will be better or worse.
Indeed, what evidence is there that Atiku is not only looking for how to get into power? When did he discover the strategy, he wants to unfold now? While some people would see him as unpatriotic if he has always known it but chose to hoard it as a joker to be pulled up only when he comes to power, others would not trust the efficacy of the strategy if it was recently hurriedly designed to capture power. All of that is politics. What matters is that everyone will be forced to communicate; some may have to publish and translate their own viewpoint into several local languages because Nigerians have had cause not to trust any group that have at one time or the other constituted the governments of their country. In the case of the 2027 elections, not all Nigerians would be simplistic enough to accept slogans as election promises. If many people are unhappy with the result of ‘subsidy is gone’ why would most people not be more irritated if ‘I will bring back subsidy’ takes us back to the dark old days when no one knew the quantity of oil produced per day in Nigeria or even the number of trucks loaded per day or their destinations. Nigeria’s civic society should grow up.
The same respected presidential candidate has come up with another well-sounding statement namely that if elected into office in 2027, he would reopen all closed borders. His main argument that trans-border trade is a legitimate business has a point but can that alone be the basis for opening or closing borders? Theoretically, it can be argued that the closure of the borders of a country can hurt the economic interests of many trans-border traders. Consequently, opening the borders may have some advantages. There is doubt however if Atiku’s conclusion that the borders were unreasonably closed is correct. As a matter of fact, there is no evidence that the borders were still closed at the point the ADC candidate was promising to open them when elected. This is because some few hours after Atiku’s statement on border closure, the presidency countered him. According to Sunday Dare, the President’s Special Adviser on Media and Public Communication, ‘the federal government had reopened most of the country’s land borders in March 2024 and had not reversed the policy.’ He therefore questioned the basis of Atiku’s pledge, asking which borders the ADC presidential candidate intended to open when the existing policy already permits legitimate movement and trade.
The truth is that because our leaders are fond of taking us for granted Nigerians did not know whether our borders had been opened or closed. The little we all know consists of several controversies attributable to liberal policies concerning national borders. There is the issue of smuggling which reportedly increased when borders were left open without control. More importantly, not many Nigerians would be excited over the opening of borders considering the complexities of herder-farmer conflicts which assumed greater proportions following the influx of migrants in the days of free movement and visa on arrival policy in Nigeria. We all had to be admonished to avoid ethnic profiling and to recognize that all Fulani are not the same. Under the circumstance, no politician should resort to these sensitive issues without properly stating the details of his intention especially the arrangements he has designed for dealing with their effects.  We welcome the quick response by the presidency to Atiku’s statements which have since affected the reaction of some groups. The ensuing discussions have clearly established the importance of political debates which when properly organized can help our people to be better educated in making informed decisions. It is too late in the day considering our nation’s stunted growth to allow our politicians to continue to take the people for granted.
It is therefore hoped that in the days ahead, all our politicians will imbibe the spirit of political debates which are integral to the presidential system of government. As stated earlier, the ADC candidate has to be more forthcoming. His absence at the recent outing of major presidential candidates in Port Harcourt under the auspices of the Nigerian Bar Association was a minus more so as his vice, Rotimi Amaechi who was present made us believe that he was yet to be on the same page as his principal.  Similarly, the incumbent president, Bola Ahmed Tinubu was also absent. In Nigeria, handlers of incumbents are fond of making the same mistake that their candidate should be absent so as to avoid being the target. The posture is wrong because during a debate, he is essentially a presidential candidate seeking votes like all others. Bearing in mind that meeting the media, facing the camera and addressing a large audience are not Tinubu’s weaknesses, it is an error of judgment on the part of his handlers to talk him out of any presidential debate. In a properly moderated debate, a seasoned anchor will give no room for anyone to be targeted. Everyone should be free to appropriately brief all voters. It is time for Nigeria to be a communicating nation.
The post 2027 campaigns: More details needed, by Tonnie Iredia appeared first on Vanguard News.

items.author: Emmanuel Okogba
items.content:
Let’s begin by giving glory to God that we are alive to witness the last Sunday in the month of August.
Lamentations 3 vs. 22 ( KJV) “ It is of the LORD’s mercies that we are not consumed, because its compassions fail not”.
Beloved, you and I are beneficiaries of the Lord’s mercy and compassion. 
As the month of August commonly called the month of a “ New Beginning”, winds down, we should be prepared to testify to a new beginning.
A new beginning begins with new results that  make one glad.
If a student has been writing exams without success and he writes one that propels  him into excellence, certainly he’ll be happy as he  begins to experience a new beginning.
However, the student must have done something.   He probably devoted more time to his studies and  prayer sessions. These two activities would bring to manifestation in this life, the word of the God in Deuteronomy 28 vs. 12 : “ The LORD shall open unto thee his good treasure, the heaven to give the rain unto thy land in his season, and to bless  all the work of thine hand: and thou shalt lend unto many nations, and thou shalt not borrow”.
The emphasis  for us here is “ to bless  all the work of thine hand”.
Brethren, blessings may not come when we do nothing.   You have to do something to get something beyond your expectation from God.
It therefore means that you must prepare for blessings to be blessed. 
Results may never come when you refuse to prepare for it but when it comes, it ushers a season of joy.   Indeed a new beginning. 
When one experiences a challenge, that person is likely to be a subject of insults from mockers .   The attitude of such a person isn’t to fight back with insults , rather, it is to go to the Lord in prayer with a simply prayer point.
“ O God cancel every insult in my life”.  This simple  prayer made in faith regularly,  would produce results  in Jesus name.
You cannot afford to give up when you haven’t gotten results even when you get results you still need prayers to sustain and retain that miracle.
Psalm 37 vs. 5 tells us : “Commit thy way unto the LORD; trust also in him; and he shall bring it to pass”.
To commit your ways unto the LORD is to make a conscious effort to build your spiritual capacity with prayers, worship, thanksgiving and service to God.
This,   is a personal decision that you have to make.
I’ll share the testimony of a lady who was waiting on the Lord after many years of marriage.
She began to confess  the word of God in Deuteronomy 7 vs. 14: “ Thou shalt be blessed above all people: there shall not be male or female barren among you, or among your cattle”.
She  regularly repeated these Bible verse in a day.
Someone saw her walking and talking.  The person called her husband and asked, “ Is anything wrong with  your wife?  I saw your wife walking and talking to herself”.
Her husband told the person that his wife is perfectly okay .
It was not long after she started the daily and regular confession of the word that the she conceived.
Brethren, to get a result, you must meditate  on the word of God regularly.  Not only that, you need to memorise the Bible passage that address the challenge you want out of your life.
For instance a lawyer that goes to a judge without making reference to any judicial precedence   or what the law says about a case will never win a case.
To be a winner, you must prepare for results.
In the case of the woman mentioned earlier, after conception, she changed her prayer point with Exodus 23 vs. 26: “ There shall nothing cast their young, nor be barren, in thy land; the number of thy days I will fulfill”.
With these words of God, she laminated her self and the baby in her against all attacks of the enemy.
At the appropriate time she gave birth to a set of triplets.
She prepared for results and God gave her more than she expected.
Brethren, those who do not sow do not harvest. The season of harvest is the time of results, it is the time of joy and celebration.  It is the time that the  farmer forgets hard labour that has been put into farm work.
For other persons,  it is  the time to put the trauma of challenges behind. 
May God help us overcome all challenges in Jesus name.
So what do results bring for us as believers?
Results,  here refers to miracles that we expect from God.
For a woman called barren like Sarah, Hannah and Rachael,  the result that would cancel insults in her life is the birth of a child.
1st Samuel 1 verses 19 &20 : “ And they rose up in the morning early , and worshipped before the LORD, and returned, and came to their house in Ramah: and Elkanah knew Hannah his wife; and the LORD remembered her”.
Note that   Hannah  prepared for a miracle by pouring out her heart to the LORD in prayer and made a vow.
You make a vow when you believe that the prayer would be answered. It takes a high level of faith to make a vow.
Verse 20: “ Wherefore it came to pass, when the time was come about after Hannah had conceived, that she bare a son, and called his name Samuel, saying, Because  I have asked him of the LORD”.
Brethren, you get what you desire from the LORD provided you also prepare for it.
Healing is another result that can cancel insult.
A person held down with sickness   is likely to be  the subject of insults from those that   pretend to pity him.
Brethren may the LORD open our spiritual eyes to see beyond the physical.
It is not all  manifestations of illness that are physical.  Some have spiritual origins.
Our father in the Lord, Daddy Enoch Adeboye once said, if you do all tests and doctors see nothing and you remain unwell, you should realize that the problem is spiritual.
Therefore, you need to turn to Jesus pleading for mercy .
This prayer point is recommended.
“Merciful father, please remove every hand  of the enemy on my health and make me whole”.
There is a promise of God for us in Exodus 15 vs. 26: “ And said, If thou wilt diligently hearken to the voice of the LORD thy God, and wilt do that which is right in his sight, and will give ear to his commandments, and keep all his statues, I will put none of these diseases upon thee, which I have brought upon the Egyptians: for I am the LORD that healeth thee”.
These words are further sealed with the word, in Isaiah 53 vs. 5: “ But he was wounded for our transgressions, he was bruised for our iniquities:  the chastisement of our peace was upon him; and with his stripes we are healed”
Prepare and claim your right in the LORD.
It shall be well.

items.author: Emmanuel Okogba
items.content:
“Let justice be done, though the heavens fall” – Lord Mansfield, 1705-1793
“Once to every man and nation comes the moment to decide; in the strife of truth with falsehood, for the good or evil side” – James Russell Lowell, 1819-1891
Until now, there was no reason to raise the question about substantial justice untainted with legal subterfuges – like the Supreme Court decision which declared a fourth place finisher in an election the winner; after awarding him more votes than INEC announced were counted. The Nigerian judiciary, since that judgment, had steadily reduced public confidence in the Third Estate of the Realm. We are in the season again when justice would be tested to the limit. But, it is not only magistrates and “Your Lordships” who will be on trial before the entire world and posterity. Every Nigerian taking a position on this matter, in the court of public opinion is also on trial. Our ethical standards are on display as well. Each one of us is being asked to declare our position on alleged forgery and doubtful particulars – as well as omissions of relevant facts. I am aware that: “Money makes everything legitimate, including bastards” (Jewish proverb). But, for once, for the sake of our nation, we should not allow ourselves to be swayed by money or appointments. Only by facts.
One Federal High Court Justice already ruffled feathers by pronouncing on a matter before the Court of Appeal. Was it human error or willful judicial rascality? If a genuine mistake was made, then, decency demanded that the judge should have publicly apologised. If the measure was deliberate, the obvious questions are: Was it induced? What induced it? As the late Chief MKO Abiola would say: “Nobody stands all day in the rain for nothing”. Insults have rained down on the judge ever since.
Since our return to civil rule in 1999, alleged forged certificates have been revealed in every election by contestants for various offices. And virtually all the known claims of forged or dodgy credentials have ended the same way. The candidate was dismissed by the courts – giving the impression that the Nigerian judiciary would not condone anybody benefiting from illegality. That was noble of the judges who handled those cases.
ALL CANDIDATES ARE EQUAL. ARE SOME MORE EQUAL THAN OTHERS?
“Laws are like cobwebs where the small flies are caught; and the great breakthrough” – Francis Bacon, 1561-1626
China recently jailed, for life, the founder of one of the biggest real estate businesses the world has ever known – the EVERGRANDE – on account of fraud. At the peak of its success, the company employed over 150,000 people directly or indirectly. The convict was a dollar billionaire. But, China is a nation with zero tolerance for corruption. That was how it climbed to become the second biggest economic and military power globally. The case lasted less than six months.
In Nigeria, a combination of ruling party politicians, EFCC, selfish and unpatriotic Senior Advocates of Nigeria, and, above all, dishonourable justices would have ensured that the case languishes in court for years; or is inevitably concluded on terms favourable to the accused. One Prince Ajudua is still being tried for crimes allegedly committed more than 20 years ago even as about six sitting senators have their case files gathering dust in the EFCC office right now. Obviously, Nigerians, including some of our chief law officers, regularly condone lawlessness – if those involved are friends and benefactors.
“The law, in its majestic equality, forbids the rich as well as the poor to sleep under bridges, to beg on the streets and to steal bread” – Anatole France, 1844-1924.
Meanwhile, our judges waste no time sending poor offenders to jail for petty theft. In the time it had taken the cases against some senators to be bottled up, hundreds of thousands of poor Nigerians have been sentenced for stealing as little as a small goat.
Collectively, Nigerians have extended that ethical duplicity to politics. A member of the House of Representatives, representing a northern state, is kicked out and prosecuted for certificate forgery; and the people of Lagos, Ogun, Oyo, Osun, Ondo and Ekiti endorse the decision. Then a Lagos politician is accused of certificate forgery; suddenly, the same people are asking Nigerians to ignore the crime; for the judiciary to throw out the case and well-paid SANs have been lined up to ensure that their client gets away with unethical and illegal conduct. The judiciary is once again put on trial.
WILL NIGERIA AND THE JUDICIARY CONTINUE TO ENDORSE FORGERY?
“To be or not to be? That is the question.”
William Shakespeare, 1564-1616, in
Nigeria is at crossroads regarding whether we want to create a nation like the Nordic nations which, though smaller in size and population as well as lacking natural resources, have far greater Gross Domestic Productivity, GDP, than us. Or the giants, China, India and Brazil, blessed with population, landmass and natural resources; which have been used to propel them to the top 20 economies; instead of remaining mired in poverty. All the leading nations have enjoyed good leadership; defined as a combination of intelligence and integrity. Nobody can become the Prime Minister of India or President of China – whose entire life history is unknown. Open any search engine and the true life history – birth, father’s and mother’s names, primary and secondary schools, university attended, work experience etc – of the German Chancellor is revealed. Nothing is hidden. Consult the same search engine; ask for information about some leaders of Nigeria. The yawning gaps in the life history of some of the leaders of Africa’s most populated nation explain more eloquently than an entire book why Nigeria lags behind tiny Singapore in GDP – as well as per capita income. The integrity gap between Nigerian leaders and those of other nations represents the missing variable.
Can anybody imagine a candidate for Mayor of New York City, NYC, leaving out of his application form the names of his primary and secondary schools; and a State High Court deciding in his favour if his candidacy is contested? Why would someone deliberately omit information, which every other applicant for elective office has provided – for verification? Is concealment of fraud intended by the omission? Nigerian courts – State High, Federal High, Appeal Courts and the Supreme Courts of Nigeria -might soon be asked to answer that question.
DOES CHARACTER MATTER TO NIGERIANS ANYMORE?
 “A precedent embalms a principle” – Lord Stowell, 1745-1836.
Whether we like it or not, Nigeria has a truth problem confronting us in the coming 2027 elections. It might be the time we finally decide as a nation if certificate forgery is acceptable for all elections, some elections or no elections. We are not only confronted with pre-meditated omissions of vital information; even the certificates presented are being challenged as fake. Then, there is the lingering matter of hundreds of thousands of dollars voluntarily forfeited to the US government during an alleged shady past; and, curiously, the US Federal Bureau of Investigations, FBI, has stubbornly refused to release information concerning the matter. Silence sometimes tells a lot more than intended. When a globally respected crime fighting organization refuses to disclose information about an alleged crime, it only deepens suspicion. Nobody can make me give up one dollar; because it would have been earned legitimately; throwing away hundreds of thousands of dollars should be out of the question – for a man whose hands are clean. 
Obviously, we are not only being asked to forgive a suspicious omission of facts. We are also being requested to overlook the possibility of certificate forgery. Worst of all, we are collectively supposed to endorse the likelihood of illicit drug dealership – despite its documented destructive impacts on nations; including Nigeria. In that case, why not start by scrapping the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency, NDLEA? When a clown becomes king or queen, the palace becomes a circus. What happens when a suspected drug Lord ascends the throne? We are being asked to determine whether to continue to condone alleged questionable deeds. 
Nigerians, in general, and the judiciary in particular, will have a choice before or in 2027.
Everyone of us must bear in mind, as we cast our votes, that we will be affirming one principle or another. We could continue to promote corruption – in all its ramifications; or, we could decide, at last, to emulate those nations which have adopted zero tolerance as state policy.
“Wisdom in people consists of the anticipation of consequences” – Norman Cousins, 1915-1990.
Africans are the slowest learners on Earth. It is not an accident that our continent is also the most backward. Corruption is believed to be more widely accepted here than anywhere else; even in the judiciary. We have experienced the consequences of having dubious leaders. Can we stop? That is the question.
Follow me on Facebook @ J Israel Biola
The post Will the Judiciary condone forgery? By Dele Sobowale appeared first on Vanguard News.

items.author: Emmanuel Okogba
items.content:
By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta
The Eselu of Iselu Kingdom in Yewa North Local Government Area of Ogun State, Oba Akintunde Akinyemi, has urged residents of the State to thoroughly scrutinise all candidates seeking to succeed Governor Dapo Abiodun in the 2027 governorship election, irrespective of their political parties.
The monarch also called on civil society organisations and the media to investigate the backgrounds, credentials and antecedents of the candidates before the election.
Oba Akinyemi, who made the call while speaking with journalists on the sidelines of his house-warming ceremony at Obada-Oko area of Abeokuta, said the responsibility of choosing the next governor should not be left entirely to political parties, stressing that the electorate would ultimately bear the consequences of the choice made in 2027.
He said, “let me use this opportunity to tell the electorate, civil society organisations and the press that whoever is going to become the next Governor of Ogun State after Dapo Abiodun should be thoroughly, and I mean thoroughly, scrutinised.
“It is very important. We do not have another place to call our state.
“Whoever wants to take over from the governor, irrespective of the political party, should be subjected to thorough scrutiny. The media and civil society organisations should come together to investigate all the candidates thoroughly, including their family backgrounds. It is very, very important.”
The traditional ruler urged residents to ask critical questions about the individuals they intend to entrust with the leadership, governance and heritage of the state.
“Everyone who belongs to this state has to ask questions. We must question whoever we plan to entrust with our heritage and governance,” he said.
“This is no longer just about politics; it is about us and the critical stakeholders in the state. Everyone who belongs here must ensure that, if issues arise, we thoroughly understand the background and credentials of anyone who aspires to lead us.”
Speaking on the internal crisis in the Ogun State chapter of the All Progressives Congress (APC), particularly the controversy surrounding the party’s primary election involving Senator Solomon Adeola and Hon. Abayomi Hunye, Oba Akinyemi urged the party leadership to intervene and resolve the matter amicably.
The monarch expressed concern over what he described as the continuing agitation and counter-agitation arising from the dispute.
“I have been following the trend of the news, including the agitation and counter-agitation. I think we have to implore the party to call them together and resolve whatever differences they may have,” he said.
He questioned the controversy surrounding the votes allegedly recorded for Hunye during the primary election.
“If Abayomi Hunye participated in the primaries, it is impossible for him to have scored zero votes because he would have at least voted for himself. So, who stole his vote?” he queried.
“Even if the majority voted for Yayi, Hunye would not have cast his own vote for Yayi. Where did that single vote go?”
According to him, the issue raises questions that require clarification, particularly regarding Hunye’s participation in the primary and the recording of his vote.
“The core question is: what happened to his vote, and why was it not recorded? Had it been properly recorded, we might not be in this situation today,” he said.
Oba Akinyemi advised the political actors involved to resolve their differences and avoid actions capable of unnecessarily heightening political tension, particularly on social media.
“My advice to them is simple: put your house in order and stop unnecessarily overheating the polity on the internet,” he said.
Speaking on the role of traditional rulers in politics, the monarch said traditional rulers must remain politically neutral while ensuring that the electorate carefully examines candidates before making its choice.
“As traditional rulers in the state and having been on the throne for 21 years myself, our role is two-fold. First, we must remain neutral. Second, we must critically scrutinise every candidate, one by one. We must ensure that we do not make the wrong choice,” he said.
“I implore all my fellow traditional rulers to exercise extreme care this time around and choose the right candidate.”
On the agitation by the Yewa people for the governorship of Ogun State, Oba Akinyemi acknowledged the argument that the people had suffered political marginalisation, but said the overriding consideration should be the ability of the prospective governor to provide good governance.
“Yes, the Yewa people are agitating for the governorship because we have been marginalised. That is an undeniable fact. However, our primary goal should remain securing a leader who will deliver good governance,” he said.
He noted that political marginalisation was not peculiar to any particular ethnic group or region, stressing that the ultimate objective should be to elect a leader capable of delivering meaningful development to the people.
“Regardless of background, my core focus is good governance. I want a leader who will deliver the dividends of democracy, prioritise basic education and empower our people. That is what is paramount to me. That is my prayer.”

North Korea’s defence minister has been dismissed as part of a reshuffle of the country’s military leadership, state media reported Sunday.
The “structural reorganization plans” were decided during a meeting on Saturday led by Kim Jong Un, the Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) said.
No Kwang Chol was not only dismissed as defence minister but also demoted in the ruling party leadership to “first vice-director of the Munitions Industry Department,” KCNA said.
Kim Song Gi, director of the General Political Bureau of the Korean People’s Army, was named as the new defence minister.
Another senior official, defence advisor Pak Jong Chon, was given the position of vice-chairman of the Central Military Commission and named to the ruling party’s Political Bureau.
Several other promotions were also announced.
The leadership shuffle comes shortly after joint annual drills between South Korea and the United States wrapped up.

items.content:
North Korea’s defence minister has been dismissed as part of a reshuffle of the country’s military leadership, state media reported Sunday.
The “structural reorganization plans” were decided during a meeting on Saturday led by Kim Jong Un, the Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) said.
No Kwang Chol was not only dismissed as defence minister but also demoted in the ruling party leadership to “first vice-director of the Munitions Industry Department,” KCNA said.
Kim Song Gi, director of the General Political Bureau of the Korean People’s Army, was named as the new defence minister.
Another senior official, defence advisor Pak Jong Chon, was given the position of vice-chairman of the Central Military Commission and named to the ruling party’s Political Bureau.
Several other promotions were also announced.
The leadership shuffle comes shortly after joint annual drills between South Korea and the United States wrapped up.
The drills, which are regularly denounced by Pyongyang as preparations for an invasion, were closely watched this year after US President Donald Trump ordered them to be shortened.
Trump criticized the drills as provocative towards the North and bashed Seoul for not supporting his war against Iran.
The US president also praised North Korean leader Kim, whom he met twice during his first term in office.
AFP

Bishop David Oyedepo, Founder of Living Faith Church Worldwide, has described Pastor William Kumuyi as a sage whose ministry impacted lives globally.
Oyedepo spoke on Saturday at the August edition of the Global Crusade with Kumuyi (GCK), with theme, ‘Total Transformation Through Christ,’ in Ota, Ogun.
He said he had followed Kumuyi’s ministry from its early days and remained amazed by its strength, spiritual impact and influence.
“This man is a sage. Today, I am amazed at the strength, the unction and the impact of this ministry all through these years,” he said.
Oyedepo said he attended the crusade because “honour must be given to whom honour is due”, describing Kumuyi as a voice that had affected many globally.
“May this grace continue to multiply, in the name of Jesus,” he prayed.
He expressed confidence that participants would experience God’s grace throughout the programme, saying he expected remarkable things to happen.
Oyedepo subsequently spoke on “How Shall We Escape, If We Neglect So Great a Salvation?”, stressing the importance of genuine salvation.
Reading from Hebrews 2:3 and 2 Corinthians 13:5, he said salvation was not merely an ideology or belief but a tangible experience.
“Salvation is not an ideology; it is an experience. May everyone gathered here tonight be set to experience the salvation of Christ,” he said.
Oyedepo said his personal conversion was a definite experience, recalling that he gave his life to Christ on February 19, 1969, at the age of 15.
“There was no guesswork. I knew what took place in my life when I did,” he said.
He identified love, joy and peace as fruits that should characterise a regenerated life, urging Christians to examine their relationship with God.
The cleric also urged believers to take spiritual responsibility by obeying God’s Word and maintaining their faith despite temptations.
He stressed that reaching heaven required commitment and spiritual discipline because valuable things often came with a cost.
“Everything of value carries a cost. Heaven is the most valuable destination. Therefore, there are definite costs,” he said.
Kumuyi, while opening his sermon titled ‘The Great Transplanting of Blessings into Your Life’, praised Oyedepo’s steadfast faith.
He said their relationship dated back to the 1970s, adding that they were renewing their fellowship and looking forward to greater things.
“We enjoy one another fellowship as he and I are going younger at heart, we are re-establishing that fellowship, greater things are yet to come,” Kumuyi said.
The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that one of the striking testimonies came from Mrs Florence Okafor, whose husband, Sunday, battled mental illness for 17 years.
The testimony was among several accounts shared during the crusade, which entered its fourth day in Ota, with the grand finale scheduled for Sunday.
(NAN)

The Argentina international was left out of the matchday squad in Seville, having been booed by his own fans last weekend in a 2-2 home draw with Villarreal.
The two forwards who started in his absence combined to great effect to give Atletico a fourth-minute lead.
Lee Kang-in, a summer signing from European champions Paris Saint-Germain, played an excellent pass in behind for Alex Baena to rifle a low shot into the net.
The Rojiblancos doubled their advantage in the 26th minute, as Ademola Lookman planted a clever shot inside Sevilla goalkeeper Odysseas Vlachodimos’s near post.
Atletico were three goals in front just seven minutes later as Spanish World Cup winner Baena scored his second.
Baena drove ashot into the bottom corner from outside the box after being teed up by Marcos Llorente.
Sevilla improved in the second half and pulled one back through Miguel Sierra’s volley, but never looked like mounting a comeback.
– Betis lose 100% record –
Earlier, Real Betis lost their perfect start as Roger Brugue helped Levante to a 5-2 victory.
Betis, whose fifth-place finish last term secured them a long-awaited return to the Champions League, would have gone top with a third win from as many outings to start their domestic campaign.
But it was not to be for Manuel Pellegrini’s charges as goals from Adrian de la Fuente, Enzo Bardeli, Brugue and Jon Ander Olasagasti secured the hosts their first win of the season.
De la Fuente broke the deadlock at the Ciutat de Valencia with a glancing header from a corner in the 24th minute.
Shortly after the half-hour, former Barcelona centre-half Marc Bartra levelled for Betis with a forceful effort from the edge of the box.
The match really sparked into life under the late summer Valencian sun as the clock ticked past 45 minutes.
Bardeli displayed fantastic technique and imagination two minutes into added time as he pounced on a loose defensive pass and launched a chip from well over 40 yards that left Betis goalkeeper Alvaro Valles helpless.
But the visitors managed to go into the break on level terms as Rodrigo Riquelme tucked in a flick-on from a corner.
But a double from Brugue — the first another set-piece goal, before he bundled home from close range after Ivan Romero had struck the post — and a late Olasagasti header sealed the win.
Real Sociedad got their first points of the season with a 2-1 home win over Espanyol.
AFP

…promises Oju-Awajir road completion, more legacy projects
By Peter Duru, Makurdi
Governor Hyacinth Alia of Benue State has announced plans to upgrade the College of Education, Oju, into a more standard tertiary institution as part of efforts to expand access to quality education and create greater opportunities for youths in the state.
Alia made the disclosure at a Town Hall Meeting with stakeholders from Oju/Obi Federal Constituency at the auditorium of the College of Education, Oju, during his statewide Thank-You Tour.
The governor, who said the institution would be given a new nomenclature following its upgrade, also assured the people of the constituency that the ongoing construction of the Oju-Awajir Road would be completed.
He said his administration would embark on additional legacy projects in the area, stressing that the government remained committed to spreading development across the state.
On industrial development, Alia disclosed that plans were underway to revive the moribund Igumale Cement Factory in Enone, saying experts had already inspected the facility ahead of its rehabilitation.
According to him, the revival of the cement factory and other industries would boost employment, increase economic activities and improve the living standards of the people.
The governor also urged Benue farmers to increase food production, assuring them that government investments in agro-industrial projects would provide ready markets for their produce.
“Our people should go into extensive farming because industries are coming. When we revive these industries, there will be a ready market for what our farmers produce,” he said.
Alia cited the Food Basket Brewery, Fruit Juice Company, revived Taraku Mills and other industrial projects as efforts to establish a functional agricultural value chain and curb post-harvest losses.
He said the emerging industrial base would end the situation where farmers were compelled to sell their produce at giveaway prices because of lack of markets.
On security, Alia reiterated his administration’s opposition to the ceding of any portion of Benue land for ranching, insisting that the land belonged to the people and must remain available for farming and other legitimate uses.
He said the government would continue the fight against insecurity until lasting peace was restored, while commending President Bola Ahmed Tinubu for approving an Army Division in Benue, with headquarters in Makurdi and deployments to strategic locations.
Alia thanked the Igede people for their support for his administration and President Tinubu, urging them to sustain the partnership and renew their mandates in 2027 to enable both governments consolidate their achievements.
Earlier, the governor had met with traditional rulers and religious leaders in Oju/Obi Federal Constituency. The monarchs subsequently conferred on him the chieftaincy title, “Ogakwu of Igede Land,” meaning “Strong Man of Igede,” in recognition of his leadership and development efforts.
The Commissioner for Youth, Sports and Creativity, Nick Oworo, who hails from the area, praised the administration’s achievements in security, infrastructure, education, healthcare and human development, describing the progress recorded in three years as unprecedented.
At the Ado/Okpokwu/Ogbadibo Federal Constituency, the governor also held meetings with traditional rulers, religious leaders, political leaders, government officials and other stakeholders.
The Deputy Governor, Dr Sam Ode, highlighted the administration’s interventions across Benue South, including road construction and rehabilitation, agricultural and agro-processing investments, healthcare and education improvements, infrastructure upgrades and measures to strengthen security.
APC State Chairman, Chief Benjamin Omale, said Alia’s administration had gone beyond physical infrastructure to prioritise the welfare of the people, urging stronger grassroots mobilisation ahead of the 2027 elections.
The Town Hall meetings, attended by political office holders, traditional rulers, religious leaders and other stakeholders, are part of the governor’s statewide appreciation and consultation tour.

By Kingsley Omonobi
The Inspector-General of Police, IGP Olatunji Rilwan Disu, has ordered intensified operations to secure the release of worshippers abducted during a recent attack on communities in the Dekara District of Borgu Local Government Area of Niger State.
IGP Disu gave the directive on Saturday, August 29, 2026, during a working visit to the state to assess the security situation and ongoing efforts to rescue the victims.
Force Public Relations Officer, CSP Ani Iniedu in a statement said the IGP visited the Niger State Government House, where he was received by the Deputy Governor, Comrade Yakubu Garba, who represented Governor Mohammed Umaru Bago, alongside the Commissioner for Homeland Security, Barr. Maurice Bello Magaji.
Disu conveyed the condolences of the Nigeria Police Force to the Niger State Government, the affected communities and families of the victims, assuring them that the safe recovery of the abducted persons and the arrest of those responsible remained the focus of ongoing operations.
The IGP commended the Commissioner of Police, Niger State Command, CP Adamu Abdullahi Elleman, for the Command’s response to the incident and timely situation reports.
He also acknowledged the support of the Niger State Government to the Police, particularly through the provision of operational vehicles, repairs of Armoured Personnel Carriers and welfare assistance for police personnel.
Addressing officers and men of the Niger State Police Command, Disu charged them to sustain intelligence-led and professionally coordinated operations, with priority given to the safety of the victims and affected communities.
He assured the Command of continued support from Force Headquarters to enhance its logistics, mobility, intelligence, training and operational capabilities.
The IGP also directed the Command to strengthen inter-agency coordination and deepen engagement with communities, stressing the importance of stronger partnerships with traditional rulers, religious leaders, community leaders and other stakeholders in intelligence gathering and early response to security threats.
The Deputy Governor, in his remarks, commended Disu for personally visiting the state to assess the situation and reinforce ongoing operations.
He reaffirmed the state government’s commitment to supporting the Police and other security agencies in protecting lives, restoring peace and securing the release of the abducted persons.
As part of the visit, the IGP also met with the Emir of Minna, Alhaji Dr. Umar Farouk Bahago, to commiserate with the Emirate and strengthen collaboration with traditional institutions in intelligence gathering, community engagement and efforts to restore peace across Niger State.
The Nigeria Police Force reaffirmed its determination to rescue the abducted persons, protect affected communities and bring the perpetrators of the attack to justice.

items.content:
Liverpool forward Cody Gakpo has decided to join Manchester City, with the two clubs reportedly in talks to reach an agreement, according to The Athletic.
The 27-year-old Netherlands international has reportedly opted against a move to Tottenham Hotspur and wants to complete a transfer to the Etihad Stadium.
Gakpo started Liverpool’s 2-2 draw with Nottingham Forest on Saturday, providing an assist during the Premier League fixture.
Gakpo’s potential departure comes after Liverpool reached an agreement to sign Paris Saint-Germain winger Bradley Barcola.
City’s interest in Gakpo was first reported on August 24, with the Manchester club looking to strengthen their attacking options following the departures of Savinho and Omar Marmoush to Tottenham this summer.
The report added that City have also agreed a €40 million (£34.3 million) deal to sign Palmeiras winger Allan Elias.
Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola had earlier said he “cannot guarantee anything” regarding Gakpo’s future at the club.
Gakpo joined Liverpool from PSV Eindhoven in December 2022 in a deal worth an initial £37 million, with the transfer potentially rising to £44 million through add-ons.
He scored seven goals in 21 Premier League appearances during the second half of his first season at Anfield.
Gakpo then enjoyed a productive 2024-25 campaign, scoring 18 goals and providing seven assists in 49 appearances as Liverpool won the Premier League title. He subsequently signed a new five-year contract with the club in August 2025.
His form declined during the second half of the 2025-26 season, although he continued to feature regularly for Liverpool.
The forward also scored three goals in four appearances for the Netherlands at the 2026 World Cup before his country exited the tournament following a penalty shootout defeat to Morocco in the last-32 stage.
Gakpo has made 180 appearances for Liverpool, scoring 50 goals and providing 23 assists.
Manchester City see the Dutch forward as an option who could provide competition and cover for Erling Haaland while also offering flexibility in wide attacking positions.
The Athletic’s Manchester City reporter Sam Lee noted that Gakpo’s Premier League experience, physicality, goalscoring record and versatility could make the proposed move a logical addition to City’s squad.
Lee also pointed to the difficulty City have faced in recruiting forwards willing to operate as alternatives to Haaland because of the striker’s established role in the team.
Gakpo’s ability to play centrally or from the wings could therefore give City additional tactical options.
The report indicates that the transfer fee is expected to be substantial, with negotiations continuing between Liverpool and Manchester City over the terms of the proposed deal.

By Golok Nanmwa, Jos
JOS- The Plateau State Police Command has said it recovered sophisticated weapons from suspected bandits during an intelligence-led operation in Barkin Ladi Local Government Area of the state.

“During the operation, the team encountered a group of suspected bandits. Upon sighting the Police operatives, the suspects immediately fled into the surrounding forest.

The police spokesman said additional personnel had been deployed to the area, while efforts were ongoing to apprehend the fleeing suspects.
He added that an investigation had commenced into the incident, noting that further developments would be communicated to the public.
Meanwhile, the Commissioner of Police in the state, CP Ayodeji Faniyan, commended the operatives for their courage and commitment to duty.
Faniyan reassured residents of the state of the Command’s determination to sustain efforts aimed at preventing criminal activities and protecting lives and property.
He also urged residents to remain vigilant and promptly report suspicious activities within their communities to the nearest police station or other relevant security agencies.

items.content:
By Peter Duru, Makurdi
A 200-level Political Science student of Rev. Fr. Moses Orshio Adasu University (MOAUM), Rose Adikwu, has been hospitalised in Makurdi after she was allegedly scalded with hot water during a disagreement with her cousin and co-tenant.
Adikwu, who is currently receiving treatment at a private hospital in the Benue State capital, was reportedly left with severe burns after the alleged attack on Friday, August 28, 2026.
The suspect, identified as Agbo Felicia, a 500-level Chemistry student, was subsequently arrested by the police following the incident.
Narrating her ordeal to the Students’ Union President, Akighirga Vitalis, and other union executives who visited her at the hospital, Adikwu said the incident followed a prolonged disagreement between her and Felicia, with whom she had been living.
According to her, tensions between them over personal matters worsened to the point where she asked Felicia to vacate the apartment.
Adikwu alleged that after Felicia packed her belongings, she went to a neighbour’s room, boiled water and mixed it with pepper, salt, onions and seasoning before allegedly returning to the apartment.
She claimed that Felicia subsequently poured the hot mixture over her, locked the door and left her inside.
“She then returned to the apartment and poured the hot mixture on me, locked the door, and left me inside while I cried for help,” Adikwu alleged.
She said her cries attracted neighbours, who intervened and rescued her, while Felicia was reportedly intercepted as she attempted to leave the area.
The police were later invited and the suspect was arrested.
Reacting to the incident, the Students’ Union President expressed concern over Adikwu’s condition, describing the alleged attack as “a grave and unacceptable assault on the life and well-being of a fellow student.”
“We are deeply concerned about this incident. The Students’ Union will follow this matter closely until justice prevails,” Vitalis told the victim and her family.
He assured the family that the union would engage relevant authorities, monitor the police investigation and follow any disciplinary proceedings that might arise within the university.
Vitalis added that if the allegations were established through due process, the union would support appropriate sanctions in line with the institution’s regulations, including expulsion where warranted.
“The Students’ Union will not condone violence or any conduct capable of endangering the life of another student,” he said.
He urged students experiencing disagreements with roommates, relatives or colleagues to seek peaceful intervention rather than resort to violence.
“I encourage students experiencing personal disagreements to seek intervention from University authorities, Students’ Union structures, or law enforcement agencies rather than resorting to violence,” he said.
The union president was accompanied during the hospital visit by other members of the Students’ Union executive.
In a statement signed by the Press Secretary to the Students’ Union President, Mark Tyodoo, and made available to newsmen in Makurdi, the union said it remained committed to the welfare and safety of students.
Meanwhile, the Police Public Relations Officer, Benue State Command, DSP Peter Aondongu, confirmed the incident and the arrest of the suspect.
Aondongu said preliminary information available to the command indicated that both students were living together before the disagreement occurred.
“Yes, it happened yesterday, Friday, August 28, 2026,” the police spokesman said.
“From the information I have, both students were staying in the same room and had an issue. The suspect allegedly boiled water, added salt and pepper, and poured the mixture on the victim and then locked her inside.
“After some time, people became aware of what had happened and were able to intervene and rescue the victim. She was subsequently taken to the hospital for treatment, while the suspect was arrested.
“I don’t have much information yet about the genesis of the disagreement or what led to the incident, but I can confirm that the incident happened. I also understand that both of them are students of the Benue State University.”
The police spokesman said investigation into the circumstances surrounding the incident was ongoing.
