items.content:
Members of Niger’s presidential guard, helped by Russian forces on Saturday, recaptured a key military base in the capital Niamey from mutinous soldiers.
Read Also: 2027 Campaign: What we want to hear from candidates – Stakeholders
Diplomatic and security sources revealed this to AFP.
“The presidential guard has retaken control of the air base with the help of the Russians,” said a diplomatic source.
The source added that several of the rebelling soldiers had been killed. Two security sources confirmed that the base had been retaken.
Confirming the latest developments, Niger’s ruling junta said it was back in control after the mutinous soldiers set off armed clashes in Niger’s capital Saturday, moving on the presidential palace and disrupting the state broadcaster.
Niger has been ruled for three years by a military junta led by General Abdourahamane Tiani that has struggled to contain jihadist violence flaring in the west African country for around a decade.
After hours of heavy exchanges around some of its most sensitive sites, the junta said it had largely wrested back control from the rebel soldiers.
The fighting appeared to have subsided later Saturday, even if a regional security source and an African diplomatic source said the rebelling troops still held two barracks around Niamey.
But by Saturday evening, diplomatic and security sources told AFP that members of Niger’s presidential guard helped by Russian forces had recaptured the air base, killing some of the mutineers.
When fighting broke out, shortly after midnight, soldiers blocked access to the presidential palace and the national television station, Tele Sahel, which went off the air for just over an hour, before being restored around 10 a.m.
Niger’s ruling junta later declared, in a statement read on state television, that it was gradually taking back control after hours of clashes.
“There was an attempt by insurgents from the Nigerien armed forces to enter the presidential palace,” a security source told AFP, adding that the presidential guard had pushed them back.
Niger’s defence minister, General Salifou Mody, said on state television that a group of soldiers had held some troops hostage at a barracks in Niamey, opening fire at “certain sensitive sites” in the city, without specifying which ones.
Troops and security forces had quickly taken back control, he added, calling on local people to remain calm.
‘Bursts of gunfire’
The first shots were heard at about 1:00 am local time and continued until daybreak, according to a video published by a local journalist filming the area around the airport.
The military issued a statement on its social media pages urging people to stay calm and “avoid sharing unverified information”.
One local resident speaking to AFP reported “heavy gunfire and explosions” at Base 101 in Niamey, a claim confirmed by several other witnesses.
Another said he had heard “bursts of gunfire” at about 7:00 am local time, adding that the weapons heard “are not the kind that terrorists on motorbikes can carry”.
He added: “I saw a military vehicle heading towards the base that had to turn back.”
Videos online showed armoured vehicles deployed to reinforce the neighbourhood near the airport.
Air Force Base 101, located within the international airport complex, is home to the headquarters of Russia’s Africa Corps in Niamey
The site is sensitive. Between December and January, it hosted a large shipment of uranium concentrate, which was held up while awaiting export. No movement of the shipment has been identified since.
The base is also the command of the unified force of the Alliance of Sahel States, of which Niger is a member with Burkina Faso and Mali.
Junta supporters called for “sincere patriots” to demonstrate in support of the authorities at a major Niamey square.
Rival jihadist groups
By late afternoon, a few dozen people had converged on the square. Military music praising General Tiani was playing as a platform intended for speeches was being set up.
Neighbouring Algeria condemned Saturday’s events and pledged support for the Niamey government.
Niamey airport has been targeted twice this year by jihadists, first by the Islamic State in the Sahel, EIS, in January, then in late June by its rival, the Group for the Support of Islam and Muslims, JNIM, the Sahel branch of Al-Qaeda.
The jihadist groups not only target civilians and the military but are also struggling for dominance over each other in the Sahel, and especially in Niger.
The EIS and JNIM are also active in neighbouring allies Burkina Faso and Mali, which are also ruled by military juntas that seized power in coups.
The three countries quit the Economic Community of West African States, ECOWAS, bloc, turned their backs on traditional Western partners in the fight against jihadist violence, especially France, and sought closer ties with Russia.
Vanguard News

items.author: Emmanuel Okogba
items.content:
The Chairman of Ifelodun Local Council Development Area (LCDA), Mr Olufemi Okeowo, has appointed another 250 Special Assistants (SAs) and Senior Special Assistants (SSAs) to strengthen governance in the area.
Okeowo disclosed this on Saturday while presenting 2,500 food packs to residents in need and cash grants to petty traders in the area.
NAN reports that Okeowo appointed 128 SSAs and SAs in July.
Okeowo said the presentation of appointment letters to another 250 SAs and SSAs reflected his commitment to building a more responsive and inclusive government.
The chairman said the appointments formed part of ongoing efforts to strengthen governance at all levels and improve policy implementation.
He said the appointments would ensure effective delivery of the dividends of democracy to residents of the LCDA.
Okeowo said the newly appointed aides were expected to complement his achievements in infrastructure, healthcare, education, youth empowerment, environmental sustainability, sports and social welfare.
He congratulated the appointees and expressed readiness to work closely with them to deepen collective efforts toward moving the council to greater heights.
The chairman said the removal of fuel subsidy had enabled his administration to provide N10,000 conditional monthly cash transfers to 1,200 households across all wards.
Okeowo said the council was also distributing N100,000 monthly OkeMoney business support to 100 petty traders and food palliatives to 2,500 households.
He said increased allocations to local governments following the removal of fuel subsidy had enabled his administration to give back to communities.
Okeowo said the development reflected the support and commitment of President Bola Tinubu’s administration to local governments.
He said the increased allocations had enabled the council to provide healthcare, free education, empowerment, palliatives and infrastructure to residents.
Okeowo noted that fuel subsidy payments had constituted a major leakage that drained the country’s economy under previous administrations.
Also speaking, the Commissioner for Basic and Secondary Education in Lagos State, Mr Tolani Alli-Balogun, described the initiatives as dividends of democracy, a new dawn and a new beginning.
Alli-Balogun said the appointment of 250 SAs and SSAs would further reduce poverty among residents of the local government.
The commissioner said the entrepreneurial loans in the form of grants to citizens of Ifelodun were also making waves and benefiting residents.
Residents and community leaders applauded the chairman’s grassroots empowerment schemes, infrastructural projects and food distribution.
One of the beneficiaries, Mr John Oke, said the food items would help sustain his family for several days.
Oke commended the chairman for providing the food items and prayed that his administration would continue to progress.

Read Also: Two dead as machete-wielding man storms IMAX cinema in Lekki
Hamzat said this on Saturday during the monthly environmental sanitation exercise in Festac, Amuwo-Odofin Local Government Area of Lagos.
Hamzat said the additional trucks would complement the operations of Private Sector Participation, PSP, operators and expand the state’s capacity to evacuate refuse, particularly from areas where existing arrangements were struggling to meet demand.
According to him, “The state government will be bringing in another 220 trucks to make sure that we supplement our PSP,” he said.
He explained that the decision was necessitated by the increasing volume of waste generated in the state as a result of its rapidly expanding population.
According to him, the continuous influx of people into Lagos has placed additional pressure on existing waste management infrastructure and services.
“A lot of people are coming to Lagos, and therefore they generate waste. So part of what you can see that we are doing is that we are getting many more trucks to actually go and evacuate,” Hamzat said.
The deputy governor urged residents to patronise accredited PSP operators rather than cart pushers, who, according to him, often operate outside the regulated waste management system.
“What we need our people to also do is to make sure that they patronise their PSP, not the cart pushers, because they are not organised.
“You don’t know where the waste is ending up,” he said.
The deputy governor called on residents to sustain environmental sanitation beyond the monthly exercise and make the cleanliness of their homes and communities a routine responsibility.
“We cannot be a people without a healthy environment. It doesn’t matter what we do, a cleaner environment is what makes a city or a state sustainable,” Hamzat said.
Hamzat also addressed environmental management concerns in Festac. Hamzat said the Federal Housing Authority had specific responsibilities in the area but stressing that residents and property managers remained subject to the environmental regulations of the Lagos State Government.

items.author: Emmanuel Okogba
items.content:
Former Senator Ben Murray-Bruce has called on President Bola Tinubu to pursue a more decentralised approach to electricity generation and distribution, arguing that Nigeria needs to reduce its reliance on the national grid and encourage community-based power solutions.
Murray-Bruce made the proposal in an open letter to the President in which he examined challenges affecting electricity generation, transmission, distribution, metering and financing in the country.
He cited data from the Nigerian Electricity Regulatory Commission, NERC, which he said showed a significant gap between Nigeria’s installed generation capacity and the amount of electricity available for dispatch. According to him, the country had 13,625 megawatts of installed capacity in April, but only about 4,286MW was available for dispatch.
He also referred to a decline in grid generation on August 22, when output, according to him, fell to about 1,132MW in the evening from more than 4,000MW earlier in the day.
“These figures should make it clear that Nigeria’s electricity challenge is not simply about building more generating capacity. We need to examine the entire structure of the sector, including how power is generated, transmitted, distributed, metered and paid for,” he said.
The former senator criticised the outcome of the 2013 electricity-sector privatisation, arguing that the reform did not deliver the transformation Nigerians expected.
“The 2013 privatisation was not the transformation Nigerians expected. In my view, it largely amounted to a transfer of custody without ensuring that the new owners had the financial strength and technical capacity required to make the system work at the scale Nigeria needs,” he said.
Murray-Bruce also highlighted the country’s metering gap, saying millions of active electricity customers remained without meters. He argued that estimated billing could make it difficult for consumers to monitor their electricity consumption and expenditure.
“A meter is a machine that tells the truth. An estimated bill is a machine that does not. If we want consumers to trust the electricity market, metering has to become a priority,” he said.
He proposed a model in which estates, communities and other local areas could develop their own electricity systems, particularly through solar generation, subject to appropriate financing and regulation.
“Every village, every estate and every community in Nigeria should have the opportunity to develop an electricity solution suited to its own circumstances,” he said.
According to him, greater community participation could create new investment opportunities while reducing pressure on the national grid.
Murray-Bruce also urged state governments to take greater responsibility for powering public facilities under their control, including streetlights, schools and primary healthcare centres, while the Federal Government focuses on federal infrastructure.
He said the Electricity Act 2023 had created greater opportunities for states to participate in electricity regulation and development.
The former senator cited Aba as an example of how localised generation and distribution could complement the national electricity system.
Murray-Bruce urged the Federal Government to coordinate reforms that would encourage decentralised generation, private investment and stronger accountability across the sector.
He expressed optimism that a combination of government reforms, private investment and community participation could improve electricity reliability and reduce the economic burden associated with power shortages.

items.author: Henry Oduah
items.content:
The late Dr Frederick Fasehun faction of the O’odua People’s Congress (OPC) on Saturday declared support for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election in 2027.
The ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‌‍​‌⁠⁠​⁠‍‌​group made the declaration in Lagos on Saturday at the celebration of its 32nd Founders Day and inauguration of a new National Executive Council (NEC).
The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) recalls that OPC was founded on Aug. 29, 1994, and was established by a group of Yoruba nationalists and activists, led by medical doctor and human rights activist, Dr Frederick Fasehun.
Speaking at the event, the OPC’s re-elected President, Mr Wasiu Afolabi, promised that the group would work for the President the same way they did for his first shot at the presidency in 2023.
He said: “We contributed our quota to ensuring the victory of Tinubu in 2023. One lesson from Fasehun is that the organisation should regard any Yoruba man in office as OPC’s corporate project.
“As a result of this orientation that our founder gave us, and if the right atmosphere is created, we shall still queue behind President Tinubu for the 2027 presidential election.
“We also urge the other regions to support the President’s second-term bid to help him perfect the visionary reforms he has embarked upon.
“The North especially, should realise that it is payback time for the backing that Tinubu gave to late President Muhammadu Buhari’s two tenures of eight years.”
Afolabi recalled the national crisis that brought about the formation of OPC in August 1994, saying that “Some 32 years ago when Dr. Frederick Fasehun took the initiative to establish OPC, it was to fulfil a divine assignment. OPC was born as a child of necessity.”
Afolabi said the June 12 mandate of late Chief Moshood Abiola was stolen by the military government, which was not only an insult to the eight million Nigerian voters, who had given that mandate to MKO but especially a direct insult to the over 40 million-strong Yoruba race.
Afolabi urged the president, governors, and all national and federal legislators to promote policies, programmes and projects that would tackle the prevailing issues and challenges in Nigeria as a matter of national emergency.
“The leaders must remember that the Nigerian Constitution they all swore to uphold says in Section 14(2)(b) that the security and welfare of the people shall be the primary purpose of government,” he said.
Afolabi also offered the assistance of OPC toward solving the “monster problem of insecurity,” saying: “We are ready to partner with relevant government agencies to secure the South-West from enemies within and enemies from outside.”
Concerning the 2027 elections, he urged the Independent National Electoral Commission and security agencies to maintain a neutral role and ensure that the vote of every voting Nigerian counts.
Also speaking, Chairman of the occasion, Mr Wale Oshun, said the group remained a foremost legacy organisation in Nigeria’s struggle for democracy after the military annulled the June 12, 1993 election of Late M.K.O. Abiola.
Oshun, who heads OPC’s Board of Trustees, said that it is a glowing tribute to the founder, Dr. Fasehun’s vision that the organisation had continued to thrive, eight years after the leader died.
NAN reports that hundreds of members of the group were on ground to celebrate its 32nd anniversary and to also endorse Tinubu’s second tenure.
(NAN)

items.title: Iran signals no retreat amid US sanctions
items.summary:
Iranian leaders are acknowledging the economic toll of war with the US, with the supreme leader urging the government to address the hardship and the president saying foreign trade has shrunk by a third due to the American sanctions and blockade.
Yet Tehran signalled no retreat on Saturday, vowing to withstand US pressure, pursue diplomacy and maintain what it said was control over the Strait of Hormuz, the strategic waterway giving Iran leverage through its ability to disrupt global energy markets.
The government said in a statement on state media that addressing economic pressures caused by sanctions and war was a central focus, including curbing inflation, managing markets, creating jobs, directing investment towards domestic production and gradually reducing dependence on the dollar.

items.author: Reuters
items.content:
Iranian leaders are acknowledging the economic toll of war with the US, with the supreme leader urging the government to address the hardship and the president saying foreign trade has shrunk by a third due to the American sanctions and blockade.
Yet Tehran signalled no retreat on Saturday, vowing to withstand US pressure, pursue diplomacy and maintain what it said was control over the Strait of Hormuz, the strategic waterway giving Iran leverage through its ability to disrupt global energy markets.
The government said in a statement on state media that addressing economic pressures caused by sanctions and war was a central focus, including curbing inflation, managing markets, creating jobs, directing investment towards domestic production and gradually reducing dependence on the dollar.
Six months after the US and Israel launched the war, negotiations are at an impasse and President Donald Trump's administration has stepped up efforts to punish Iran financially with what it has billed as an "economic D-Day".
Washington has warned countries to cut business ties with Iran or face secondary sanctions, though the Treasury Department stopped short of imposing penalties against major Iranian trade partners such as China and India, which could have repercussions for the US and global economies.
The Treasury imposed sanctions on Egypt's Banque Misr for doing business with Tehran, proposing a rule that would cut off the bank's branches in the United Arab Emirates from dollar transactions.
Egypt's central bank said it and the foreign ministry were in contact with US officials concerning the matter, adding the measure was limited to Banque Misr UAE's US dollar transactions with correspondent banks only.
Banque Misr said on Saturday it was reviewing the US Treasury notice, adding that its branch in the UAE continued to provide banking services to its customers.
The US has also issued sanctions targeting an entity based in Hong Kong and a person linked to Iran's Bank Melli, according to a notice on the Treasury website.
The sanctions drive compounds the toll of the war on Iran's economy, where annual inflation hit 66% last month.
Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei - who has not been seen publicly since he was injured in the initial February 28 attack that killed his father and former Supreme Leader, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei - called on the government to tackle the economic hardship.
"There is the need to seriously address the chain of economic and livelihood challenges, such as inflation, unemployment, management of prices and the market for goods and services," he said, according to a written statement attributed to Khamenei.
President Masoud Pezeshkian told state media that Iranian exports and imports had slumped nearly 35% because of US sanctions and a naval blockade of Iranian ports.
But he said Iran was able to sell about 90 million barrels of oil during the short-lived memorandum of understanding that the US and Iran signed in June, when Washington permitted Iranian oil sales.
Later on Saturday, Pezeshkian called on state TV for a revival of the interim deal, which was signed on June 17 but quickly unravelled amid disagreements over what had been agreed, especially on the status of the Strait of Hormuz.
"We can solve our problems and gain our privileges with the memorandum of understanding," he said of a document that had offered Iran, among other things, immediate relief from US sanctions and the release of its frozen assets.
With the US focused on its economic pressure campaign, others have sought to revive diplomatic efforts to end the war.
Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani met with Iranian leaders in Tehran on Thursday. He said he had stressed during the meeting the importance of returning to the pre-war status of open shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi on Friday described the talks with Al Thani as "creative".
In Saturday's statement, Iran said diplomacy and defence were "two complementary, coordinated and inseparable wings" for protecting the country's national interests, security and territorial integrity. It said it would pursue both tracks in a balanced manner.
Qatar, a US ally and Gulf neighbour to Iran, and Pakistan helped broker the June memorandum of understanding.
Before the war, the Strait of Hormuz carried 20% of the world's oil and LNG. US military commanders say American forces have cleared sea mines from the strait that had been laid months ago by Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.
Trump has repeatedly said the strait is open, but the Revolutionary Guards' navy said in a statement that such claims "are an obvious lie", reiterating that the waterway remained closed to ships without Iranian permission.

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Saturday ordered immediate action against eight people identified by an inquiry committee over the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS) neonatal ward fire, approving their suspension as well as departmental and criminal proceedings.
The directives came after fourteen newborn babies were killed on Wednesday after a fire broke out on the third floor of the Mother and Child Hospital ward.
According to a statement issued by the Prime Minister's Office, the premier presided over a high-level meeting on the incident, during which he was presented with the inquiry committee's interim report and CCTV footage of the incident lasting around two minutes.
The prime minister directed that those found responsible for criminal negligence be prosecuted without discrimination and said they did not deserve any concession.
Among the eight people identified by the committee are PIMS Executive Director Prof Dr Imran Sikandar, Joint Executive Directors Dr Mutahir Shah and Chaudhry Dr Owais Ali Shah, head of the neonatal department Prof Dr Sadia Riaz, senior registrar Dr Naghma, Dr Nousheela Amjad, PIMS Assistant Director Security Mohammad Usman and Capital Development Authority Emergency Services Director General Dr Abdul Rehman.
The prime minister also approved action against the security company deployed at the hospital and its officials.
He directed that those responsible be brought to justice, stressing that exemplary punishment would be ensured so that no mother would again lose her child due to anyone's criminal negligence.
"The death of innocent children is a tragic incident over which the entire nation is grieving," the prime minister said, adding that he and the entire nation stood with the bereaved parents.
The prime minister approved the conferment of the Sitara-e-Khidmat and a cash reward of Rs10 million for nurse Raziya Noreen, who risked her life to save a newborn during the fire at the hospital.
He paid tribute to Noreen for demonstrating an exceptional sense of responsibility by rushing through the fire and rescuing a baby moments before the nursery was engulfed by the blaze.
"Nurse Raziya Noreen has demonstrated an exceptional example of responsibility and bravery," the prime minister said.
He said the entire nation, including himself, was proud of Noreen for putting her own life at risk to save the life of the child. "People who demonstrate such dedication to their duty cannot be praised enough," Shehbaz said.
He also ordered that a nurse and a female guard present in the ward be made officers on special duty (OSD) and directed further investigation into their roles.
The prime minister directed Dr Mohammad Salman, CEO of the National Institutes of Health (NIH), to be appointed acting executive director of PIMS.
He further ordered the immediate and simultaneous appointment of new officials in place of those removed from their posts.
The prime minister also directed that the interim report of the inquiry committee be made public immediately. The report, according to the meeting, would be uploaded on the Ministry of National Health's website shortly.
 
Rs1m for the nurse
PM Shehbaz also approved the Sitara-i-Khidmat award and a Rs1 million cash reward for nurse Razia Noreen, who "saved a child without regard for her own life", the PMO said.
Report
The interim report presented to the prime minister said the precise source of ignition had not yet been "conclusively established".
It noted that questions requiring forensic, technical or documentary examination - including the exact ignition source, the contribution of specific deficiencies to the incident and the final determination of individual responsibility - had been left for the committee's comprehensive report.
"The committee considers it important that uncertainty regarding the first spark should not prevent examination of the protective systems that should have prevented an initial fire from becoming a mass fatality event. The cause of ignition and the causes of the consequences are related but analytically distinct."
The report also reconstructed the incident using CCTV footage, which it described as providing "the most objective reconstruction" of what happened.
According to the footage, the first visible sign of an emergency appeared at around 6:38:15am, when charge nurse Nasreen hurriedly emerged from the nursery and sought assistance. About 20 seconds later, she and security guard Maria entered the nursery, with reflections of flames visible.
Staff nurse Razia entered the nursery at around 6:38:56am and emerged eight seconds later carrying a baby, thereby rescuing the child. She then attempted to re-enter the nursery shortly afterwards.
Dr Abdul Rehman emerged at around 6:39:12am, while Camera 16 was largely obscured by smoke by about 6:39:15am. The adjoining corridor door visible on Camera 12 was opened at around 6:39:45am, and that camera was also obscured by smoke by about 6:40:08am.
The report said the footage established that conditions inside the nursery deteriorated "catastrophically" within approximately two minutes. The footage of the incident was also shown to the premier and other meeting attendees.
The interim report of the inquiry committee said various accounts had attributed the fire to an air conditioner, an incubator or warmer, or an electrical short circuit or overloaded plug.
According to the report, Iesco records showed no contemporaneous fault or tripping on the external feeder, shifting the focus of the electrical-causation inquiry to Pims's internal electrical distribution system, including sockets, plugs, wiring and connected equipment.
The report noted that preventive maintenance records showed several incubators had recently been serviced and returned to working condition. However, it said these records did not conclusively establish the electrical safety of the equipment, plug, socket or associated circuit.
"Accordingly, an internal electrical/equipment-related origin remains plausible, but it would be premature to identify any particular appliance or component as the established cause," the report said.
Charge nurse Nasreen and security guard Maria have been directed to remain off duty and not perform any duties until further orders. A decision on whether to proceed against them will be taken after the inquiry committee submits its final report, added the interim report.
The initial findings showed that Pims had no detailed standard operating procedures (SOPs) or training for dealing with fires or other emergency situations. Of the hospital's 13 SOPs, references to fire or emergency situations were found in only two subsections, the meeting was told.
The interim report of the inquiry committee said the record showed that rescue and evacuation efforts had been made, but did not establish that there was an approved, communicated, trained and rehearsed fire and evacuation SOP specifically for the neonatal nursery.
It noted that while Pims had SOPs covering various clinical and administrative functions, no comparably detailed procedure had been produced for fire detection, alarm activation, external notification, incident command, extinguisher use, oxygen or electrical isolation, unlocking emergency exits, evacuation priorities or the safe relocation of non-ambulatory newborns.
The report, however, pointed out that Pims' Security Department SOP, dated May 27, 2023, expressly recognised fire safety as an institutional responsibility. It required the security department to ensure fire safety for the protection of infrastructure, equipment, patients, visitors and staff, while assigning the assistant director security responsibility for ensuring the availability of fire exits, the functionality of firefighting equipment and the training of relevant personnel.
Pims had also nominated personnel for specialised fire-safety training before the incident, the report said, adding that the key question was therefore not whether fire risks had been recognised administratively, but whether the assigned responsibilities and available training had translated into actual preparedness at the neonatal nursery.
The report said the Capital Emergency Services (CES) had separately found fire and life-safety arrangements to be inadequate and compromised. It said emergency exits and escape routes were locked or obstructed, security personnel hindered aspects of the initial response and crowd management was inadequate. According to the CES account, firefighters had to forcibly open locked fire-exit doors and other access points.
The committee described these as serious prima facie deficiencies but said it was still verifying the status and location of each relevant door before assigning responsibility.
It also said the corridor door adjoining the nursery, visible on CCTV, required separate consideration. The door was initially closed but was opened at around 6:39:45am, after rescue activity had already begun through another access point.
The report cautioned that controlled access to a neonatal unit had a legitimate security purpose and that a locked or controlled door could not, by itself, be treated as evidence of negligence. The key questions, it said, were whether the door was a designated or required emergency exit, whether it could be opened immediately in an emergency and whether its condition had materially delayed evacuation or rescue.
The inquiry committee said certain safety measures could not be deferred until submission of its comprehensive report. It recommended that Pims immediately conduct a hospital-wide fire, life-safety and electrical audit through competent and preferably independent technical experts, beginning with the NICU/neonatal nursery, intensive care units, operating theatres and other high-risk areas.
According to the report, smoke and heat detection systems, alarms, fire extinguishers, hydrants, emergency lighting, electrical protection systems and all designated fire exits should be physically inspected, tested and documented. Any mandatory emergency exit found locked, obstructed or incapable of being opened immediately in an emergency should be rectified without delay. At the same time, legitimate controlled access to sensitive neonatal areas should be maintained through fire-safe arrangements.
The committee further recommended an urgent technical inspection of all incubators, warmers, air-conditioning and IVAC installations, sockets, plugs, distribution boards, circuit breakers, earthing and other safety-critical electrical systems in high-risk clinical areas.
It said Pims should introduce temporary fire-watch arrangements wherever automatic detection or protection systems were deficient and conduct practical fire and neonatal evacuation drills involving doctors, nurses, security and engineering staff.
The report also called for an immediate, clear and tested emergency notification and incident-command protocol. Under the proposed system, detection of a fire should trigger a simultaneous internal alarm, mobilisation of designated responders and direct notification of CES/Rescue 1122, without relying on informal communication through multiple administrative layers. The officer responsible for each step should be identified by designation and the process tested periodically, it said.

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
Balochistan Home Minister Mir Ziaullah Langove said on Saturday that security forces apprehended two young girls who were being prepared as suicide bombers by the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA), designated as Fitna al-Hindustan, during an intelligence-based operation in southern Balochistan.
Speaking to media at a news conference in Quetta, Langove said the operation resulted in the safe custody of 16-year-old Zainab and her 12-year-old cousin, Fatima. He appeared alongside the two girls during the presser.
The home minister stated that the primary purpose of the briefing was to expose the "illegal and destructive tactics" employed by the BLA.
He noted that the law enforcement agencies were continuing efforts against such activities, adding that while the public often questioned security measures when an attack occurred, authorities quietly prevented dozens of similar plots.
The federal government last year officially designated all terrorist groups operating in Balochistan as 'Fitna al-Hindustan', accusing India of sponsoring a proxy war through these outfits.
According to the details shared during the presser, Zainab said her husband, Saif, was targeted and killed by a local BLA commander after refusing to work for the group. She said the same terrorist network was responsible for the deaths of eight to 10 other members of her family.
Following Saif's killing, the commander repeatedly contacted Zainab and falsely blamed state institutions for her husband's death, seeking to emotionally manipulate her into seeking revenge.
Fatima, whose father was also killed in a BLA attack, was drawn into the network due to her close proximity to Zainab.
The two girls travelled to a covert location where they were held for 40 days. During their captivity, they were subjected to physical violence by terrorists, while the local commander made inappropriate advances towards Zainab.
Whenever the girls asked to meet the commander directly, they were told he was travelling in a neighbouring country and would meet them upon his return.
The plot came to an end when security forces acted on intelligence while the girls were being transferred between hidden locations
Given their age and the circumstances of their entrapment, the state chose not to pursue strict legal action. Instead, authorities facilitated their reunion with their families and offered them an opportunity to return to normal life and raise awareness in their communities about the reality of these terrorist networks.
Officials said the BLA operated as a proxy for foreign interests, particularly supported through New Delhi, while its leadership hid in safe havens across Kabul, Kandahar and Europe and exploited vulnerable local families.
They said the recruitment of young children as suicide bombers directly violated Islamic principles and traditional Baloch cultural values, which historically prioritised the protection of women and minors.
Both Zainab and Fatima expressed gratitude to the security forces for saving their lives and appealed for a general pardon from the government and the nation.

items.author: Nasir Butt
items.content:
The Gul Plaza tragedy was not simply a story of a devastating fire but of known dangers left unaddressed, delayed emergency response and rescue opportunities that slipped away, a 78-page judicial commission report has found, exposing a systemic failure involving government agencies and the building management that turned a fire into a mass-casualty disaster.
On January 17, 2026, a fire at the Gul Plaza shopping mall in Karachi killed 80 people and injured over 20. The Sindh government formed a single-member judicial commission, led by Sindh High Court's Justice Agha Faisal, on February 4 to probe the cause of the tragedy.
The commission prepared a report on the conflagration, which the Sindh Home Department has released. According to the report Gul Plaza had continued to operate as a commercial building despite being hazardous and in violation of fire-safety requirements. It concludes that responsibility cannot be pinned on a single institution or government, but lies in the collective failure of systems meant to identify risks, enforce safety rules, fight fires and rescue people in emergencies.
The commission found that the dangers at the plaza were known well before the tragedy. Civil Defence inspections in 2024 and 2025 had identified the absence of fire-safety equipment, the presence of inflammable commercial material and deficiencies in exit routes. Yet the identified shortcomings were not rectified and no effective legal action followed.
The report described the failure of Civil Defence as not a failure to know about the danger, but a failure to enforce action against a known danger.
The building's management was also held responsible for failing to rectify known defects. Its regularised plan provided for 1,102 shops, while 1,153 shops were actually operating in the building, with large quantities of inflammable commercial goods stored inside.
The commission also questioned the role of the district administration, finding that Gul Plaza was not subjected to a joint audit despite a three-tier fire-audit mechanism established on the directions of the Sindh High Court. The office of the Deputy Commissioner South was held institutionally responsible for failing to activate the available system of audit and oversight.
The Sindh Building Control Authority, too, could not escape responsibility by relying on the position that inspections were conducted only on complaints, the commission said. The Sindh Building Control Ordinance gave the authority powers to take corrective action against dangerous buildings, while Gul Plaza's incomplete records and ineffective fire-safety oversight also reflected institutional failure.
The report found failures at the scene of the fire as well.
There was an "extremely unwise" delay in informing the fire brigade, while the fire brigade itself arrived later than its prescribed response standard. Effective firefighting began only after approximately 35 to 40 minutes.
Water shortages and repeated refilling further hampered firefighting and rescue operations. The commission questioned how effective water supplies were not available during the crucial initial phase despite claims that fire stations had water reserves.
It also found that the delayed deployment of critical firefighting equipment reduced the chances of rescuing people who remained accessible inside the building.
The decision to disconnect electricity created another deadly obstacle: darkness inside the building further reduced the chances of people escaping from the upper floors. Although a speaker system was installed in the building, it was not used to issue evacuation instructions or guide those trapped inside.
The commission also highlighted a missed rescue opportunity involving Rescue 1122. Rescuers reached the scene while a meaningful window for intervention still remained. Rescue was possible between around 11:15pm and 11:20pm, when some victims were still visible, while access through the ramp remained possible until approximately 11:30pm. The commission found that Rescue 1122 failed to turn this remaining opportunity into a large-scale rescue operation.
The report further raised questions over electrical safety, noting that the law required regular inspections of electrical installations and equipment. However, according to the Electric Inspector's statement, no regular electrical inspection had been conducted.
Overall, the commission rejected the idea that the tragedy could be attributed to one department, one institution or one government. It found that the legal powers, audit mechanisms, building-control authorities, firefighting services and emergency-response institutions existed across different periods. But the system as a whole failed to function effectively. The victims did not die from fire alone. Delays, darkness, blocked exits, obstructive windows, inactive safety systems, ineffective oversight and rescue opportunities that were not used in time all contributed to the loss of life.
In a sombre preface to the report, Justice Faisal quoted poet Mustafa Zaidi: "Whose hands should I search for my blood? The whole city is wearing gloves."

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
Despite a string of cuts since the government introduced daily pricing, petrol has ended up Rs25.87 per litre costlier, while diesel has also recorded a net increase of Rs17.09, an analysis of price changes shows.
By August 29, the price of petrol had risen by a net Rs25.87 per litre, while diesel had become Rs17.09 per litre more expensive, according to an analysis of price changes made under the daily pricing mechanism.
The daily mechanism for determining petroleum product prices was introduced on July 21. Since then, prices of petrol and diesel have been increased and reduced several times, but both products have recorded an overall increase.
According to the data, petrol prices were increased 15 times and reduced 12 times between the introduction of the mechanism and August 29.
During this period, the cumulative increase in petrol prices amounted to Rs44.67 per litre, while the total reduction stood at Rs18.80 per litre. Consequently, petrol recorded a net increase of Rs25.87 per litre under the daily pricing mechanism.
Similarly, diesel prices were increased 18 times and reduced nine times during the same period.
The cumulative increase in diesel prices amounted to Rs62.26 per litre, while the total reduction stood at Rs45.17 per litre, resulting in a net increase of Rs17.09 per litre.
The data shows that despite multiple reductions in petrol and diesel prices at different points since the introduction of the daily pricing mechanism, both products have ultimately become more expensive.
It is pertinent to note that the introduction of frequent fuel-price revisions has also raised concerns about the uncertainty it creates for consumers and businesses.
While the mechanism allows prices to respond more quickly to changes in international oil prices and other costs, repeated increases can make it difficult for transport operators, traders and households to plan their monthly expenses.
Critics of higher petroleum prices argue that their impact extends well beyond motorists. Fuel is a major input for road transport and logistics, meaning an increase in petrol and diesel prices can raise the cost of transporting agricultural produce, food items and other essential goods. Higher transport costs can subsequently feed into prices across the wider economy.
The burden is particularly significant for households dependent on public transport and for workers whose incomes are closely tied to daily travel. Any increase in fares or freight charges can therefore translate into higher household expenditure even for people who do not own vehicles.
The issue is also likely to remain a source of pressure on the government, particularly if successive increases outweigh the reductions announced under the new mechanism.
Transporters, traders and other affected groups have responded to sharp fuel-price increases with demands for fare adjustments and calls for protests and strikes.

items.author: Press Release
items.content:
Nishat Group’s NexGen Auto has officially launched the OMODA 7 SHS-P in Pakistan at an Ex-Factory Price of PKR 10,649,000, ending months of speculation and teasers since the plug-in hybrid SUV first appeared at the PakWheels Auto Show in Karachi. The launch marks the moment the brand’s flagship SUV moves from anticipation to a vehicle Pakistani buyers can now book and own.
The OMODA 7 arrives as a plug-in hybrid, pairing a 1.5-litre turbocharged engine with an electric motor for a combined output of 341 hp and 525 Nm of torque. An 18.4 kWh battery pack delivers 90+ km of pure electric range for daily commuting, while the combined petrol-electric range stretches up to 1,250 km, positioning it as a genuine do-it-all SUV for buyers who want electrified efficiency without range anxiety on longer trips.
The launch line-up leans heavily on comfort and detail: Stargazing Zero Gravity Seats, a 12-speaker SONY sound system, illuminated front bumper lights, a Star Rail Glide Screen, an 8-point massage seat, luxury fragrance dispensers, and 20-inch alloy wheels with a T-type spare, making it one of the most comprehensive and detail-oriented SUVs available in the Pakistani market today. In 2026 alone, Omoda in the UK has crossed 15,000 registrations, making it one of the fastest growing brands in the United Kingdom.
At PKR 10,649,000, the OMODA 7 positions itself as a premium option in the C-SUV segment, with a price-lock offer. The vehicle can be booked online or through any of the 20 OMODA & JAECOO dealerships now operating across Pakistan.
Backed by Nishat Group
The OMODA 7’s launch builds on a foundation Nishat Group has laid since August 1, 2025, when its subsidiary NexGen Auto introduced the OMODA and JAECOO brands to Pakistan at a landmark event at Expo Centre Lahore, led by Group founder Mian Mohammad Mansha. That launch unveiled five models at once: the Omoda E5, Jaecoo J6, Jaecoo J7, Omoda 7, and Jaecoo J5. Exactly one year later, all five are now available in the market.
Pakistan delivered OMODA & JAECOO’s highest first-month sales of any market globally, and the brand has since gone on to cross 10,000 vehicle deliveries in the country within its first year. Globally, OMODA & JAECOO have expanded into 64 markets, with Pakistan standing out as one of the fastest-growing markets in that story.
What’s Next: OMODA 4 Coming to Pakistan Soon
With the OMODA 7 launched, attention turns to the next addition to the line-up: OMODA 4, set to launch in Pakistan soon following its regional debut in Indonesia. Where the OMODA 7 leads on comfort and detail, OMODA 4 leads on intelligence, combining futuristic Cyber Mecha design with a Super AI Cockpit built around ten coordinated AI Agents and support for five languages, positioning it as a potential “Young People’s First AI Dream Car.”
The AI Cockpit lets users issue combined natural-voice commands instead of separate instructions, adjusting air-conditioning, closing windows, activating seat ventilation, changing ambient lighting, and playing music all in one request, alongside intelligent navigation for multi-stop journeys.
Exterior-wise, OMODA 4 carries the brand’s Cyber Mecha design language, with Cyber Lightning headlights, a sculpted body, and an F1-inspired flip-up ignition button, while the cabin follows a “Cyber Verse” concept built around music, gaming, entertainment, social interaction, pet travel, and outdoor activities, aiming to turn the cockpit into a “third living space” for younger consumers.
Globally, the OMODA 4 is offered in BEV, HEV, and ICE powertrains. We will find out whether Pakistan gets all three or a combination in the coming months.
A First Year to Remember
Between the OMODA 7’s launch and the OMODA 4’s arrival on the horizon, NexGen Auto is closing out its first year in Pakistan with its full five-model line-up on the road, over 10,000 deliveries behind it, and a technologically ambitious new model already generating buzz ahead of its local debut. For Pakistani buyers, the message is consistent across both launches: OMODA & JAECOO isn’t just adding SUVs to the market, it’s building a line-up designed around comfort, capability, and intelligent technology.

Under the POS
items.author: Shahbaz Rana
items.content:
After a lull, the government's drive to integrate large retailers with the tax system picked up momentum in the last fiscal year and the figure jumped to over 17,300 businesses – an increase of nearly one-third, amid concerns to retain the growing base due to the introduction of a new small trader scheme.
According to figures compiled by the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR), about 17,337 large retailers integrated with the Point of Sale (POS) network in the fiscal year 2025-26. There was an increase of 4,124 businesses or 31% in the base within one year.
The scheme had been launched in December 2019 but it largely remained dormant due to multiple issues impacting its integration with the tax system. The FBR also earns Rs1 on every shopping receipt generated through the POS and the money is used for the welfare of the tax officials.
In the last fiscal year, the FBR earned Rs871 million, which was about 17% higher than the preceding year, according to official details.
Under the POS system, a bill is generated electronically and a copy reaches FBR at that moment. The shop cannot later report a smaller figure, because the record already exists.
However, the introduction of the new small trader scheme could dent the drive to digitise the sale record of the retailers, as at least two conditions that make it binding for the retailers to register under the POS have been compromised.
The traders using the debt and credit card machines and having annual sales of over Rs80 million are required to be integrated with the FBR system. Now, the government has offered the retailers to avail the new scheme if their annual sales are up to Rs200 million. The small trader having up to Rs200 million annual sales would also be exempted from installing digital payment processing machines.
The government would charge only 1% tax from small traders on their annual sales compared to almost 35% being charged from the salaried class.
Due to one-third increase in the number of integrated retailers, the tax authorities said that the revenues collected from them also surged by 16% to Rs132 billion in the last fiscal year.
Tier-1 retailers are required to integrate all their branches, point of sale terminals with the FBR's computerised system aimed at digitising their economic transactions to collect due sales tax and income tax from them.
Over the past seven years, the FBR made multiple changes in the rules governing the POS framework in the hope to further broaden the base.
The establishment of a new threshold of withholding tax payments under section 236G and 236H also helped expand the network, said the officials. Retailers whose deductible withholding tax exceeds Rs100,000 or in certain cases Rs500,000 are required to integrate their businesses.
The FBR's focus largely remains on restaurants, textile, garments shops but the network of service providers remains large and majority of it is still outside the net. The tax authorities said that the professional services like doctors are not willing to disclose their real transactions and were resisting the integration of clinics and hospitals.
The FBR officials said that in late July, the Pakistan Medical Association refused to accept the same electronic billing requirement for private clinics, calling it bureaucratic overreach and warning that doctors may shut down health facilities across the country rather than comply. Its argument is that healthcare is a professional service, not a shop, and that treating a clinic like a retail outlet is legally wrong.
The FBR officials said that the rule was a common standard for everyone and was not aimed at any one profession. The shopkeepers and restaurateurs, who had the least organised lobby and the strongest practical case for objecting, have been inside the system for years, and their tax payments rose 78% once they joined it. The professions are still arguing about whether it was meant for them, they added.
According to the rules business such as restaurants, hotels, motels, guest houses, marriage halls, marquees, clubs, inter-city travel by road, courier services, cargo service, beauty parlours, clinics and slimming clinics, massage centres, pedicure centres, all medical service providers including dentists, hair implant surgeons, and pathological laboratories, medical diagnostic laboratories are required to integrate.
Nearly 13,000 shops and restaurants have been connected to the FBR's electronic billing system since 2019. Comparing what each of them paid in the three months before it was connected with the three months after, sales tax payments rose from Rs5.8 billion to Rs10.4 billion, said the official while underscoring the benefits of integration.
The 78% increase in tax payments was without raising rates and without raiding their shops, said the tax authorities.
The sharpest change came from restaurants. Across 698 of them, sales tax payments rose from Rs183.8 million in the quarters before joining to Rs729.4 million in the quarters after, an increase of almost 300%, they added.
One of the reasons for this increase was that people preferred paying through credit cards due to the 5% sales tax rate compared to the 18% rate for cash-payments.
Each of these restaurants was paying an average of about Rs263,000 in sales tax over three months before it joined. Afterwards the average was over Rs1 million. These are not small roadside establishments. They are large enough that the law already required them to be in the system, the tax authorities added.
As of July 2026, a total of 46,813 branches of these 17,300 businesses were on the digital invoicing system.
Behind these numbers sits a wider shift. FBR is moving the country to a system where sales are reported as they happen rather than reconciled months later, and where income tax and sales tax draw on the same live record. It is among the most ambitious documentation exercises attempted in Pakistan, and seven years of accumulated evidence now suggest it is working.
Tax authorities in other documented economies have reported gains from similar reforms, though measured differently. What distinguishes the Pakistani result is its consistency: whichever year a business joined, and whatever it sold, its declared tax went up once the record started existing with the FBR.

Singapore state investor Temasek, the majority shareholder of Singapore Airlines (SIA), on Saturday backed the airline's investment in Air India, as scrutiny grows over its stake in the loss-making Indian carrier.
Air India's request for about $1.5 billion in fresh equity from owners Tata Sons and Singapore Airlines was first reported by Reuters this week. Singapore Airlines owns 25.1% of India's second-largest airline, with the rest owned by Tata. News of the funding request prompted Kenneth Tiong, a lawmaker from Singapore's opposition Workers' Party, to urge that Temasek's funds not to be used to shore up the Indian carrier.
Singapore's Business Times also ran a commentary arguing that Singapore Airlines could not realistically exit its Air India stake, with Tata the only plausible buyer. It questioned what its 25.1% holding offered beyond a board seat and a share of the losses, while saying the strategic logic of the investment still held. In a letter to the newspaper responding to that commentary, Juliet Teo, joint head of portfolio development at Temasek Singapore, said Temasek viewed Singapore Airlines' decision to invest in Air India from a long-term perspective and was supportive of it.
The letter said the transformation of Air India involved complex, multi-year operational and integration challenges, with outcomes shaped by industry developments and external factors such as airspace disruptions, geopolitical developments and fuel price volatility.
"Efforts of this scale take time and are not expected to be linear," it said.
Temasek did not address whether it would support any capital contribution by Singapore Airlines to Air India. Air India's multibillion-dollar revamp has been under way since Tata took control of the former state-owned carrier in 2022.
Air India has been hit by Pakistan's airspace ban on Indian carriers, disruptions from the US-Israeli war with Iran, and the fallout from a crash last year that killed 260 people. In the year to March, the airline and its budget unit Air India Express posted combined losses of $2.33 billion, weighing on Singapore Airlines' profits.
Singapore Airlines said on Thursday its board would carefully consider any requests for additional capital from Air India, taking into consideration the group's other capital requirements and Air India's business strategy.
Singapore MP opposes Temasek funding for Air India
A Singapore opposition lawmaker has urged that state investor Temasek's money not be used to shore up Air India, after Reuters reported the Indian carrier had asked owners Tata Sons and Singapore Airlines, of which Temasek is the majority owner, for about $1.5 billion.
Kenneth Tiong, a member of parliament for the opposition Workers' Party, said in a social media post on Wednesday that because Singapore Airlines owns about 25% of Air India and Temasek in turn owns most of the Singapore carrier, the request was "not only a question for private shareholders."
"I will not support, nor expect, any future use of Temasek's funds to prop up Air India via Singapore Airlines. If Singapore Airlines wants to continue its bet on Air India, it should do so on its own two feet, and not on Temasek's," he said.
"Whichever of the two writes the cheque, it will have a significant impact on Temasek," he added, without elaborating.
Singapore's Ministry of Transport, Temasek, Air India, Tata Sons and Tiong did not respond to emails seeking comment.
A Singapore Airlines spokesperson said its board would carefully consider any requests for additional capital from Air India, weighing the group's other capital requirements and the Indian airline's business strategy.
Tiong said he had also filed a question for oral answer in parliament on September 8, asking the transport minister whether losses from and the carrying amount in Singapore Airlines' foreign associates have been assessed against its capacity to provide essential transport services.

items.content:
Minister of State for Finance and Railways Bilal Azhar Kayani on Saturday visited the Karachi Chamber of Commerce and Industry (KCCI) for an extensive meeting with representatives of the trading and industrial community.
The meeting was attended by representatives of trade and shopkeeper associations from across Karachi, Hyderabad and Sukkur and focused on a comprehensive briefing regarding the newly operationalised "Asaan Tax Scheme" and its mobile application. Kayani highlighted that the scheme was introduced on the direct demand of traders and shopkeepers to simplify tax processes while expanding the national tax net, said a press release.
To ensure seamless execution, focal persons from the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) and trade representatives had been designated across various regions of the country. The initiative introduces a simplified, user-friendly registration process featuring an Urdu-language form that shopkeepers can easily submit online.
Under the scheme, shopkeepers will pay a streamlined 1% tax on their declared annual sales turnover, with taxes deducted through utility bills and being fully adjustable.
Enrolled retailers will receive a green registration plate from the FBR and displaying the green plate will ensure that FBR personnel do not visit the shop for routine questioning. Furthermore, participating shopkeepers will generally be exempt from audits, will not be required to install Point of Sale (POS) machines and will not need to act as withholding agents. To further support the business community, Kayani announced that, under the directives of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, senior FBR officials would spend one week every month in Karachi to resolve commercial grievances on the spot and provide immediate facilitation for businesses.
This initiative was launched in August and will continue on a systematic basis to ensure immediate relief for traders. Representatives of trade organisations and the KCCI commended the state minister for his continuous engagement and appreciated PM Sharif for efforts to address the challenges facing the business sector.

items.title: Karachi’s New Rs. 750 Million Flyover Opens to Traffic
items.summary:
Karachi Mayor Murtaza Wahab has inaugurated a new flyover at Korangi No. 5, a project built at a cost of nearly Rs. 750 million to improve traffic movement and connectivity in the area.

Wahab described the project as part of the ongoing development work being carried out in Karachi under the #KarachiWorks initiative. The inauguration marks the completion and opening of another road infrastructure project aimed at improving transportation links within the city.

items.author: Arsalan Khattak
items.content:
The Punjab Food Authority (PFA) has destroyed 1,000 kilograms of rotten and foul smelling meat during an operation against an illegal slaughterhouse in Al Madina Colony, Shahdara, on the directions of Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif.
PFA Director General Raja Mansoor Ahmed said the slaughterhouse had already been sealed, but the owner allegedly continued preparing meat there without permission.
Officials found the meat heavily infested with flies and stored in extremely unhygienic conditions. A veterinary specialist inspected the meat at the site and declared it unfit and hazardous for human consumption, after which authorities destroyed it.
The slaughterhouse also lacked mandatory records, meat tagging, a valid license and other required documents. Inspectors found open drains, broken flooring, stagnant dirty water and a foul smell in the slaughtering area.
According to the PFA, the owner allegedly tried to obstruct officials during the operation, damaging an official vehicle. Authorities stopped his attempt to flee, arrested him and registered a case against him.
Raja Mansoor Ahmed said the PFA would continue taking action against businesses that violate food safety regulations under its zero tolerance policy. He urged citizens to report food related complaints through the PFA helpline 1223.

items.title: Leaked DLSS 5 Build Is Turning Game Characters Into Nightmares
items.summary:
An unfinished version of Nvidia DLSS 5 has leaked online, allowing modders to run the neural rendering technology in several games and revealing some unusual results.
The leaked build was reportedly found inside the early access version of NBA 2K27. Modders identified a file called nvngx_dlssnr.dll as version 310.8.0.0 of Nvidia DLSSNR, which contains an unreleased DLSS 5 Neural Rendering runtime.
The RenoDX modding community quickly began experimenting with the technology and managed to get DLSS 5 running in Control.
Since then, modders have also enabled it in The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim, Final Fantasy VII Rebirth, and Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas.

items.author: Afaq Wajdan Malik
items.content:
An unfinished version of Nvidia DLSS 5 has leaked online, allowing modders to run the neural rendering technology in several games and revealing some unusual results.
The leaked build was reportedly found inside the early access version of NBA 2K27. Modders identified a file called nvngx_dlssnr.dll as version 310.8.0.0 of Nvidia DLSSNR, which contains an unreleased DLSS 5 Neural Rendering runtime.
The RenoDX modding community quickly began experimenting with the technology and managed to get DLSS 5 running in Control.
Since then, modders have also enabled it in The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim, Final Fantasy VII Rebirth, and Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas.
Modders unlock experimental NVIDIA DLSS 5 hours after DLL discovery (image comparisons in Control)www.resetera.com/threads/16…
— NESbot (@nesbot.bsky.social) 2026-08-27T18:10:11.918Z
DLSS 5 Can Change More Than Image Quality
Nvidia introduced DLSS 5 earlier this year as a major expansion of its AI-based rendering technology.
Unlike traditional upscaling, the system can use generative AI to alter how parts of a game scene actually look.
That approach immediately caused controversy. Some players described the effect as a “yassification filter,” while others criticized it as AI-generated visual content.
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang later rejected those criticisms, saying gamers were “completely wrong” about the technology.
The leaked build now gives modders an early opportunity to see how the system behaves in existing games. Results vary significantly.
In Control, environmental improvements can look relatively convincing, particularly when DLSS 5 adds additional detail to scenes.
Character rendering is much less consistent.
In Final Fantasy VII Rebirth, Cloud can look noticeably different from his original design, while CJ in GTA: San Andreas takes on a particularly unusual appearance.
DLSS 5 can also change the overall visual style of games. Tests in Skyrim, for example, show the technology significantly altering the game’s original atmosphere.
&&&&&&&
Performance Takes a Major Hit
The unfinished DLSS 5 build is also extremely demanding.
One modder in the RenoDX Discord community reported an almost 50% performance loss while using the leaked version.
That could change considerably before release, as the current runtime was never intended for public use.
The examples also involve games that were not designed around DLSS 5, which means titles developed specifically for the technology may produce much better results.
For now, the leak offers only an early look at Nvidia’s next generation of neural rendering.
Whether the final version retains these dramatic visual changes remains unclear, but the leaked build shows that DLSS 5 could have a much larger effect on game graphics than previous versions of DLSS.

Selected candidates will receive a monthly salary of Rs. 60,000, along with allowances according to PEF’s HR policy.
District-Wise Vacancies
PEF has announced a total of 26 vacancies across different districts and tehsils of Punjab.
The positions are available in Bahawalnagar, Bhakkar, Dera Ghazi Khan, Faisalabad, Jhelum, Kasur, Khanewal, Layyah, Lodhran, Mandi Bahauddin, Multan, Murree, Muzaffargarh, Okara, Rahim Yar Khan, Rajanpur, Rawalpindi, Sahiwal, Sargodha, Sialkot, Taunsa and Vehari.

Interested candidates can apply through Central Testing Services Pakistan (CTS) by following the application procedure mentioned in the advertisement.
The deadline for submitting the online application through CTS is September 7, 2026, at 5:00 PM.
Applicants must also submit the required documents, including their CV, deposit slip, NOC where applicable, domicile, two photographs, CNIC, academic documents and experience proof.

items.author: Afaq Wajdan Malik
items.content:
OpenAI plans to end its partnership with Cursor following the coding startup’s $60 billion acquisition by SpaceX, giving developers a little over two months to prepare for the change.
Under OpenAI’s proposal, Cursor’s direct access to its models will end on November 12, 2026.
The decision comes just two weeks after SpaceX completed its acquisition of Cursor on August 14. The all-stock transaction valued the coding startup at $60 billion.
SpaceX had held an option to acquire Cursor since April, when the companies began working together to train an AI model. SpaceX exercised that option two months later.
Before the acquisition, Cursor relied heavily on models from OpenAI alongside Anthropic’s Claude and Google’s Gemini.
OpenAI Says Trust is the Main Issue
OpenAI said its decision is based on concerns about whether SpaceX will use its technology in accordance with its terms of service.
The company pointed to previous contract violations involving Elon Musk’s companies but did not specify exactly how it believes SpaceX could misuse OpenAI models through Cursor.
The ownership change is central to the decision. OpenAI did not present the move as a problem with Cursor itself but as a consequence of SpaceX taking control of the company.
OpenAI also acknowledged that developers who use its models through Cursor will be the most affected and said it is prepared to support them during the transition.
The decision also highlights growing competition around AI models. SpaceX and xAI are both controlled by Musk, while OpenAI increasingly competes directly with xAI in the broader AI market.
Cursor’s Multi-Model Strategy Faces a Test
Cursor has grown into one of the most widely used AI coding platforms.
The company reached a $29.3 billion valuation in late 2025 and was generating more than $1 billion in annualized revenue before SpaceX agreed to acquire it for $60 billion.
Fortune reported in March that Cursor was being used by 67% of Fortune 500 companies and generating around 150 million lines of enterprise code every day.
Cursor CEO Michael Truell has argued that the company’s strategy is to offer developers the best AI models available rather than depend on a single provider.
He previously compared coding tools made directly by AI model companies to “concept cars,” while describing Cursor as the equivalent of a manufactured car that combines technology from different providers.
OpenAI’s planned departure on November 12 will put that strategy to the test.
Cursor currently supports models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and other providers through a model selector inside its chat and agent interface. Losing direct access to OpenAI will therefore not make Cursor unusable, but it will remove one of its major model suppliers.
AI Companies Are Tightening Model Access
OpenAI’s decision also comes as AI companies place tighter restrictions on how third-party coding tools access their models.
Anthropic previously cracked down on unauthorized access to Claude through third-party coding tools, forcing services such as OpenCode toward approved API access rather than using consumer subscriptions indirectly.
OpenAI took a different approach and worked with OpenCode to allow users to access its models using ChatGPT or Codex subscriptions.
The different approaches highlight a broader shift across the industry as AI companies take greater control over how third-party products distribute and integrate their models.
For Cursor users, the immediate question is what happens after November 12.
OpenAI has not explained exactly what its promised support for affected developers will involve, including whether it could provide migration assistance, temporary exceptions or other transition options.
What developers now have is a proposed deadline: November 12, 2026.

How to Review a Wrong E-Challan Online
Motorists can follow the steps below to request a review of an incorrect e-challan.
Step 1: Visit the E-Challan Website
Open the official PSCA e-challan portal. The portal provides access to e-challan information and the review facility.
Step 2: Enter the Required Details
Enter the required information on the portal to search for your e-challan. Make sure the details are entered correctly so the relevant challan can be found.
Step 3: Find the Relevant E-Challan
After entering the required details, search for the e-challan that you believe has been issued incorrectly. Check the available challan information before proceeding with the review.
Step 4: Click the Review Button
Once you have found the relevant e-challan, click the “Review” button. This will allow you to proceed with the request to have the challan reviewed.
Step 5: Complete the Review Process
Follow the instructions displayed on the portal and complete the required steps for the review. Submit the request after providing the necessary information.
Step 6: Wait for the Review Outcome
After the applicant submits the request, the authorities will review the e-challan and inform the applicant about the outcome.
Helpline for Assistance
Motorists who need further assistance can contact Lahore Traffic Police at 0322-5638888.
Additionally, motorists can use the helpline to seek guidance if they face any difficulties. They can also contact Lahore Traffic Police for more information about the e-challan review process.

items.author: Reuters
items.content:
US President Donald Trump signed an order on Friday creating a US Space ​Academy, billing it as a new military and civilian institution modeled after West Point and other military service academies.
The proposed academy would build on ‌Trump's space agenda, which he and White House officials have described as a key component of his legacy. Trump launched the US Space Force as a sixth branch of the military during his first term, has attended multiple NASA launches and now aims to return Americans to the moon and eventually reach Mars.
An eight-member commission, led by NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman, will advise the president on launching ​the institution, which Trump's proclamation said would "develop a professional corps of civically grounded leaders prepared to advance American interests within the space domain."
Speaking at the Lyndon ​B. Johnson Space Center in Houston, Trump said he would choose the location for the academy "very shortly," and hinted that the Texas ⁠congressional delegation in attendance wanted the institution in the Lone Star State.
He has pledged that the US will land astronauts on the moon during his final year in office.
"A ​nation cannot be first on Earth if we're going to be second in space," Trump said during a ceremony to award the Congressional Space Medal of Honor to the ​four crew members of the Artemis II mission.
That crew -- Commander Reid Wiseman, Pilot Victor Glover, Mission Specialist Christina Koch and Canadian Space Agency Mission Specialist Jeremy Hansen -- spent more than nine days in space, circumnavigating the moon and traveling deeper into space than any human before.
Moon program
The multibillion-dollar US moon program is targeting its first astronaut landing in 2028, involving SpaceX's giant Starship rocket system. That rocket's ​development has been delayed, risking the timeline - but another moon lander from Jeff Bezos' Blue Origin that is also under development might make the 2028 deadline instead.
Read More: New NASA telescope to probe dark energy, dark matter and exoplanets
The Artemis ​program rivals the lunar ambitions of China, which is aiming for its own crewed moon landing around 2030 following a series of increasingly ambitious robotic missions.
Both countries are seeking to establish a ‌long-term crewed presence ⁠on the lunar south pole, where coveted water ice embedded in the lunar soil could be a key ingredient for fuel on the moon.
Trump added that the US would launch a separate nuclear-powered spacecraft to Mars in 2028 that would be the gateway to broader interplanetary travel.
Isaacman said the missions would "inspire the next generation to carry the fire of exploration even further."
Trump's order said implementing those goals requires new institutions to recruit and train future astronauts, engineers and scientists.
Staffing challenges
It is unclear how logistics for the space ​academy -- including building the campus, creating the ​programming and recruiting students -- would work. ⁠Funding would need to be approved by Congress, which is historically gridlocked.
Space Force officer candidates are generally commissioned through the Air Force Academy in Colorado Springs, Colorado. The Naval Academy in Annapolis, Maryland, also has a long tradition of its graduates becoming astronauts.
"You think ​of West Point, and you think of Annapolis, and you think of the Air Force Academy, and you think of ​the Coast Guard Academy. They're ⁠all good," Trump said. "But we're going to have now the Space Force Academy for what the people in this room love the most."
Many US space companies have struggled to attract new talent as the industry rapidly expands, with demand for spacecraft services and rocket launches soaring. Major players such as Elon Musk's SpaceX and Bezos' Blue Origin have ramped up competition ⁠in the sector, ​driving up the cost of new hires for some smaller companies, analysts say.
Staffing challenges have also snagged ​the U.S. Space Force, whose workforce is 25% lower than what Congress requires for the branch, according to a 2025 watchdog report, opens new tab.
Trump also spent part of his two-day trip in Texas raising money for Republican Senate ​nominee and Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton ahead of November's midterm elections.
