items.author: Zihan Fajrin
items.content:
Jakarta, Gizmologi – Google Cloud belum lama ini menghadirkan Gemini Enterprise untuk financial services dan legal. Solusi ini hadir sebagai rangkaian pertama dari solusi industri khusus yang dibangun di atas platform Gemini Enterprise.
“Para profesional di sektor keuangan membutuhkan platform AI yang tidak mengharuskan mereka bergantung pada satu model atau ekosistem tertentu, dapat terhubung dengan sistem IT yang mereka gunakan sehari-hari, serta memiliki tingkat keamanan dan kepatuhan yang tinggi,” ujar Thomas Kurian, CEO Google Cloud.
Platform Gemini ini berbeda dari Gemini biasanya namun tetap menggunakan teknologi dari Google AI. Gemini Enterprise dihadirkan untuk membantu para profesional di berbagai bidang dan berbagai workflow mereka. Lalu apa yang ditawarkan Gemini Enterprise untuk financial services dan legal?
Baca Juga: Google Assistant Bakal Disetop Bulan Depan, Siap Digantikan Oleh Gemini
Komponen Utama Gemini Enterprise untuk Financial Services
Gemini Enterprise untuk financial services menghadirkan agen financial research. Kegunaan agen ini ialah mengotomatiskan seluruh proses riset, sekaligus memberikan penjelasan yang transparan mengenai hasilnya. Dibangun dengan lebih dari 50 foundational skills, agen ini memberikan transparansi mengenai proses penalarannya (reasoning) melalui confidence scores, metodologi yang jelas, data snapshots untuk mempermudah audit, serta kutipan sumber yang presisi sehingga setiap hasil dapat diverifikasi.
Pengguna dapat mengakses agen secara langsung melalui aplikasi Gemini Enterprise atau mengintegrasikannya ke dalam workflow agent yang sudah ada melalui API Agent-to-Agent (A2A). Agen ini juga dapat terhubung langsung ke berbagai sumber data enterprise melalui integrasi Model Context Protocol (MCP), sehingga pengguna dapat membuat laporan dan dokumen yang disesuaikan dengan kebutuhan mereka.
Lalu, purpose-built skills menyediakan shortcuts untuk berbagai tugas repetitif, mulai dari menerapkan panduan brand dan memformat laporan hingga mengakses data tertentu. Mulai dari spesialis private equity dan wealth manager hingga tim kepatuhan, solusi ini dapat disesuaikan dengan berbagai workflow, seperti penilaian risiko kredit, pemantauan portofolio, merangkum berita pasar, dan riset keuangan investigatif. Skills ini akan tersedia di agen Financial Research dan juga dapat digunakan pada agen yang dibangun oleh pelanggan.
ilustrasi mencari kandidat pekerja (Foto: Freepik)
Di Gemini Enterprise untuk financial services dan legal juga dapat menggunakan connectors. Ini merupakan solusi yang menyediakan 13 integrasi yang aman dengan sumber data berlisensi seperti CoinDesk Data & Indices, Daloopa, Dun & Bradstreet, FactSet, Finnhub, Fiscal.ai, Guidepoint, LSEG, Moody’s, MSCI, PitchBook, S&P Global, dan SEC Edgar, yang dapat dikonfigurasi langsung di lingkungan pelanggan.
Gemini Enterprise for Financial Services juga menyediakan akses terintegrasi ke berbagai third-party agent dari ekosistem mitra Google Cloud, seperti D&B Business Verification Agent untuk mempercepat proses onboarding bisnis dan memperkuat kepatuhan Know Your Customer (KYC), FlowX Agents untuk memastikan kelengkapan loan pack, ekstraksi dan rekonsiliasi dokumen untuk pasar modal, Obin Financial Agent untuk membantu tim private markets dan commercial lending mempercepat analisis keuangan yang kompleks, S&P Global Data Retrieval Agent untuk analisis multi-step, pembuatan laporan, dan workflow riset, serta S&P Global Energy Horizons Agents yang membantu mengolah data energi dan keberlanjutan yang kompleks menjadi sebuah insight untuk mendukung kebutuhan sektor keuangan.
Google Cloud menjelaskan bahwa solusi untuk pekerja profesional ini telah digunakan oleh institusi keuangan global seperti CME Group dan Deutsche Bank, yang merupakan salah satu design partner utama untuk agen Financial Research. Peluncuran ini melanjutkan momentum penggunaan Gemini Enterprise yang terus berkembang di berbagai institusi keuangan terkemuka, seperti BNY, Citi Wealth, Lloyds Banking Group, Macquarie Bank, dan Signal Iduna.
Institusi-institusi tersebut menggunakan Gemini Enterprise untuk membekali tenaga kerja mereka dengan berbagai tools workflow berbasis agentic AI guna mendorong pertumbuhan dan efisiensi. Gemini Enterprise for Financial Services kini tersedia dalam tahap preview bagi pelanggan Google Cloud secara global.

items.title: How Much Storage Do You Need on a Smartphone?
items.summary: In recent years, storage space has become one of the most influential factors behind a a new smartphone purchase. While powerful performance allows you to install and play high-end games and great cameras help capture higher-resolution photos, all of these can eat through gigabytes surprisingly quickly. At the same time, 64GB phones have largely become outdated, and 128GB usually serves as a starting point on most affordable and mid-range smartphones. Some flagships also offer 256GB as the base storage, albeit a premium price.

Spek Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3i Bisa Ditingkatkan
Kehadiran NPU di Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3i ini memiliki kemampuan hingga 17 TOPS ini mampu
items.author: Zihan Fajrin
items.content:
Jakarta, Gizmologi – Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3i 14IWC11 hadir di Indonesia, yang dirancang untuk produktivitas harian pengguna di Indonesia. Perusahaan mengklaim, laptop terbarunya menjadi laptop pertama yang ditenagai oleh prosesor Intel Core Series 3.
“Melalui Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3i yang didukung prosesor AI serta opsi upgrade memori dan penyimpanan, pengguna dapat berinvestasi pada laptop yang siap mendukung produktivitas mereka lebih lama,” ujar Santi Nainggolan, Consumer Lead Lenovo Indonesia.
Intel Core Series 3 merupakan prosesor terbaru yang telah dilengkapi Neural Processing Unit (NPU) untuk mendukung komputasi AI, yang sebelumnya hanya ditemukan di lini prosesor kelas atas. Lenovo mengatakan, terobosan ini membawa standar baru dalam industri PC mainstream.
Baca Juga: Lenovo IdeaTab Plus Resmi Dijual di Indonesia, Harga Mulai Rp6,1 Jutaan
Spek Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3i Bisa Ditingkatkan
Kehadiran NPU di Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3i ini memiliki kemampuan hingga 17 TOPS ini mampu menangani berbagai beban kerja kecerdasan buatan secara mandiri. Dengan pemrosesan AI yang terisolasi di NPU, laptop sanggup menjalankan berbagai tugas secara simultan dengan efisiensi daya tinggi.
Penghematan daya dari arsitektur Intel Core Series 3 ini makin optimal berkat dukungan baterai berkapasitas besar 50Whr, yang memungkinkan waktu pakai lebih panjang untuk menemani aktivitas harian pengguna. Saat harus mengisi daya secara cepat, teknologi Rapid Charge Boost siap membantu. Cukup melakukan pengisian daya selama 15 menit, pengguna sudah memperoleh tambahan waktu pakai hingga 2 jam untuk mendukung mobilitas tinggi tanpa hambatan.
Di samping dukungan prosesor dengan NPU terintegrasi, Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3i hadir dengan pilihan kapasitas penyimpanan SSD yang lega hingga 256GB/512GB. Salah satu nilai unggul utama perangkat ini terletak pada fleksibilitas perangkat kerasnya.
Berbeda dengan tren laptop entry-level di kelasnya yang menggunakan memori soldered tanpa opsi ekspansi, Lenovo membekali IdeaPad Slim 3i dengan slot memori/RAM dedicated (Extension & Repairable). Pengguna dapat dengan mudah menambah atau meng-upgrade RAM perangkat ini hingga 32GB DDR5 sesuai dengan kebutuhan produktivitas yang terus meningkat di masa depan.
Konektivitasnya pun sangat fleksibel dan lengkap tanpa perlu repot membawa banyak dongle atau adapter tambahan. Perangkat ini dibekali full-function Type-C port (10Gbps) yang mendukung Power Delivery dan DisplayPort, 2 × USB-A (5Gbps) untuk transfer data dan periferal, HDMI untuk koneksi monitor eksternal atau proyektor, Headphone / Mic Combo jack, serta microSD Card Reader untuk mentransfer file media dengan praktis.
Laptop ini mengadopsi layar dengan aspek rasio 16:10 dengan desain bingkai 4-side narrow bezel yang menghasilkan 90%+ Active Area Ratio. Lenovo juga memprioritaskan keamanan para pengguna dengan menghadirkan privacy shutter fisik pada kamera IdeaPad Slim 3i.
Selain itu, perusahaan menyematkan fitur Crystal Clear Collaboration dan sektor audio didukung oleh Dolby Audio, serta user-facing speaker untuk keluaran suara yang lebih tajam dan kaya. Untuk input suara, hadir teknologi dual microphone array yang dipadukan dengan Smart Noise Cancellation. Fitur ini secara cerdas meredam bising di sekitar (ambient noise), sehingga suara pengguna tetap terdengar jernih dan fokus saat berbicara.
Konsumen yang membeli laptop baru Lenovo ini akan mendapatkan paket lengkap. Konsumen bisa mendapatkan tas ransel, lisensi resmi Office Home 2024 mencakup aplikasi Microsoft Word, Excel, dan PowerPoint, ditambah langganan gratis 1 tahun Microsoft 365 Basic (termasuk penyimpanan cloudOneDrive).
Terdapat juga 2 tahun Accidental Damage Protection (ADP) dan 2 tahun Premium Care. Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3i saat ini saat ini sudah tersedia di Indonesia dan dan bisa didapatkan di Lenovo Exclusive Store dan official store yang tersedia di ecommerce, seperti Tokopedia, Shopee dan Blibli.com dengan harga mulai dari Rp11,799,000.

Jakarta, Gizmologi – Indosat Ooredoo Hutchison (IOH) melalui IM3 meluncurkan AIrena Kreatif, sebuah wadah bagi anak muda hingga UMKM. IM3 bersama dengan Adobe Express berkolaborasi untuk menghadirkan program ini.
“Di Indosat kami percaya semua orang memiliki kreativitas dan dapat menghasilkan karya berkualitas tinggi tanpa harus menjadi seorang ahli. Hal ini yang melandasi dibalik hadirnya inisiatif AIrena Kreatif,” ujar Apoorva Mehrotra, Director and Chief Growth Officer Indosat Ooredoo Hutchison.
Program AIrena Kreatif ditujukan untuk siapa saja yang ingin belajar, bereksperimen, berkolaborasi, dan mengasah kreativitas mereka. Kolaborasi IM3 dan Adobe Express dimulai dengan kampanye “Lancar Sampai Pro”.

Bagaimana Program AIrena Kreatif Bersama Adobe Express?
Program AIrena Kreatif bersama dengan Adobe Express ini akan menghadirkan berbagai workshop dan sesi berbagi bersama kreator serta praktisi kreati
items.author: Zihan Fajrin
items.content:
Jakarta, Gizmologi – Indosat Ooredoo Hutchison (IOH) melalui IM3 meluncurkan AIrena Kreatif, sebuah wadah bagi anak muda hingga UMKM. IM3 bersama dengan Adobe Express berkolaborasi untuk menghadirkan program ini.
“Di Indosat kami percaya semua orang memiliki kreativitas dan dapat menghasilkan karya berkualitas tinggi tanpa harus menjadi seorang ahli. Hal ini yang melandasi dibalik hadirnya inisiatif AIrena Kreatif,” ujar Apoorva Mehrotra, Director and Chief Growth Officer Indosat Ooredoo Hutchison.
Program AIrena Kreatif ditujukan untuk siapa saja yang ingin belajar, bereksperimen, berkolaborasi, dan mengasah kreativitas mereka. Kolaborasi IM3 dan Adobe Express dimulai dengan kampanye “Lancar Sampai Pro”.
Baca Juga: Indosat Hadirkan Paket IMClass 30GB Hanya Rp1 untuk PJJ
Bagaimana Program AIrena Kreatif Bersama Adobe Express?
Program AIrena Kreatif bersama dengan Adobe Express ini akan menghadirkan berbagai workshop dan sesi berbagi bersama kreator serta praktisi kreatif. Kolaborasi ini turut memperkenalkan benefit yang diluncurkan beberapa waktu yang lalu yaitu Adobe Express Premium selama enam bulan senilai Rp493.000 secara gratis bagi pelanggan IM3, yang tersedia melalui Freedom Internet, Paket Istimewa, serta aktivasi kartu perdana IM3.
Layanan ini memberikan pelanggan IM3 akses ke jutaan aset premium, fitur AI Adobe Firefly, editing visual dan video langsung dari HP, serta hasil bebas watermark. Berbagai fitur seperti Generative AI, Resize, Clip Maker, Brand Kit, dan Enhance Speech juga memungkinkan pengguna mengembangkan ide ke berbagai format konten dengan lebih praktis.
Menandai peluncurannya, Airena Kreatif akan hadir melalui sebuah creative workshop pada Jumat, 28 Agustus 2026 di The Brickhall Fatmawati, yang mempertemukan anak muda, kreator, UMKM, komunitas, dan praktisi kreatif untuk belajar sekaligus mengeksplorasi proses kreatif secara langsung. Melalui rangkaian sesi yang dirancang dari proses membangun sebuah karya hingga mengembangkannya menjadi konten yang bernilai dari para praktisi di bidangnya.
Perjalanan kreatif dimulai melalui sesi Visual Design Principle bersama Visual Artist Muklay, yang akan membahas dasar komposisi, kombinasi warna, dan prinsip visual untuk menghasilkan karya yang lebih kuat. Selanjutnya, Brilian Fairiandi, AI Visual Director dan Kristo Imanuel, Content Creator & Film Maker sekaligus Brand Ambassador kampanye IM3 x Adobe Express, akan membagikan Content Creation Hacks dengan memanfaatkan fitur berbasis AI serta perspektif mengenai Create & Earn, termasuk bagaimana mengoptimalkan proses kreatif hingga membuka peluang monetisasi.
Sementara itu, Aulion, Content Creator dan Andre Edfan, Creative Director Yord Studio, akan mengajak peserta mengembangkan ide, storytelling, dan narasi yang lebih engaging. Sejalan dengan semangat di atas, diperkenalkan pula IM3 Friends, sebuah platform komunitas yang dinaungi IM3 sebagai growth partner bagi para kreator melalui tiga semangat utama: Connect, Create, dan Grow.
Di sini, IM3 membuka akses bagi kreator untuk memperluas koneksi, bertukar pengetahuan, dan mendapatkan insight dari sesama kreator maupun praktisi; mendorong kolaborasi dan eksplorasi ide untuk menghasilkan karya yang lebih bermakna; serta membuka akses terhadap pengetahuan, teknologi, dan berbagai kesempatan untuk mengembangkan kemampuan serta potensi kreator. Dukungan tersebut diperkuat dengan ekosistem teknologi IM3, mulai dari jaringan 5G sebagai enabler konektivitas yang lebih unggul hingga berbagai solusi berbasis AI melalui kolaborasi strategis dengan mitra teknologi global seperti Google dan Adobe.
Dukungan nyata terhadap komunitas kreatif juga telah dibawa lebih dekat oleh IM3 melalui kegiatanAdobe Express IRL (In Real Life), rangkaian pengalaman kreatif yang mengajak content creator dan komunitas untuk mengolah inspirasi dari dunia nyata menjadi karya digital menggunakan Adobe Express Premium. Berlangsung pada 15, 16, 22, dan 23 Agustus 2026, rangkaian ini menghadirkan sesi kreatif seperti Photo Walk & Visual Storytelling, Wedding Photography Talk, dan Zine Making Workshop bersama sejumlah praktisi, termasuk Bill Satya, Ridwan Didot, Mas Agung Wilis, dan Rukii Naraya, yang berbagi proses sekaligus mengajak peserta bereksplorasi secara langsung.

Key Startup Funding Highlights Of The Week
At the sectoral level, ecommerce led this week’s startup funding trends, with four startups raising $58.5 Mn. Third Wave Coffee’s $43 Mn funding round, led by WestBridge Capital, accounted for 73.5% of the sector’s total funding and 20% of the $210.3 Mn raised by startups overall this week.
Advanced hardware & technology was a distant second, with three deals bringing in $49.9 Mn, helped by Airbound’s $37 Mn raise.
AI and cleantech also recorded four deals each, while consumer services and fintech saw three and two deals, respectively.
Early-stage funding also saw healthy traction, with three seed and pre-seed startups raising a total of $3.45 Mn.
Capital 2B and Equanimity Investments emerged as the most active investors this week, backing two startups each.
Startup M&As This Week
Startup mergers and acquisitions (M&As) also picked up in the last week of August, with three deals announced during the week.
Infineon Technologies is acquiring Peak XV-backed C2i Semiconductors to expand its semiconductor engineering capabilities in India.
Healthtech startup Healthify has merged with US-based nutrition care company Berry Street to build an insurance-covered AI metabolic health platform for the US market.
Deepinder Goyal’s wearable startup Temple has acquired London-based longevity medicine practice Longevous to strengthen its clinical and scientific teams ahead of the launch of its first product.
Startup Fund Announcements Of The Week
Micromax Informatics has launched a ₹250 Cr family office to invest in deeptech startups across AI, semiconductors, defence tech, spacetech and robotics. It will dish out initial cheque size in the range of ₹10 Cr to ₹20 Cr.
The/Nudge Foundation’s impact investment platform TILT has launched a ₹250 Cr fund to back early stage startups building solutions for India’s “Next Billion”.
Deeptech fund Industrial47 has marked the first close of its ₹200 Cr debut fund at ₹85 Cr. The fund is targeting a ₹150 Cr corpus, plus a ₹50 Cr greenshoe option, to back early-stage startups in defence, space, energy and maritime intelligence.
Startup IPO Developments This Week
ESDS Software Solution’s IPO was 2.1X subscribed on the first day, led by NIIs (3.51X) and retail investors (2.69X). QIB demand remained muted at 0.01X.
Purple Style Labs, the parent of Pernia’s Pop Up Shop, has raised nearly ₹306 Cr from anchor investors ahead of the commencement of the bidding for its IPO on August 31.

items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Chief Minister Punjab Maryam Nawaz Sharif held high-level strategic discussions with senior Huawei executives during her visit to China, exploring a comprehensive roadmap to advance artificial intelligence, cloud technologies, digital infrastructure, talent development, and smart public services across Punjab. Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif was accompanied by Mr. Ali Dar, Advisor to the Chief Minister on Artificial Intelligence, along with several provincial ministers and senior officials from the Government of Punjab.
With a shared vision of making Punjab “the most AI-enabled province in South Asia,” both sides discussed expanding cooperation from individual technology projects toward a province-wide AI and digital transformation ecosystem that can support economic growth, innovation, employment, and improved public services.
The discussions focused on developing secure and sovereign AI infrastructure within Pakistan, strengthening computing and data-center capabilities, and gradually deploying AI across government, public services, and industry. Huawei presented a proposed four-layer AI ecosystem covering infrastructure, AI capacity building, open and commercial AI models, and practical applications tailored to Punjab’s governance and economic needs.
Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif welcomed Huawei’s continued engagement with Punjab and appreciated the company’s willingness to support the province in building a modern, technology-driven and AI-enabled governance ecosystem. She emphasized the government’s commitment to using emerging technologies to improve efficiency, transparency, decision-making, and the quality and accessibility of services provided to citizens.
The proposed collaboration would also encourage the development of localized AI capabilities by combining cloud infrastructure, computing resources, relevant data, and specialized AI models. The objective is to ensure that AI solutions are responsive to Punjab’s local requirements and can be progressively expanded across government departments and key economic sectors.
Talent development and inclusive access to technology will be key pillars of Punjab’s AI strategy. Both sides will work together to strengthen AI skills across government, industry, academia, and local communities through training and talent development initiatives.
The exchange marks an important step in strengthening China-Pakistan digital cooperation, with Punjab advancing its vision of becoming the “Most AI-Enabled Province in South Asia.” Huawei will continue to work with Punjab to drive AI innovation, digital transformation, and sustainable development across the province.
To translate the shared vision into practical results, the proposed roadmap includes strengthening AI and cloud infrastructure, launching high-impact pilot projects, and developing successful use cases for wider deployment. Both sides also discussed the importance of an efficient government-enterprise coordination mechanism to facilitate communication, clarify responsibilities, accelerate decision-making, and ensure effective implementation.
Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif appreciated Huawei’s commitment to supporting Punjab’s digital transformation and welcomed deeper cooperation in AI, cloud computing, smart governance, digital skills, and emerging technologies. She said strategic partnerships with leading global technology companies could play an important role in building a digitally empowered, AI-enabled, innovative, and citizen-focused Punjab.
From Huawei, the meeting was attended by Mr. Mr. Antonony Gu Global President of Huawei Cloud Stack, Mr. Todd Liu Chairman of Huawei Pakistan and Mr. Ahmed Bilal Masud, CEO of Huawei Pakistan Cloud and AI Business.
The discussions laid the foundation for deeper cooperation aimed at building a smarter, more innovative, and digitally empowered Punjab. Through investment in infrastructure, human capital, innovation, and practical AI applications, the province aims to advance steadily toward its vision of becoming the most AI-enabled province in South Asia.

items.title: How to Transfer Contacts From Android to iPhone: A Step-by-Step Guide
items.summary: Apple allows users to transfer their contacts from an Android phone to a new iPhone using simple steps. If you are migrating to a new iPhone from an Android handset, you can download the Move to iOS app from the Google Play Store on your Android phone to transfer the data. However, this will only work when you are setting up your new iPhone. If you have already set up your iPhone, you can choose to sync your Android phone's contacts with your Google account and log in with the same Google account on your iPhone.

Jadwal MPL ID S18 Hari Ini 22 Agustus 2026
Team Liquid ID (TLID) akan menjalani pertemuan pertama mereka melawan langganan juara MPL Indonesia, yakni Onic pada laga pembuka pada hari Sabtu, 29 Agustus 2026.
Diperkuat Aran, Kevinn, Drichel, Lyoni, dan Keven, TLID sejauh ini masih mencari gaya permainan terbaik mereka setelah kalah 0-2 dari Navi, namun sebaliknya menang 2-0 atas Evos.
Onic sendiri juga baru mencatat kekalahan pertama mereka di MPL ID S18 ini saat melawan BTR pekan lalu.
Laga menarik lain di hari yang sama adalah Alter Ego melawan Evos. Kedua tim sama-sama dikenal memiliki gaya bermain agresif, sehingga pertemuan mereka berpotensi berjalan ketat.
Hari kedua Week 3 ditutup dengan RRQ Hoshi menghadapi BTR. Tim yang diperkuat Joshua, Demonkite, Hajirin, Said, dan Arthur ini baru mengantongi sat kemenangan.
Sementara itu, BTR datang sebagai juara Games of the Future 2026 dan belum terkalahkan di musim ini, menjadikan duel kedua tim menjadi ujian berat bagi RRQ untuk mempertahankan momentum.

MLBB
Minggu, 30 Agustus, giliran Onic menghadapi Navi pukul 14.00 WIB — kesempatan bagi Onic untuk bangkit usai kekalahan dari BTR. Di jam berikutnya, RRQ Hoshi bertemu Geek Fam pukul 17.00 WIB, sebelum Week 3 ditutup oleh laga Team Liquid ID kontra Alter Ego pukul 20.00 WIB.

Format MPL ID Season 18
Regular Season MPL ID S18 memakai format double round robin dengan seluruh pertandingan dimainkan dalam format Bo3. Setiap kemenangan memberikan satu match point.
Enam tim teratas pada akhir Regular Season berhak melaju ke playoff.
Pada playoff, tim peringkat ketiga hingga keenam bermain lebih dulu di Round 1 dengan sistem single elimination. Dua tim teratas langsung mendapatkan tempat di Round 2, ketika kompetisi berlanjut dengan sistem double elimination.
Mayoritas pertandingan playoff menggunakan format Bo5, sedangkan Lower Bracket Final dan Grand Final dimainkan dalam format Bo7.

items.content:
….as DGN honours him, Andy Boyo, Multi choice at directors’ Week, awards show in Lagos
By Benjamin Njoku
Legendary filmmaker Tunde Kelani has urged young Nigerian directors to look inward for stories and embrace technology, saying Artificial Intelligence is a tool to enhance, not erase, African creativity.
Kelani made this assertion, while speaking at the maiden edition of Directors Guild of Nigeria, DGN Week and Awards 2026 in Lagos. The internationally acclaimed director, popularly known as TK, was honoured with a Special Recognition Award for his contributions to the Nigerian film industry.
“I want to advise our young filmmakers to look back to Africa for their authentic stories and never to be afraid to embrace new technology,” TK said. “AI is not going to take away your history, your artistry or your languages. It is a tool to enhance your work.”
The three-day event, held from August 19 to 21, 2026, at the Alliance Française/Mike Adenuga Centre, Ikoyi, brought together directors, producers, policymakers, investors, and other stakeholders to discuss the future of Nigeria’s screen industry.
Alongside Kelani, revered filmmaker and Nollywood patron, Mr. Andy Boyo received the Industry Service Award. Multichoice Nigeria was also honoured for its outstanding contribution to the country’s creative economy.
Kelani, whose career spans over four decades and is best known for screen adaptations of Nigerian novels and plays, described the award as deeply meaningful.
“As directors, we don’t only entertain. We are custodians of our history, our languages and traditions. This award would remain precious to me for the rest of my life. It came at a time when I’m still working, learning and making mistakes,” he said.
Andy Boyo, known for producing a one-cast movie that earned him recognition in the United States, urged other Nollywood guilds to emulate DGN by rewarding excellence. He revealed his next ambitious project would also be a none-cast film, which he hopes to commence shooting in 2029.
The maiden Directors’ Week featured masterclasses, a directors’ round-table, industry panels, and networking sessions. Discussions centered on career sustainability, financing, intellectual property, distribution, co-productions, streaming, advertising, sports, television, faith-based filmmaking, and artificial intelligence.
National President of DGN, Uche Agbo, said the programme was designed to place directors at the center of conversations shaping Nigeria’s cinematic identity. The event also witnessed the induction of new DGN Fellows including Charles Inojie, Andy Chukwu, Omoni Oboli, and Obi Emelonye, Sam Dede, Ifeanyi Ikpoenyi, John Njamah among others. Also, about 42 new members and associate members including Mike Ezuruonye, Daniel Etim-Effiong, Wale Ojo, Yomi Frederick, Stanley Obi and Juliet Ibrahim, were inducted into the Guild.
On the award nominees, Head of Jury, Dr. Shaibu Hussein, disclosed that the panel reviewed over 150 entries across various categories.
“The quality of entries was exceptionally strong. The process of arriving at winners was rigorous and demanding,” he said.
According to the organizers, the awards recognized outstanding directors and organizations whose work and commitment have helped shape Nigeria’s film industry, while also creating opportunities for emerging directors to learn from established professionals.
The event also witnessed the premiere of “The Angry Six”, a documentary chronicling the history and evolution of the Directors Guild of Nigeria. The documentary represents part of the organization’s effort to preserve its institutional history and document the experiences of previous generations of directors.
With the successful launch of Directors’ Week and the DGN Awards, the Directors Guild of Nigeria has signalled its determination to strengthen the professional standing of directors while contributing to the continued growth, development and professionalization of Nigeria’s film and television industry.
The Directors’ Week ended with a call for stronger collaboration, knowledge-sharing, and professional relationships to grow Nigeria’s screen sector.
The post Tell authentic African stories, embrace AI, Tunde Kelani charges young filmmakers appeared first on Vanguard News.

items.content:
…BBNaija Season 11 faces backlash from viewers
By Tony-Okafor Favour
Big Brother Naija Season 11 is four weeks in, and instead of buzz, the conversation online is about boredom. Themed “Show Ya Sef”, the current season has come under heavy criticism from viewers who describe it as one of the uninspiring editions in the show’s history.
The backlash started after the July 26 premiere that introduced 24 housemates competing for a ₦160 million grand prize, including ₦100 million cash and a brand-new SUV. But the initial hype has quickly faded.
Fans on X and Instagram say the house lacks drama, storylines, and the high-energy moments BBNaija is known for.
Social media user Umuojime (@umuojime) called it “arguably the worst season in the history of this show,” adding that watching now “feels like a chore.”
“They tagged this season ‘Show Ya Sef’ but nobody in that house actually has anything to show us,” he wrote.
Other viewers agreed. Ama (@Ama676245296870) said, “Oh my guy I just turned off my TV, it’s boring.” Emeka (@Emeneks), a self-described “BBN fanatic, queried what the housemates are doing in the house. “I don’t even know what they’re doing in the house”,he wrote.
On his part, Abimbola Barakah Onibudo said “Till now I don’t know some housemates.”
Some viewers are even comparing Season 11 unfavorably to “No Loose Guard” Season 9 which was also once called boring.
BBNaija No Loose Guard had way more drama, entertainment and actual storylines than this season,” wrote Lowkey (@Lowkeytake). “Only a handful of housemates are actually putting in their best during tasks and wagers. Do they even know why they’re on the show?” Renelle Oppong (@OppongR…)asked.
The low energy was flagged early. During the first live show, host Ebuka Obi-Uchendu told housemates to stop waiting for things to happen and “start making things happen.”
It hasn’t been completely quiet. Week 4 saw Neche’s voluntary exit, an HoH twist, changes to the prize structure, and Cassi’s eviction.
Some housemates are also gaining traction. An independent Week 4 social media ranking by Ranks Africa put Temi Nkem at No.1, followed by Tram, Sheba, Goddessa and Keivo.
Not all fans are on board with the criticism. GlazedLens (@MealdredO) pointed out that people complaining are still watching. The bigger issue may be competition. BBNaija is no longer the only “appointment TV.” With TikTok, Instagram Reels, and YouTube dominating attention, the show has to fight harder to own the culture.
For years, BBNaija housemates’ fights and evictions dominated national conversations. Season 11 hasn’t hit that mark yet. With weeks still to go, the housemates have time to turn things around. But right now, a growing number of viewers are asking: is it “Show Ya Sef” or “Show Us Nothing”?

By Benjamin Njoku
Nollywood actress and producer Etta JoMaria has been named one of seven finalists for the British Council Film Lab Africa 2 Producers Lab. She was selected from a competitive pool of over 1,000 applications across the continent.
Delivered in partnership with EbonyLife Creative Academy and Iconic Steps, the Producers Lab is a core part of Film Lab Africa 2, the British Council’s flagship film and television accelerator. The programme is designed to equip emerging African filmmakers with practical training, mentorship, and support to develop original screen projects.
For Etta, the selection has been both validating and transformative.
“Being selected from over 1,000 applications was already a huge encouragement for me,” she said.
“But the real value has been everything I’ve learned. It has challenged me to look at producing beyond the administrative side and understand the producer as someone who is deeply involved in shaping the story and the creative vision.”
According to her, the programme has also strengthened her confidence in collaborating with writers, directors, and other creatives.
“I’ve gained a much deeper understanding of creative producing, from shaping a story and working closely with a creative team to navigating the practical, strategic and collaborative demands of bringing a project from development to the screen,” she added.
“It has made me more confident in the decisions I make as a producer and more intentional about the kind of stories I want to tell.”
Etta noted that one of her biggest takeaways is seeing the producer as both a creative and strategic force. “You have to understand the story, the audience, the team and the realities of production, and find a way to bring all those elements together. That is something I will continue to carry with me beyond this programme,” she said. The experience has also reinforced her commitment to developing stories that reflect African realities while connecting with global audiences.

The House of Representatives candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) for Ijebu Central Federal Constituency, Wale Ogunbanjo, has told the people of the constituency that only effective representation at the National Assembly could guarantee them the needed dividends of democracy.
Ogunbanjo, who earlier represented the constituency between 2003 and 2007, said at the flag-off of his campaign at Ijebu-Ode that the legacies he left behind during his first tenure in the National Assembly are still visible in the constituency right now.
He said that the water projects and other infrastructure facilities he facilitated as a lawmaker are still being used in the constituency to date, adding that the people needed to return him to the Green Chamber so that he could do more for the constituency.
He assured the people of Ijebu-Ode, Odogbolu and Ijebu North-East of his determination to represent them effectively in the Green Chamber, adding that his performance during his first tenure and his consistent contributions to the welfare of the people should stand him out.
“I promise to deliver more dividends of democracy if given another opportunity in the 2027 general election,” he said.
Ogunbanjo, whose declaration was witnessed by the governorship candidate of the PDP in Ogun State, Hon. Oladipupo Adebutu, and his deputy, Alhaja Lateefat Showunmi-Kolapo, the senatorial candidate for Ogun East, Engr. Omotayo Omo-Owo, erstwhile Commissioner for Women Affairs, Ambassador Folake Marcus-Bello, among other PDP leaders, noted that it was instructive that no indigene of Ijebu Ode has had the opportunity to represent the constituency since he left the Green Chamber almost 20 years ago.
He reassured the people that if he is voted into office for a second term, he would deliver more projects that would positively impact them, adding that the people needed to come out en masse to vote for all the PDP candidates in the forthcoming general election.
The PDP candidate thanked the party for giving him another opportunity to serve the people of Ijebu-Ode, Odogbolu and Ijebu North-East, and reminded the constituents of some of the key projects he facilitated during his first term in the National Assembly.
According to him, some of the projects included at least nine motorised boreholes which cut across Ijebu-Ode, Odogbolu and Ijebu North-East; reconstruction of Okun-Owa Town Hall, in Odogbolu Local Government Area; rural telephony project at Itamapako, Ijebu-Ode Local Government; bursaries and scholarships to students across the constituency, as well as renovation of the female ward of the General Hospital, Ijebu-Ode, among other projects.

items.author: Nwafor
items.content:
FRANKFURT — Two workers at Germany’s Frankfurt Airport have died after contracting malaria in an unusual outbreak believed to have been caused by an infected mosquito transported into the country aboard an aircraft.
Fraport, the company that operates Frankfurt Airport, said six employees had contracted what is known as airport malaria, with two subsequently dying. The four other workers have recovered, according to German media reports.
“We are shocked and deeply saddened by the loss of our colleagues, and our thoughts are with their families and friends,” Fraport said.
Airport malaria is an extremely rare form of transmission that occurs when an infected mosquito survives a flight from a malaria-endemic country and subsequently transmits the disease at or near an airport.
Germany’s national public health institute, the Robert Koch Institute (RKI), reported in July that several airport employees had developed malaria after falling ill between July 4 and 6.
The institute said an Anopheles mosquito brought into Germany aboard an aircraft was believed to be responsible for the infections.
Health authorities in Frankfurt are investigating the outbreak.
According to the RKI, malaria among German residents occurs almost exclusively among long-distance travellers who contract the disease in areas where malaria is endemic. Airport transmission is considered rare and may result in delayed diagnosis because health professionals do not initially suspect the disease.
The institute stressed that early diagnosis and treatment are critical to preventing severe illness and death.
Fraport said it had advised employees to inform their doctors that they work at Frankfurt Airport and that cases of airport malaria had been reported, to help ensure appropriate medical examination and treatment.
Mosquito traps have also been installed at the airport. The captured mosquitoes will undergo genetic analysis by the Institute of Tropical Medicine in Antwerp, Belgium, to determine their species and origin.
The RKI said the last reported case of airport malaria in Germany occurred in 2023, also at Frankfurt Airport.
Frankfurt Airport is Germany’s busiest airport by passenger traffic and serves as the main hub of the country’s flag carrier, Lufthansa.

KAMPALA — King Oyo Nyimba Kabamba Iguru Rukidi IV of Uganda’s Tooro Kingdom, who became the world’s youngest reigning monarch after ascending the throne at the age of three, has died at 34.
The monarch died at about 10 p.m. local time on Thursday, according to the Prime Minister of the Tooro Kingdom, Calvin Armstrong Rwomiire Akiiki, who announced his death in a post on X.
“It is with profound sadness and a heavy heart that I announce the passing of His Majesty the Omukama of Tooro, King Oyo Nyimba Kabamba Iguru Rukidi IV,” Akiiki said.
No cause of death was immediately disclosed.
Oyo was crowned King of Tooro on September 12, 1995, following the death of his father, Rukirabasaija Patrick David Matthew Kaboyo Olimi III.
Tooro is one of several traditional kingdoms in Uganda that were restored under the country’s republican system. Although the monarchies have no formal political authority, they retain significant cultural and social influence.
The Tooro Kingdom is located in western Uganda, near the border with the Democratic Republic of Congo.
Before his death, Ugandan government minister Balaam Barugahara had said the king was receiving medical treatment in the United States.
Describing the monarch’s death as “an immeasurable loss,” Akiiki said the king had left an heir, assuring that the succession and continuity of the Tooro crown were secure.
Oyo, who was unmarried, had remained a prominent cultural figure in Uganda and attracted international attention after becoming the youngest reigning monarch in the world in 1995.
His death sparked widespread grief across Uganda, with political leaders, public figures and citizens paying tribute to the late monarch.
Uganda’s leading opposition figure and musician, Bobi Wine, described the news as devastating.
“Most devastating news! May His Majesty the King’s soul rest in eternal peace,” he said in a post on X.
In April, during celebrations marking Oyo’s birthday, the Tooro Kingdom Prime Minister had described the monarch as a young leader closely connected to the realities of his generation.
“Our King is not distant from the realities of his people; he is part of this generation, part of this ecosystem, growing, learning, and leading,” the Prime Minister had said.
He added that the king’s youth was “not a limitation” but a source of energy, fresh perspective and courage to envision a different future for Tooro.
CNN

Fintech unicorn Raise Financial Services has roped in former Upstox executive Abhishek Singh as the chief executive officer (CEO) of its new insurtech vertical Pluto Insurance.
Singh confirmed the development in a post on LinkedIn. His bio on the networking platform also reflected the new designation.
“Twenty-three years in this industry, and I am as excited as I was on day one. Happy to announce that I am joining Pluto Insurance… I’ve spent most of my career wanting to build things that solve real problems for real people, not just move numbers on a board. Pluto Insurance gives me that shot, at scale, in a category that badly needs it,” said Singh.
In his post, Singh added that Pluto plans to build a platform for “what the customer actually needs, backed by cutting edge tech and AI”.
An alumnus of ICFAI Business School, Singh counts more than two decades of experience under his belt. He previously served at companies like Aviva India, PNB Metlife and Edelweiss Tokio Life Insurance. He was last working as a senior director at Upstox, according to his LinkedIn profile.
While the website of the new platform is yet to go live, it is already inviting users to join its waitlist. As per its website, Pluto Insurance will be housed under GreenLife Insurance Broking Pvt Ltd (GIBL), and bears the same IRDAI registration number and licence code as GIBL.
The appointment comes three months after Raise Financial acquired GIBL in an undisclosed cash-and-stock deal. At the time, the fintech unicorn had said that it would invest $15 Mn in GIBL to build a direct consumer insurance distribution platform.
Notably, recent reports also suggested that GIBL has been rebranded to Pluto Insurance. However, Raise Financial has made no public announcement of the same.
Notably, Singh is the second senior executive onboarded by the company in the past two months. In late-July, Ranjeet Walunj said that he had joined Pluto Insurance as its chief product and technology officer (CPTO).
While there appears no clarity on what Pluto Insurance exactly does, Walunj earlier said that the platform would streamline insurance for consumers. “At Pluto, we aim to build this (insurance) business differently: spam-free, easy-to-use, product-tech led, enabled with AI and most importantly, a platform that puts consumers and their needs first!” Walunj said then.
Nevertheless, Pluto Insurance will look to leverage GIBL’s strong presence in the B2B insurance distributor space and its offline network spanning over 50 cities and towns.
Founded in 2021 by former Paytm Money CEO Pravin Jadhav, Alok Pandey, Jay Prakash Gupta, and Raunak Rathi, Raise Financial is a unicorn that operates a gamut of fintech platforms.
Besides stock broking platform Dhan, Raise also owns and operates financial market information platform Upsurge, market research platform ScanX, and AI-driven trading insights platform FuzzAI. It also acquired new-age media startup Filter Coffee last year.
The startup entered the unicorn club in October last year after raising $120 Mn in its Series B round led by Hornbill Capital and Japan’s MUFG at a valuation of $1.2 Bn.

By Samuel Oyadongha, Yenagoa
The Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU), Niger Delta University (NDU) branch, has suspended its indefinite strike following an agreement with the Bayelsa State Government on the implementation of outstanding allowances and wage award arrears.
The union had embarked on the strike over the state government’s delay in implementing the Consolidated Academic Tools Allowance (CATA) and Professional Allowance.
Addressing journalists on Friday in Yenagoa, the ASUU-NDU Chairperson, Lucky Bebeteidoh, said the strike was suspended following the signing of a Collective Bargaining Agreement (CBA) between the union and the state government.
“The Academic Staff Union of Universities, NDU branch, just suspended its indefinite strike action, and this is resulting from a Collective Bargaining Agreement signed between the Bayelsa State Government and the branch,” Bebeteidoh said.
Under the agreement, the state government will commence payment of CATA and Professional Allowance from October 2026.
The government also agreed to begin payment of nine months’ arrears of the CATA and Professional Allowance, as well as 19 months’ wage award arrears, from January 2027.
Bebeteidoh said the agreement also provided that no member of ASUU would be victimised for participating in the industrial action.
He said the union would take appropriate steps to suspend the strike in line with the agreement.
“The government has agreed to commence the payment of the Consolidated Academic Tools Allowance (CATA) and the Professional Allowance from October 2026.
“The Bayelsa State Government has agreed to commence the payment of the nine-month CATA/Professional Allowance arrears from January 2027.
“The Bayelsa State Government has agreed to pay the 19-month wage award arrears from January 2027,” he said.
The agreement further provides that in the event of a substantial breach by the state government, the union may take appropriate action in accordance with labour laws.
“In the event of substantial breach of the agreement by the Government of Bayelsa State, the union shall take such actions as it may seem necessary within appropriate labour laws,” it stated.
While thanking Governor Douye Diri for his intervention and support, Bebeteidoh raised concerns over the university’s funding and staff accommodation.
He said the current subvention arrangement was putting increasing pressure on the institution and could undermine its ability to function effectively.
“As a branch, we are using this medium to again appeal that NDU is facing a lot of challenges; from subvention, the subvention policy of the state government is grinding the university down slowly,” he said.
Bebeteidoh also expressed concern over the lack of adequate accommodation for university staff, saying many lecturers travel daily between Yenagoa and the university’s Amassoma campus.
According to him, some members of staff travel about 64 kilometres daily, covering 32 kilometres each way.
“There is no way you come back from work, either through public transport or by your own means, that you will be productive after work,” he said.
He appealed to the state government to review the subvention policy and provide housing units for staff.
“So, we are appealing to His Excellency, Senator Douye Diri, to listen to our cry on the subvention policy. The subvention policy, as it is presently, is grinding the university to a halt.
“The government should look at it critically and see how the policy can be set aside. Also, on housing, we are appealing to the state government to come in and build housing units for staff of the university,” Bebeteidoh said.

items.content:
By Udeme Akpan, Energy Editor
A Nigerian chemical engineer, Godswill Chidiebere Agomuo, has called for increased local formulation and production of specialised oilfield chemicals, saying the move could reduce operating costs, promote technology transfer and strengthen Nigeria’s technical capacity in the oil and gas industry.
At an estimated average of about $40 per barrel, Nigeria’s crude oil production costs are among the highest in the OPEC+ group, far above the bloc’s roughly $10-per-barrel average.
However, Agomuo, Technical Manager at Pacegate Energy & Resources Ltd (PEARL), who has more than two decades of experience in production chemistry, said locally formulated production chemicals could be effectively deployed across production platforms and flow stations while being adapted to the specific characteristics of Nigerian crude.
He made the case while highlighting the importance of production chemistry and flow assurance to reliable hydrocarbon production.
According to him, the continued reliance on finished, imported specialty production chemicals limits the development of indigenous technical capacity in the petroleum industry.
“For many decades, the reliance on finished, imported specialty production chemicals in Nigeria has been a significant departure from the Federal Government’s resolve to promote credible indigenous participation in the oil and gas industry,” Agomuo said.
“In my view, locally formulated and blended production chemicals can be developed and deployed effectively across production platforms and flow stations.”
He said developing the capability locally would not only reduce dependence on imported products but also enable Nigerian engineers and service companies to develop solutions that respond to changing production conditions.
“This approach has the potential to promote technology transfer while strengthening the technical capacity of Nigerian engineers and other industry professionals,” he said.
“One of the key advantages of developing local formulation capability is that production chemicals can become more cost-effective and readily available to operators.”
Agomuo further said locally produced chemicals could be modified to meet the changing requirements of individual oilfields.
“More importantly, locally formulated and blended products can be re-engineered and optimised to meet specific crude-oil treatment requirements as field conditions and reservoir chemistry change,” he stated.
His comments come against the backdrop of efforts by Nigeria’s oil industry to increase crude production, improve the performance of existing assets and deepen local participation across the petroleum value chain.
One of the technical areas where production chemistry is critical is flow assurance, which deals with maintaining the reliable movement of hydrocarbons through wells, pipelines and production facilities.
Crude oil contains different hydrocarbon components that can behave differently when temperature and pressure change. Under certain conditions, paraffin or wax can separate from crude and deposit inside production systems.
Such deposits can restrict flow and create operational challenges, making the selection and application of appropriate chemical treatments important to maintaining production efficiency.
Agomuo said the selection of an appropriate chemical treatment should begin with a detailed understanding of the crude oil.
“The approach is simple, but it is fundamentally data-driven,” he said.
“It involves integrating chemical engineering and chemistry principles from the initial laboratory evaluation. We first establish key crude-oil properties, including the wax appearance temperature (WAT), wax content and composition, API gravity, viscosity and the overall oil composition.”
He explained that the information is subsequently used to assess available chemical formulations against specific performance requirements.
“These parameters provide the basis for screening different wax-inhibitor, or pour-point depressant (PPD), chemistries against defined key performance indicators (KPIs),” he said.
However, Agomuo stressed that laboratory performance alone cannot determine whether a chemical solution will work effectively in an operating oilfield.
“The objective is to identify the best-performing product that meets the required technical KPIs. However, laboratory performance is only the first stage,” he said.
According to him, the selected formulation must subsequently undergo field evaluation.
“The selected product must subsequently be evaluated under actual field operating conditions to establish how it performs in the production environment before a final selection decision is made,” he stated.
This approach is particularly important because conditions in operating oilfields can differ significantly from controlled laboratory environments.
Temperature, pressure, crude composition, water content, equipment configuration, chemical dosage and production rates can all affect the performance of a treatment programme.
Consequently, production chemistry involves more than simply supplying chemicals to an operator. It requires the identification of a specific production problem, laboratory analysis, formulation selection, field testing and continuous optimisation.
Agomuo’s experience includes work on the re-engineering of paraffin-wax inhibitor formulations at Asharami Energy, where the objective was to improve flow-assurance performance while reducing chemical injection requirements.
Such optimisation can have commercial implications because chemical treatment is a recurring operating cost for producers.
Reducing the quantity of chemical required while maintaining or improving performance can potentially lower operating expenditure and improve the economics of production operations.
Agomuo said Nigeria should therefore focus on developing local capabilities that combine chemical formulation with engineering and field knowledge.
“Building this capability means that we are not simply manufacturing chemicals locally; we are developing the technical knowledge, formulation expertise and engineering capacity required to respond to the evolving needs of Nigeria’s oil and gas production industry,” he said.
He argued that this would represent a deeper form of local content, moving beyond the procurement of locally supplied goods and services to the development of indigenous technology and specialised expertise.
The engineer’s position also comes as Nigerian oilfield-service companies seek greater opportunities to provide specialised services to upstream operators.
Agomuo has contributed to technical engagements involving ND Western and NDPR (Aradel), including multimillion-dollar contracts.
His professional qualifications include registration and licensing as an engineer with the Council for the Regulation of Engineering in Nigeria (COREN), as well as professional membership and licensing with the Institute of Registered Chemists of Nigeria.
He said production chemistry and flow assurance should receive greater attention as Nigeria seeks to improve crude production and optimise existing petroleum assets.
“The future of production chemistry and flow assurance in Nigeria will be increasingly defined by our ability to develop indigenous technical expertise, local formulation capability, and innovative chemical solutions that support safe, reliable, and economically sustainable oil and gas production,” Agomuo said.
He added that the disciplines should be regarded as strategic components of the petroleum industry.
“In my view, production chemistry and flow assurance should therefore no longer be regarded simply as supporting functions within oil and gas operations,” he said.
“They are strategic disciplines capable of directly influencing production reliability, asset integrity, operational efficiency, and the long-term competitiveness of Nigeria’s petroleum industry.”
According to him, developing such capabilities locally would help Nigeria reduce dependence on imported technical solutions while creating opportunities for technology transfer and specialist skills development.
“Developing this capability locally will be an important step toward building a more technologically independent, resilient, and globally competitive energy sector in Nigeria,” he said.

items.content:
By Damilola Samuel
The Nigerian Association of Resident Doctors (NARD) has called on the Oyo State Government to urgently address welfare and manpower challenges affecting resident doctors at the Ladoke Akintola University of Technology (LAUTECH) Teaching Hospital, Ogbomoso.
The association made the appeal as the August 28 deadline for the ultimatum issued by the hospital’s Association of Resident Doctors (ARD) approaches.
In a statement signed by its President, Dr Mohammad Usman Suleiman, NARD said several issues raised by the doctors remained unresolved despite the suspension of an earlier industrial action on June 27 and an eight-week period given to the authorities to address their concerns.
NARD expressed concern over the shortage of resident doctors at the hospital, saying several doctors had left in recent months without replacement, while doctors who completed their residency training had also not been replaced.
According to the association, some key specialties, including Anaesthesia, Chemical Pathology and Haematology, currently have no resident doctors, a situation it said could affect specialist training and patient care.
The association also listed outstanding minimum wage arrears, promotion and accoutrement allowance arrears, implementation of the new professional allowance and release of the Medical Residency Training Fund among the issues requiring urgent attention.
Other demands include the renovation of call rooms and on-call facilities, as well as enforcement of work-hour regulations to reduce excessive duty schedules and burnout among doctors.
NARD commended the LAUTECH resident doctors for remaining patient and continuing to provide healthcare services despite the challenges.
However, it warned that their patience should not be taken for granted.
“Patience must not be mistaken for acceptance of prolonged neglect,” the association said.
NARD urged the Oyo State Government and hospital management to engage the doctors in what it described as “good-faith, high-level negotiations” before the ultimatum expires.
The association warned that failure to resolve the issues could lead to another escalation of the dispute and disrupt specialist healthcare services for residents of Ogbomoso, Oyo, Iseyin and neighbouring communities.
It stressed that improving doctors’ welfare, staffing, training and working conditions was directly linked to patient safety and the quality of healthcare delivery.
“A functional health system cannot be sustained on the continued sacrifice of an overworked and demoralised workforce,” NARD said.
The association expressed hope that the state government would respond to the demands and prevent further disruption of healthcare services at the teaching hospital.

items.content:
By Henry Umoru
ABUJA — Ahead of the 2027 presidential and general elections, the Obi-Kwankwaso (OK) Movement has rejected any proposal to merge or absorb the organisation into another political body, insisting that it will remain an independent support group.
The movement, a political platform established to mobilise support for the joint ticket of Peter Obi and Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, also reaffirmed John Ughulu as its founder and Director-General, rejecting proposals for his replacement.
The resolutions were contained in a communiqué issued after the National Leadership Summit of the OK Movement held in Abuja.
The communiqué was signed on behalf of the geopolitical zonal coordinators and the 37 state coordinators by the Convener, Barr. Oladipo Johnson; Deputy Director-General (North), Prince Suleiman Abubakar; Deputy Director-General (South), Mrs Oluwatoyin Lanihun; and National Secretary, Saadatu Mohammed Sani.
The summit was attended by national leaders, zonal and state coordinators, as well as local government and ward-level mobilisers from the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory.
The movement said it was established to mobilise Nigerians behind the vision of a better Nigeria and had built its structure from the grassroots.
On the leadership of the organisation, the summit affirmed Ughulu as founder and Director-General, saying his leadership had been instrumental to building the movement’s grassroots structure.
“Our reasoning is practical rather than sentimental. The Movement was built ward by ward, largely on the personal credibility of its founder with the volunteers who make up its ranks,” the communiqué said.
It added that the loyalty of its members was based on the leadership and relationships built by Ughulu rather than merely on his official title.
“Social media handles can be reassigned; the confidence of thousands of grassroots mobilisers cannot,” it said.
On the issue of merger, the movement resolved that it “shall remain an independent organisation and shall not be merged into or absorbed by any external political body.”
It said any consolidation imposed from outside could disrupt ongoing programmes, blur its identity and undermine the momentum built over time.
The movement, however, stressed that its independence did not mean isolation, saying it remained willing to coordinate with allied groups in pursuit of shared political objectives.
On reconciliation, the summit invited Ms Jacky Wayas to return to the movement as Director for Strategic Implementation and Planning, working under the leadership of the Director-General.
The movement described Wayas’ contributions as valuable and said it would welcome her return.
It also announced the appointment of Prince Suleiman Abubakar as Deputy Director-General (North), following the resignation of Amb. Muhammad Auwal Musa.
The movement thanked Auwal Musa for his service and welcomed Abubakar to the position.
On the possible removal of the Director-General or loss of the movement’s independence, the leadership warned that such moves could affect its grassroots structure.
It said state, local government and ward leaders had indicated that they would not continue to operate under an arrangement that removed Ughulu or compromised the organisation’s independence.
“We do not say this to apply pressure. We say it because Nigerians deserve an accurate picture of what would, and would not, remain available on the ground,” the communiqué said.
At the conclusion of the summit, the national leadership visited former Kano State Governor and 2027 presidential hopeful, Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, at his residence to brief him on the outcome of the deliberations.
The leaders also visited Alhaji Buba Galadima, head of the movement’s Advisory Council, who, according to the communiqué, reaffirmed the importance of unity within the organisation.
Galadima was said to have encouraged the movement to remain an independent support group and cautioned against any proposal to merge it into the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC).
The movement said it remained committed to the vision of a better Nigeria and urged that the collective position of its grassroots members be respected.

items.author: Nwafor
items.content:
…Deploys 500,000 vaccine doses, expands treatment centres
By Chidinma Chukwu, Abuja
ABUJA — The Federal Government has activated an emergency multi-agency task force to contain a diphtheria outbreak affecting children in parts of Katsina and Kano states.
As part of the immediate response, the government has deployed 500,000 doses of diphtheria vaccines to the two states and commenced measures to expand access to treatment for affected communities.
The directive was issued by the Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Prof. Muhammad Ali Pate, according to a statement signed by the ministry’s Assistant Director, Information and Public Relations, Ado Bako, on Friday.
The ministry said the emergency task force would strengthen disease surveillance, close immunisation gaps and ensure that suspected and confirmed cases receive prompt treatment and referral care.
It said the response was part of the Federal Government’s broader efforts to protect children from vaccine-preventable diseases and strengthen the country’s capacity to detect and respond rapidly to disease outbreaks.
The task force was constituted by the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare in collaboration with the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC), National Primary Health Care Development Agency (NPHCDA), the affected state governments and international health partners.
According to the statement, the committee would be co-chaired by the Director-General of the NCDC and the Director of Public Health.
It would include representatives of the NPHCDA; health commissioners from Katsina, Kano, Zamfara and Sokoto states; the World Health Organisation (WHO); UNICEF; and the National Tuberculosis and Leprosy Control Programme in Katsina State.
The ministry’s Chief Epidemiologist will serve as secretary of the task force.
Under the emergency response plan, the NPHCDA has deployed 500,000 doses of vaccines to Katsina and Kano for intensified immunisation of unvaccinated children in affected and high-risk communities.
The task force will also conduct detailed investigations into the outbreak, strengthen surveillance and intensify community mobilisation and sensitisation to identify children who have not received the required doses and ensure they are vaccinated.
To improve access to treatment, the Katsina State Government is expected to establish treatment annexes in hospitals across the state’s three senatorial districts — Katsina, Daura and Funtua.
The ministry said the treatment centres would bring care closer to affected communities and enable suspected and confirmed cases to receive early medical attention.
The Federal Government is also mobilising emergency support for the Federal Teaching Hospital, Katsina, which serves as the principal referral centre for the state and parts of neighbouring states.
The support will include Diphtheria Antitoxin (DAT), intravenous antibiotics, additional clinical personnel and personal protective equipment for health workers managing diphtheria cases.
The ministry said the task force had been directed to submit weekly updates to the Coordinating Minister on the progress of the response, emerging challenges and additional resources required.
It added that any bottlenecks identified during the response would be escalated for immediate resolution to ensure that interventions were implemented promptly.

items.content:
…Seeks 65-year retirement age for clinical health workers
By Chidinma Chukwu, Abuja
ABUJA — The Nigeria Medical Association (NMA) has called on the Federal Government to urgently conclude and implement the outstanding Collective Bargaining Agreement (CBA) with health workers, warning that continued delays are fuelling dissatisfaction and encouraging the migration of medical professionals from the country.
The association also called for the implementation of the 65-year retirement age for clinical health workers as part of measures to retain experienced professionals and address the shortage of skilled personnel in the health sector.
The NMA made the demands on Friday at a press briefing in Abuja following resolutions reached at its National Executive Council (NEC) meeting.
Presenting the communique signed by him and the association’s Secretary-General, Dr Tamunokuro Diamond, the NMA President, Prof. Afekhide Ernest Omoti, said prolonged delays in addressing the concerns of health workers had contributed significantly to dissatisfaction within the workforce.
Omoti urged the Federal Government to conclude, approve, sign and implement the outstanding CBA in time for its provisions to be captured in the 2027 Appropriation Bill.
The association said retaining experienced clinicians had become increasingly important amid the shortage of skilled healthcare professionals and the continued migration of medical workers.
It said implementing the 65-year retirement age for clinical health workers would help retain experienced personnel while the country addressed the broader challenges of workforce shortages and migration.
Insecurity threatens healthcare delivery
On security, the NMA expressed concern over worsening insecurity across the country, describing kidnapping, banditry, terrorism and killings as major threats to national security and a public health emergency.
It said healthcare workers could not effectively serve communities when their lives and safety were constantly under threat.
The association therefore called on the Federal Government and security agencies to intensify efforts to tackle insecurity and strengthen protection for healthcare workers and facilities, particularly in vulnerable communities.
It also appealed for the safe release of a medical practitioner from Niger State who, according to the association, had reportedly been in captivity for about four months.
The NMA said: “Healthcare workers are essential to the survival and wellbeing of our communities. They should not have to choose between serving their patients and protecting their own lives.
“The NMA therefore makes a strong appeal to the Federal Government and all relevant security agencies to intensify efforts to end banditry, kidnapping, terrorism and other forms of insecurity across Nigeria.
“We particularly urge government to strengthen security around healthcare facilities and personnel in vulnerable communities and ensure that every effort is made to secure the safe release of the abducted doctor and all other citizens being held in captivity.”
NMA seeks tax relief for doctors
The association also called for tax waivers, rebates and other relief measures for healthcare professionals in both the public and private sectors.
It expressed particular concern over multiple taxation of doctors operating private hospitals and the high cost of electricity, noting that such expenses could ultimately be transferred to patients.
“Medical practitioners and other healthcare workers provide essential services under demanding and often hazardous conditions, including working long hours, responding to emergencies and providing care in underserved communities.
“The NMA therefore calls on the Federal Government to consider and grant appropriate tax waivers, rebates or other tax relief measures to medical practitioners and other healthcare professionals, both in the public and private sectors.
“Doctors in private hospitals need special protection from multiple taxation and the heavy electricity tariff burden, whose cost may ultimately be transferred to poor Nigerian patients,” the association said.
The NMA added that such measures would contribute to improving the welfare and retention of health professionals in Nigeria.
It also called for the universal applicability of salaries, wages and income to doctors, irrespective of their places of employment, including federal and state institutions, universities and local government areas.
Bad roads hamper healthcare delivery
On access roads to healthcare facilities, the association expressed concern over the poor condition of roads across the country, saying the situation was having serious consequences for healthcare delivery.
It said bad roads could delay patients from accessing emergency care, impede referrals, disrupt the transportation of medicines and medical supplies, and make it difficult for healthcare workers to reach underserved communities.
The association therefore called on governments at all levels to prioritise the construction, rehabilitation and maintenance of roads leading to healthcare facilities, particularly in rural and underserved areas.
Drug abuse among youths
The NMA further raised concern over the growing prevalence of drug and substance abuse among young Nigerians, describing it as an emerging public health emergency with serious consequences for mental health, families, communities and the country’s productive workforce.
It called on the Federal Government to declare drug and substance abuse among youths a national public health priority.
The association urged the government to strengthen prevention and public enlightenment programmes, regulate access to harmful substances, and expand mental health and addiction treatment services at the primary, secondary and tertiary levels of healthcare.
Omoti acknowledged the government’s investments in healthcare infrastructure and service delivery but stressed that infrastructure alone could not guarantee an effective health system without a motivated, adequately protected and properly remunerated workforce.
He said the NMA remained committed to working with the government to address the challenges confronting the health sector, adding that the association’s demands were aimed at strengthening the healthcare system.
“We are partners with government in the development of Nigeria’s healthcare system. Our criticisms and demands are therefore made in the spirit of constructive engagement and a genuine desire to build a healthier, safer and more prosperous Nigeria.
“We acknowledge the progress being made by government in several areas of healthcare infrastructure and service delivery.
“However, we urge government to match infrastructure development with investment in the healthcare workforce.
“A hospital building without doctors, nurses, pharmacists, laboratory scientists and other skilled professionals cannot provide the quality of care Nigerians deserve.
“Nigeria is losing some of its finest medical professionals to other countries because of difficult working conditions, insecurity, inadequate remuneration, limited career opportunities and other systemic challenges. “This trend must be urgently reversed,” the association said.
The post Implement CBA to stem medical brain drain, NMA tells FG appeared first on Vanguard News.

items.author: Akinbayo Wahab
items.content:
The African Democratic Congress has said it does not need a coalition with other opposition parties to win the 2027 presidential election, although it remains open to cooperation with other political groups.
Bolaji Abdullahi, spokesperson for the ADC, stated this on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Friday while discussing the chances of the party ahead of the 2027 general election.
Abdullahi said the coalition initially envisaged by opposition politicians was expected to make it easier to defeat the ruling All Progressives Congress, but the political landscape had since changed following the movement of some key figures to other parties.
“When we started building this coalition, we started on the assumption that if we are able to build a broad-based coalition, it would make our job of beating the APC easier. But that didn’t pan out the way we expected,” he said.
He noted that Peter Obi, whom he described as one of the key figures in the coalition, had moved to the National Democratic Congress, with former Kano State governor Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso as his running mate.
“One of the key players, leaders in the coalition, has gone to the NDC, and that’s His Excellency Peter Obi, and of course Governor Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso as his running mate. We are in the African Democratic Congress,” Abdullahi said.
The ADC spokesman maintained that while a broad opposition alliance could strengthen the party’s chances, it was not a prerequisite for victory.
“What I’m saying is that we don’t need a coalition to win this election. The African Democratic Congress does not need a coalition to win this election,” he said.
“If we are able to build the kind of coalition that we started, maybe it’ll make our job easier, but we don’t need that coalition. We don’t necessarily need the coalition to win the election.”
Abdullahi, however, said discussions among opposition parties were continuing, with the focus shifting from producing a single presidential candidate to identifying areas where the parties could work together.
“We are still having conversations among ourselves, opposition political parties, and there are different areas. You’ve heard about the G100, mobilizing everybody, trying to bring everybody together,” he said.
According to him, one area of possible cooperation is election monitoring and protecting votes during the 2027 polls.
“But the conversation is not about how do we produce a single presidential candidate. The conversation predominantly is about what areas of cooperation is possible,” Abdullahi said.
“For example, if we are able to develop a common protocol for election monitoring and for policing our votes, that is major.”
