items.author: Nwafor
items.content:
…Recovers 205,000 litres of stolen crude products, arrests 15 suspects
By Kingsley Omonobi
ABUJA — Troops of the Nigerian Armed Forces conducting operations across the country have rescued 43 kidnapped victims, neutralised 26 terrorists and arrested 15 suspected criminals in the past week.
The troops also foiled attempts to steal about 205,000 litres of crude oil and illegally refined petroleum products in the Niger Delta, the Director of Defence Media Operations, Major General Michael Onoja, disclosed on Friday.
Giving an update on military operations across the various theatres, Onoja said troops of Operation Fansan Yamma rescued several abducted persons in the North-West.
He said six victims were rescued along the Dandume-Sheme Road in Dandume Local Government Area of Katsina State on August 22, with N800,000 allegedly collected from them by their captors recovered.
On August 23, troops rescued six victims at Gadan Manya village in Anka LGA of Zamfara State, three of whom sustained minor injuries.
Three abducted children were also rescued in Kachia LGA of Kaduna State on August 24 and reunited with their families.
Onoja said 14 abducted persons were rescued at Magazu village in Tsafe LGA of Zamfara State on August 25, with one sustaining gunshot injuries.
The following day, troops rescued two female captives at Hayin Babangida in Igabi LGA of Kaduna State. A male farmer abducted during the same incident was, however, found dead from gunshot wounds.
The troops also disrupted arms trafficking and kidnapping networks in the zone.
On August 23, they intercepted disassembled canoes allegedly belonging to a terrorist kingpin along the Zamfara-Kebbi axis and arrested three suspected gunrunners along the Kaura Namoda-Shinkafi Road.
An assault rifle concealed in a bag of millet and allegedly destined for a terrorist kingpin in Zamfara State was recovered.
The same day, troops arrested a suspected terrorist kingpin, Mallam Sanusi Mai Glass, and his associate in Dutsinma LGA of Katsina State, recovering a vehicle.
Two other suspected terrorists were arrested in Maradun LGA of Zamfara State on August 25, with firearms, communication equipment and cash recovered. Incriminating images and videos were also recovered from a suspect’s mobile phone.
North-East
In the North-East, troops of Operation Hadin Kai intercepted eight abducted persons, comprising three women and five children, around Ngoshe in Gwoza LGA of Borno State on August 22.
Three minors who escaped from terrorist enclaves near Amuda Bridge in Gwoza were also rescued the same day.
Between August 23 and 27, troops arrested suspected terrorist logistics suppliers, spies and fighters in Biu, Guzamala and Damboa LGAs of Borno State, as well as Michika LGA of Adamawa State.
Onoja said troops repelled an attempted terrorist infiltration along the Gulumba Gana axis in Dikwa LGA of Borno State on August 27, neutralising one terrorist while two others escaped with gunshot wounds.
He said all rescued persons were handed over to camp officials and community leaders for further care.
During a clearance operation at Kopre Mountain in Hong LGA of Adamawa State between August 26 and 27, troops neutralised 21 terrorists and destroyed their camp.
The operation also yielded six AK-47 rifles, 23 magazines and 586 rounds of ammunition.
The military further recorded several surrenders and arrests of suspected terrorists and their collaborators.
Between August 22 and 25, a terrorist leader, several fighters and their family members surrendered to troops at Kumburi, Bula Daloye and New Abaram Resettlement Village in Bama LGA of Borno State.
The military said the surrendering terrorists cited sustained military pressure and internal clashes between rival terrorist factions as reasons for their decision.
On August 25, troops, in collaboration with the Department of State Services (DSS), arrested a suspected kidnapper at Madara Village in Katagum LGA of Bauchi State.
Two suspected logistics suppliers linked to a terrorist leader were also arrested in Bauchi LGA on August 27 but were subsequently neutralised while allegedly attempting to escape from custody.
North-Central
In the North-Central, troops of Operation Whirl Stroke arrested an alleged accomplice of a previously apprehended gunrunner at Dorowa in Wukari LGA of Taraba State on August 22.
The suspect reportedly confessed to supplying four AK-47 rifles and about 6,000 rounds of ammunition.
On August 23, troops arrested a suspected terrorist and his courier around Okene LGA of Kogi State.
Two kidnap victims were rescued in separate operations in Lokoja LGA of Kogi State between August 24 and 26, while a weapon abandoned by fleeing kidnappers was recovered.
Troops also engaged suspected terrorists at Ahungwa in Katsina-Ala LGA of Benue State on August 27, neutralising one while another escaped into a nearby forest.
A suspected gunrunner was also arrested in Jalingo LGA of Taraba State in connection with alleged arms trafficking to rebel elements in Cameroon.
Meanwhile, troops of Operation Enduring Peace arrested a suspect following a report of gunshots around DTV in Bassa LGA of Plateau State on August 22.
A locally made hunting gun was recovered from the suspect, who allegedly claimed he fired the weapon while hunting. Investigations are ongoing to determine the circumstances of the incident.
Also, troops of Operation Savannah Shield engaged terrorists at Dekara in Borgu LGA of Niger State on August 23, forcing the attackers to flee into the Kainji Lake National Park.
Troops subsequently recovered an AK-47 rifle, ammunition, six motorcycles, 49 mobile phones, nine phone batteries and 10 memory cards along the terrorists’ withdrawal route.
Oil theft
In the Niger Delta, troops of Operation Delta Safe, under Operation Delta Sentinel, disrupted suspected crude oil storage infrastructure containing about 93,000 litres of stolen crude around Allison Community in Bonny LGA of Rivers State on August 20.
The following day, troops intercepted two vehicles conveying about 8,500 litres of suspected illegally refined petroleum products along the Ejemekuru-Obudi-Agwa axis of Imo State and arrested three suspects. Other suspects reportedly fled, abandoning one of the vehicles.
On August 22, personnel of Nigerian Navy Ship Pathfinder disrupted three illegal refining sites around the Ohaji axis of Egbema-Ndoni LGA of Rivers State and recovered about 103,000 litres of suspected illegally refined Automotive Gas Oil (AGO).
On August 27, troops intercepted two tanker trucks allegedly preparing to siphon crude oil from an illegal collection point at Aleto in Eleme LGA of Rivers State and arrested two suspects.
South-East
In the South-East, troops of Operation Udoka intercepted two vehicles conveying suspected illegally refined petroleum products derived from stolen crude oil along the Agwa-Ejemekuru Road in Oguta LGA of Imo State on August 21.
Three suspects were arrested.
The military said preliminary investigations revealed the alleged involvement of the leader of a local security group in Orlu, who reportedly fled after being directed to report for verification.
The matter has been reported to the leader of the local security group in Imo State to assist in locating the suspect for further investigation.
On August 22, troops, in collaboration with the DSS and a local security group in Anambra State, raided suspected IPOB/ESN strongholds at Obene and Abator villages in Ogbaru LGA.
One suspected terrorist was neutralised, while pump-action guns, motorcycles and materials allegedly intended for the fabrication of improvised explosive devices were recovered.
CDS commends troops, Air Peace
Onoja also said the Chief of Defence Staff, General Olufemi Oluyede, commended troops for their recent successes and appreciated Air Peace for a gesture by its staff and passengers toward Nigerian military personnel.
He said the gesture followed a directive by the airline’s Chairman, Allen Onyema, that military and police personnel be accorded priority boarding and applauded in recognition of their service and sacrifices to the nation.
According to him, the gesture reflected public goodwill toward the nation’s security forces amid prevailing security challenges.
The CDS commended the troops for their gallantry, discipline and commitment to rescuing abducted citizens, neutralising terrorists, dismantling criminal and secessionist networks and disrupting illegal oil bunkering activities.
He also commended the collaboration between the military and other security agencies, including the Nigeria Police Force, DSS, local security groups and other stakeholders.
Oluyede further urged members of the public, traditional rulers and community leaders to continue providing useful information to security agencies to strengthen the nation’s security architecture.
He assured Nigerians that the Armed Forces would sustain the current tempo of operations across the country.

By Henry Umoru
ABUJA — Ahead of the 2027 presidential and general elections, Deputy President of the Senate, Senator Barau Jibrin (APC, Kano North), has urged constituents in his senatorial district to remain united and support President Bola Tinubu, Kano State Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf, himself and other candidates of the All Progressives Congress (APC).
Barau made the call at the National Assembly while receiving two delegations from Dambatta Local Government Area of Kano North Senatorial District.
He also disclosed that one of his ongoing empowerment initiatives provides N100,000 in start-up capital to 1,300 petty traders, artisans and other beneficiaries every month.
A statement issued by his Special Adviser on Media and Publicity, Ismail Mudashir, said the delegations comprised representatives from the 21 wards of Dambatta LGA, led by Hon. Hafiz Sani Maidaji, a former three-term member of the Kano State House of Assembly, and another group led by Barau’s Senior Legislative Aide in Dambatta, Alhaji Abdullahi Dan Bayero.
According to the statement, the groups visited the Deputy President of the Senate to appreciate him for various projects, empowerment programmes and other interventions being implemented across Kano North.
The initiatives include the monthly provision of N100,000 start-up capital to 1,300 petty traders, artisans and other beneficiaries, as well as the distribution of fertilisers, water pumps, grinding machines, sewing machines, motorcycles, refrigerators and other support items.
Barau assured the people of Dambatta and Kano North that his commitment to their development remained unwavering.
He said he would continue to support programmes in empowerment, education, agriculture, infrastructure and other areas aimed at improving the livelihoods of his constituents.

By Henry Umoru
ABUJA — Ahead of the 2027 presidential and general elections, the National Speaker of the Women Parliament of the Social Democratic Party (SDP), Ambassador Sa’adatu Abdullahi, has called on women leaders across the country to strengthen grassroots mobilisation and build functional party structures.
Abdullahi made the call on Friday at the SDP National Secretariat, Abuja, during a strategic meeting between the party’s national women leadership and state women leaders.
She urged the women to organise and establish strong structures across states, wards and communities to ensure their voices and contributions were felt within the party and the broader political space.
Abdullahi said political success could not be achieved through wishful thinking but required organisation, sacrifice, strategy, commitment and effective grassroots engagement.
She said the SDP Women Parliament was determined to strengthen its structures and mobilise more women to participate actively in the party’s activities.
“This meeting gives us an opportunity to assess where we are, identify our weaknesses, strengthen our structures and develop practical strategies for taking the SDP message to every ward, community and household,” she said.
The National Speaker urged state women leaders to see themselves as strategic pillars of the party, stressing the need for focus, discipline, teamwork and commitment to the collective vision of the SDP.
She also called on the women to put aside their differences and work together, noting that unity would strengthen the party’s structures and amplify their voices.
Abdullahi commended the state women leaders for their sacrifices, particularly those who travelled long distances at their own expense to attend the meeting.
She urged them to return to their respective states with renewed determination and translate the resolutions reached at the meeting into measurable results.
“Our strength is in our unity, our power is in our organisation, and our weapon is our determination. We must organise, mobilise and deliver results,” she said.
In his remarks, the National Chairman of the SDP, Prof. Sadiq Gombe, represented by the South-South Deputy National Chairman, Senator Ugochukwu Uba, assured the women of greater inclusion in the affairs of the party.
He said the party was undergoing reforms and reorganisation to strengthen its structures and prepare for future political activities.
Gombe said the SDP was committed to giving women their rightful place in political appointments, party activities and elections.
He added that the party’s forthcoming manifesto would outline its policies across various sectors, including measures to promote greater participation and inclusion of women.
The national chairman described the SDP as an ideological party committed to the welfare of Nigerians and the principles enshrined in Chapter Two of the Nigerian Constitution.
He urged the women leaders to sustain their grassroots mobilisation efforts and prepare women across the country for active participation in the party’s future campaigns and activities.
Gombe also commended the National Speaker and other women leaders for their commitment and sacrifices toward mobilising women for the growth of the party.

Update | August 29, 01:54 AM IST
Hours after Sandhya Devanathan said that she had stepped down as the India and Southeast Asia vice president of social media giant Meta, it has now emerged that she is joining AI giant OpenAI.
The ChatGPT maker told Techcrunch that Devanathan, in her new role at OpenAI, will now oversee consumer growth, enterprise adoption and partnerships, regulatory engagement and operations across Southeast Asia and Australia. She will reportedly be based out of Singapore and report to OpenAI’s Asia-Pacific managing director, Kiran Mani.
As per the report, Meta’s India managing director, Arun Srinivas, will now report directly to the company’s vice president for Asia Pacific, Benjamin Joe.
Inc42 has reached out to both Meta and OpenAI for comments on the matter. This story will be updated upon receiving their statement.
Original | August 28, 05:54 PM IST
Meta’s India and Southeast Asia vice president Sandhya Devanathan has stepped down after more than a decade at the social media giant.
In a LinkedIn post, Devanathan said, “After more than a decade at Meta, I’ve made the bittersweet decision to move on to my next adventure.”
“After a short break, I’m looking forward to my next exciting chapter — will share more on that soon,” she added.
Devanathan did not disclose her next destination. It is also unclear who will replace her at Meta.
Devanathan joined Facebook, now Meta, in 2016 as group director for its ecommerce, travel, and financial services businesses in Southeast Asia. She subsequently served as Facebook Singapore’s MD and business head for Vietnam.
In 2020, she took charge of Meta’s gaming vertical in the Asia-Pacific region, which she described on LinkedIn as one of the company’s five largest business verticals. The company appointed her as its India head and vice president in November 2022, and she assumed the role in January 2023.
Meta expanded Devanathan’s responsibilities to include Southeast Asia in June 2025. The company appointed Arun Srinivas as its MD and head for India around the same time, with Srinivas reporting to Devanathan.
Before joining Meta, Devanathan spent almost a decade at Citi and more than six years at Standard Chartered Bank.
Since February 2026, she has also served as a founding board member of Reliance Enterprise Intelligence Ltd, the enterprise AI joint venture between Meta and Reliance. She is a board observer at Jio Platforms and a member of the advisory board of the College of Integrative Studies at Singapore Management University.
It is not clear if Devanathan will continue in her positions at Reliance Enterprise Intelligence, Jio Platforms, and Singapore Management University following her departure from Meta.
Devanathan’s exit comes months after CRED founder Kunal Shah took over as WhatsApp’s global head and stepped away from the fintech unicorn’s day-to-day operations. Meta also invested $900 Mn (about ₹8,550 Cr) in CRED through a mix of primary and secondary transactions.
Her departure also comes at a time when Meta is facing increasing regulatory scrutiny in India, one of its largest markets. Earlier this month, the Centre sought technical changes from the company to tackle child sexual abuse material, deepfakes, and unlabelled AI-generated content across its platforms.
Meta subsequently began acting on the government’s concerns following multiple rounds of discussions.

items.content:
Many travellers were feared abducted after bandits blocked the Gusau-Funtua highway, less than a kilometre from Tsafe town, headquarters of Tsafe Local Government Area of Zamfara State, on Friday.
The incident, which occurred on Friday, caused panic among commuters as the bandits reportedly took over the road around the mountainous area of Tsafe.
A commuter who narrowly escaped the attack told Daily Trust that the bandits blocked the road and abducted passengers travelling in a Sharon Toyota vehicle and a petroleum tanker.
The commuter, who requested anonymity for security reasons, said the incident triggered sporadic shooting that lasted for a considerable period.
Youths protest alleged killing of UNIPORT graduate by police
3 youths allegedly arrested for posting Borno LG’s FAAC allocation on Facebook
Two other residents of Tsafe town also confirmed the attack but said they could not ascertain the number or identities of those abducted.
“Quite all right, we heard sporadic shooting, and the sound of the gunfire was very serious. It lasted for a long time before everything returned to normal,” one of the residents said.
Another commuter who passed through the area after security personnel had cleared the road said he saw a Sharon vehicle and a petroleum tanker abandoned on the road with their doors open.
“The security personnel cleared the road for us. As we entered Tsafe town, I saw a Sharon vehicle that had apparently been used to transport passengers. Its doors were open, but there was no one inside, only luggage and bags that had been left behind.
“Only God knows what happened to those who were inside. Perhaps they managed to escape, or perhaps they were abducted,” he said.
The commuter added that he also saw a fuel tanker with its doors open and its engine still running slowly, but there was no one inside.
“It is possible that the people who were inside fled, or perhaps they were kidnapped too,” he said.
He further said a bus painted in yellow colours had overturned near the two abandoned vehicles.
“It is possible that the driver panicked while trying to turn and lost control, causing the vehicle to overturn, or perhaps it was the work of the bandits. Allah knows best,” he said.
Another traveller, who was among commuters stranded while waiting for security personnel to clear the road, commended the security forces for their efforts.
“Honestly, our security personnel did their best. There was gunfire all around, and their efforts gave us hope that the road would eventually be cleared,” he said.
The Gusau-Funtua highway is one of the major routes linking Zamfara and Katsina states and has witnessed security challenges, including attacks and abductions, in recent times.
Efforts to obtain confirmation from the Zamfara State Police Command spokesperson, DSP Yazid Abubakar, and the state Chairman of the Petroleum Tanker Drivers Association (PTD), Alhaji Shu’aibu Lili, were unsuccessful as they did not respond to calls and text messages sent to them.

Residents of the area told Daily Trust on Friday that the police personnel on duty at Agip junction/Ada George shot to death the late Anthony, who was waiting for his call-up letter from the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC), and injured three others, who were inside the car he was driving.
The late Anthony was said to have used his vehicle to run a transport service to save money for his planned National Youth Service, before the unfortunate incident.

A policeman attached to the patrol team allegedly shot the man, as a stray bullet also hit a POS operator sitting under her umbrella by the road side, injuring her.
The passengers of the bus and other injured victims at the bus stop were rushed to the nearby health facility, Palmas Hospital, for emergency care, where the driver of the bus was confirmed dead.
The youths, who took to the street on Friday, called for the arrest and prosecution of the police officer who allegedly fired the deadly round that killed the victim.
Meanwhile, some residents of the area, who witnessed what transpired between the deceased and the police officers, said the UNIPORT graduate had allegedly failed to stop when he was flagged down by the police officers on patrol around the Junction.
They said that one of the officers allegedly opened fire at the vehicle after the driver refused to stop.
The father of the deceased, Mr. Princewill Obodo, from Agba Ndele, Emohua Local Government Area of Rivers State, expressed anger with reports that described his son as a fraudster popularly known as Yahoo Boy after the incident.
He called for justice over the alleged killing of his son, saying that as a struggling young man, his late son was only doing a legitimate business to fend for himself before he was untimely murdered.
Police authorities in Rivers State are yet to speak on the incident, as the Police Public Relations Officer of the Rivers State Police Command, ASP Agabe Blessing Kaborlo, didn’t pick calls since Thursday evening and throughout Friday to confirm the incident.

items.content:
Three youths in Shani Local Government Area of Borno State, Salihu Yahaya, Haruna Mohammed and Muhammed Mallum, have allegedly been arrested by the police following a Facebook post on the council’s receipt of about N3.11 billion in Federation Account Allocation Committee (FAAC) funds between January and June 2026.
The youths were reportedly arrested at the instance of the chairman of the local government, according to sources close to the affected persons.
The Facebook post, seen by our reporter, contained an image with the caption: “Shani Local Government Received 3.110 Billion Allocation From Federal Government From January To June 2026.”
The figure was based on an analysis of the monthly FAAC disbursement reports for Shani LGA.
Troops kill 2 terrorists, recover 2 AK-47 rifles, motorcycles in Sokoto
Man rescued after jumping off bridge in Plateau
Sources close to the arrested youths said they were taken into police custody in Shani and subsequently threatened with transfer to the State Criminal Investigation Department (CID) or the Department of State Services (DSS) in Maiduguri, the Borno State capital.
According to the sources, the youths did not engage in any other activity apart from sharing or posting the information on Facebook.
One of the sources said the arrests had generated concern among young people in the area, with several youths taking to social media to demand the release of the affected persons.
“Our concern is that they only shared information about the allocation received by the local government. If the authorities believe the information is wrong, they should explain where the figures are wrong instead of arresting them,” the source said.
Another source said the development had created fear among youths who use social media to discuss issues concerning the local government.
As of the time of filing this report, the whereabouts and current status of the three youths could not be independently confirmed by our reporter.
Efforts to reach the chairman of Shani Local Government Area for his reaction were unsuccessful as calls and text messages sent to him were not responded to as of press time.
The police authorities in Borno State could also not be reached for their reaction to the alleged arrests and the reasons for the detention.
FAAC report confirms amount
Report by the Office of the Accountant General of the Federation monthly FAAC disbursement for January to June 2026 shows that Shani Local Government Area of Borno State received a total of N3.11 billion in allocations from the Federation Account Allocation Committee (FAAC).
An analysis of the reports showed that the local government’s allocation fluctuated during the six-month period, with the highest monthly allocation of N551.90 million recorded in May and the lowest, N474.92 million, recorded in March.
In January, Shani received N514.80 million as its total net allocation. The amount comprised N225.94 million in net statutory allocation, N12.07 million from the Electronic Money Transfer Levy (EMTL), N6.78 million in net share of ecology and N270.02 million in Value Added Tax (VAT).
The local government received N533.46 million in February. The allocation comprised N184.33 million in net statutory allocation, N22.85 million in augmentation, N6.22 million in net share of ecology and N320.05 million in VAT.
In March, the allocation dropped to N474.92 million, comprising N266.01 million in net statutory allocation, N7.98 million in net share of ecology and N200.94 million in VAT.
The April allocation stood at N496.11 million. The amount included N274.29 million in net statutory allocation, N45.71 million in augmentation, N13.54 million from solid mineral revenue, N10.01 million in net share of ecology and N152.58 million in VAT.
Shani recorded its highest allocation during the period in May, when it received N551.90 million.
The May allocation consisted of N252.02 million in net statutory allocation, N57.13 million in augmentation, N9.27 million in net share of ecology and N233.47 million in VAT.
In June, the local government received N538.95 million, comprising N325.28 million in net statutory allocation, N9.76 million in net share of ecology and N203.91 million in VAT.
The six-month analysis also showed that VAT and statutory allocation constituted the major components of Shani’s FAAC receipts during the period, while additional components such as augmentation, EMTL and solid mineral revenue varied from month to month.
The total monthly allocations were N514.80 million in January, N533.46 million in February, N474.92 million in March, N496.11 million in April, N551.90 million in May and N538.95 million in June.
Cumulatively, the six-month receipts amounted to N3,110,132,578.97.

items.content:
In politics, victories are often credited to candidates, but history teaches that behind every successful presidential campaign stands a strategist capable of transforming political possibilities into electoral realities. Campaigns are won not merely by popularity or incumbency, but by organization, coalition-building, discipline, persuasion and the ability to convert political goodwill into votes.
President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s decision to appoint Senator Abdulaziz Abubakar Yari as Director-General of the APC Presidential Campaign Council for the 2027 general elections appears to be one of those strategic decisions whose significance may only become fully appreciated in retrospect. The appointment is not merely about rewarding loyalty or balancing political interests. It is a calculated choice rooted in Yari’s extensive political experience, his grassroots reach, his coalition-building capacity and his demonstrated ability to navigate Nigeria’s complex political terrain.
Like the legendary campaign architects who shaped presidential victories across the world, Yari enters the 2027 contest not simply as an administrator of a campaign but as a political field marshal entrusted with coordinating one of the most ambitious electoral operations in Nigeria’s democratic history.
The Making of a Political Maverick
Political mavericks are not manufactured overnight. They emerge through years of political contests, negotiations, victories, setbacks and reinventions.
Abdulaziz Yari’s political journey reflects this evolution. From his early days as a party organizer in Zamfara State to becoming governor, Chairman of the Nigeria Governors’ Forum, and later a senator, Yari has accumulated experience across virtually every level of Nigeria’s political architecture.
Unlike politicians whose influence is confined to their constituencies, Yari’s political reach extends beyond geography. His years in public service have enabled him to cultivate relationships across the North, South, East and West, making him one of the few contemporary politicians whose network cuts across regional, ethnic and political boundaries.
This ability to build bridges in a country often divided by fault lines is perhaps one of the strongest arguments in favor of his emergence as campaign director-general.
The Liberal Latitude of a Consensus Builder
One of Yari’s most enduring political attributes is his capacity to accommodate diverse interests without losing strategic direction.
Successful campaign directors are rarely ideological extremists. They are consensus builders who understand that electoral success in a plural society requires the harmonization of competing interests.
Nigeria’s electoral map demands exactly this kind of leadership.
Winning a presidential election requires engaging farmers in Zamfara, entrepreneurs in Lagos, traders in Aba, professionals in Abuja and fishermen in the Niger Delta with equal sincerity. The campaign director must understand their aspirations, communicate a unifying message and ensure that every segment feels represented within the broader national vision.
Yari’s political style has consistently demonstrated this expansive outlook. His politics has often reflected pragmatism rather than exclusion, coalition rather than confrontation, and engagement rather than isolation.
Such liberal latitude could prove invaluable as the APC seeks to consolidate support across Nigeria’s diverse political constituencies.
A Tested Organizer
Campaigns are ultimately exercises in organization.
The most brilliant political messages fail without structures capable of transmitting them to voters.
The history of modern elections is filled with examples of charismatic candidates defeated by superior organization.
Yari’s greatest strength may well be his understanding of political structures.
From party administration to governance and legislative engagement, he has spent decades building and sustaining political networks. Those who have observed his political career often point to his ability to identify talent, mobilize supporters and maintain loyalty within large political organizations.
These are precisely the skills required of a campaign director-general.
The 2027 election will not be won solely on television screens or social media platforms. It will be won in wards, polling units, local governments and communities where political organization remains the decisive factor.
Few politicians possess Yari’s familiarity with these grassroots realities.
The Northern Advantage
Every presidential campaign requires strategic geographical anchors.
For Tinubu and Shettima, the North remains a critical electoral battleground.
Yari’s political stature within Northern Nigeria provides the campaign with an important asset. His influence extends beyond Zamfara and resonates across significant segments of the North-West, one of the country’s most electorally consequential regions.
Beyond numbers, however, Yari brings credibility.
Political messages resonate more effectively when delivered by individuals who command trust within their constituencies. Yari’s long-standing engagement with Northern political stakeholders positions him as a bridge between the campaign and a crucial voting bloc.
A Pro-Nigerian Political Outlook
The strongest political campaigns are built around national aspirations rather than sectional interests.
One of the expectations accompanying Yari’s appointment is his ability to project a message that transcends regional calculations and speaks to the broader Nigerian experience.
Nigeria’s electorate increasingly seeks leaders and political institutions capable of addressing common challenges: economic growth, job creation, security, infrastructure development and national cohesion.
The success of the Renewed Hope agenda will ultimately depend on convincing Nigerians that progress remains possible and that continuity offers the best pathway to achieving it.
As Director-General, Yari’s responsibility extends beyond campaign logistics. He must help articulate a vision that connects government achievements with the everyday expectations of citizens.
This is where his national outlook becomes particularly relevant.
A successful campaign in 2027 cannot be framed as a contest between regions. It must be presented as a collective national project.
The Strategist Behind the Candidate
Every successful political leader requires trusted lieutenants capable of translating vision into execution.
President Tinubu himself has long been recognized as one of Nigeria’s most gifted political strategists. His appointment of Yari therefore carries additional significance.
Strategists recognize strategists.
The selection suggests confidence not only in Yari’s loyalty but also in his capacity to coordinate the enormous political machinery required for a nationwide presidential campaign. Tinubu’s official campaign council announcement places Yari at the center of a structure designed to deliver electoral success in January 2027.
In many respects, Yari’s role resembles that of renowned campaign architects who have shaped presidential victories elsewhere: mobilizing resources, harmonizing interests, maintaining discipline, inspiring confidence and ensuring that political momentum translates into electoral outcomes.
The Road to 2027
The road ahead will not be without challenges.
Every election presents uncertainties.
Opposition parties will organize, narratives will compete and voters will scrutinize records and promises.
Yet successful campaigns are not those that avoid challenges; they are those that anticipate them and prepare accordingly.
This is where Yari’s political experience becomes indispensable.
His understanding of party structures, his network of relationships, his grassroots credibility and his organizational competence provide the APC campaign with a significant strategic advantage.
The task before him is enormous, but so too is the opportunity.
Why His Appointment Matters
Political appointments are often judged by symbolism.
Some, however, are judged by their strategic value.
Abdulaziz Yari’s emergence as Director-General of the Tinubu-Shettima Campaign Council belongs to the latter category.
It reflects a recognition that elections are won through preparation, coordination, coalition-building and disciplined execution.
For supporters of the APC, his appointment signals seriousness of purpose.
For observers of Nigerian politics, it represents the elevation of a seasoned political operator whose career has been defined by resilience, organization and influence.
And for President Tinubu, it may ultimately prove to be one of the most consequential decisions of the 2027 campaign season.
If campaigns require architects, then Yari’s assignment is clear: to design, coordinate and deliver a political operation capable of transforming the APC’s electoral ambitions into another national victory.
Whether history ultimately remembers him as the master strategist behind a successful re-election bid remains to be seen.
But one thing is already evident: the choice of Abdulaziz Yari is not merely an appointment.
It is a statement of intent.
Abdullahi O Haruna Haruspice is a political commentator, editor, columnist and Event Compere

items.author: Rilwan Muhammad
items.content:
The Vice Chairman of Geidam Local Government Area of Yobe State, Abubakar Muhammad Nur, has alleged that soldiers of the Nigerian Army assaulted him while he was carrying out his official duties in the town on Friday.
Nur alleged that the soldiers beat him despite identifying himself as the Vice Chairman of the local government.
He said the incident occurred amid heightened security tensions in Geidam following an exchange of fire between security forces and suspected Boko Haram terrorists on the outskirts of the town.
“They have been assaulting people since they exchanged fire with Boko Haram terrorists,” Nur said in a message to reporters.
Troops kill 2 terrorists, recover 2 AK-47 rifles, motorcycles in Sokoto
Man rescued after jumping off bridge in Plateau
He alleged that soldiers had been beating residents indiscriminately, adding that no curfew had been officially announced in the state.
“As my Chairman is absent for other official engagements, by the constitution I am supposed to be the chief security officer in town,” he said.
Nur said he went out on Friday morning to assess the situation after noticing residents fleeing the town.
“I decided not to run because I am innocent and I was on my official duty,” he said.
According to him, soldiers from the 159 Battalion, Geidam, approached him and started beating him even after he identified himself as the Vice Chairman.
He alleged that one of the soldiers struck him on the forehead, causing heavy bleeding, while another hit his hand, leaving him with what he described as a serious injury.
Nur said he was receiving treatment at an emergency room when he sent the message to reporters.
He also shared photographs showing injuries to his forehead and other parts of his body.
Meanwhile, a resident of Geidam, Idris Abdullahi Baffa, told Daily Trust that residents had remained indoors for three days following restrictions imposed after the security incident.
According to him, a 24-hour curfew was imposed on the first day following intense gunshots and the use of tear gas in the area, with residents instructed to remain indoors for their safety.
He said the restriction was reduced to 20 hours on the second day, allowing residents to move around between 12pm and 3pm, although intermittent gunshots were still reported.
“We are still indoors and have not received any official notice or communication from the relevant authorities regarding the lifting or further relaxation of the curfew,” Baffa said.
He added that residents had continued to remain indoors for their safety pending further instructions from the authorities.
When contacted, the Acting Assistant Director, Public Relations Unit, Operation Hadin Kai Sector 2, Damaturu, Lt. A. Kandala, said he was not aware of the incident.
Kandala, however, promised to get back to our reporter after making enquiries but had not done so as of the time of filing this report.
Geidam has witnessed heightened security concerns over the past three days following an exchange of fire between security forces and suspected Boko Haram terrorists on the outskirts of the town.
The alleged assault occurred against the backdrop of the ongoing security operation, with residents expressing concerns over movement restrictions and the conduct of security personnel in the town.

items.author: Muhammad Bilal
items.content:
Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif has directed the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) to complete its reform measures within the stipulated timeframe and ensure third party audits to assess their transparency, effectiveness and sustainability.
The directives came during a weekly review meeting on FBR reforms held in Islamabad, where the prime minister was briefed on the restructuring of PRAL, digitalization of the tax system and measures to curb smuggling and tax evasion.
Shehbaz said reforms in the tax system were being implemented to support the country’s development and emphasized that digitalization, production monitoring and automated systems were key pillars of the FBR’s reform agenda. He welcomed the appointment process for goods elevators with good reputations in the FBR and commended the FBR chairman and his team for their efforts.
The prime minister also directed authorities to intensify action against tax evasion, smuggling and illegal businesses. He ordered officials to accelerate reforms aimed at modernizing the tax system, improving revenue collection and completely eliminating smuggling.
The meeting was informed that phased work is underway on IRIS 3.0, the new tax operating model and a central data hub to make the tax system more modern, integrated and data driven. International consultants have been engaged to design IRIS 3.0, while new senior leadership appointments have been made at PRAL in technology, data security, operations and tax related areas.
Officials said work is progressing on further improving the tax system under IRIS 3.0, including plans to pilot the auto tax concept and eventually use artificial intelligence and machine learning to improve tax collection.
The meeting was also briefed on the impact of faceless assessment in customs. Average revenue per goods declaration increased by 12 percent from January to June 2026, while the system also improved the identification and monitoring of irregularities in imports.
The recruitment process for 280 goods elevators is in its final stages as part of efforts to further integrate the customs assessment system. Work is also underway to establish the Central Assessment Unit in Islamabad, which is expected to become operational under interim arrangements by December 31, 2026. A fully integrated facility is planned for activation in a new complex by June 2027.
Digital invoicing has also recorded a sharp increase. Transactions worth Rs. 236 billion were processed through digital invoicing in July 2025, compared with more than Rs. 2.5 trillion in July 2026. The government has set a target of Rs. 4 trillion in digital invoicing transactions by December 2026.
On efforts to curb smuggling, officials said several measures have been completed to prevent the illegal movement of petroleum products. These include GIS tagging of all legal petrol pumps, GPS tracking of petroleum products, linking the enterprise resource planning systems of oil marketing companies with the tracking system and developing a central tracking app for law enforcement agencies.
Through the Rah e Raftar app, authorities have shut down 2,500 illegal petrol pumps and taken legal action against them. Work is also continuing on digital monitoring of petroleum product sales and other anti smuggling measures.
Shehbaz directed officials to complete all FBR reform measures within the stipulated timeframe and ensure independent third party audits. He called for faster implementation of reforms to modernize the tax system, strengthen revenue collection and eliminate smuggling.

items.author: Business Desk
items.content:
Pakistan’s capital-market regulators are moving toward a fully digital investor onboarding system, with the Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan (SECP) requiring market infrastructure to support API-based processing, instant issuance of investor identifiers and automated account integration.
Under the new framework issued through Circular No. 19 of 2026, the Centralized Know Your Customer Organization (CKO), Central Depository Company (CDC) and National Clearing Company of Pakistan Limited (NCCPL) will be connected with authorised market intermediaries to streamline the onboarding process.
The framework envisages onboarding on a 24/7 basis without manual or human intervention.
The system will enable API-based integration for instant issuance of Unique Identification Numbers (UINs), opening of CDC sub-accounts and integration with customers’ accounts.
This could significantly reduce the need for investors to repeatedly provide the same information to different market intermediaries.
The SECP has also allowed authorised intermediaries to rely on identity verification already carried out by scheduled banks, digital banks, microfinance banks and electronic money institutions regulated by the State Bank of Pakistan, subject to the prescribed requirements.
Similarly, where an IBAN has already been generated or verified by an authorised financial institution, the intermediary, CKO or Asaan Connect will not have to repeat the verification.
Certain mobile-number and email verification requirements can also be avoided where the information has already been verified through an authorised financial institution.
The regulator said the framework is designed around secure, encrypted and API-based data transmission to improve data accuracy, integrity, confidentiality and auditability while reducing manual processing.
A key component is the Centralized Gateway Portal (CGP), which will connect regulated intermediaries with the centralised onboarding infrastructure.
Intermediaries will be required to integrate their online account-opening portals with the CGP and regularly share and update information and documents relating to individual resident customers, subject to customer consent.
The CKO and CGP may then share the information with other authorised market intermediaries in accordance with joint procedures and with the customer’s consent.
The SECP has directed all relevant platforms and intermediaries to maintain confidentiality and implement adequate data-security measures.
The framework also expands the scope of digital onboarding, allowing customer relationships to be established remotely through websites, online portals, mobile applications and other approved digital channels.
Digital onboarding will be available for residents and non-residents, individuals and companies, as well as single and joint accounts.
Despite the increased reliance on automated verification, the SECP has retained responsibility for AML/CFT compliance with the regulated intermediaries.
They will remain responsible for ongoing monitoring, risk-based due diligence, sanctions screening and reporting of suspicious or currency transactions where applicable.
The new framework replaces the SECP’s earlier Circular No. 6 of 2023 and gives specified regulated intermediaries three months to update their account-opening forms and establish the required connectivity with the centralised digital platforms.

items.author: Anjali Jain
items.content:
Voice AI startup Gnani.ai has unveiled Artha, an end-to-end sovereign AI stack aimed at Indian enterprises and public institutions.
The platform was unveiled by India’s vice president CP Radhakrishnan in New Delhi today.
Artha combines two of Gnani.ai’s core offerings – Evon v3.3, a 30 Bn-parameter open weight model trained natively across 11 Indian languages, and Plexus, the startup’s agentic AI platform.
While Evon v3.3 provides the underlying language intelligence, Plexus enables organisations to build and deploy AI agents for specific workflows. Gnani.ai said the integrated stack will allow enterprises to use AI while retaining control over their data and technology infrastructure.
The weights for Evon v3.3 are available upon request on AI model repository Hugging Face under an Apache 2.0 licence. Model weights contain the patterns and relationships learned by an AI model during training and determine how it interprets inputs and generates responses.
Evon v3.3 is Gnani.ai’s first large language model launch, Gnani.ai cofounder and CEO Ganesh Gopalan told Inc42. The 30 Bn-parameter model has been trained on 2 Tn tokens, with a focus on reasoning and Indic-language performance.
The startup now plans to expand the model family with 70 Bn- and 100 Bn-parameter models, depending on the complexity of use cases. Moreover, Gnani.ai is also looking to expand the model’s language coverage from 11 to 22 languages in the near term.
Gopalan said that the 30 Bn-parameter model has been developed with Gnani.ai’s upcoming speech-to-speech technology in mind, where low-latency reasoning will be critical. The startup has not disclosed a timeline for the launch of its speech-to-speech model.
Nevertheless, it said that Evon v3.3 consumes around 40% fewer tokens for Indian-language workloads than comparable models, helping lower compute costs. Gopalan said the focus on efficiency is particularly important as Gnani looks to deploy its models in production rather than build them purely for benchmark performance.
According to Gnani.ai, Artha has been developed to address three challenges faced by Indian organisations adopting AI – data sovereignty, the cost of deploying AI at scale, and the ability to work effectively across Indian languages and real-world use cases.
Gopalan said Gnani.ai has started showing the model to select customers, with five of 20 enterprises that attended a recent customer meeting in Pune already expressing interest and beginning to build on top of Evon. Its potential use cases include underwriting, advertising and payments reconciliation, although these engagements are currently at the early stage and no deployments of Evon have gone live yet.
While some voice AI workflows are already largely autonomous, Gopalan said regulated use cases such as underwriting and payments reconciliation will initially retain humans in the loop. He expects more routine tasks, such as document and data matching during loan onboarding, to become increasingly autonomous.
Gnani’s Sovereign AI Pitch
The launch comes as the Indian government is pushing for development of indigenous foundational models to reduce the country’s dependence on foreign AI systems.
Gnani.ai was among the startups selected under the IndiaAI Mission in 2025 to develop homegrown foundational AI models. The startup was selected to build a multilingual, real-time voice AI foundational model with reasoning capabilities.
In December 2025, it launched Vachana STT, a speech-to-text (STT) model for Indian languages trained on more than 1 Mn hours of real-world voice data. The model was developed under the IndiaAI Mission and was part of the startup’s broader voice technology stack.
Founded in 2017 by Gopalan and Ananth Nagaraj, Bengaluru-based Gnani.ai offers voice AI products for enterprises. Its offerings include virtual assistants, tools that provide real-time guidance to customer service agents, and voice biometrics for fraud detection.
The startup caters to enterprises and government bodies, with its products used across sectors such as banking, insurance, healthcare, telecom, and government services.
Gnani.ai expects Evon and Plexus to contribute 20-30% of its business within the next year, even as its existing voice AI business continues to grow. Gopalan said the company is currently adding around 10–15 customers a month to its traditional voice business.
Earlier this year, Gnani.ai raised $10 Mn in a Series B round led by Aavishkaar Capital, with participation from existing investor Info Edge Ventures. It said the capital would be used to expand internationally, strengthen its agentic AI capabilities, develop multilingual and industry-specific products, and expand its engineering and product teams.

items.author: Reuters
items.content:
Iran condemned the United States' new economic sanctions on Friday as "state terrorism", while its supreme leader said he was banning acts that could harm "social cohesion" amid concern that more financial pain could spark unrest at home.
With the war now at the six-month mark, and negotiations at an impasse, President Donald Trump's administration has stepped up efforts to cripple Iran financially, with what it has billed an "economic D-Day".
The sanctions drive compounds the toll of the war on Iran's economy, where annual inflation hit 66% last month. The standoff over the Strait of Hormuz remains the conflict's biggest unresolved flashpoint.
Washington has warned countries to cut their business ties with Iran or face secondary sanctions, though the Treasury Department stopped short of actually imposing penalties.
Iran's Foreign Ministry said in a statement on Friday that all countries were obligated under international law to refrain from implementing US sanctions against Tehran, adding that participation in them amounted to complicity in imposing one state's unlawful will on independent states.
It branded the new US measures a "crime against humanity" that put the health and livelihood of millions of civilians at serious risk, and called on other nations and United Nations bodies to uphold the rule of law.
Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei, who was injured and has not been seen publicly since the February 28 attack that killed his father, said in a written statement on Friday that he had banned officials from "committing anything that harms social cohesion".
He urged authorities to avoid any "discouraging statements that weaken national and public motivation," amid concern among Iran's leaders that more financial pressure on its war-battered economy could trigger protests.
Khamenei urged the government to seriously address economic and livelihood challenges, including inflation, unemployment, prices and the management of markets for goods and services.
 
New measures target Egyptian Bank
Later on Friday, a US official told Reuters the Trump administration plans to impose limits on Egypt's Banque Misr United Arab Emirates branches for doing business with Tehran.
The official said the proposed rule, if finalised, would withdraw Banque Misr UAE's ability to process transactions through US financial institutions.
Treasury officials separately issued sanctions targeting one entity based in Hong Kong and one person linked to Iran's Bank Melli, according to a notice posted on the department's website.
With the US focused on its economic pressure campaign, others have sought to revive diplomatic efforts to end the war.
Mediators have pushed to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, which handled 20% of world oil supplies before the war began six months ago and whose status remains the biggest obstacle to a peace deal.
Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani said he had stressed during talks with Iranian leaders in Tehran on Thursday the importance of returning to the pre-war status of open shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.
 
'Pressure doesn't work,' Iran tells US
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi on Friday described the talks with Al Thani as "creative", and he renewed his appeal to the US to stop putting military and economic pressure on his country and to resume negotiations.
"Putting diplomacy back on track isn't impossible. It hinges on US understanding of one simple fact: pressure doesn't work," Araqchi said on X.
Qatar, a US ally, and Pakistan helped broker a memorandum of understanding in June that led to a ceasefire but that quickly unravelled due to disagreements between Iran and the US over the Strait of Hormuz.
 
Iranian leverage
After the US and Israel launched the war on February 28, Iran threatened to strike any vessel transiting the strait without its authorisation, driving down traffic and sending up the price of oil.
The US insists that the strait remain an open international waterway.
Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, said on Thursday Iran was preparing a list of conditions for reopening the strait. In the past Iran's conditions have included an end to the US blockade on Iranian ports, compensation and removal of sanctions.
US military commanders say American forces have cleared sea mines from the strait that had been laid months ago by Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.
Trump has repeatedly said the strait is open, but many vessels have opted against sailing through it because of Iranian threats, and ship tracking services have estimated activity at roughly 5% to 15% of normal volumes.
Preliminary shipping data released on Friday showed that only seven commodity vessels had transited the Strait of Hormuz on Thursday, down from 17 a day earlier and below the 10-day average of 15.
However, oil prices fell on Friday and were on track for a weekly drop, amid what analysts said were signs that more oil was flowing through the strait despite the diplomatic stalemate and that producers were increasingly adapting to the new realities in the Gulf region.

items.author: Naeem Asghar
items.content:
The Senate and the National Assembly on Friday moved to establish a special committee to investigate the PIMS nursery fire that killed 14 newborns, with lawmakers across party lines demanding accountability, public disclosure of findings and concrete reforms to prevent similar tragedies.
Both houses separately debated the incident and approved motions for a parliamentary investigation. The proposed committee will include representation from all political parties and examine the causes of the fire, emergency response, fire-safety and measures needed to prevent such incidents in the future.
In the Senate, PPP parliamentary leader Senator Sherry Rehman moved a resolution seeking a house committee to investigate the tragedy, which was approved. Senator Manzoor Kakar said the Senate chairman and National Assembly Speaker would jointly constitute the parliamentary committee.
The Senate debate saw opposition lawmakers strongly criticise the government and demand action against those responsible. Senator Rehman called for measures to ensure that such incidents did not recur and questioned PIMS's capacity to provide healthcare.
Challenging the PIMS executive director's claim that ward gates were not closed when the fire broke out, she said firefighters had reported that doors were closed and demanded examination of exit gates, reports of locked gates and other fire-safety arrangements.
PTI Senator Falak Naz Chitrali severely criticised Health Minister Syed Mustafa Kamal and claimed that the bodies of newborns had been handed to parents in shopping bags and that families were told not to speak about the matter and leave.
Senator Sadia Abbasi said she had been a member of the board that appointed the PIMS executive director and had strongly opposed the appointment. She alleged that the bureaucracy had supported the appointment and described the executive director as a highly influential official.
Senator Khurram Zeeshan called for the resignation of the entire federal cabinet and questioned why the the prime minister had not visited PIMS despite being in Islamabad. Senator Abdul Qadir said PIMS had no alarm system when the fire broke out and demanded strict punishment for those responsible.
Senator Shahadat Awan said responsibility for hospital administration rested with the executive director and alleged that the ward's emergency exit had been locked. "There was no alternative route. That is why the windows were broken," he said, holding the PIMS administration responsible.
PTI Senator Mashal Azam said the government was responsible for the deaths. Senator Zarqa Suharwardy Taimur said the healthcare system had failed because no one was held accountable. Opposition Leader Allama Raja Nasir Abbas demanded immediate removal of the PIMS executive director.
Responding to the criticism, Health Minister Mustafa Kamal described the tragedy as horrific and said there could be no justification for what had happened. He said he had offered himself for accountability and welcomed the formation of a parliamentary committee.
"Form a parliamentary committee, but do not impose a time limit on it," he told the house. He assured the house that anyone found responsible for the PIMS tragedy would not be spared. Kamal said that the country's healthcare system was "rotted" and required comprehensive reform.
Kamal said political parties represented in the Senate were also governing different provinces, making healthcare improvement a collective responsibility. He offered to present a detailed account of his ministry's performance before the house.
In the National Assembly, Law Minister Tarar moved the motion, saying the speaker, in consultation with the Senate chairman, would constitute the committee. He said the speaker should be authorised to formulate or amend its terms of reference and revise its composition when necessary.
Tarar said the government would treat the tragedy as a "test case" and ensure that necessary action was taken after completion of the ongoing inquiry. He said Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif had already constituted two separate committees after the incident, with clearly different mandates.
The first committee, headed by a former senior government official, was specifically investigating the PIMS fire and did not include any PIMS or Health Ministry official, Tarar said, adding that this arrangement was intended to ensure an impartial inquiry.
The second committee, headed by Dr Azhar Kayani, was tasked with examining the future administration, improvement and provision of healthcare facilities at PIMS. It has been directed to submit a working paper within 30 days proposing measures to improve the hospital.
Tarar said the second committee included experts from different fields, including a doctor, retired civil servant and lawyer, who would assess the hospital's future requirements. "We have determined to treat this as a test case," he said, stressing that the matter would be pursued to its logical conclusion.
The both the houses passed the respective motions. Chairing the Senate session, Manzoor Kakar announced that the Senate chairman and National Assembly speaker would jointly constitute the parliamentary committee. Later both the houses were prorogued sine die.
(WITH INPUT FROM APP)

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar on Friday warned India that any attempt to deprive Pakistan of waters allocated under the Indus Waters Treaty (IWT) could have "profound consequences" for regional peace and security, while calling for the decades-old agreement to be respected and implemented.
Addressing a virtual seminar in Washington on "The Indus Waters Treaty: South Asian Security at the Crossroads", Dar said the 1960 treaty remained "valid, binding and fully operative" despite India's unilateral decision in April 2025 to place its obligations under the agreement in abeyance.
The foreign minister said the treaty had survived wars, military crises, diplomatic breakdowns and prolonged political tensions for more than six decades because both countries recognised that water on which hundreds of millions depended was too fundamental to be subjected to political fluctuations.
Dar said Pakistan had consistently sought to resolve differences through dialogue, diplomacy and mechanisms provided under the treaty. He pointed to continuing treaty-based proceedings concerning Indian hydroelectric projects, particularly Kishenganga and Ratle, as evidence that the agreed legal framework remained relevant.
The deputy prime minister stressed that approaching the Permanent Indus Commission, a neutral expert or the Court of Arbitration was not an act of confrontation but implementation of mechanisms agreed by both countries.
Separately, speaking in London at the conclusion of his August 24-28 visit, Dar said British officials had praised Pakistan's mediation efforts between the United States and Iran during his visit to the UK, particularly the leadership of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Army Chief Field Marshal Asim Munir.
Dar described the trip as "extremely useful" and said that he had held comprehensive talks with British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband on bilateral relations and counter-terrorism cooperation. He added his discussions with Commonwealth Secretary-General Shirley Ayorkor Botchwey focused on reforms and youth initiatives, while he also highlighted Pakistan's vulnerability to climate change.
Dar said he had held detailed meetings over 10 Pakistani nationals held hostage aboard the MT Honour 25 by Somali pirates, stressing that international maritime rules prohibited ransom payments because they could encourage piracy.
On the economy, Dar said Pakistan had moved beyond concerns over default, with inflation now in single digits and policy rates having almost halved. He said the government's focus was now on economic growth, development and raising per-capita income.
He also held telephone conversations with Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan and Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan on regional developments and preparations for an upcoming meeting of Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, Turkiye and Egypt.
Dar said Pakistan would continue pursuing engagement, diplomacy and peaceful settlement, presenting the country's diplomatic approach as one centred on stability and cooperation in both South Asia and the wider region.

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Friday said that the recently signed Makkah Joint Defence Agreement between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye brought the three countries even closer together and sent a message of unity and peace throughout the region.
The prime minister, in a meeting with Minister of Environment, Water and Agriculture of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia Engineer Abdulrahman bin Abdulmohsen Al-Fadley, who called on him here, reaffirmed the deep-rooted and fraternal ties between Pakistan and Saudi Arabia and conveyed his warmest regards for the Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques King Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, and Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud.
While welcoming the Saudi dignitary, he underscored that as strategic partners, both Pakistan and the kingdom must now focus their energies towards deepening economic and agriculture ties to translate their longstanding relationship into a stronger, mutually beneficial trade and investment partnership.
He expressed satisfaction at the constructive engagement between the two sides, particularly with regards to export of agricultural products by Pakistan to the Kingdom.
Both sides also exchanged views on enhancing agricultural productivity in Pakistan, through the use of technology, research and development and more efficient use of water resources.
Prime Minister Shehbaz announced that a delegation of agricultural experts from Pakistan would soon visit Riyadh to carry forward these discussions with a view to realize the full potential of this partnership.
The Saudi minister thanked the prime minister for the warm hospitality extended to him and his delegation and reaffirmed the Kingdom's commitment to deepening cooperation with Pakistan across the agriculture, water and food security sectors.
The meeting was attended by a number of federal ministers including Rana Tanveer Hussain, Mohammad Aurangzeb, Atta Tarar, Jam Kamal Khan, Dr. Musadik Malik, Junaid Anwar Chaudhry, Dr. Syed Tauqir Shah, and Bilal Azhar Kiyani, SAPM Tariq Fatemi, and senior government officials.
 
Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir
Minister of Environment, Water and Agriculture of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia Eng. Abdulrahman Abdulmohsen AlFadley called on Chief of Army Staff (COAS) and Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir, NI (M), HJ here on Friday at General Headquarters (GHQ).
During the meeting, matters of mutual interest were discussed, said a news release issued by Inter Services Public Relations (ISPR).
The COAS highlighted the deep-rooted brotherly relations between Pakistan and Kingdom of Saudi Arabia and reaffirmed Pakistan's commitment to further strengthening the longstanding strategic partnership between the two brotherly countries, it further said.

items.author: Hasnaat Malik
items.content:
The Federal Constitutional Court (FCC) has ruled that the power to do complete justice under Article 187 of the Constitution must be exercised within the framework of the Constitution and the law and cannot be used to defeat legislative intent or override mandatory statutory requirements.
A three-member bench headed by FCC Chief Justice Amin-ud-Din Khan gave the ruling in a case concerning the entitlement of landowners to enhanced compensation awarded to other landowners under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.
The judgment addressed the question of whether a landowner who neither sought a reference under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act nor challenged the collector's award within the prescribed period could subsequently claim enhanced compensation granted to other landowners through constitutional jurisdiction, execution proceedings or any other collateral proceedings before superior courts.
"Article 187 empowers the court to pass such decree or make such order as may be necessary for doing complete justice in any matter pending before it," the judgment said.
"Nevertheless, the jurisdiction conferred by Article 187 is supplementary and procedural in nature; it does not authorize the court to create substantive rights or disregard mandatory statutory provisions."
The 44-page judgment noted that Article 187 empowers both the Supreme Court and the FCC to do complete justice. The court stated that land acquisition is the legal process through which the state compulsorily acquires private land for a public purpose in return for compensation.
In Pakistan's legal framework, it said, land acquisition represents the statutory expression of the doctrine of eminent domain—the sovereign prerogative of the state to appropriate private property for the greater public good subject to conditions imposed by law.
The judgment noted that land acquisition in Pakistan is primarily governed by the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, enacted during British colonial rule on February 2, 1894, and continuing to operate subject to provincial amendments.
The FCC ruled against the adjudication of matters relating to land acquisition by constitutional courts, particularly high courts, where statutory remedies and limitations apply.
The court observed that Article 175 of the Constitution envisages an independent judiciary exercising judicial authority within limits prescribed by the Constitution and the law.
"The legitimacy and strength of judicial power emanate not from its ability to mould legislation according to perceived notions of equity but from its fidelity to the statutory text," the judgment said.
"Once a court departs from the language employed by the legislature and engrafts into a statute a remedy which the legislature has not provided, it ceases to interpret the law and instead assumes the legislative function, thereby disturbing the constitutional equilibrium among the state organs," it added.
The judgment further held that judicial sympathy could not override a statutory command, particularly where doing so would introduce into the law a remedy that Parliament had deliberately omitted.
"We are convinced that the enhanced compensation awarded in proceedings under Section 18 should not automatically extend to persons who neither sought a reference nor remained parties to the proceedings," the court ruled.
It said recognising such a right would require the court to supply a casus omissus—an omission in legislation—and enlarge the statutory remedy beyond the legislative text.
Such an approach, the court observed, would amount to assuming a legislative function and would be expressly inconsistent with the constitutional doctrine of separation of powers.
It stressed that judicial decisions must ultimately rest on constitutional and statutory authority rather than sympathy or perceived hardship.
"Compassion, however commendable, cannot furnish an independent source of legal power," the judgment said, adding that courts were constitutionally bound to administer justice according to law rather than personal notions of fairness.
The court referred to the maxim that "hard cases make bad law", observing that equitable considerations must remain subordinate to the rule of law.
It said the plight of landowners might evoke sympathy, but such sympathy could not justify creation of substantive rights that the legislature had not recognised.
The judgment further emphasised the constitutional separation between legislative and judicial functions. "While courts are entrusted with the interpretation and application of law, they are not authorized to legislate under the guise of interpretation," it said.
Referring to the maxim Judicis est jus dicere, non-dare, the court said it was the function of a judge to declare the law, not to make it. It also cited A verbis legis non est recedendum, under which courts should not depart from the plain language employed by the legislature.
The court held that judicial interpretation must therefore remain faithful to statutory text rather than substitute judicial notions of fairness for legislative policy.
It cautioned courts against adopting an interpretation which, in the guise of achieving parity, effectively rewrote the legislative framework enacted by Parliament.
"Constitutional guarantees of equality cannot be employed to nullify statutory conditions expressly attached to the exercise of a legal right," the judgment said.
The court held that the right to seek enhanced compensation was not an inherent or continuing right but a statutory right regulated by Sections 18 and 31 of the Land Acquisition Act.
"Once those conditions cease to exist, the right itself stands exhausted," it ruled.
According to the judgment, the act envisages two categories of landowners: those who challenge the award under Section 18 after receiving compensation under protest or without accepting the award, and those who accept the award without protest, in whose case the matter attains finality.
The statute does not contemplate a third category comprising landowners who accept an award but later seek enhanced compensation merely because another landowner successfully pursued the statutory remedy, the court held.
"Recognition of such a category would amount to judicial legislation and would defeat the carefully balanced scheme enacted by Parliament," the judgment concluded.

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
The parliamentary set-up of the newly elected Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) Legislative Assembly was completed on Friday with Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N)-backed Barrister Syed Iftikhar Ali Gillani taking the oath as the 17th prime minister and Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) leader Chaudhry Muhammad Yasin being appointed Leader of the Opposition.
The oath was administered to Gillani by AJK Acting President Chaudhry Tariq Farooq during a televised ceremony held at the AJK Legislative Assembly in Muzaffarabad.
In his maiden speech as premier, the newly elected AJK prime minister thanked PML-N supremo Nawaz Sharif, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz, Rana Sanaullah and other senior party leaders for their support.
"I will work hard round the clock to ensure that I maintain the confidence of the party leadership and the people in our government," he said.
The premier also called on the people of AJK, particularly fellow lawmakers elected to the lower house, to join him in his efforts to take the region forward. "Let us move forward together and build an AJK that is exemplary to the whole world," he said.
Addressing the ceremony, the premier said his government would make provision of livelihood opportunities its top priority. "This will enable the youth to achieve a better future," he said, adding that livelihood was closely linked to access to education, healthcare and other essential amenities.
Noting that it was impossible to give government jobs to all Kashmiris, he said there was a need to rely on technology to create jobs and livelihood. "AJK will digitalise the economy," Gillani stressed, acknowledging a need to widen internet access across the valley.
While announcing reforms in the health and education sector, he said his government will launch a citizen portal for complaint registration as the first step towards resolution of issues.
During his speech, PM Gillani said, "Pakistan and Kashmir are incomplete without each other."
He emphasised that the Kashmir issue was not just a dispute over a piece of land. "It is an issue concerning the rights of the people of Kashmir and their right to self-determination in line with the United Nations resolutions"
The AJK premier also condemned India's August 5, 2019, action and the atrocities committed against Kashmiris in his first address to the legislative assembly members. In contrast, he said, Kashmiris in AJK sleep peacefully because of the sacrifices made by the Pakistan Armed Forces under the leadership of Field Marshal Asim Munir.
The newly elected premier also said he wished to replicate the progress of Punjab under the leadership of Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz in AJK.
Meanwhile, the assembly speaker, Chaudhry Tariq Farooq, formally notified Yasin's appointment as Leader of the Opposition.
Yasin previously served as Leader of the Opposition in the AJK Legislative Assembly from 2016 to 2021.
A veteran politician, Yasin has remained active in practical politics for more than three decades and is considered one of the senior PPP figures in AJK.
Separately, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Friday congratulated Barrister Iftikhar Gillani on his election as the prime minister of AJK, expressing hope that he would play an active role in the development and prosperity of the region.
According to a statement issued by the Prime Minister's Office, the prime minister said the PML-N victory in AJK was the result of the efforts of the party leadership, particularly former prime minister and party leader Nawaz Sharif, alongside party workers.
PM Shehbaz expressed confidence that the newly elected AJK premier would work vigorously for the development of the region and the welfare of its people.
He reaffirmed that the federal government would continue to extend all possible cooperation to AJK for its development and prosperity and for improving the living standards of its people.
The prime minister also welcomed the continuation of the democratic process in AJK, describing it as a positive development.
Acting President of Pakistan Sardar Ayaz Sadiq also congratulated Barrister Gillani on his successful election as the prime minister.
In a statement issued by his office, Sadiq wished the newly appointed premier the best for his tenure, saying that Gilani's election reflected the confidence reposed in his leadership abilities by members of the AJK Legislative Assembly.
Resting hope in the political insight and leadership of Barrister Gillani, the acting president said he would steer AJK towards greater development, prosperity and public welfare.
He reaffirmed that the federal government would extend its full support and cooperation for the "development and prosperity" of Azad Jammu and Kashmir.
"Welfare and well-being of the people of AJK remains a priority for the federal government," Sadiq said.
