items.author: Akinbayo Wahab
items.content:
The Police Command in Niger has arrested five suspects for alleged criminal conspiracy and armed robbery.
Police Public Relations Officer (PPRO) of the command, SP Wasiu Abiodun, said the command also recovered a Beretta pistol and two rounds of live ammunition from one of the suspects.
He disclosed this in a statement issued on Tuesday in Minna.
He said that on Aug. 11, at about 6.00 a.m., the Tudun-Wada Division received a report that armed robbers had invaded Sauka-Kahuta and carted away laptops.
He said the robbers also stole handsets, motorcycles and other valuables during the attack.
The PPRO said division operatives visited the scene after receiving the report, recovered some exhibits, and commenced the investigation.
Abiodun said the investigation led to the arrest of the gang leader, a 25-year-old man from Maitumbi area, on Aug. 17, behind the U.K. Bello Theatre Centre.
Abiodun said the suspect led detectives to arrest other members of the syndicate.
He said the other suspects included three men aged 27, 35 and 28, who were arrested at different locations in Niger and Nasarawa states.
Abiodun said the four suspects confessed to committing armed robbery around Mandela, Sauka-Kahuta, Barkin-Sale, Farm Centre and Highpoint areas of Minna.
He said the suspects also disclosed that a 50-year-old man from Maitumbi area kept their firearm.
“Police moved to the location on Aug. 19, arrested the man and recovered a Beretta pistol with two rounds of live ammunition in his possession,” the PPRO said.
Abiodun said further investigation revealed that the suspects usually sold the stolen items to a receiver identified as Ahmed, also known as Genuine, of Maitumbi area.
He said all the suspects were under investigation at the State Criminal Investigation Department (SCID), Minna.
He added that efforts to arrest Ahmed, the alleged receiver, were ongoing.

items.summary:
Motorists and travellers using the Benin-Agbor-Asaba route have been stranded for days as severe traffic congestion continues to disrupt movement between the South-South, South-East and Lagos.
The gridlock, which has reportedly persisted for about five days, has left motorists spending long hours on the road, with some travellers unable to reach their destinations.
The situation has been attributed largely to the poor condition of sections of the road, which has been further worsened by heavy rainfall in the area.

items.author: Haruna Gimba Yaya
items.content:
The United Nations Industrial Development Organization (UNIDO), with funding from the European Union (EU), has organised a capacity building workshop for local stakeholders to use small hydropower for Nigerian farming, in effort to bring clean power to rural farms and grow the local food industry.
The one-day workshop held Monday in Gombe, featured the Balanga Dam Small Hydropower Project (SHP) in the state as a case study, bringing together stakeholders from the public and private sectors in the renewable energy space.
Speaking at the opening of the workshop on Monday, UNIDO’s Representative and Sub-regional Director, Ambassador Philbert Johnson, said it aimed to raise awareness of the viability of SHP as a reliable means of generating electricity and driving economic growth, while promoting the exchange of experiences and knowledge in SHP project development.
He highlighted Nigeria’s significant renewable energy potential, including hydropower, wind, solar and biomass.
“Among these renewable energy sources, SHP holds great potential towards providing access to electricity and addressing climate change,” he said.
Amb. Johnson noted that recent government estimates place Nigeria’s total hydropower potential at approximately 24,000 MW, of which small hydropower accounts for about 3,500 MW.
He, therefore, stressed the need to develop effective strategies that bridge existing gaps and incorporate international best practices.
“The project is being implemented by UNIDO in collaboration with the Federal Ministry of Power, the Federal Ministry of Water Resources and Sanitation, Rural Electrification Agency as well as key States where the power plants will be located, such as Gombe,” he added.
The UNIDO representative stressed that the workshop focused on raising awareness among policy makers, project developers and financial institutions on the viability of small hydropower as an effective means of generating electricity and enhancing economic development.
Amb. Johnson explained that the choice of this event in Gombe state clearly highlights the commitment of Gombe state to advancing clean technologies to generate energy that will boost economic development for residents of the state.
“The Balanga Dam Small Hydropower Project is more than a mere energy infrastructure initiative. It provides us with a hands-on opportunity to examine how our water resources can be optimally harnessed to support economic transformation, improve livelihoods and strengthen energy security,” he said.
In his remarks, the Deputy Governor of Gombe State, Dr Manassah Daniel Jatau, commended the EU delegation, UNIDO, the Global Environment Facility and the Rural Electrification Agency for their generous contributions, “without which this vital Project would not have been possible.”
He said the Balanga Dam Small Hydropower Project is extremely strategic to the state, adding that beyond generating clean electricity, “it supports irrigation, water supply, flood control, and livelihoods for our people.”
Dr. Jatau expressed the continued commitment of the state government to the successful completion of the project.
“We will provide the enabling environment for the speedy completion of the Balanga Small Hydro Project (SHP) as well as the agro-processing cluster which will serve as the primary off taker of the electricity generated.
“We will integrate SHP development into our rural electrification and irrigation master plan. We will ensure community ownership so that the project is protected, sustained, and delivers benefits to the host communities,” he added.

items.summary:
Residents of Romi village in Dawakin Tofa Local Government Area of Kano State have called for the reconstruction of a collapsed bridge linking the community to the local government headquarters, as well as the rehabilitation of the 6.7-kilometre road connecting them to the area.
The residents, who said they had endured years of hardship due to the deplorable condition of the infrastructure, also threatened to boycott the forthcoming elections if the bridge, which has remained unreconstructed for nearly three decades, is not rebuilt.
Our reporter, who recently visited the community, reports that the bridge linking Romi village with Dawakin Tofa Local Government headquarters was initially constructed through a self-help initiative and later completed by the local government council in 1995.
The road serves as a strategic link for residents of nearly 20 communities, including Kwa, Dungurawa, Bumburawa, Babbar Ruga and Cedi Babbar Ruga, among others.

Residents of Romi village in Dawakin Tofa Local Government Area of Kano State have called for the reconstruction of a collapsed bridge linking the community to the local government headquarters, as well as the rehabilitation of the 6.7-kilometre road connecting them to the area.
The residents, who said they had endured years of hardship due to the deplorable condition of the infrastructure, also threatened to boycott the forthcoming elections if the bridge, which has remained unreconstructed for nearly three decades, is not rebuilt.
Our reporter, who recently visited the community, reports that the bridge linking Romi village with Dawakin Tofa Local Government headquarters was initially constructed through a self-help initiative and later completed by the local government council in 1995.
The road serves as a strategic link for residents of nearly 20 communities, including Kwa, Dungurawa, Bumburawa, Babbar Ruga and Cedi Babbar Ruga, among others.

However, commuters continue to face serious difficulties using the route, which terminates at Government Science Secondary School, Dawakin Tofa.
A community leader, Isa Adamu Abdullahi, said the bridge had not been reconstructed since it collapsed in 1996.
“As it is we heavily rely on motorcycle and bicycle to reach Dawakin Tofa town where all our critical needs like hospital, school and market as well as other social activities are there. You know how difficult it is to go there by bicycle,” Abdullahi said.
For Magaji Hussain, a commuter, the prolonged neglect has become unacceptable, saying he would not vote in the forthcoming elections unless the bridge is rebuilt.
” As you can see we are heading to Dawaki from Bambarawa.From Gangaren Dutse, Kwa to Romi, Malunfashi, Bamburawa,Katoge and Kashirmo- all are linked by this road. But honestly, we are facing difficulty on this road, especially whenever it rains. Once it is dark people, do not travel for fear of being robbed.
“We are not saying no to elections but this road is our vote. If it is fixed, we will vote and support polio vaccination as well as all government programmes,” Hussain said.
Another resident, Junaidi Danladi, said the poor condition of the road has also exposed commuters to attacks by motorcycle thieves, with some incidents allegedly resulting in loss of lives.
Despite the challenges, Ahmad Isa, the APC Secretary of Romi Ward, said residents remain hopeful that the bridge would eventually be reconstructed and the road rehabilitated.
He expressed optimism that the long-standing infrastructure problems affecting the community would be addressed.

items.author: Business Desk
items.content:
The Capital Development Authority (CDA) has issued a final show-cause notice to M/s Yar Muhammad Scheme in Bani Gala, Islamabad, over alleged unauthorized development.
CDA has ordered an immediate halt to all unapproved construction, land development, marketing, plot transfers and property allotments in the scheme.
According to the notice, the scheme was developed without the mandatory approval of its Layout Plan (LOP) and No Objection Certificate (NOC) from the CDA, in violation of applicable planning laws and regulations.
The authority said several warnings and public notices issued between 2016 and 2025 were not followed.
The developers have been given seven days to remove illegal structures, stop unauthorized land use and submit a written explanation.
Failure to comply will allow the CDA to begin ex parte proceedings and take enforcement action, including demolition of unauthorized structures and sealing of project offices. The cost of demolition and restoration will be recovered from those responsible.
CDA also cited Supreme Court and Islamabad High Court rulings supporting action against unauthorized developments in Bani Gala.
The notice has been shared with the ICT Administration, Islamabad Police, IESCO, SNGPL, SECP and PID. Utility providers have been directed to withhold connections to unauthorized structures, while relevant authorities have been asked to stop promotional and marketing activities related to the scheme.

items.content:
The Deputy President of the Senate, Senator Barau I. Jibrin, has felicitated Muslims across Nigeria and beyond on the occasion of Eid-El-Maulud 1448 AH, commemorating the birth of the noble Prophet Muhammad (Peace Be Upon Him).
In a message to the Muslim Ummah through his Special Adviser on Media and Publicity, Alhaji Ismail Mudashir, Senator Barau urged Muslims to use the occasion to reflect on the exemplary life, teachings and virtues of the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH), particularly his lessons of compassion, patience, justice, honesty, forgiveness and peaceful coexistence.
He said the best way to honour the Prophet is to emulate his noble character and apply his teachings in their daily lives, families, communities and responsibilities as citizens.
Senator Barau, who is the First Deputy Speaker of the ECOWAS Parliament, urged Muslims and other Nigerians to intensify prayers for the country, particularly for lasting peace, security, unity and progress.
According to him, the challenges confronting the country require collective prayers, patriotism and commitment from all Nigerians.
As the country approaches the 2027 general elections, the Deputy President of the Senate appealed to political leaders, supporters and citizens to place the interest of Nigeria above partisan considerations.
He urged all political actors to conduct their activities with decorum and respect for democratic values, while avoiding hate speech, violence, misinformation and other actions capable of threatening the peace and unity of the Nation.
“Let us draw inspiration from the life and teachings of the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH), particularly his emphasis on peace, justice, patience and brotherhood. As we approach the 2027 elections, we must ensure that our political differences do not divide us as a people or undermine the peace of our dear country, the Federal Republic of Nigeria,” he said.

items.title: 9,000-year-old arrowheads covered in strange markings leave archaeologists puzzled
items.summary: Unearthed from the depths of Turkey, ancient arrowheads reveal enigmatic hand-carved symbols. These Neolithic treasures showcase intentional incisions rather than random scratches, prompting researchers to ponder their origins. Despite thorough investigations, the specific purpose behind these markings remains unknown. Observations indicate that this intriguing practice was limited to select communities, leaving archaeologists grappling with unanswered questions about their significance.

items.author: Usama Iqbal
items.content:
ISLAMABAD
The Senate Standing Committee on Commerce, chaired by Senator Anusha Rahman on Tuesday, held a detailed briefing on Pakistan's missing commercial presence in China, last fiscal year's trade performance, export growth, foreign direct investment, special economic zones and rising business costs.
The meeting was attended by Commerce Minister Jam Kamal Khan, the Secretary Commerce, the Chairman of the Trade Development Authority of Pakistan (TDAP), and other relevant officials.
A special briefing was presented on the establishment of a Pakistan Chamber of Commerce office in China. The secretary commerce informed the committee that a foreign chamber in China can be set up either as a joint chamber or as a branch. However, no Pakistani joint chamber is currently registered in China, nor is any Pakistani trade representative organisation registered there.
Officials stated that, legally, a joint chamber of commerce can be established in China, and Pakistan can also set up a representative foreign chamber. A joint chamber requires at least 50 members each from Pakistan and China, along with a minimum operational fund of 100,000 Chinese yuan. According to the Secretary commerce, an application for establishing a joint chamber in China would be submitted by the Pakistani ambassador. Pakistan's private sector can set up a chamber in Beijing or Shanghai, provided Chinese laws and conditions are met.
Rehman questioned why a Pakistani chamber or trade representative office has not yet been established in China. In response, the Secretary Commerce said that trade organisations themselves would be better placed to answer this.
Rehman emphasised that a joint chamber is essential for promoting bilateral trade with China. She noted that while many Pakistanis are doing business in China, no chamber or representative office has been set up, which creates difficulties in follow-ups for Pakistani companies.
She added that various Chinese chambers operate in Pakistan, and Chinese nationals are also engaged in business here individually in large numbers. Given China's size, she stressed the need to examine how the business credentials of individuals entering Pakistan are verified. She reiterated that Pakistan's business community should have its own chamber in China to further strengthen trade and business ties between the two countries.
The secretary commerce said the Ministry of Commerce would provide full support to any chamber interested in establishing a joint chamber or representative office in China, though the requirements for the two differ. He added that input should also be sought from the Federation of Pakistan Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FPCCI) and other relevant chambers.
On exports, the Chairman of TDAP briefed the committee on last fiscal year's trade performance. The TDAP chief executive said that while the authority is often blamed for stagnant exports, export performance depends on multiple factors beyond TDAP, including production costs, electricity prices and financing costs.
Senator Aamir Waliuddin Chishti asked what steps TDAP is taking to increase exports, noting that Pakistan has rarely attracted more than $2 billion in foreign direct investment, which also hampers export growth. He said government policies play a key role in attracting investment.
Khan informed the committee that numerous recommendations are submitted to the government for policy improvements. He said the prime minister has been advised to work on reciprocal incentives to boost exports. According to the minister, the Ministry of Commerce is working on new proposals to improve global marketing and increase exports, adding that maintaining high product quality and competitive pricing is essential.
Regarding special economic zones, Rehman asked about the challenges they face. Khan said there is ample space in these zones, but the main issues are electricity, taxation and financing. He added that the International Monetary Fund (IMF) programme has constrained the government, while energy costs, taxes and financing remain major challenges for businesses.
The committee emphasised the need for practical steps to increase exports, promote foreign investment, reduce the cost of doing business, and improve access for Pakistani products in global markets, including China. It also stressed the importance of advancing the establishment of a joint chamber or representative office in China to provide Pakistani companies with an effective platform for business linkages, marketing and trade follow-up.

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
The Pakistan Association of Automotive Parts & Accessories Manufacturers (PAAPAM) has appealed directly to Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and senior cabinet members to retain safeguards against the misuse of used-car import schemes as the government finalises the Auto Policy 2026-31.
In a letter to the prime minister, the finance minister, the minister for industries and production, and other relevant authorities, PAAPAM Chairman Usman Aslam Malik warned that dropping the proposed one-year mandatory non-transfer condition on vehicles imported under overseas facilitation schemes would inflict serious damage on the domestic automotive sector and undo recent gains in documenting the national economy. According to the association, roughly 1.8 million jobs tied to local auto-parts manufacturing are at stake if imports go unregulated. Every used car brought in from abroad displaces close to Rs1.5 million worth of locally manufactured components, PAAPAM said, directly squeezing domestic production capacity.
The scale of the trade has grown substantially. Annual used-car imports reached an estimated 50,000 units last year, capturing nearly 30% of the domestic market, according to PAAPAM figures. The association estimates the informal trade surrounding these imports has fuelled a black-money ecosystem worth approximately Rs200 billion, with the potential to divert overseas remittances away from formal banking channels and back into informal hundi and hawala networks.
PAAPAM also pointed to compounding pressure from tariff policy. Under the National Tariff Policy 2025-30, duties on used-car imports are being gradually reduced, from a 40% premium over new vehicles in the current fiscal year down to zero by FY30. That reduction, combined with a cut in customs duty to 30% on new completely-built-up vehicles of 850cc or below announced in the 2026-27 budget, and depreciation allowances of up to 36%, is making imported used cars increasingly attractive to commercial traders, the association said.
Malik cautioned that scrapping the one-year non-transfer restriction would be especially damaging for parts manufacturers, who currently supply up to 65% of components by value to domestic vehicle assemblers.
PAAPAM has asked the prime minister and his economic team to ensure the final version of the Auto Policy 2026-31 keeps the non-transfer condition intact, so that overseas facilitation schemes serve their intended beneficiaries rather than commercial dealer networks operating outside the formal economy.

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
Pakistan has transitioned from restricting virtual assets to establishing a dedicated regulatory framework, positioning the country for the next generation of digital finance, Chairman Pakistan Virtual Assets Regulatory Authority (PVARA) Bilal Bin Saqib said on Tuesday.
Addressing the inaugural Silk Road Finance & Technology Forum in Tashkent, Saqib outlined how artificial intelligence, tokenisation and digital assets are beginning to reshape financial institutions, capital markets and the global movement of value.
He argued that governments must build regulatory institutions capable of keeping pace with technologies developing far faster than traditional policy cycles. Saqib noted that Pakistan's 2018 restrictions on virtual assets did not eliminate market activity but pushed significant activity toward offshore platforms, reducing regulatory visibility and leaving consumers with limited protection.
Pakistan has since enacted the Virtual Assets Act, 2026, establishing PVARA as the country's dedicated virtual assets regulator. The authority has notified its licensing regulations and opened its licensing portal, creating a formal pathway for virtual asset service providers to operate within a regulated environment.
He also highlighted the State Bank of Pakistan's (SBP) Circular 10, which enables regulated banks to provide accounts to licensed virtual asset service providers, including segregated client-money accounts.
Saqib said artificial intelligence will increasingly change not only financial products but the institutions responsible for supervising them. As financial markets become faster and more automated, regulators will need to use technology to strengthen supervision, compliance and risk detection.
He outlined Pakistan's interest in applying tokenisation to sovereign investment products, particularly to improve access for the Pakistani diaspora. PVARA and the SBP are studying a model for a digitally native sovereign note that could be issued on regulated blockchain infrastructure, settle on the same day and remain interoperable with Pakistan's existing financial system. Such a model could reduce investment ticket sizes, shorten settlement times and increase transparency around securities ownership.
Saqib also emphasised that Pakistan's young population should move from being consumers of emerging technologies to becoming builders of the companies and financial infrastructure created around them.
PVARA's regulatory sandbox provides developers and entrepreneurs with a supervised environment to test new products before entering the wider market.

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
Housing finance under the Wazir-e-Azam Apna Ghar Programme has surged, with approved financing nearly doubling from Rs144 billion to Rs279 billion since June, as the government pushes to expand access to finance across priority sectors, according to a statement from the Ministry of Finance on Tuesday.
Federal Minister for Finance and Revenue Senator Muhammad Aurangzeb chaired a meeting of the Access to Finance Steering Committee, which reviewed progress on initiatives across housing, agriculture, SMEs, exports, information technology and renewable energy.
The committee noted that total housing finance increased from around Rs294 billion at end-June to Rs307 billion by mid-August. Applications under the housing programme rose 52% to nearly 139,000, approvals increased 84% to over 46,000, and loans disbursed rose 59% to over 7,600.
The momentum is being supported by a strengthened legal and regulatory framework, including the State Bank of Pakistan's (SBP) revised Prudential Regulations for Housing Finance and the passage of the Financial Institutions (Recovery of Finances) (Amendment) Act, 2026 (FIRA), which strengthens the legal framework for recovery and enforcement of mortgage-based lending.
On agriculture, borrowers increased from around 3.26 million at end-June to 3.37 million by mid-August, while financing remained around Rs1.26 trillion. Under the Zarkhez-e-Asaan Zarai Qarza scheme, more than 58,000 farmers have registered, with bank approvals rising 12% to nearly 16,700 and loans disbursed increasing 13% to nearly 5,000.
SME formal financing stood at around Rs1.05 trillion, covering approximately 330,000 businesses. The committee reviewed an ongoing credit-scoring pilot across 13 banks aimed at improving credit assessment through proxy and alternative methods.
The medium-term ambition is to expand agriculture and SME financing to Rs1.5 trillion by June 2027 and Rs2 trillion by June 2028.
The committee also reviewed progress on the Pakistan Accelerated Vehicle Electrification (PAVE) Programme, with more than 83,000 applications received, around 15,800 approved and nearly 4,000 loans disbursed by mid-August.
Aurangzeb emphasised that access to finance should increasingly operate as an integrated economic-enablement framework, combining legal and regulatory reforms, digitalisation, better credit assessment and performance-based incentives.
Separately, German Ambassador Ina Lepel called on the finance minister and extended felicitation on Pakistan's recent sovereign credit rating upgrade by Moody's, noting that the improved rating reflected greater confidence in Pakistan's economic outlook and reform efforts.

items.author: Anne Florentyna
items.content:
Pernia Pop Up Shop’s parent Purple Style Labs’ (PSL) consolidated net loss for the year ending March 31, 2026 (FY26) widened by 51.5% to ₹285.4 Cr compared to a loss of ₹188.4 Cr incurred in the previous year.
Operating revenue for the fiscal increased by about 14% to ₹557.8 Cr from ₹489.9 Cr in the previous fiscal year. Including other income of ₹9.2 Cr, the IPO-bound company’s total income for the fiscal rose 14.8% to ₹567.1 Cr.
Pernia’s gross merchandise value (GMV) for the fiscal year increased 23% YoY to ₹721.6 Cr. The company’s international GMV contribution declined from 28.38% in FY25 to 20.3% in FY26, while US GMV fell from ₹97.4 Cr to ₹76.8 Cr.
This comes despite the company opening its New York store in February 2026 and positioning international expansion as a key growth opportunity.
Founded in 2015 by Abhishek Agarwal, Purple Style Labs operates multi-brand luxury omnichannel fashion platform Pernia’s Pop-Up Shop. Selling via its D2C platform as well as 12 experience centres, the company sells luxury fashion, sourced from 1,109 active designer brands.
These designer brands include Seema Gujral, Anushree Reddy, Amit Aggarwal, Rohit Gandhi & Rahul Khanna.
The company’s product categories span across womenswear, menswear, and others including jewelry, accessories and kidswear, with a focus on wedding and occasion wear. The company served a total of 66,713 customers in the fiscal, down 6% from 70,651 in FY25.
It has raised a private equity funding of about $78 Mn till date from investors like Harish Shah Family Office, Masaba Gupta, among others.
The company filed its red herring prospectus (RHP) for initial public offering, and the IPO comprises only a fresh issue of shares worth up to ₹680 Cr, with no offer for sale component.
Pernia’s parent filed its draft IPO papers with SEBI in September 2025 and got the regulator’s approval to proceed with the IPO in January.
A huge portion of the net proceeds will be used to fund lease liabilities of Pernia’s Pop Up Stores’ experience center networks, while the remaining will fund sales and marketing expenses till FY30.
Zooming Into PSL’s Expenses
The company spent an overall of ₹734.5 Cr in the year under review for all its expenses, marking a 31% increase from the previous year’s ₹559.6 Cr. Here is a breakdown of its total expenditure:
Depreciation And Amortisation Expenses: Spending under this head rose 84.4% to ₹100.7 Cr in the year under review, from ₹54.6 Cr in FY25.
Purchases Of Stock-In-Trade: Constituting 47.6% of the overall costs, expenses under this area stood at ₹349.8 Cr, marking a 15.6% increase from ₹302.6 Cr in the previous year.
Employee Benefit Expenses: Employee costs including gratuity, wages, provident fund and others stood at ₹82 Cr in FY26, up 23.9% from ₹66.2 Cr in the previous fiscal.

items.content:
Pakistani banks are expected to pay around $256 million to foreign banks this fiscal year for processing workers’ remittances after the government ended its financial support scheme, the Senate Standing Committee on Finance was told on Tuesday.
The committee was informed that local banks pay charges to overseas banks to receive remittances sent to Pakistan.
Pakistani banks have historically paid around $800 million annually to foreign banks for remittance-related services.
State Bank of Pakistan Deputy Governor Dr. Inayat Hussain said the government had provided Rs. 124 billion in FY2025 and Rs. 72 billion in the following fiscal year under the remittance-related financial scheme.
The government has discontinued the scheme effective July 2026 and has not allocated funds for it in the current fiscal year. As a result, Pakistani banks will now have to bear the charges payable to overseas banks themselves.
The central bank executive warned that if banks do not absorb the cost, the charges could eventually be passed on to people sending remittances to Pakistan.
The committee was specifically informed that banks are expected to pay around $256 million in such charges during the current fiscal year.
The issue is significant for Pakistan because workers’ remittances remain an important source of foreign exchange for the country.

items.author: Gargi Sarkar
items.content:
India’s pet care ecosystem is undergoing a structural shift. What was once a fragmented market dominated by neighbourhood pet stores, a limited number of veterinary clinics, and imported pet-food brands is steadily becoming a broader consumer category.
Today’s pet parents aren’t shying away from spending on much more than just food. Because of this shift in behaviour, the pet care ecosystem now spans nutrition, medicines, veterinary care, grooming, accessories, diagnostics, insurance, boarding, at-home care, and even quick commerce.
The shift gathered pace after the pandemic. Lockdowns pushed more people towards pet companionship, while rising disposable incomes, delayed marriages and smaller families created a growing pool of urban consumers willing to spend more on their pets.
Now, as pets increasingly become part of the family, spending on them is moving from a discretionary expense to a recurring household priority. This has given a much-needed boost to India’s pet care market that is expected to reach $7 Bn-$8 Bn by 2030, with pet healthcare and services growing faster than the traditional pet-food category.
The opportunity has attracted startups across the value chain. Drools, Heads Up For Tails, Vetic, PetKonnect and JustDogs have built businesses around different parts of the ecosystem. At the same time, ecommerce platforms such as Amazon and Flipkart have expanded their pet offerings, while offline veterinary chains have increased their footprint.
Supertails, however, is betting that the bigger opportunity lies in connecting these fragmented pieces. Founded in 2021 by Varun Sadana, Aman Tekriwal and Vineet Khanna, the company started as an online pet-food platform. It has since expanded into accessories, pharmacy, teleconsultations, private-label pet food, veterinary clinics and quick commerce.
The expansion has translated into rapid top-line growth. Supertails’ operating revenue rose from ₹109 Cr in FY25 to more than ₹200 Cr in FY26, while losses remained broadly unchanged despite investments in clinics, dark stores and healthcare infrastructure. The startup expects revenue of ₹350 Cr-₹400 Cr this financial year and now serves nearly one million pet parents.
But the next phase is likely to be more difficult than the first.
Supertails has spent five years building the infrastructure around pet parenting. Now, it has to prove that these different pieces can work together well enough to create a durable and financially sustainable business.
“We’ve entered a phase where this is no longer just about growth. It’s about building a business where the unit economics and profitability make complete sense,” said Vineet Khanna, cofounder of Supertails.
Supertails Factsheet
Supertails’ Sustainability Push
For years, the playbook for the startup was straightforward: acquire customers, expand the assortment, enter new cities and chase topline growth.
Supertails is now at the point where simply adding another vertical or opening another location will not be enough. The startup increasingly has to make the existing ecosystem work harder.
The company believes the path to sustainable growth lies in increasing the value of each customer while making its existing infrastructure more productive. Three pillars underpin that approach:
Vertical Expansion: From Pet Food To The Entire Pet-Care Basket
When Supertails started in 2021, ecommerce was the obvious entry point. The founders had identified a fragmented market where consumers bought food from one platform, medicines from another, consulted veterinarians separately and relied on neighbourhood stores for other needs. Rather than compete for a share of one category, Supertails decided to build across the pet-care value chain.
But the startup did not attempt to capture everything at once. Pet food came first, helping the brand establish a recurring purchase relationship. Accessories was the next category. The startup then added pharmacy and teleconsultations before moving into physical veterinary care and, more recently, quick commerce.
Each layer expanded the startup’s addressable customer relationship. The most important shift came with healthcare. Around 18 months ago, Supertails began opening veterinary clinics after finding that teleconsultations alone could not address every healthcare need. It now operates 12 clinics in Bengaluru and employs more than 110 veterinarians.
The same logic extends to quick commerce. With pet parents increasingly accustomed to receiving products within minutes, Supertails has added a network of 45 partner-operated dark stores across three cities. Rather than building and owning the entire infrastructure, the startup manages inventory, technology and customer experience while relying on third-party operators.
For Supertails, the objective is not simply to add revenue streams. It is to increase the number of occasions on which a pet parent interacts with the platform.
“Supertails has already invested in clinics, healthcare infrastructure, inventory and delivery infrastructure. The next phase therefore cannot simply be about adding more categories. It has to be about improving utilisation of what the startup has already built,” Khanna said.
That is why Supertails is currently resisting aggressive expansion into new cities, even as categories such as insurance, boarding and at-home care remain on its longer-term roadmap.
Doctor Consultations: Turning Healthcare Into The Engagement Engine
The second pillar is healthcare. For Supertails, veterinary care is not simply another revenue vertical. It creates a different relationship with the customer.
Supertails assigns new customers a ‘Super Companion’, a pet relationship manager who interacts with pet parents. Purchase history, veterinary records and consultations are then combined to build a more detailed profile of the pet.
This changes how the startup thinks about customer acquisition and recommendations. An eight-month-old cat has very different needs from a 12-year-old dog. A dog with allergies requires different products from an otherwise healthy pet. A puppy entering its vaccination cycle creates different purchase opportunities from an ageing pet requiring medicines and specialised food.
Supertails’ proposition is that repeated interactions across commerce and healthcare allow it to understand the pet rather than simply the customer. This data is also used to improve recommendations and support veterinarians.
With AI now becoming mainstream, Supertails is building a recommendation engine for better understanding of a pet, more relevant purchases and potentially higher customer retention.
Private Label: Bringing Margin Into The Ecosystem
The third pillar is private labels. The decision emerged directly from Supertails’ healthcare interactions. Veterinarians were prescribing specialised diets and recommending products that were either expensive because they were imported or difficult to source in India. The founders saw an opportunity between premium imported food and lower-priced domestic products.
The result was Henlo, Supertails’ premium pet-food brand positioned around products made for the Indian market. Private label gives Supertails something its marketplace business does not: greater control over product economics. That makes it strategically important as the startup moves from growth towards sustainability.
The marketplace can increase selection and transaction frequency, healthcare can deepen engagement, and private labels can potentially improve monetisation and margins on that existing customer base.
The combination is more important than any one vertical individually. A customer may enter through pet food, interact with a veterinarian, receive a recommendation for a specialised diet, purchase that product through Supertails and subsequently return for medicines or another consultation. That is the ecosystem flywheel Supertails is trying to create.
Supertails
Supertails Now Has To Make The Numbers Work
Supertails more than doubled its revenue to over ₹200 Cr in FY26 while keeping losses broadly unchanged. While this suggests the startup has been able to grow without a proportional deterioration in its cost base, it also means the next stage cannot be built purely on topline expansion.
The startup has already made substantial investments in three areas it considers foundational: delivery infrastructure, healthcare infrastructure and data infrastructure.
The question is no longer whether Supertails can add another vertical. It is whether the existing customer base can generate enough frequency across food, pharmacy, healthcare and other categories to make the infrastructure increasingly productive.
Quick commerce provides a useful example. Supertails says its quick commerce business is growing at double-digit month-on-month rates, with retention and repeat purchases improving as customers use the platform for medicines, food, toys and accessories.
The startup also argues that the economics improve as demand scales because shorter delivery distances, negligible returns and higher infrastructure utilisation can make the model cheaper than conventional ecommerce.
But the more important test is whether this increased convenience creates incremental frequency rather than simply shifting existing orders from standard ecommerce to a faster channel.
The same question applies to clinics and private labels. More clinics can increase healthcare revenue, but they also add fixed costs. Private labels can improve margins, but only if Supertails can generate sufficient volume and customer adoption. Recommendations can improve conversion, but only if the underlying customer data translates into higher retention and purchase frequency.
Supertails’ Next Act
Supertails’ first five years were largely about building. It built an ecommerce business, expanded into healthcare, launched its own brand, opened clinics and created a faster delivery network. The next five years will require a different kind of execution.
The startup wants to become the largest specialised pet-care platform in India and expects to reach that milestone in the coming quarters. But market leadership alone will not pave the way for attractive economics.
Therefore, three sets of metrics will become increasingly important.
First, customer retention and purchase frequency. If pet parents use Supertails across food, medicines, healthcare and other categories, the startup can potentially increase customer lifetime value without having to reacquire the same customers repeatedly.
Second, utilisation and economics of healthcare and delivery infrastructure. Clinics and dark stores only become assets rather than cost centres when enough demand flows through them.
Third, the margin contribution of private labels and other owned products. These businesses could help SuperTails capture more value from transactions that it already generates.
The startup is also targeting financial sustainability over the next 24-36 months, with a longer-term ambition of becoming public. Its IPO ambition put another layer of pressure on the business. Public markets tend to reward growth, but they also demand visibility into margins, cash flows and the path to profitability.
For now, Supertails has become successful in building a large pet-care platform. The next part is making every cog in the wheel work together.
[Edited by Shishir Parasher]

items.author: Anne Florentyna
items.content:
Consumer appliances brand Atomberg filed its draft IPO papers with market regulator SEBI, for a proposed public issue comprising a fresh issue of shares worth up to ₹450 Cr and an offer for sale (OFS) of up to 7.65 Cr equity shares.
Institutional investors A91 Partners, Temasek Holdings, Inflexor Ventures, and Steadview Capital intend to dilute their stake in the company via the IPO. Including the selling shareholders, the company has a total of 69 shareholders till date.
A91 Partners holds the highest stake of 21.02% in the company via holding entity A91 Emerging Fund I. The investor first backed the startup in 2019, as part of its Series A funding round of $10 Mn, along with Whiteboard Capital and Survam Partners, back then.
Following A91, cofounders Manoj Kumar Meena and Sibabrata Das own 17.73% and 10.02%, respectively. Meena and Das are not selling any shares in the IPO.
Meanwhile, Temasek, via its holding entity V-Sciences Investments, commands 11.8% ownership in Atomberg. While Jungle Ventures (JV4) holds 10.03%, Steadview Capital Mauritius and Jongsong Investments own 7% and 6.98% in the company, respectively,
Further, Inflexor Ventures, via Inflexor Opportunities Fund I and Inflexor Technology Fund, holds 6.08% ownership in Atomberg.
Founded in 2012 by Meena and Das, Atomberg initially focused on selling energy-efficient brushless direct current (BLDC) fans to businesses before entering the consumer market in 2016.
It has since then expanded beyond fans into categories such as mixer grinders, water purifiers, and cold-pressed juicers. However, fans continue to be its largest revenue-generating product category.
Atomberg now sells its products through offline retailers, online marketplaces, and its own website.
The company obtained the board approval for its public listing, about a week ago. Additionally, the board also approved the raise of up to ₹90 Cr via a pre-IPO placement of equity shares.
On the financial front, the consumer appliances company saw its consolidated net loss widen 26.8% to ₹148.9 Cr in FY26 from ₹117.4 Cr in the previous fiscal year. Operating revenue jumped 34.8% to ₹1,293.8 Cr in the year under review from ₹959.5 Cr in FY25.
A Break Down Of Atomberg’s Leadership Deck
Board of Directors
Manoj Kumar Meena
Meena is the managing director and chairman of the company. He founded Atomberg and headed the company as its chief executive for the first 14 years.
Sibabrata Das
Das is the CEO and executive director of Atomberg. He cofounded the company along with Meena and headed as the chief operating officer till 2025. Prior to that, he was the CEO for almost a year of online personal care brand 24×7 Styles.
Abhay Kumar Pandey
A91 Partners’ general partner Pandey is the nominee director on Atomberg’s board. While he has been a general partner at A91 Partners for nearly eight years, he previously worked with Peak XV Partners for over 11 years. He has been part of the boards of companies like Awfis, Bira 91, curatio, among others.
Anand Kantilal Vora
United Phosphorus Ltd’s CFO Vora is an independent director on Atomberg’s board. Over a finance career spanning nearly four decades, Vora has worked with companies like Dow Chemical & Dow AgroSciences, Ranbaxy Brazil and HTMT Global Solutions.
Suman Gopalan
Gopalan, who has been the managing partner at Rivendell Advisory for over two years, has been on the board of Atomberg for about four months as an independent director. Previously, she has also worked with Freshworks as chief HR officer for about five years.
Subhasis Chaudhuri
Chaudhur, also an independent director at Atomberg, has been a full time professor at IIT Bombay since 1990. Besides, he is currently the chairperson of BSE’s board, a position he has held for nearly two years.
Key Managerial Personnel
Manish Kumar Bansal
Bansal is the chief financial officer of the company for nearly four years. Prior to this stint, he was working with L’Oreal for more than six years. Holding an overall experience of 20 years, he previously worked with Marico and kaya skin care.
Priti Baria
Joined on November 11, 2024 as manager of legal function, Baria is now the lead of legal, company secretary and compliance officer at Atomberg. Prior to this, she worked with WestRock Company as India legal and company secretary for over a year. She holds an overall experience of 15 years, working with companies like Bajaj Consumer Care, Knight Frank India and Parker Hannifin, among others.

items.author: Bambang Dwi Atmoko
items.content:
XPENG selama ini lebih dikenal sebagai produsen mobil listrik asal China. Namun, bisnis yang kini mendapat suntikan modal lebih dari USD900 juta atau sekitar Rp15,9 triliun bukanlah mobil. Bisnis XPENG robot humanoid baru saja meraih pendanaan yang memberi valuasi lebih dari USD6,3 miliar, atau sekitar Rp111,3 triliun berdasarkan kurs Rp17.670 per USD. Dana tersebut akan digunakan untuk mempercepat pengembangan dan produksi massal robot humanoid XPENG IRON.
Pendanaan ini datang ketika industri robot humanoid mulai bergerak dari sekadar demonstrasi kemampuan berjalan, menari, atau melakukan gerakan kompleks menuju tahap yang jauh lebih sulit: membangun robot dalam jumlah besar dan menemukan aplikasi komersial yang benar-benar dibutuhkan.
Baca juga: XPENG Bawa Revolusi Mobilitas Berbasis AI & Robot Humanoid
Menurut XPENG, bisnis robotikanya telah menandatangani perjanjian pembelian saham dengan sejumlah investor dan mengumpulkan lebih dari USD900 juta. Putaran tersebut dipimpin IDG Capital, dengan partisipasi Gaorong Ventures serta dukungan Tencent dan Alibaba sebagai investor strategis.
Reuters melaporkan, perusahaan menargetkan kapasitas produksi XPENG robot humanoid IRON mencapai 1.000 unit per bulan pada akhir 2026. Robot tersebut rencananya lebih dulu digunakan di toko dan kawasan industri XPENG, sebelum penjualan dan pengiriman yang lebih luas ke pasar China dan internasional dimulai pada 2027.
Bisnis XPENG Robot Humanoid Kini Bernilai Lebih dari Rp111 Triliun
He Xiaopeng, chairman dan CEO Xpeng
Pendanaan lebih dari USD900 juta tersebut menjadi putaran pendanaan pertama bagi bisnis XPENG robot humanoid. Setelah transaksi, perusahaan menyebut valuasi post-money bisnis tersebut mencapai lebih dari USD6,3 miliar. XPENG juga menyatakan tetap mempertahankan kepemilikan pengendali atas bisnis robotikanya. Dengan demikian, unit tersebut masih akan dikonsolidasikan ke dalam laporan keuangan grup.
Reuters mencatat pendanaan tersebut menjadi rekor baru untuk satu putaran pendanaan swasta di sektor embodied AI China, melampaui rekor sebelumnya yang dipegang TARS Robotics dengan pendanaan lebih dari USD455 juta pada tahun ini.
Besarnya pendanaan menunjukkan bahwa investor tidak lagi hanya melihat robot humanoid sebagai proyek riset jangka panjang. Setidaknya dalam kasus XPENG, investor kini memberikan valuasi tersendiri bagi bisnis tersebut sebelum IRON benar-benar memasuki penjualan komersial dalam skala besar.
Bagi XPENG sendiri, pendanaan eksternal juga membuka jalur pembiayaan terpisah untuk bisnis yang membutuhkan investasi besar. Pengembangan Xpreng robot humanoid tidak hanya membutuhkan hardware, tetapi juga data, model AI, infrastruktur komputasi, fasilitas produksi, serta pengembangan supply chain.
XPENG mengatakan dana baru tersebut akan digunakan untuk pengembangan hardware dan software robotika, pelatihan serta iterasi model Physical AI, pengumpulan data berkualitas tinggi, pembangunan fasilitas produksi massal, hingga ekspansi komersial global.
XPENG Targetkan Produksi 1.000 Robot IRON per Bulan
Bagian paling konkret dari rencana XPENG robot humanoid justru berada pada target produksinya. Perusahaan menargetkan produksi robot humanoid IRON dapat mencapai 1.000 unit per bulan pada akhir 2026. Target tersebut masih merupakan rencana perusahaan dan belum mencerminkan kapasitas produksi yang telah dicapai saat ini.
Pada tahap awal, IRON direncanakan digunakan di toko dan kawasan industri XPENG. Setelah itu, perusahaan menargetkan peluncuran serta pengiriman kepada pelanggan eksternal di China dan pasar internasional mulai 2027.
Target tersebut penting karena memperlihatkan perubahan fokus industri humanoid. Tantangan berikutnya bukan lagi sekadar membuktikan bahwa robot dapat bergerak menyerupai manusia, tetapi apakah teknologi tersebut dapat diproduksi secara konsisten, memenuhi standar keamanan, dan menjalankan pekerjaan yang memiliki nilai ekonomi.
Produksi massal juga tidak otomatis berarti robot humanoid telah memasuki pasar massal. Perusahaan masih harus membuktikan apakah penggunaan di toko, layanan, atau lingkungan industri dapat menghasilkan permintaan yang berkelanjutan.
XPENG Membawa Teknologi EV ke Robot Humanoid
XPENG mengembangkan IRON sebagai bagian dari strategi Physical AI, istilah yang digunakan perusahaan untuk menggambarkan penerapan AI pada sistem yang berinteraksi langsung dengan dunia fisik.
XPENG Robot humanoid ini menggunakan tiga chip Turing AI dengan total kemampuan komputasi hingga 2.250 TOPS, menurut XPENG. Sistem tersebut dirancang untuk menjalankan model Physical AI langsung di robot sehingga IRON dapat memproses dan menjalankan tugas tanpa harus dikendalikan dari jarak jauh.
Dari sisi mekanik, XPENG menyebut IRON memiliki 76 degrees of freedom di seluruh tubuh serta 21 degrees of freedom pada masing-masing tangan. Kombinasi tersebut dirancang untuk memberikan rentang gerak dan kemampuan manipulasi yang lebih mendekati aktivitas manusia.
Namun, angka spesifikasi tersebut bukan inti dari strategi XPENG. Yang lebih penting adalah upaya perusahaan memanfaatkan teknologi yang sebelumnya dikembangkan untuk mobil listrik dan intelligent vehicle ke dalam robot humanoid. XPENG telah membangun chip AI sendiri, infrastruktur komputasi, model AI, sistem kontrol, serta kemampuan manufaktur yang sebelumnya digunakan untuk bisnis kendaraan.
CEO XPENG He Xiaopeng bahkan secara langsung memimpin bisnis robotika perusahaan. Reuters mencatat humanoid robotics dipandang memiliki kedekatan teknologi dengan pengembangan kendaraan cerdas, mulai dari software dan sensor hingga pengelolaan supply chain.
Strategi tersebut menjelaskan mengapa XPENG tidak memperlakukan robot humanoid sebagai bisnis yang sepenuhnya terpisah dari mobil listrik. Perusahaan mencoba membangun satu fondasi teknologi yang dapat digunakan di beberapa kategori, termasuk smart EV, robotaxi, dan humanoid robot.
Dalam laporan keuangan kuartal II 2026, XPENG bahkan secara eksplisit menempatkan robotics bersama pengembangan teknologi Physical AI lainnya. Perusahaan menyebut IRON akan menjadi salah satu bagian dari ekspansi bisnis tersebut, dengan rencana meningkatkan kapasitas produksi hingga beberapa ribu unit per bulan pada 2027 apabila permintaan pasar mendukung.
Industri Robot Humanoid China Mulai Masuk Fase Baru
Pendanaan XPENG datang pada saat investasi terhadap industri robot humanoid China sedang meningkat. Beberapa hari sebelumnya, Unitree menarik perhatian pasar setelah debutnya di bursa Shanghai. Saham perusahaan robot tersebut sempat melonjak tajam pada hari pertama perdagangan, meski kemudian mengalami koreksi besar. Pergerakan tersebut memperlihatkan tingginya minat investor terhadap industri robotics sekaligus risiko ketika ekspektasi pasar bergerak lebih cepat daripada perkembangan komersialnya.
Konteks ini penting bagi XPENG. Perusahaan tidak hanya bersaing untuk membuat robot yang mampu melakukan gerakan semakin kompleks, tetapi juga harus membuktikan bahwa robot humanoid dapat digunakan dalam skenario nyata secara konsisten.
Unitree sendiri telah menjadi salah satu contoh bagaimana perhatian publik terhadap humanoid robot dapat berkembang sangat cepat. Namun, pertanyaan mengenai aplikasi komersial yang benar-benar dapat menghasilkan pendapatan dalam skala besar masih menjadi salah satu tantangan utama industri ini.
Bagi XPENG, pendanaan Rp15,9 triliun memberikan sumber daya untuk menghadapi tahap tersebut. Dana tersebut akan digunakan bukan hanya untuk menyempurnakan robot, tetapi juga membangun apa yang disebut perusahaan sebagai siklus data, model, dan deployment.
Semakin banyak Xpeng robot humanoid yang beroperasi di lingkungan nyata, semakin banyak pula data yang secara teoritis dapat digunakan untuk melatih dan meningkatkan model AI. XPENG berharap siklus tersebut dapat mempercepat kemampuan IRON beradaptasi dengan berbagai tugas dan lingkungan.
Namun, efektivitas pendekatan ini baru dapat diuji ketika IRON benar-benar mulai digunakan di luar lingkungan demonstrasi dan pengembangan perusahaan.
Robot XPENG IRON Sudah Pernah Muncul di Indonesia
Kemunculan Xpeng Iron di GIIAS 2026
Meski belum ada pengumuman mengenai penjualan XPENG IRON di Indonesia, robot humanoid tersebut bukan teknologi yang sepenuhnya asing bagi publik Tanah Air. XPENG sebelumnya memperkenalkan visi Physical AI dan menampilkan IRON pada ajang IIMS 2026 dan GIIAS 2026. Saat itu, perusahaan menempatkan robot humanoid tersebut bersama pengembangan kendaraan berbasis AI sebagai bagian dari arah teknologi jangka panjangnya.
Kehadiran IRON di Indonesia saat itu belum berarti robot tersebut akan dipasarkan secara lokal. Namun, langkah tersebut menunjukkan bahwa XPENG telah menggunakan pasar Indonesia sebagai salah satu tempat untuk memperkenalkan ambisinya di luar bisnis kendaraan listrik.
Pendanaan terbaru membuat ambisi tersebut kini memiliki skala yang jauh lebih konkret. Dengan valuasi lebih dari USD6,3 miliar dan target produksi 1.000 unit per bulan pada akhir 2026, bisnis robotika XPENG kini mulai berdiri sebagai salah satu taruhan teknologi terbesar perusahaan.
Pertanyaan berikutnya bukan lagi apakah XPENG mampu membuat robot humanoid. IRON sudah ada dan perusahaan telah menetapkan roadmap menuju produksi. Tantangan yang lebih besar adalah apakah Xpeng robot humanoid tersebut dapat menemukan pekerjaan dan pengguna yang cukup banyak untuk membenarkan investasi miliaran dolar yang kini masuk ke industri Physical AI.

items.author: Amiya Johar
items.content:
Indian data centre company AM Intelligence placed an order for around 9,000 Nvidia Rubin GPUs, aiming to deploy one of Asia’s first Vera Rubin clusters at a new AI factory in southern India.
The company said the GPUs will be deployed as Nvidia Vera Rubin NVL72 rack-scale systems at a 30MW AI factory in the city of Hyderabad. The facility is slated to come online in Q1 2027.
AM Intelligence said the site is being designed to run trillion-parameter models and agentic AI applications and will target customers including cloud providers, AI labs and organisations developing sovereign AI models. It further explained Vera Rubin’s platform architecture is designed to cut AI inference token-serving costs by up to 10 times compared with Nvidia’s previous Grace Blackwell generation.
“The electron-to-token opportunity allows us to take this capability further, converting power infrastructure into frontier AI compute at scale,” noted AM Group Chairman Anil Chalamalasetty.
Based in Hyderabad, AM Intelligence is the AI infrastructure arm of Indian green energy and technology conglomerate AM Group. The firm builds large-scale, renewable-powered AI computing infrastructure and data centres to support AI models, cloud-service providers and AI labs.
The Hyderabad site marks the first phase of AM Intelligence’s planned buildout of 1GW of Compute-as-a-Service capacity across India, the US, Finland and Malaysia. The company plans to bring an initial 200MW online, with the wider buildout involving more than $8 billion in capital expenditure.
By 2030, AM Intelligence aims to hit 5GW of data centre capacity across India, US and Europe, with facilities designed for high-density AI compute and liquid cooling.
Hunting desperately
Demand for high-end AI computing infrastructure continues to rise, with major technology players including Microsoft, Google and Amazon seeking capacity to train increasingly large AI models.
Mahesh Kolli, founder and president of Greenko Group, which is part of AM Group, told Bloomberg that customers are “hunting desperately” for capacity. He added that India faces few operational constraints, with undersea cables allowing US companies to use AI compute with latency of about 300 milliseconds.

items.author: Business Desk
items.content:
Housing finance under the Prime Minister’s Apna Ghar scheme has nearly doubled since June, with approved financing rising by 94 percent from Rs. 144 billion to Rs. 279 billion by mid-August, according to the Finance Division.
The figures were reviewed at a meeting of the Access to Finance Steering Committee chaired by Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb on Tuesday.
Applications under the PM’s Apna Ghar Program increased 52 percent since June to nearly 139,000, while approvals jumped 84 percent to more than 46,000.
The number of housing loans disbursed also rose 59 percent to over 7,600, with total disbursements exceeding Rs. 38 billion.
Overall housing finance in Pakistan increased from around Rs. 294 billion at the end of June to Rs. 307 billion by mid-August.
The Finance Division said recent regulatory reforms are aimed at expanding mortgage lending, including a 90:10 loan-to-value ratio, a 65 percent debt-burden ratio, simplified property valuation and documentation, digital processing and longer financing tenors.
The committee also highlighted the Financial Institutions (Recovery of Finances) (Amendment) Act, 2026, saying stronger recovery rules could encourage banks to increase mortgage lending.
Agriculture and SME financing also showed growth. Agriculture borrowers increased by around 115,000 to 3.37 million by mid-August, while agriculture financing stood at about Rs. 1.26 trillion.
Formal SME financing reached around Rs. 1.05 trillion, covering approximately 330,000 businesses.
The government is targeting agriculture and SME financing of Rs. 1.5 trillion each by June 2027 and Rs. 2 trillion each by June 2028.
The committee also reviewed export financing and the new Performance-Based Rebate on Incremental Exports, under which exporters can receive a rebate of up to 2 percent on additional exports.

items.title: Gold Suddenly falls in Pakistan
items.summary:
Gold prices in Pakistan reported small losses following a decrease in international gold prices.
The price of 24 karat gold decreased by Rs. 600 to Rs. 486,536 per tola, according to the All Pakistan Gems and Jewellers Sarafa Association (APGJSA).
The price of 10 gram gold also decreased by Rs. 514 to Rs. 417,126.
Gold had gained Rs. 4,200 per tola on Monday, reaching Rs. 487,136.
In the international market, gold decreased by $6 to $4,640 per ounce, including a $20 premium.
Meanwhile, silver prices also decreased today. Rates closed at Rs. 7,279 per tola after losing Rs. 100 on Tuesday.

items.summary:
The Lahore Electric Supply Company (LESCO) has completed special arrangements to ensure uninterrupted electricity supply during Eid Milad-un-Nabi gatherings and religious events across its service area.
According to LESCO, uninterrupted power supply will be maintained during gatherings and Milad events scheduled for the night between Tuesday and Wednesday.
LESCO has assigned special duties to staff across all its circles, divisions and subdivisions to respond quickly to any emergency or power supply issue.
The company has also directed relevant officers and field staff to continuously monitor the electricity supply system and immediately address any technical faults.
LESCO said it has completed all necessary arrangements to ensure uninterrupted electricity supply to citizens during Eid Milad-un-Nabi.

items.author: Daily Trust
items.content:
Plateau State Governor, Caleb Manasseh Mutfwang, has felicitated with the Muslim Ummah in the State and across Nigeria as they join millions of faithful worldwide to commemorate the Eid-el-Maulud, marking the birth of the Holy Prophet Muhammad (SAW).
In a goodwill message issued by the Gyang Bere, Director of Press and Public Affairs to the Governor, Mutfwang urged Muslim faithful to use the sacred occasion to reflect deeply on the exemplary life and teachings of Prophet Muhammad, particularly his virtues of peace, justice, compassion, tolerance and respect for people of different faiths.
Mutfwang noted that the lessons of the Prophet’s life remain highly relevant to contemporary society, especially at a time when peaceful coexistence, mutual understanding and respect for diversity are critical to the stability and development of Plateau State and Nigeria.
The Governor particularly commended the Jos Annual Maulud Committee of the Jama’atu Nasril Islam (JNI) for adopting the theme, “Emulating the Prophetic Way of Peace, Mutual Respect and Religious Freedom,” describing it as a timely and appropriate message capable of reinforcing the values required for peaceful coexistence in a religiously and culturally diverse society.
He therefore called on Muslim faithful to make the occasion a period of prayers for peace, unity and security across Plateau State, while urging all citizens to reject violence, hatred and other actions capable of undermining the peaceful coexistence of communities.
According to the Governor, the responsibility for sustaining peace should not be left to government alone, stressing that citizens, irrespective of religious or ethnic background, have a crucial role to play in building trust, promoting tolerance and protecting the peace of their communities.
Mutfwang further reaffirmed the commitment of his administration, under the “Time Is Now” agenda, to creating an enabling environment where every citizen can freely practise his or her faith without hindrance, discrimination or intimidation.
He also assured the people of Plateau that his administration would continue to take decisive measures against criminals and other elements seeking to disrupt the peace, security and stability of the State.
While congratulating the Muslim Ummah on the occasion, the Governor called for renewed commitment to the shared values of brotherhood, compassion, mutual respect and peaceful coexistence, which he said were essential to building a stronger and more united Plateau.
Mutfwang, on behalf of the Plateau State Government and the people of the State, prayed that the Eid-el-Maulud celebration would bring abundant blessings, lasting peace, unity and prosperity to Plateau State and Nigeria.

items.author: Gaurav Bagur
items.content:
Update | August 25, 18:57 IST
Cult Fitness Pvt Ltd cofounder Rishabh Telang has moved the Karnataka High Court to quash the FIR filed against him by his brother-in-law and cofounder Deepak Poduval.
The Court did not order a stay on the investigation, but sought responses from Poduval and the State on the plea.
It further noted that the police had issued Telang a notice under Section 35 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita and he would not be facing an immediate arrest.
The matter is scheduled for a hearing on September 2.
Original | August 8, 21:03 IST
Deepak Poduval, cofounder of Cult Fitness Pvt Ltd, has filed an FIR against his cofounder and brother-in-law Rishabh Telang at Bengaluru’s Bellandur Police Station, alleging forgery, cheating and criminal conspiracy in connection with the 2016 transfer of certain assets and intellectual property (IP) from the company to Cultfit Healthcare Pvt Ltd, a part of IPO-bound Cult.fit.
Poduval alleges that Telang forged his signature on documents used to wind up Cult Fitness without his authorisation including a board resolution, an EGM notice explanatory statement, a shareholder consent, a Form STK-4 affidavit and Form STK-3 indemnity bond, and a chartered-accountant-certified statement of account, as well as statutory financials filed in August 2016..
He further alleged that he did not receive payment arising from the transaction with Cultfit Healthcare, a subsidiary of Cult.fit, and that his 50% shareholding in Cult Fitness was “extinguished without a rupee of consideration”.
“From February 2016, I was systematically excluded from management, meetings and financial decisions, despite remaining an equal shareholder and director,” Poduval said.
He claimed that he only discovered that the company had been struck off recently after perusing MCA documents and filed the FIR soon after. According to Poduval, the dealings with Cultfit Healthcare were “a premeditated move to run our business through a parallel vehicle while cutting me out.”
Telang has denied the allegations, while Cult.fit said neither it nor its subsidiary is an accused in the FIR.
Cult Fitness, a Bengaluru-based fitness centre chain, was founded by Poduval and Telang in 2015. A year later, Cultfit Healthcare acquired certain assets and IP rights of the company, including the ‘Cult – The Workout Station’ brand.
Responding to the allegations, Telang said the matter would be addressed through the ongoing legal proceedings.
“Deepak was fully involved in the transactions with Cultfit Healthcare Pvt Ltd as well as the winding up of Cult Fitness Pvt Ltd, of which I possess multiple correspondence,” said Telang in a statement shared with Inc42 by Cult.fit.
He further claimed that the Ministry of Corporate Affairs acknowledged the winding up of Cult Fitness through an email dated March 12, 2020, and alleged that Poduval had received consideration under the transaction.
Telang also questioned the timing of the FIR, alleging that it was filed with “mala fide” intentions. He pointed to a property settlement lawsuit filed by Poduval’s wife, who is also Telang’s sister, on July 1, 2026.
Separately, Cult.fit said that it has not received any communication from the authorities in connection with the matter.
“The accused entity, Cult Fitness Pvt Ltd, was a separate independent company of the complainant himself and we did not have any ownership or management control,” it said in its statement.
It added that its transaction with Cult Fitness was carried out “under appropriate contractual arrangements and for consideration which was duly paid and also acknowledged by the complainant”.
“With this, this acquisition stood consummated and closed,” the company stated.
Inc42 has reached out to Poduval for his response. The story will be updated if and when a response is received.
The development is the latest instance of legal proceedings involving founders of IPO-bound startups. Earlier this year, former RentoMojo cofounder Ajay Nain moved the NCLT, alleging oppression and mismanagement and seeking to halt the company’s proposed IPO by challenging a share sale completed in 2023. The proceedings were subsequently disclosed in RentoMojo’s DRHP.
The latest development comes nearly a month after Cult.fit filed its draft IPO papers for a proposed IPO. The company plans to raise up to ₹950 Cr through a fresh issue of shares, while existing investors are looking to offload up to 17.86 Cr shares through an offer for sale. The total IPO size is expected to be around ₹4,000 Cr.
On the financial front, Cult.fit’s net loss narrowed 47.6% YoY to ₹251.8 Cr in FY26. The company’s operating revenue grew 41.5% YoY to ₹1,720.6 Cr. Total expenses jumped almost 16% to ₹2,027.5 Cr.
Editor’s Note: The story has been updated to incorporate Deepak Poduval’s statement.

items.author: Anadolu Agency
items.content:
United States President Donald Trump launched the February offensive against Iran despite explicit warnings from his intelligence chief, vice president and senior military advisers that the conflict could trigger a global energy crisis and lead to a more hard-line Iranian leadership, The Wall Street Journal reported.
According to people familiar with pre-war meetings, then-director of National Intelligence Tulsi Gabbard told Trump that killing Iran’s supreme leader would likely “usher in a more hard-line” successor and force the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, a strategic waterway through which one-fifth of global oil and gas trade passes.
US Vice President JD Vance also advocated a more “cautious”, negotiation-first approach, arguing that a diplomatic deal would be less costly than a war with “unwieldy consequences”.
While top military officials, including Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth and Joint Chiefs Chairman General Dan Caine, briefed Trump on “decisive” strike options, other officials raised concerns about munitions shortages and risks to an “overstretched force”. Trump reportedly dismissed those concerns, suggesting the military could “handle any problems” as they arose.
Read More: Iran, Oman mull proposal for joint shipping route through Hormuz Strait
The report said Trump was initially pleased with the start of the war and “puffed out his chest” at a Mar-a-Lago fundraiser when informed of the killing of then-Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei.
However, as fuel prices soared and the war stalled, regional leaders from Saudi Arabia and Qatar pressed the White House for a diplomatic solution. Internal polling showed nearly 80% of Americans favoured an agreement to end the war, prompting Trump to pursue the June interim truce.
Some Republicans also warned Trump about the potential impact of a prolonged war on their chances in the November midterm elections.
The 60-day window for nuclear negotiations ended on August 17 without a final settlement.
The administration has since shifted back to Operation Economic Outcast, a campaign of economic warfare aimed at weakening the Iranian government through a sustained naval blockade and sanctions.

According to the Pakistan Economic
items.author: Web Desk
items.content:
The federal government on Tuesday increased the price of petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs1.12 and Rs1.11 per litre, respectively, from August 26 to August 27.
According to a notification issued by the Petroleum Division, the price of petrol has been fixed at Rs343.10 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs371.80 per litre till August 27.
The latest revision comes a day after the government increased the price of petrol and HSD by 39 paisas and Rs2.40 per litre, respectively, for August 25.
Read: Govt raises petrol price by 39 paisas, HSD by Rs2.40 per litre for Aug 25
Last month, the government announced a new pricing mechanism under which petroleum product prices would be reviewed and notified on a daily basis, replacing the weekly pricing mechanism, as renewed tensions between the United States and Iran continued to drive volatility in global oil markets and raise concerns over fuel supplies.
According to the Pakistan Economic Survey 2024-25, petroleum products constitute one of the country's largest import categories, making the economy highly vulnerable to changes in global crude oil prices. Domestic refineries satisfy only part of national demand, while the remainder is met through imports of crude oil and refined petroleum products. Consequently, every increase in international oil prices raises Pakistan's import bill, pressures foreign exchange reserves, and contributes to inflation.
Pakistan previously exercised significant government control over petroleum pricing through subsidies and administrative interventions. While these measures temporarily protected consumers, they imposed substantial fiscal costs. During periods of elevated global oil prices, successive governments delayed passing price increases to consumers, creating financial pressures for oil marketing companies, refineries, and the national budget. Large fuel subsidies widened fiscal deficits, increased public borrowing, and weakened macroeconomic stability.
Global geopolitical developments continue to pose significant risks. International oil prices are influenced by decisions taken by OPEC+, conflicts in the Middle East, sanctions on oil-producing nations, and disruptions in critical shipping routes such as the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea. Any interruption in these supply chains can immediately increase crude oil prices and freight costs. Since Pakistan imports the majority of its petroleum requirements, these developments quickly translate into higher domestic fuel prices.
Oil prices on Tuesday fell about 4% to ​a one-week low as traders shrugged off the latest US sanctions campaign against Iran, ‌viewing economic pressure as posing less risk to oil supplies than a military escalation.
Brent crude futures were down $3.74, or 4.1%, at $88.43 a barrel by 2 pm ET (1800 GMT), while US West Texas Intermediate crude futures fell $2.85, or 3.4%, to $81.67, paring earlier losses.
The shift from military conflict to economic pressure in the US-Israeli war with Iran has reduced some ​of the oil market's anxiety, said Saxo Bank head of commodity strategy Ole Hansen, adding ⁠the US sanctions announcement was not as forceful as some traders had expected.

items.title: Brazil fines TikTok owner ByteDance for unlawful processing of teenagers' data
items.summary:
Brazil's data protection authority (ANPD) has fined TikTok owner ByteDance 153.8 million reais ($29.81 million) for allegedly violating the country's General Data Protection Law, according to a decision published in the official gazette on Tuesday.
ANPD said that the local unit of China's ByteDance had processed personal data of teenagers aged 13 to 18 without a valid legal basis.
ByteDance Brasil did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
Brazilian authorities are stepping up scrutiny of online platforms' safeguards for children and teenagers, part of a broader global trend that has seen countries including Australia, France and China impose or consider stricter rules on minors' use of social media.
Earlier this month, ANPD ordered chat platform Discord to suspend livestreaming features over concerns about children's and teenagers' exposure to harmful content.

items.content:
Brazil's data protection authority (ANPD) has fined TikTok owner ByteDance 153.8 million reais ($29.81 million) for allegedly violating the country's General Data Protection Law, according to a decision published in the official gazette on Tuesday.
ANPD said that the local unit of China's ByteDance had processed personal data of teenagers aged 13 to 18 without a valid legal basis.
ByteDance Brasil did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
Brazilian authorities are stepping up scrutiny of online platforms' safeguards for children and teenagers, part of a broader global trend that has seen countries including Australia, France and China impose or consider stricter rules on minors' use of social media.
Earlier this month, ANPD ordered chat platform Discord to suspend livestreaming features over concerns about children's and teenagers' exposure to harmful content.
Read More: IHC moved for regulating social media use by kids
According to Tuesday's decision, ByteDance must delete the personal data of teenagers whose legal representation or assistance is not regularized within 60 business days and notify third parties with whom it shared the data.
It must also submit a technical report signed by its data protection officer, along with system audit logs demonstrating compliance, within five business days after the initial deadline expires.
The company faces fines of 137,081.49 reais per day if it fails to comply with the data-deletion, reporting or notification requirements.
The total fine could be reduced by 25% if ByteDance waives its right to appeal within 10 business days and pays the penalty within 20 business days, according to ANPD.

items.content:
Jakarta, Gizmologi – Samsung Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra menghadirkan lebih dari sekadar layar besar yang dapat dilipat. Main Screen 8 inci yang mampu bekerja berdampingan dengan Cover Screen 6,5 inci menciptakan pengalaman kerja yang fleksibel, mulai dari riset, perencanaan perjalanan, hingga pengeditan konten, semuanya dapat dilakukan dengan satu perangkat saja. Ditenagai Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 Mobile Platform for Galaxy, Z Fold8 Ultra tetap responsif saat menjalankan multitasking intensif dan fitur berbasis AI tanpa lag atau panas berlebihan.
Keunggulan pertama adalah kemampuan berpindah antara Cover Screen dan Main Screen tanpa kehilangan posisi pekerjaan. Anda bisa memulai aktivitas saat perangkat masih dilipat, kemudian membukanya dan langsung melanjutkan dari titik yang sama dengan ruang kerja yang lebih luas untuk memeriksa spreadsheet, meninjau foto detail, atau bekerja di beberapa aplikasi sekaligus. Fleksibilitas ini berarti tidak perlu lagi memulai ulang atau mencari kembali file yang sedang dikerjakan hanya karena berpindah antar mode layar.
Multi Window adalah fitur yang mengubah cara bekerja. Anda bisa menjalankan dua atau tiga aplikasi secara bersamaan di Main Screen dengan ukuran jendela yang dapat disesuaikan, membuat kombinasi kerja seperti melihat kalender sambil membalas pesan, mencari informasi di internet saat meninjau presentasi, atau menggunakan kalkulator ketika memeriksa anggaran menjadi sangat mudah. Pop-up View menambah fleksibilitas dengan memungkinkan aplikasi tampil sebagai jendela yang dapat dipindahkan dan diubah ukurannya di atas ruang kerja utama, sehingga Anda tidak perlu terus-menerus berganti aplikasi.
Untuk mempercepat alur kerja, Taskbar di bagian bawah Main Screen berfungsi seperti tablet atau desktop biasa dengan aplikasi favorit yang siap diakses cepat. Fitur App Pair memungkinkan Anda menyimpan kombinasi aplikasi yang sering digunakan, misalnya Calendar dan Messages, lalu membukanya kembali dalam Split View hanya dengan satu ketukan, menghemat waktu setup setiap kali bekerja dengan susunan yang sama.
